description: IN VIVO STRUCTURAL-BASED QUANTITATIVE MODELING OF AQUEOUS OUTFLOW DYNAMICS IN GLAUCOMATOUS EYES - PROJECT SUMMARY GLAUCOMA IS THE GLOBAL LEADING CAUSE OF IRREVERSIBLE BLINDNESS. IT IS AN INSIDIOUS OFTEN ASYMPTOMATIC, NEURODEGENERATIVE OCULAR DISEASE THAT, IF LEFT UNTREATED, CAN RESULT IN COMPLETE LOSS OF VISUAL PERCEPTION. THIS MAKES EARLY DETECTION OF GLAUCOMA A CRITICAL FOCUS OF RESEARCH IN OPHTHALMOLOGY. ONCE DIAGNOSED, DISEASE PROGRESSION CAN BE SLOWED USING A VARIETY OF EFFECTIVE TREATMENT STRATEGIES, ALL OF WHICH AIM TO REDUCE INTRAOCULAR PRESSURE (IOP). ELEVATED IOP IS THE LEADING RISK FACTOR RESULTING FROM A DEFECTIVE AQUEOUS HUMOR OUTFLOW (AHO) MECHANISM. CURRENT STANDARD CLINICAL TREATMENT FOR GLAUCOMA CONSISTS OF EYE DROPS, SELECTIVE LASER TRABULECTOMY (SLT), AND FILTRATION SURGERIES, ALL OF WHICH AIM TO FACILITATE EGRESS OF AQUEOUS FROM THE EYE’S ANTERIOR CHAMBER INTO THE BLOOD STREAM UNTIL A LOWER, TARGET IOP IS ACHIEVED. THESE THERAPIES CAN VARY IN SUCCESS AND LONGEVITY IN BOTH LOWERING IOP AND SLOWING DOWN DISEASE PROGRESSION. DESPITE TREATMENT MECHANISMS TARGETING AHO CELLULAR AND STRUCTURAL COMPONENTS, IN VIVO AHO MORPHOLOGY IS NOT FULLY UNDERSTOOD, IN HEALTH OR DISEASE. THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP IS AT LEAST IN PART DUE TO LIMITED VISIBILITY OF AHO AND A LACK OF QUANTITATIVE ANALYSIS TOOLS. THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS THESIS IS TO ESTABLISH A MORPHOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE AHO SYSTEM IN HEALTHY AND GLAUCOMATOUS EYES IN LIVE PEOPLE. THE STRATEGY IS AN INTEGRATIVE APPROACH, COMBINING IN VIVO ANTERIOR SEGMENT OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY (AS-OCT) IMAGING WITH ADVANCED IMAGE PROCESSING, DEEP LEARNING (DL) AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING BASED ON OUTFLOW FACILITY TO DESCRIBE THE AHO PATHWAY MORPHOLOGY IN HEALTHY AND GLAUCOMATOUS EYES. BY CHARACTERIZING THE THREE-DIMENSIONAL (3D) ARCHITECTURE OF KEY AHO STRUCTURES AND EVALUATING ITS CHANGES UNDER VARIOUS DISEASE STATES, THIS STUDY WILL ESTABLISH A COMPREHENSIVE IN VIVO MODEL OF THE AHO SYSTEM FOR THE FIRST TIME, PAVING THE WAY FOR IMPROVED KNOWLEDGE OF GLAUCOMA PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND POTENTIAL NOVEL TREATMENT OUTCOME MEASURES FOR IMPROVED GLAUCOMA CARE. THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS IS THAT DETECTABLE STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCES WITHIN THE AHO PATHWAY CAN BE OBSERVED IN THE AHO STRUCTURE BETWEEN HEALTHY AND GLAUCOMA USING COMPREHENSIVE IN VIVO MODELING, ENABLING PERSONALIZED OUTCOME MEASURES, PROGRESSION TRACKING, AND ADDITIONAL DISCRIMINATION BETWEEN HEALTH AND DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNDERSTANDING PHYSIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF SEASONAL REPRODUCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT IN HUMANS AND OTHER MAMMALS, STARVATION, EXTENSIVE EXERCISE, AND COLD EXPOSURE DEPLETE FAT RESERVES AND CAUSE WEIGHT LOSS. THE DEPLETION OF ENERGY STORES ATTENUATES THE FUNCTION OF THE REPRODUCTIVE AXIS, CAUSING HYPOGONADISM, DELAYS IN MATURATION AND INFERTILITY. THIRTEEN-LINED GROUND SQUIRRELS (ICTIDOMYS TRIDECEMLINEATUS) ARE OBLIGATORY HIBERNATORS THAT SPEND 7 MONTHS WITH NO ACCESS TO FOOD OR WATER AT LOW ENVIRONMENTAL AND BODY TEMPERATURE. FOR MOST MAMMALS THESE CONDITIONS ARE INHABITABLE AND CAN LEAD TO INFERTILITY AND ULTIMATELY DEATH. FEMALE GROUND SQUIRRELS MATE ONCE ANNUALLY, AND THEIR FERTILE WINDOW IS TIGHTLY LOCKED TO EMERGENCE FROM HIBERNATION, WITH PEAK MATING SUCCESS IN THE FIRST WEEK POST EMERGENCE. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT FEMALE GROUND SQUIRRELS UNDERGO SEXUAL MATURATION DURING HIBERNATION, AND THEIR REPRODUCTIVE AXIS IS AT LEAST PARTIALLY UNCOUPLED FROM METABOLISM AND ENERGY BALANCE. CONSISTENT WITH THIS HYPOTHESIS, OUR PRELIMINARY DATA REVEALED INCREASED LEVELS OF SEX HORMONES AND GROWTH OF REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS IN FEMALE GROUND SQUIRRELS DURING HIBERNATION. THE NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL AND MOLECULAR PATHWAYS UNDERLYING THIS REMARKABLE BIOLOGICAL CAPACITY ARE UNKNOWN. HERE WE AIM TO INVESTIGATE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS SUPPORTING SEXUAL MATURATION DURING HIBERNATION AND REVEAL HOW THE REPRODUCTIVE AXIS BECOMES UNCOUPLED FROM METABOLISM. THROUGH THE SUPPORT OF THIS FELLOWSHIP, WE AIM TO REVEAL THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE PROCESS OF FEMALE SEXUAL MATURATION VIA THE UNIQUE PERSPECTIVE OF FEMALE THIRTEEN-LINED GROUND SQUIRRELS. THIS STUDY WILL BE CONDUCTED AT YALE UNIVERSITY IN THE LABORATORY OF DR. ELENA GRACHEVA. THROUGH AIM 1, WE PROPOSE A SERIES OF LONGITUDINAL EXPERIMENTS TO REVEAL CHANGES IN ACTIVITY OF THE REPRODUCTIVE AXIS ACROSS SEASONS USING MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH INCLUDING RNA IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION, BLOOD BIOCHEMISTRY AND MORPHOMETRIC ANALYSIS OF THE REPRODUCTIVE TRACT. WITHIN AIM 2, WE WILL ASSESS THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR CHANGES ACROSS PHYSIOLOGICAL STATES IN KISSPEPTIN (REPRODUCTIVE) NEURONS IN THE ARCUATE NUCLEUS OF THE HYPOTHALAMUS USING SINGLE NUCLEUS SEQUENCING, ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY AND IN VIVO IMAGING. THIS PROPOSAL HIGHLIGHTS GENERAL PRINCIPLES OF REPRODUCTIVE NEUROPHYSIOLOGY IN MAMMALS AND WILL FURTHER OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE NEUROENDOCRINE SYSTEM DURING EXTREME DEFICITS IN ENVIRONMENTAL AND BODY CONDITIONS. OUR WORK WILL LAY FOUNDATION FOR RATIONAL DESIGN OF PHARMACOLOGICAL TOOLS TO UNDERSTAND HOW LIFE IN MAMMALS CAN PERSIST DURING PROLONGED COLD EXPOSURE AND STARVATION AND HOW THE REPRODUCTIVE AXIS FUNCTIONS UNDER EXTREME NEGATIVE ENERGY BALANCE. RESULTS FROM THIS PROPOSAL WILL GENERATE TESTABLE HYPOTHESES REGARDING THE REGULATION OF REPRODUCTION AND ALLOW US TO PREDICT WHETHER HIBERNATION CAN BE INDUCED IN OTHER MAMMALS, INCLUDING HUMANS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING HOW HISTONE METHYLTRANSFERASES CAUSE GENE SILENCING IN THE C. ELEGANS GERMLINE - PROJECT SUMMARY IN EUKARYOTES, THE GENOMIC INTEGRITY OF GERM CELLS IS MAINTAINED BY CHROMATIN AND SMALL RNA PATHWAYS, CONFERRING GERMLINE IMMORTALITY AND FERTILITY. IN THE CAENORHABDITIS ELEGANS (C. ELEGANS) GERMLINE, NUCLEAR RNA INTERFERENCE (RNAI) FACTORS, IN COMPLEX WITH SMALL RNAS AND NASCENT TARGET TRANSCRIPTS, RECRUIT HISTONE METHYLTRANSFERASES (HMTS) THAT DEPOSIT REPRESSIVE HISTONE MODIFICATIONS, THEREBY TRIGGERING HETEROCHROMATIN FORMATION. THIS PROCESS HAS ALSO BEEN OBSERVED IN OTHER EUKARYOTES. THE COMPLEX INTERPLAY BETWEEN SMALL RNA AND HETEROCHROMATIN PATHWAYS PRESENTS A CHALLENGE IN STUDYING HOW INDIVIDUAL HMTS CONTRIBUTE TO GENE SILENCING AND GERMLINE IMMORTALITY. THE RECENT DEVELOPMENT OF AN ASSAY IN C. ELEGANS THAT USES THE LAC OPERATOR-LAC REPRESSOR BINDING SYSTEM FROM ESCHERICHIA COLI (E. COLI) TO TETHER HMTS UPSTREAM OF A TRANSGENE (GFP) REPORTER HAS ENABLED DIRECT STUDY OF HMT EFFECTS ON GENE EXPRESSION. PRELIMINARY STUDIES USING THIS SYSTEM HAVE SHOWN THAT TETHERING AN H3K9 METHYLTRANSFERASE (MET-2 OR SET-25) TRIGGERS CIS-SILENCING OF THE DOWNSTREAM GFP REPORTER, TRANS-SILENCING OF A SECONDARY UNTETHERED GFP REPORTER INTRODUCED BY CROSSING, AND PRODUCTION OF SMALL RNAS TARGETING THE GFP REPORTER. SUBSEQUENT ANALYSIS IDENTIFIED SEVERAL NUCLEAR RNAI FACTORS REQUIRED FOR TRANS-SILENCING. THESE FINDINGS IMPLICATE TRANS-SILENCING IN THE MAINTENANCE OF GERMLINE IMMORTALITY. HOWEVER, IT REMAINS UNCLEAR WHAT THE PRECISE ROLES OF HETEROCHROMATIN AND SMALL RNAS ARE IN HMT TETHERING-INDUCED SILENCING, HOW THE GFP REPORTER TRANSCRIPTS ARE RECOGNIZED AS TARGETS FOR SMALL RNA PRODUCTION, AND WHICH OTHER GENETIC FACTORS ARE REQUIRED TO INITIATE AND/OR MAINTAIN CIS- AND TRANS-SILENCING INDUCED BY HMT TETHERING. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO UNDERSTAND HOW HMTS CAUSE GENE SILENCING AND SMALL RNA PRODUCTION IN THE C. ELEGANS GERMLINE. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE THE ROLES OF HETEROCHROMATIN AND SMALL RNAS IN HMT TETHERING-INDUCED CIS- AND TRANS-SILENCING. CHROMATIN PROFILING WILL BE USED TO IDENTIFY HISTONE MODIFICATIONS ENRICHED AT THE REPORTER LOCUS FOLLOWING TETHERING, AND CATALYTICALLY INACTIVE HMT MUTANTS WILL BE TETHERED TO DETERMINE IF METHYLTRANSFERASE ACTIVITY IS REQUIRED FOR CIS- AND TRANS-SILENCING. TO INVESTIGATE SMALL RNAS, A NUCLEAR RNAI FACTOR WILL BE IMMUNOPRECIPITATED AFTER HMT TETHERING, AND BOUND SMALL RNAS WILL BE SEQUENCED. HMTS WILL ALSO BE TETHERED IN A MUTANT STRAIN DEPLETED FOR SMALL RNAS, AND TRANS-SILENCING WILL BE MEASURED. AIM 2 WILL CHARACTERIZE REPORTER TRANSCRIPT PROCESSING AND LOCALIZATION AFTER HMT TETHERING USING LONG-READ DIRECT RNA SEQUENCING AND RNA FLUORESCENCE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION, RESPECTIVELY. AIM 3 WILL IDENTIFY GENETIC FACTORS REQUIRED TO INITIATE AND MAINTAIN CIS- AND TRANS-SILENCING. CRISPR/CAS9 GENE EDITING WILL BE USED TO GENERATE MUTATIONS IN CANDIDATE FACTORS BEFORE OR AFTER HMT-TETHERING, AND CIS- AND TRANS-SILENCING WILL BE MEASURED. THIS WORK WILL ELUCIDATE HOW HMTS AND SMALL RNAS COOPERATE TO CONTROL GENE SILENCING AND MAINTAIN GERMLINE IMMORTALITY, AND PROVIDE THE FELLOW WITH TRAINING IN WORM GENETICS, RNA BIOLOGY, CHROMATIN DYNAMICS, MICROSCOPY, AND BIOINFORMATICS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING THE PLACENTAL SELENOPROTEOME - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SELENIUM (SE) IS AN ESSENTIAL TRACE ELEMENT REQUIRED FOR A HEALTHY PREGNANCY, AND IT HAS BEEN ESTIMATED THAT 2.8 BILLION PEOPLE WORLDWIDE DO NOT CONSUME ENOUGH SE. MATERNAL SE DEFICIENCY IS ASSOCIATED WITH MISCARRIAGE, INFERTILITY, PRETERM BIRTH, FETAL GROWTH RESTRICTION (FGR), PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION, GESTATIONAL DIABETES MELLITUS, AND PREECLAMPSIA. SE IS INCORPORATED INTO SELENOPROTEINS FOR FUNCTION. SELENOPROTEINS ARE PRODUCED BY THE PLACENTA AND ARE CRITICAL FOR CELLULAR METABOLISM AND MITIGATION OF OXIDATIVE STRESS. THE PLACENTA IS A HIGHLY METABOLIC ORGAN WHOSE GROWTH AND FUNCTION ARE REQUIRED FOR PROPER FETAL DEVELOPMENT. METABOLIC DYSREGULATION CAN LEAD TO THE ACCUMULATION OF REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES AND COMPROMISE FUNCTION. DESPITE THE WELL-ESTABLISHED INVOLVEMENT OF SE AND SELENOPROTEINS IN THESE PROCESSES AND THE LINKS BETWEEN ADVERSE PREGNANCY OUTCOMES AND SE DEFICIENCY, THERE HAS BEEN NO INVESTIGATION WHICH TRULY OUTLINES THE FUNCTIONAL SIGNIFICANCE OF SELENOPROTEINS PRODUCED BY THE PLACENTA. THESE INCLUDE IODOTHYRONINE DEIODINASE 2 (DIO2), A SELENOPROTEIN RESPONSIBLE FOR THYROID HORMONE METABOLISM, WHICH IS INDISPENSABLE FOR HUMANS. MOREOVER, A RATE-LIMITING FACTOR OF SELENOPROTEIN BIOSYNTHESIS, SECIS BINDING PROTEIN 2 (SBP2), IS ALSO PRODUCED BY THE PLACENTA. SBP2 MUTATIONS MANIFEST IN ADULT INFERTILITY AND SIGNIFICANTLY IMPACTED GROWTH AND ABNORMAL THYROID HORMONE PROFILES. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS F31 PREDOCTORAL FELLOWSHIP IS TO USE OUR IN VIVO PLACENTA-SPECIFIC LENTIVIRAL-MEDIATED RNA INTERFERENCE (RNAI) TECHNIQUE TO DIRECTLY INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF THE PLACENTAL SELENOPROTEOME DURING THE FIRST HALF OF GESTATION USING THE SHEEP MODEL. AIM 1 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT PLACENTAL DIO2 DEFICIENCY RESULTS IN PLACENTAL INSUFFICIENCY AND ABNORMAL THYROID HORMONE METABOLISM IN SHEEP AT MIDGESTATION [75 DAYS OF GESTATIONAL AGE (DGA)]. AIM 2 WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT PLACENTAL SBP2 DEFICIENCY WILL RESULT IN A DECREASED PLACENTAL SELENOPROTEOME, LEADING TO PLACENTAL METABOLIC DYSFUNCTION AND OXIDATIVE STRESS, WITH ABERRANT PLACENTAL DEVELOPMENT AND SIGNIFICANT FGR RESULTING AS CONSEQUENCE AT MIDGESTATION (75 DGA). THESE PROJECTS WILL BE THE FIRST TO DIRECTLY IDENTIFY THE ROLE OF PLACENTAL SELENOPROTEINS IN PREGNANCY. ALL WORK WILL BE COMPLETED AT THE ANIMAL REPRODUCTION AND BIOTECHNOLOGY LABORATORY AT COLORADO STATE UNIVERSITY AND OVERSEEN BY MY SUPPORTIVE SPONSOR, DR. QUINTON WINGER, AND CO-SPONSOR, DR. JANE STREMMING, WHO RESIDES AT THE UNIVERSITY OF COLORADO ANSCHUTZ MEDICAL CAMPUS. MY TAILORED TRAINING PLAN IS DESIGNED TO SUPPORT MY DEVELOPMENT INTO A WELL-ROUNDED, INDEPENDENT BIOMEDICAL SCIENTIST. IT WILL EMPHASIZE MY ADVANCEMENTS IN SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION AND GRANTSMANSHIP, SURGICAL AND LEADERSHIP SKILLS, AND OVERALL UNDERSTANDING OF PLACENTAL AND FETAL PHYSIOLOGY AS PREGNANCY PROGRESSES. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO UNDERSTAND HOW THE PLACENTAL SELENOPROTEOME CONTRIBUTES TO PREGNANCY OUTCOMES. THIS PROPOSAL DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THE NICHD’S RESEARCH GOAL 3: “SETTING THE FOUNDATION FOR HEALTHY PREGNANCIES AND LIFELONG WELLNESS” THROUGH THE USE OF INNOVATIVE BASIC AND TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE APPROACHES TO FURTHER UNDERSTAND IMPACTS ON THE PLACENTA AND ITS RESULTING FETAL IMPACTS IN GESTATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CEREBELLAR GABAERGIC PERTURBATION IN A NDD MOUSE MODEL - PROJECT SUMMARY AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD) IS A NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER (NDD) THAT AFFECTS MORE THAN 2% OF THE US POPULATION. DESPITE THE HIGH PREVALENCE AND KNOWN GENETIC CAUSES, LACK OF UNDERSTANDING OF CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF ASD IS A MAJOR BARRIER TOWARDS DEVELOPING EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS FOR THIS COMPLEX DISORDER. MUCH OF THE UNDERSTANDING OF THE GENETIC ETIOLOGY IN ASD COMES FROM LARGE SCALE GENOME SEQUENCING EFFORTS, WHICH HAVE REVEALED A GROWING LIST OF HIGH CONFIDENCE RISK GENES. OF THESE RARE BUT STRONGLY CAUSAL ASD RISK GENES, THE CHROMATIN REMODELING FACTOR (CRF) CHROMODOMAIN HELICASE DNA-BINDING PROTEIN 8 (CHD8) HAS AMONG THE MOST FREQUENT AND HIGHEST PENETRANCE FOR DE NOVO MUTATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH ASD DIAGNOSIS. CHD8 HAS BEEN BROADLY CHARACTERIZED AS A REGULATOR OF NEUROGENESIS AND BRAIN DEVELOPMENT THOUGH MUCH REMAINS UNKNOWN REGARDING DIRECT AND INDIRECT ROLES OF THIS PROTEIN IN SPECIFIC CELL TYPES IN THE DEVELOPING BRAIN. STUDIES OF MICE WITH GERMLINE HETEROZYGOUS LOSS-OF-FUNCTION (LOF) MUTATIONS TO CHD8 HAVE FOUND BEHAVIORAL AND COGNITIVE DEFICITS, SUBTLE SOCIAL PHENOTYPES, AND MACROCEPHALY, AS WELL AS TRANSCRIPTIONAL, CELLULAR, AND MOLECULAR PATHOLOGY RELEVANT TO ASD. MOST MOLECULAR STUDIES INTO THE FUNCTION OF THIS GENE ARE FOCUSED ON NEURODEVELOPMENT IN THE CORTEX. AND ALTHOUGH TYPICALLY STUDIED IN THE CONTEXT OF MOTOR FUNCTION, THE CEREBELLUM (CB) PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE IN HIGHER ORDER COGNITIVE FUNCTIONS AND CB DYSFUNCTION HAS BEEN SHOWN TO BE CORRELATED WITH ASD AND NDD. THERE HAVE BEEN A FEW STUDIES ON THE ROLE OF CHD8 IN THE CB, WHICH HAVE SHOWN REQUIREMENT FOR CHD8 FOR CB DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTION. HOWEVER, PREVIOUS REPORTS HAVE USED CONDITIONAL KNOCKOUT APPROACHES RATHER THAN THE ASD-RELEVANT GERMLINE HETEROZYGOUS STATE, AND LARGELY FAILED TO IDENTIFY IMPACTS IN HETEROZYGOUS MUTANT MICE IN THE CB IN PURKINJE NEURON (PN) AND GRANULE CELL PROGENITOR CKOS. PRELIMINARY DATA IN OUR LAB FOUND CELL TYPE SPECIFIC TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND FUNCTIONAL PERTURBATION TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF CB GABAERGIC CELL TYPES, INCLUDING PNS. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE HETEROZYGOUS CHD8 MUTATION CONTRIBUTES TO ASD PATHOGENESIS THROUGH DEVELOPMENTAL DYSREGULATION OF PNS, THE ONLY PROJECTING CELL TYPE FROM THE CB CORTEX. HERE I PROPOSE WORK TO CHARACTERIZE THE EFFECT OF CHD8 HAPLOINSUFFICIENCY ON THE FUNCTION AND DEVELOPMENT OF PNS USING TRANSLATIONALLY RELEVANT CONSTITUTIVE HETEROZYGOUS CHD8 MUTANT MICE. IN AIM 1, I WILL INTEGRATE HISTOLOGY, ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, AND TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO TEST WHETHER THE COMPOSITION AND FUNCTION OF PN SUBTYPES IS ALTERED IN CHD8 HAPLOINISUFFICIENT MICE. IN AIM 2, I WILL USE SINGLE CELL TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO TEST IF GABAERGIC NEUROGENESIS IS ALTERED IN THE CB VENTRICULAR ZONE. THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISM AND EFFECTS OF DECREASED CHD8 DOSAGE ON A KEY CELL TYPE IN THE CB. IF SUCCESSFUL, THIS PROPOSAL WILL INFORM FUTURE DIRECTIONS FOR MEASURES TO TREAT UNDERLYING PATHOLOGY AND PROVIDE A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLE CRFS PLAY IN CB NEUROGENESIS AND ASD ETIOLOGY.

description: FUNCTIONALLY SPECIALIZED TEMPORAL AND FRONTAL LOBE REGIONS FOR IDENTITY RECOGNITION AND UPDATING - PROJECT SUMMARY A CENTRAL QUESTION IN SOCIAL BEHAVIOR RESEARCH IS HOW INDIVIDUAL IDENTITIES ARE RECOGNIZED AND UPDATED AS FEATURES CHANGE OVER TIME. DIFFICULTIES WITH IDENTITY RECOGNITION AND THEIR SOCIAL CONSEQUENCES CAN LEAD TO SOCIAL WITHDRAWAL, WHICH MAY WORSEN OTHER CONDITIONS. IDENTITY RECOGNITION IS IMPAIRED IN INDIVIDUALS WITH NEUROPSYCHIATRIC AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS LIKE ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD), CAUSING SIGNIFICANT DISRUPTIONS IN DAILY LIFE. THE DORSOLATERAL PREFRONTAL CORTEX (DLPFC) IS KNOWN TO SUPPORT HIGH-LEVEL COGNITIVE TASKS, INCLUDING PROCESSING TARGET IDENTITY, UNCERTAINTY, AND SOCIAL PREDICTION. CONVERSELY, THE SUPERIOR TEMPORAL SULCUS (STS) PROCESSES CONSPECIFIC IDENTITY AND FEATURES. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW NEURONAL ACTIVITY IN DLPFC AND STS SHIFTS TO ADAPT TO IDENTITY UPDATING AND HOW THE PROJECTION FROM STS TO DLPFC (STSDLPFC) FACILITATES THIS PROCESS. FACES AND VOICES ARE THE MOST CRUCIAL ASPECTS OF CONSPECIFIC IDENTITY, WITH HUMANS AND NONHUMAN PRIMATES EVOLVING HIGH VARIABILITY IN THESE FEATURES TO AID RECOGNITION. IN AIM 1, TO STUDY IDENTITY RECOGNITION AND UPDATING BEHAVIOR, I WILL TRAIN MARMOSET MONKEYS ON A NOVEL FACE-VOICE MATCHING TASK THAT TEACHES THEM TO RECOGNIZE SEVERAL CONSPECIFIC IDENTITIES FROM VIDEOS OF VOCALIZING INDIVIDUALS. AFTER LEARNING AN IDENTITY, WE WILL ALTER A FACIAL FEATURE'S COLOR OR SHAPE WHILE KEEPING THE VOICE UNCHANGED, ANCHORING IDENTITY THROUGH VOICE RECOGNITION AND REQUIRING SUBJECTS TO “UPDATE” THEIR FACIAL REPRESENTATION. I WILL FUNCTIONALLY LOCALIZE THE ACTIVE DLPFC AND STS DURING THE UPDATING PROCESS USING FDG-PET SCANS, AND IMPLANT MULTIELECTRODE ARRAYS INTO DLPFC AND STS TO RECORD NEURAL ACTIVITY DURING IDENTITY RECOGNITION AND UPDATING. I PREDICT THAT POPULATION ACTIVITY PATTERNS IN DLPFC WILL INITIALLY DIFFER FOR THE ALTERED FEATURES BUT WILL EVENTUALLY CONVERGE TO THE LEARNED IDENTITY AFTER UPDATING, PARALLELING BEHAVIORAL PERFORMANCE. ADDITIONALLY, I EXPECT STS ACTIVITY TO PREDICT DLPFC ACTIVITY, ESTABLISHING A CAUSAL RELATIONSHIP, ALTHOUGH ACTIVITY IN STS RELATED TO ALTERED FEATURES WILL REMAIN DISTINCT FROM THE LEARNED IDENTITY AFTER UPDATING. IN AIM 2, I WILL EXAMINE THE NECESSITY OF THE STSDLPFC PROJECTION FOR IDENTITY UPDATING. USING CHEMOGENETIC APPROACHES WITH NOVEL VIRAL VECTORS, I WILL ASSESS HOW INHIBITION OF STSDLPFC AFFECTS BEHAVIORAL UPDATING PERFORMANCE. I PREDICT THAT INACTIVATING STSDLPFC DURING UPDATING, BUT NOT RECOGNITION, WILL DECREASE PERFORMANCE ACCURACY AND INCREASE RESPONSE LATENCY. THE INSIGHTS FROM THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL PROVIDE A NEW FRAMEWORK FOR UNDERSTANDING NEURAL CIRCUITS INVOLVED IN IDENTITY PROCESSING, WHICH COULD INFORM HOW THESE CIRCUITS BREAK DOWN IN NEURODEGENERATIVE AND NEUROPSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS SUCH AS AD AND ASD. THIS WORK WILL BE CONDUCTED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH, WHERE I WILL BE SUPPORTED BY MENTORS WHO WILL TRAIN ME IN SCIENTIFIC CONCEPTS, TECHNIQUES, AND PROFESSIONALISM. MY TRAINING WILL ENCOMPASS BEHAVIORAL, NEUROIMAGING, CHEMOGENETIC, NEUROPHYSIOLOGICAL, AND COMPUTATIONAL METHODS TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF IDENTITY PROCESSING. DEVELOPING THESE SKILLS IS ESSENTIAL FOR MY GOAL OF BECOMING AN INDEPENDENT NEUROSCIENTIST SPECIALIZING IN IDENTITY PROCESSING AND MULTISENSORY INTEGRATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DETERMINING THE ROLE OF THE PARABRACHIAL NUCLEUS IN CHEMOSENSITIVITY AND EPILEPSY - ABSTRACT SUDDEN UNEXPECTED DEATH IN EPILEPSY (SUDEP) IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH IN PATIENTS WITH REFRACTORY EPILEPSY. SUDEP IS SECOND ONLY TO STROKE IN YEARS OF POTENTIAL LIFE LOST TO NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE, THEREFORE REPRESENTING A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH ISSUE. VICTIMS ARE OFTEN FOUND ALONE, MAKING THE EVENTS PRIOR TO DEATH ELUSIVE AND DIFFICULT TO DEFINE. ALTHOUGH SUDEP IS A DIAGNOSIS OF EXCLUSION, SEVERAL ETIOLOGIES HAVE BEEN PROPOSED FOR SUDEP. THE FIELD HAS INCLUDING CARDIAC AND RESPIRATORY DYSREGULATION FOLLOWING SEIZURE TERMINATION AS CRITICAL CONTRIBUTORS TO A POTENTIALLY FATAL OUTCOME. AN ADDITIONAL ETIOLOGY THAT IS POSTULATED IS POST-SEIZURE, OR POST-ICTAL, IMPAIRED AROUSAL. SEIZURES IMPAIR ONE’S ABILITY TO APPROPRIATELY RESPOND TO STIMULI. THIS IS INCLUSIVE OF STIMULUS THAT NORMALLY RESULTS IN AROUSAL. AMONG AROUSAL STIMULI, ONE THAT IS PARTICULARLY RELEVANT TO SUDEP IS CO2. CO2 RISES FOLLOWING SEIZURES AND IS PART OF THE SEIZURE CESSATION MECHANISM. SEIZURES ARE FREQUENTLY ASSOCIATED WITH ICTAL AND POST- ICTAL CENTRAL AND OBSTRUCTIVE APNEAS. AN APNEIC EPISODE FURTHER EXACERBATES THE ACCUMULATION OF CO2. IMPAIRMENT OF THE CO2-AROUSAL MECHANISM IS PROPOSED AS AN ETIOLOGICAL FACTOR IN ANOTHER SUDDEN DEATH ENTITY, SUDDEN INFANT DEATH SYNDROME, WHICH HAS MANY PARALLELS WITH SUDEP. INVESTIGATING THE MODULATION OF CHEMOSENSITIVE POPULATIONS FOR PROPER CO2-AROUSAL PROVIDES AN INITIAL COURSE OF ACTION IN UNDERSTANDING WHAT POPULATIONS ARE IMPAIRED IN THE CONTEXT OF SEIZURES AND EPILEPSY. THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY HOW CO2-AROUSAL CAN BE PROMOTED AND WHAT POPULATIONS ARE ASSOCIATED WITH NEGATING SEIZURE-INDUCED DEATH. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DETERMINE THE CHEMOSENSITIVE PROPERTIES OF THE CALCITONIN GENE-RELATED PEPTIDE-EXPRESSING SUBPOPULATION IN THE EXTERNAL LATERAL REGION OF THE PARABRACHIAL NUCLEUS (PBELCGRP) BY EVALUATING CO2-AROUSAL DURING OPTOGENETIC INHIBITION. WE WILL TEST WHETHER SUPPRESSING PBELCGRP NEURONAL ACTIVITY PROLONGS AROUSAL LATENCY TO A CO2 STIMULUS. PROLONGED CO2-AROUSAL LATENCY WOULD PROVIDE ADDITIONAL EVIDENCE THAT PBELCGRP NEURONS CONTRIBUTE CRITICALLY TO THE ASCENDING AROUSAL SYSTEM THAT MEDIATES HOMEOSTATIC RESPONSES TO HYPERCAPNIA. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER OPTOGENETIC ACTIVATION OF THE PBELCGRP NEURONS REDUCES SEIZURE-INDUCED DEATH BY PROMOTING RECOVERY OF RESPIRATORY AND BEHAVIORAL FUNCTION IN A MOUSE MODEL OF SEIZURE-INDUCED DEATH. THIS MODEL, WHICH EXHIBITS A DEATH PHENOTYPE RESEMBLING SEIZURE-INDUCED RESPIRATORY ARREST, ALLOWS US TO COMPARE FINDINGS BETWEEN MICE THAT DIE AND THOSE THAT SURVIVE, MAKING THESE STUDIES HIGHLY RELEVANT TO SUDEP. SIGNIFICANT REDUCTION IN MORTALITY WOULD ESTABLISH THE PBELCGRP SUBPOPULATION AS A LOCATION FOR INTERVENTION AND FURTHER INVESTIGATION TO PROMOTE RECOVERY. COMBINED WITH PREVIOUS WORK, WE WILL HAVE A POWERFUL, RIGOROUS, AND TRANSLATABLE APPROACH TO IDENTIFY CONVERGENT AND DIVERGENT MECHANISMS ACROSS MODELS FOR HOW IMPAIRED CO2- AROUSAL CONTRIBUTES TO SUDEP RISK AND WHAT POPULATIONS CAN MITIGATE THIS RISK. THE PROPOSED WORK WILL HAVE AN IMMEDIATE POSITIVE IMPACT AS IT WILL FORM THE INITIAL FOUNDATION TO EXPAND UPON FOR FUTURE RESEARCH OF POST-ICTAL IMPAIRED AROUSAL IS A CONTRIBUTING MECHANISM OF SUDEP.

description: ELUCIDATING NEURON-ASTROCYTE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING ULTRASOUND STIMULATION FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURODEGENERATIVE CONDITIONS LIKE ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IMPOSE A GROWING PUBLIC HEALTH BURDEN, AFFECTING OVER SEVEN MILLION AMERICANS AND COSTING MORE THAN $360 BILLION ANNUALLY. AD IS CHARACTERIZED BY AMYLOID-BETA (AΒ) BUILDUP, NEURONAL HYPERACTIVITY, AND COGNITIVE DECLINE, BUT GROWING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT DISRUPTED COMMUNICATION BETWEEN NEURONS AND ASTROCYTES PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN DISEASE PROGRESSION. ASTROCYTES ARE ESSENTIAL FOR MAINTAINING SYNAPTIC AND CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS THROUGH TIGHTLY REGULATED CALCIUM (CA2+)- DEPENDENT SIGNALING. HOWEVER, IN AD, ABERRANT ASTROCYTE CA2+ WAVES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH NEURAL HYPEREXCITABILITY AND IMPAIRED NETWORK FUNCTION. ELUCIDATING WHETHER MODULATING THESE ABERRANT CA2+ WAVES CAN RESTORE CIRCUIT STABILITY AND DISRUPTED NEURON-ASTROCYTE COMMUNICATION REPRESENTS A PROMISING, YET UNDEREXPLORED, THERAPEUTIC AVENUE. THIS GAP IN NEURON-ASTROCYTE COMMUNICATION PRESENTS AN URGENT NEED FOR NOVEL APPROACHES TO MITIGATE DISEASE PROGRESSION. LOW-INTENSITY PULSED ULTRASOUND (LIPUS) HAS EMERGED AS A NON-INVASIVE NEUROMODULATION APPROACH CAPABLE OF INFLUENCING CELLULAR ACTIVITY THROUGH MECHANOSENSITIVE PATHWAYS, BUT ITS UNDERLYING MECHANISMS IN AD REMAIN UNCLEAR. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LIPUS RESTORES HEALTHY NEURON-ASTROCYTE COMMUNICATION BY ACTIVATING ASTROCYTIC CA2+ SIGNALING TO REDUCE HIPPOCAMPAL HYPERACTIVITY AND IMPROVE COGNITION. THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH THE MECHANISTIC ROLE OF ASTROCYTE CA2+ IN MEDIATING THE THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS OF LIPUS AND ASSESSING ITS POTENTIAL TO AMELIORATE CIRCUIT DYSFUNCTION AND COGNITIVE DECLINE IN AD. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER ASTROCYTE CA2+ IS NECESSARY FOR LIPUS-INDUCED MODULATION OF NEURONAL HYPERACTIVITY IN THE HIPPOCAMPAL CA1 REGION OF APP/PS1 MICE. USING VIRAL VECTORS TO REDUCE ASTROCYTIC CA2+ (CALEX) COMBINED WITH IN VIVO ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, WE WILL RECORD SPONTANEOUS AND EVOKED NEURAL ACTIVITY DURING ONE MONTH OF LIPUS OR SHAM TREATMENT TO TEST WHETHER REDUCED ASTROCYTE CA2+ DIMINISHES LIPUS EFFICACY. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS THE LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF LIPUS ON NEURONAL AND ASTROCYTIC CA2+ DYNAMICS, AMYLOID PATHOLOGY, AND COGNITION. USING DUAL-COLOR FIBER PHOTOMETRY AND BEHAVIORAL ASSAYS (NOVEL OBJECT RECOGNITION AND BARNES MAZE), WE WILL EVALUATE WHETHER LIPUS NORMALIZES NEURON-ASTROCYTE CA2+ ACTIVITY, DECREASES AΒ PLAQUE LOAD, AND IMPROVES COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE RELATIVE TO SHAM OR GAMMA-ENTRAINMENT (GENUS) CONTROLS. ACHIEVING THESE AIMS WILL ESTABLISH ASTROCYTE CA2+ AS A KEY MECHANISTIC MEDIATOR OF LIPUS EFFICACY AND REVEAL HOW ULTRASOUND NEUROMODULATION RESTORES NEURAL CIRCUIT STABILITY IN AD. THROUGH MY TRAINING PLAN, MY SPONSOR AND CO-SPONSOR WILL PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE MENTORSHIP IN ULTRASOUND TECHNOLOGIES, ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY, FIBER PHOTOMETRY, AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE MODELING. COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL EQUIP ME TO BRIDGE MECHANISTIC NEUROSCIENCE AND NEUROENGINEERING – DEVELOPING NEXT-GENERATION, NON-INVASIVE TECHNOLOGIES THAT TARGET NEUROGLIAL DYSFUNCTION TO IMPROVE OUTCOMES IN AD AND RELATED NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS.

description: LINKING STIMULATION PATTERN-DRIVEN AND CELL-SPECIFIC MYELINATION TO COGNITIVE OUTCOMES IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AFFECTS MILLIONS OF AMERICANS AND IS CHARACTERIZED BY EARLY MYELIN LOSS, CIRCUIT INSTABILITY, AND COGNITIVE DECLINE. MYELIN, PRODUCED BY OLIGODENDROCYTES, IS ESSENTIAL FOR MAINTAINING NEURAL CIRCUIT STABILITY, YET CURRENT NEUROMODULATION STRATEGIES FOCUS ALMOST EXCLUSIVELY ON NEURONAL ACTIVITY, OVERLOOKING HOW OLIGODENDROCYTES RESPOND TO STIMULATION. THIS PROJECT TESTS THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT DISTINCT PATTERNS OF BRAIN STIMULATION CAN DRIVE OLIGODENDROCYTE CALCIUM ACTIVITY TO PRODUCE SPECIFIC MYELINATION OUTCOMES, AND THAT TARGETING PARTICULAR NEURONAL SUBTYPES WILL DIFFERENTIALLY INFLUENCE MYELINATION AT THE CELL- SPECIFIC AND NETWORK LEVEL, WITH IMPLICATIONS FOR COGNITIVE FUNCTION. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE HOW INTRACORTICAL MICROSTIMULATION PATTERNS EVOKE OLIGODENDROCYTE CALCIUM DYNAMICS AND DRIVE PARADIGM-SPECIFIC MYELIN REMODELING IN VIVO. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER STIMULATING INHIBITORY OR EXCITATORY NEURONAL SUBTYPES ALTERS MYELINATION AT THE CELL AND NETWORK LEVEL AND HOW THESE CHANGES AFFECT COGNITION IN A MOUSE MODEL OF AD. BY INTEGRATING LONGITUDINAL IMAGING, ULTRASTRUCTURAL ANALYSIS, AND BEHAVIORAL ASSESSMENT, THIS RESEARCH WILL ELUCIDATE MECHANISMS LINKING NEURONAL ACTIVITY, MYELIN REMODELING, AND CIRCUIT FUNCTION, ESTABLISHING A FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE STRATEGIES TO PRESERVE COGNITIVE FUNCTION IN AD AND RELATED NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: STEREOVISION: NORMAL CIRCUITS AND IMPACT OF DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS - PROJECT SUMMARY A LARGE MISMATCH IN VISION THROUGH THE TWO EYES DURING DEVELOPMENT IS KNOWN TO CAUSE LASTING DEFICITS IN VISION EVEN AFTER NORMAL VISION HAS BEEN RESTORED, INCLUDING REDUCED VISUAL ACUITY IN ONE EYE AND IMPAIRMENTS IN STEREOVISION OR STEREOPSIS. CURRENT TREATMENTS FOR THESE VISION DEFICITS ARE LIMITED, AND VISUAL IMPAIRMENTS PERSIST INTO ADULTHOOD. FOR NORMAL STEREOPSIS, THE BRAIN MUST CALCULATE AN OBJECT’S DEPTH BASED ON THE SLIGHT DIFFERENCES IN POSITION AN IMAGE CREATES IN EACH EYE, A PROCESS KNOWN AS BINOCULAR DISPARITY. PRIMARY VISUAL CORTEX (V1) IS ONE OF THE FIRST BRAIN AREAS IN THE VISUAL PROCESSING HIERARCHY WITH NEURONS THAT RECEIVE BINOCULAR INPUT AND SHOW SELECTIVITY TO BINOCULAR DISPARITY. THE IMPACTS OF IMPAIRED VISUAL DEVELOPMENT ON DISPARITY TUNING IN V1 HAVE NOT BEEN EXPLORED FULLY AT THE LEVEL OF NEURAL CIRCUITS, AND THERE ARE LIMITED STUDIES LINKING CHANGES BETWEEN PHYSIOLOGY AND CIRCUIT STRUCTURE WITH STEREOSCOPIC BEHAVIOR. THIS RESEARCH TRAINING PROJECT AIMS TO USE A MULTI- TECHNIQUE APPROACH TO STUDY DISRUPTIONS IN BINOCULAR DISPARITY PROCESSING IN V1 AND STEREOSCOPIC BEHAVIOR CAUSED BY DISRUPTED BINOCULAR VISION DURING DEVELOPMENT, USING THE FERRET AS A MODEL. FERRETS ARE HIGHLY VISUAL CARNIVORES, THEIR VISUAL SYSTEM IS SIMILAR TO THAT OF PRIMATES, AND THEIR EARLY BIRTH MAKES THEM AN EXCELLENT MODEL FOR STUDYING VISUAL DEVELOPMENT. IN AIM 1, THIS PROJECT WILL EXAMINE DISRUPTIONS IN NEURAL ENCODING OF DISPARITY TUNING IN V1 CAUSED BY ALTERED VISUAL DEVELOPMENT, AND HOW THEY RELATE TO BEHAVIORAL DEFICITS IN STEREOSCOPIC VISUAL BEHAVIOR. AIM 2 WILL USE 2-PHOTON CALCIUM IMAGING TO EXAMINE THE ORGANIZATION OF NORMAL CIRCUIT STRUCTURE FOR BINOCULAR DISPARITY TUNING IN V1 AND TEST FOR POSSIBLE DISRUPTIONS AFTER ALTERATIONS IN VISUAL DEVELOPMENT, AGAIN RELATING RESULTS TO DEFICITS IN BEHAVIOR. IN TOTAL, THIS PROJECT WILL BRIDGE KEY GAPS IN THE STUDY OF STEREOPSIS AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS BY UTILIZING MULTIPLE TECHNIQUES IN A NOVEL MODEL. IN ADDITION TO PROVIDING THE CANDIDATE WITH TRAINING IN EXPERIMENTAL TECHNIQUES SUCH AS 2-PHOTON IMAGING AND BEHAVIORAL PSYCHOPHYSICS, THIS PROPOSAL WILL ALSO FACILITATE CAREER DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES, TRAINING IN SCIENTIFIC COMMUNICATION AND MENTORING SKILLS, AND NAVIGATING THE TRANSITION TO A FACULTY ROLE AT AN ACADEMIC RESEARCH INSTITUTION. THIS PROJECT IS SPONSORED BY THE LAB OF DR. KRISTINA NIELSEN, A RESEARCHER WITH EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN STUDYING THE DEVELOPMENT OF VISUAL STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION, IN THE MIND BRAIN INSTITUTE AND DEPARTMENT OF NEUROSCIENCE AT JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY. THIS ENVIRONMENT IS EXCELLENT FOR POSTDOCTORAL TRAINING IN NEUROSCIENCE AND WILL PROVIDE THE BEST POSSIBLE SUPPORT FOR THE RESEARCH AND CAREER DEVELOPMENT GOALS OUTLINED IN THIS PROPOSAL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF PEROXISOMAL MEMBRANE PROTEIN TRAFFICKING - PROJECT SUMMARY PEROXISOMES ARE ESSENTIAL CELLULAR ORGANELLES INVOLVED IN LIPID METABOLISM AND CELLULAR DETOXIFICATION, YET THE INTRICACIES OF THEIR FORMATION AND MAINTENANCE REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. PEROXISOME BIOGENESIS DISORDERS (PBDS), INCLUDING ZELLWEGER SPECTRUM DISORDER (ZSD) AND X-LINKED ADRENOLEUKODYSTROPHY, AFFECT 1 IN 50,000 BIRTHS AND CAUSE DEVASTATING NEUROLOGICAL AND METABOLIC DYSFUNCTION DUE TO DEFECTIVE ORGANELLE FORMATION. A CRITICAL STEP IN PEROXISOME BIOGENESIS INVOLVES SOLUBLE AND MEMBRANE PROTEIN IMPORT TO IMMATURE PEROXISOMES. THIS RESEARCH PROJECT AIMS TO UNRAVEL THE FUNDAMENTAL MECHANISMS OF PEROXISOME BIOGENESIS, WITH A FOCUS ON MEMBRANE PROTEIN TRAFFICKING TO THE PEROXISOMES. WHILE SOLUBLE PROTEIN IMPORT TO PEROXISOMES IS WELL CHARACTERIZED, PEROXISOMAL MEMBRANE PROTEIN (PMP) TRAFFICKING MECHANISMS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD, REPRESENTING A CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAP THAT IMPEDES OUR UNDERSTANDING AND TREATMENT OF PBDS. TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, I PROPOSE TO DISSECT THE MOLECULAR DETAILS OF PMP INTERACTION WITH THE PEROXISOME IMPORT RECEPTOR AND CHAPERONE- PEX19. AIM 1 INVESTIGATES THE BIOCHEMICAL AND STRUCTURAL BASIS OF HUMAN PMP- PEX19 COMPLEX FORMATION. THIS AIM WILL DEPICT THE MOLECULAR INTERACTIONS BETWEEN PMPS AND THE IMPORT MACHINERY TO DETERMINE HOW POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATIONS AND PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS GOVERN ORGANELLE ASSEMBLY. AIM 2 EXAMINES THE DISRUPTIONS OF PEX19-DEPENDENT PMP TRAFFICKING IN THE CONTEXT OF GENETIC DISEASES, AND UPON DRUG TREATMENT. I WILL USE CRISPR-ENGINEERED, AND ZSD PATIENT-DERIVED CELL LINES TO GAIN HOLISTIC INSIGHTS INTO TRAFFICKING DISRUPTIONS IN BOTH DISEASE AND THERAPEUTIC CONTEXTS. THE PROJECT WILL EMPLOY A MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH, COMBINING CUTTING-EDGE STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY TECHNIQUES, BIOPHYSICAL ASSAYS, AND ADVANCED CELLULAR IMAGING TO INVESTIGATE KEY PROTEIN INTERACTIONS INVOLVED IN PEROXISOME FORMATION. FINDINGS FROM THIS STUDY WILL ELUCIDATE THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS OF PMP IMPORT IN PEROXISOMAL BIOGENESIS AND OPEN NEW DOORS TO DEVELOPING FUTURE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES FOR PBDS.

description: CONNECTWELL: BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP NETWORK - PROJECT ABSTRACT PROJECT TITLE: CONNECTWELL: BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP NETWORK  CONNECTWELL IS A FIVE-YEAR COMMUNITY CAPACITY-BUILDING INITIATIVE THAT WILL STRENGTHEN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY ACROSS MADISON AND PLATTE COUNTIES, NEBRASKA. THROUGH A COORDINATED COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP NETWORK, LEARNING COLLABORATIVE, AND CONNECTION PRESCRIPTION NETWORK, THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE PREVENTION, EARLY IDENTIFICATION, COORDINATED RESPONSE, AND RECOVERY BY EQUIPPING COMMUNITY PARTNERS WITH SHARED TOOLS, TRAINING, REFERRAL PATHWAYS, AND DATA SYSTEMS THAT ADDRESS THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF CRIME, VIOLENCE, TRAUMA, AND COMMUNITY DISORDER. THE WELL NE WILL IMPLEMENT CONNECTWELL IN MADISON AND PLATTE COUNTIES, NEBRASKA, TWO RURAL MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONAL SHORTAGE AREAS EXPERIENCING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, AND LIMITED ACCESS TO CARE. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY CAPACITY RATHER THAN CREATE NEW DIRECT SERVICE PROGRAMS BY IMPROVING COLLABORATION, REFERRAL PATHWAYS, WORKFORCE TRAINING, AND SHARED COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE. THE PROJECT WILL BENEFIT YOUTH, ADULTS, AND FAMILIES IMPACTED BY CRIME, VIOLENCE, TRAUMA, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, OR SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, WITH PRIORITY FOR RURAL RESIDENTS, JUSTICE-INVOLVED INDIVIDUALS, VETERANS, VICTIMS OF INTERPERSONAL VIOLENCE, AND HISPANIC AND IMMIGRANT POPULATIONS. INDIVIDUALS RECEIVING CONNECTION PRESCRIPTIONS MAY RECEIVE BARRIER-REDUCTION ASSISTANCE TO INCREASE ENGAGEMENT WITH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, RECOVERY, AND COMMUNITY RESOURCES. KEY STRATEGIES INCLUDE ESTABLISHING A COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP NETWORK (BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY COALITION); CONDUCTING A COMMUNITY NEEDS AND RESOURCE ASSESSMENT; DEVELOPING A COMMUNITY STRATEGIC PLAN; IMPLEMENTING A LEARNING COLLABORATIVE THAT PROVIDES EVIDENCE-BASED TRAINING AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE; CREATING STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PATHWAYS AND A MICROSOFT-BASED COMMUNITY RESOURCE PLATFORM; IMPLEMENTING THE CONNECTION PRESCRIPTION NETWORK; AND SUPPORTING CONTINUOUS QUALITY IMPROVEMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING. PROJECT GOALS ARE TO STRENGTHEN CROSS-SECTOR COLLABORATION, INCREASE COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND RESPOND TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES ASSOCIATED WITH CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND DISORDER, IMPROVE ACCESS TO COORDINATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND RECOVERY SUPPORTS, AND BUILD SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE. OBJECTIVES INCLUDE ESTABLISHING A COMMUNITY PARTNERSHIP NETWORK WITHIN THREE MONTHS; COMPLETING A COMMUNITY NEEDS ASSESSMENT AND DEVELOPING A COMMUNITY STRATEGIC PLAN DURING YEAR 1; LAUNCHING THE CONNECTION PRESCRIPTION NETWORK, SHARED RESOURCE PLATFORM, AND STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PATHWAYS BY THE END OF YEAR 1; DELIVERING EVIDENCE-BASED TRAINING THROUGH THE LEARNING COLLABORATIVE; AND INCREASING OUTREACH, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH REFERRALS, RECOVERY SUPPORTS, AND TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE TRAINING WHILE COLLECTING ALL REQUIRED SAMHSA PERFORMANCE MEASURES.

description: SAN DIEGO COMMUNITY RESILIENCE COLLABORATIVE PROJECT - SURVIVORS OF TORTURE, INTERNATIONAL (SURVIVORS) PROPOSES THE SAN DIEGO COMMUNITY RESILIENCE COLLABORATIVE (SDCRC), A FIVE-YEAR COUNTYWIDE INITIATIVE THAT WILL STRENGTHEN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY BY BUILDING CROSS-SECTOR PARTNERSHIPS, EXPANDING ACCESS TO TRAUMA-INFORMED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, AND INCREASING COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO PREVENT AND RESPOND TO THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF CRIME, VIOLENCE, COMMUNITY DISORDER, AND TRAUMATIC EVENTS AMONG SAN DIEGO COUNTY'S MOST VULNERABLE POPULATIONS. FOR NEARLY THREE DECADES, SURVIVORS HAS SERVED AS SAN DIEGO COUNTY'S TRUSTED LEADER IN TRAUMA-INFORMED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CARE FOR INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY TORTURE, VIOLENT CRIME, FORCED DISPLACEMENT, AND OTHER SIGNIFICANT TRAUMA. AS THE REGION'S ONLY INTERNATIONALLY ACCREDITED TORTURE TREATMENT CENTER, A CALIFORNIA-CERTIFIED TRAUMA RECOVERY CENTER, AND A COUNTY-CONTRACTED SHORT-DOYLE MEDI-CAL BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CLINIC, SURVIVORS PROVIDES AN INTEGRATED CONTINUUM OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH TREATMENT, CARE COORDINATION, PREVENTION, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT.  THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL SERVE COMMUNITIES THROUGHOUT SAN DIEGO COUNTY, CALIFORNIA, WITH PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON EAST, CENTRAL, AND SOUTH SAN DIEGO COUNTY, WHERE CRIME, VIOLENCE, POVERTY, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES ARE MOST CONCENTRATED. CAPACITY-BUILDING EFFORTS WILL ADDRESS FRAGMENTED REFERRAL SYSTEMS, LIMITED CROSS-SECTOR COORDINATION, WORKFORCE SHORTAGES, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH STIGMA, AND BARRIERS TO ACCESSING CULTURALLY AND LINGUISTICALLY RESPONSIVE CARE. THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES YOUTH, ADULTS, OLDER ADULTS, AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY CRIME, VIOLENCE, COMMUNITY DISORDER, TRAUMATIC EVENTS, AND FORCED DISPLACEMENT, WITH PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON REFUGEES, ASYLUM SEEKERS, ASYLEES, SPECIAL IMMIGRANT VISA HOLDERS, HUMANITARIAN PAROLEES, VICTIMS OF VIOLENT CRIME, AND OTHER HISTORICALLY UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS EXPERIENCING OR AT INCREASED RISK FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, INCLUDING DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, PTSD, PROLONGED GRIEF, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, AND OTHER TRAUMA-RELATED DISORDERS. FORMAL REFERRAL PATHWAYS WILL EXPAND YOUTH ACCESS TO SERVICES.  4. EXPAND CAPACITY OF CHICAGO’S FAR SOUTH SIDE COMMUNITIES TO RECOGNIZE AND INTERVENE ON YOUTH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH NEEDS THROUGH TRAININGS AND COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT EVENTS. STARTING MONTH 9, WE WILL PROVIDE MENTAL HEALTH LITERACY AND TRAUMA-INFORMED TRAININGS FOR COMMUNITY ORGANIZATIONS, SCHOOL PERSONNEL, PARENTS, CAREGIVERS, AND COMMUNITY MEMBERS. description: IMPLEMENTING BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY PARTNERSHIPS - THIS IS A COMPREHENSIVE, FIVE-YEAR CAPACITY BUILDING PROJECT TO SUPPORT COMMUNITIES IN REDUCING THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND DISORDER; TO STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY SAFETY; AND TO IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR YOUTH AND FAMILIES. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE A BROAD GROUP OF YOUTH IN NEED TO OPTIMIZE ITS IMPACT. THE INDIVIDUALS TO BE SERVED INCLUDE A) YOUTH AFFECTED BY VIOLENCE, PLACING THEM AT-RISK FOR LATER ENGAGING IN VIOLENCE; B) YOUTH REFERRED TO OR ALREADY INVOLVED IN THE JUSTICE OR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEMS; C) YOUTH ENCOUNTERING LAW ENFORCEMENT THROUGH CRISIS CALLS; AND D) UNACCOMPANIED HOMELESS YOUTH. THE BH-CSC WILL BUILD BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CAPACITY USING MULTI-METHODS, INCLUDING IMPLEMENTING AND TESTING THE FEASIBILITY OF TWO EVIDENCE-BASED EARLY INTERVENTION PROGRAMS; BOLSTERING THE PEER SUPPORT WORKFORCE, CRISIS INTERVENTION, AND POST-TRAUMA RESPONSES FOR YOUTH AND COMMUNITIES; STRENGTHENING THE REFERRAL PROCESS FROM SCHOOLS, LAW ENFORCEMENT, AND HOSPITALS TO EVIDENCE-BASED EARLY INTERVENTION AND VIOLENCE PREVENTION SERVICES; INCREASING ACCESS TO RECOVERY AND RESILIENCY SERVICES; DEVISING SOLUTIONS TO YOUTH HOMELESSNESS; AND LEVERAGING FUNDING STREAMS TO MAINTAIN YOUTH AND FAMILY ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED PROGRAMS THAT REDUCE VIOLENCE AMONG YOUTH WITH BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS.   THE PROJECT GOALS AND OBJECTIVES ADDRESS ALL SIX OF THE SAMHSA STRATEGIC PRIORITIES:  GOAL 1: TO EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, CRISIS INTERVENTION, AND RECOVERY AND RESILIENCY SERVICES FOR YOUTH AGE 12 TO 25 AND THEIR FAMILIES BY IMPLEMENTING SERVICES TO ENHANCE COMMUNITY SAFETY AND STABILITY.   OBJECTIVES INCLUDE:  A) DEVELOP A SUSTAINABLE BH-CSC COMPRISING YOUTH-SERVING STATE AGENCIES, PROVIDERS, AND INDIVIDUALS WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE;  B) IDENTIFY AND IMPLEMENT FEASIBLE EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES AND CRISIS INTERVENTION APPROACHES THAT ARE SCALABLE TO OTHER COMMUNITIES IN THE COMMONWEALTH; AND  C) CREATE A STANDARDIZED REFERRAL PROCESS FROM TO APPROPRIATE EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES.  GOAL 2: STRENGTHEN THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE CAPACITY TO INCORPORATE AND SUSTAIN EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES THAT REDUCE CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES AND THEIR IMPACT ON YOUTH AND FAMILIES.    OBJECTIVES INCLUDE:  A) DEVISE A STRATEGY FOR LEVERAGING MASSHEALTH DOLLARS TO SUSTAIN FUNDING FOR EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROGRAMS THAT REDUCE VIOLENCE;  B) PROVIDE STATEWIDE TRAINING TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS IN EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES AND VIOLENCE RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS; AND  C) STRENGTHEN THE WORKFORCE OF RETURNING CITIZENS AND PEERS WITH LIVED EXPERIENCE TO PROVIDE SUPPORTS LONGER-TERM RECOVERY AND RESILIENCY.  GOAL 3: DEVELOP A STATEWIDE PLAN FOR SERVICES TO HOMELESS YOUTH AND RESPONSES TO TRAUMA AND EMERGING THREATS TO COMMUNITY SAFETY AND SECURITY   OBJECTIVES INCLUDE:  A) DEVISE AND IMPLEMENT ACTION-ORIENTED SOLUTIONS FOR IMPROVING SERVICES TO YOUTH AND FAMILIES EXPERIENCING HOMELESSNESS;  B) COMPLETE AND IMPLEMENT A PLAN FOR IDENTIFYING EMERGING THREATS AND POST-TRAUMA RESPONSE.

PROJECT DAWN WILL STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY CAPACITY TO IDENTIFY, ENGAGE, AND SUPPORT YOUTH, ADULTS, AND FAMILIES EXPERIENCING OR AT RISK FOR BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES RELATED TO CRIME, VIOLENCE, SUBSTANCE USE, TRAUMA, AND COMMUNITY DISORDER.   BEXAR COUNTY, HOME TO MORE THAN 2.1 MILLION RESIDENTS, CONTINUES TO EXPERIENCE SIGNIFICANT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH DISPARITIES, INCREASING RATES OF MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, SUBSTANCE USE, SUICIDE, OVERDOSE DEATHS, AND VIOLENT CRIME. THESE ACTIVITIES WILL IMPROVE THE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONCERNS AND EXPAND THE COMMUNITY'S ABILITY TO RESPOND EFFECTIVELY TO INDIVIDUALS IN NEED. BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, PROJECT DAWN ANTICIPATES SCREENING AT LEAST 500 INDIVIDUALS AND ENROLLING AT LEAST 250 HIGH-RISK YOUTH AND FAMILY MEMBERS IN BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, PREVENTION, RECOVERY, OR SUPPORTIVE SERVICES; AND PROVIDING PREVENTION, COPING SKILLS, AND RESILIENCE EDUCATION TO AT LEAST 600 COMMUNITY MEMBERS THROUGH 48 PRESENTATIONS, TRAININGS AND WORKSHOPS. THE SERVICE AREA INCLUDES A POPULATION EXCEEDING 1.3 MILLION RESIDENTS, WITH A HIGH PROPORTION OF YOUTH AND SIGNIFICANT RURAL DISPARITIES, PARTICULARLY IN WILLACY COUNTY. THE PROJECT WILL PRIORITIZE CAPACITY BUILDING, COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES TAILORED TO LOCAL NEEDS. THE PROJECT WILL WORK TO STRENGTHEN REFERRAL PATHWAYS AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND SUPPORT SERVICES ACROSS THE REGION. OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, THE CARE COALITION WILL REACH AT LEAST 2,000 INDIVIDUALS ANNUALLY THROUGH COMMUNITY OUTREACH, PREVENTION PROGRAMMING, SCREENING, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH EDUCATION, AND REFERRAL ACTIVITIES; SCREEN AT LEAST 500 INDIVIDUALS ANNUALLY FOR TRAUMA-RELATED CONCERNS, MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, AND SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS, WITH AT LEAST 75 PERCENT SUCCESSFULLY LINKED TO SERVICES; PROVIDE RECOVERY-SUPPORT, FAMILY-SUPPORT, CASE-MANAGEMENT, PEER-SUPPORT, AND CARE-COORDINATION SERVICES TO A MINIMUM OF 300 INDIVIDUALS AND FAMILIES/YEAR; AND TRAIN AT LEAST 250 PROFESSIONALS ANNUALLY IN TRAUMA-INFORMED CARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH LITERACY, PREVENTION STRATEGIES, REFERRAL PROCEDURES, AND COORDINATED RESPONSE PRACTICES.

description: SAN BERNARDINO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, COMMUNITY HEALING, AND SAFETY PARTNERSHIP INITIATIVE - EL SOL NEIGHBORHOOD EDUCATIONAL CENTER PROPOSES THE SAN BERNARDINO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, COMMUNITY HEALING, AND SAFETY PARTNERSHIP INITIATIVE, A FIVE-YEAR PROJECT TO ADDRESS THE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS OF CRIME, VIOLENCE, AND TRAUMA AMONG YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND RESIDENTS OF THE CITY OF SAN BERNARDINO. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN COMMUNITY SAFETY AND WELL-BEING BY EXPANDING COMMUNITY-BASED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PREVENTION, EARLY INTERVENTION, RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND COORDINATED SYSTEMS OF CARE THROUGH A COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER (CHW)-LED MODEL.  THE PROJECT WILL SERVE RESIDENTS IN FIVE HIGH-NEED ZIP CODES (92410, 92411, 92404, 92405, AND 92408), WHERE EXPOSURE TO CRIME AND VIOLENCE CONTRIBUTES TO SIGNIFICANT BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES. SAN BERNARDINO'S VIOLENT CRIME RATE IS APPROXIMATELY TWICE THE CALIFORNIA AVERAGE, WHILE AN ESTIMATED 15,354 COUNTY RESIDENTS WITH MENTAL HEALTH NEEDS GO WITHOUT SERVICES EACH YEAR. AMONG YOUTH, ONLY 9.1% OF THOSE NEEDING MENTAL HEALTH COUNSELING RECEIVE CARE, AND THE YOUTH SUICIDE RATE INCREASED 33% BETWEEN 2019 AND 2023. AT THE SAME TIME, THE REGION FACES SEVERE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH WORKFORCE SHORTAGES AND FRAGMENTED SERVICE SYSTEMS THAT LIMIT TIMELY ACCESS TO CARE.   BUILDING UPON EL SOL'S EXISTING INTERDISCIPLINARY PARTNERSHIPS, THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND COMMUNITY SAFETY COALITION CONSISTING OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, SCHOOLS, PUBLIC HEALTH AGENCIES, FAITH-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, HEALTHCARE PROVIDERS, PUBLIC SAFETY PARTNERS, AND COMMUNITY RESIDENTS. THE COALITION WILL GUIDE A COMMUNITY NEEDS AND RESOURCES ASSESSMENT, DEVELOP A COMMUNITY STRATEGIC PLAN, STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF FIVE COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS, AND IMPLEMENT COORDINATED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTREACH, SCREENING, NAVIGATION, REFERRAL, RECOVERY SUPPORT, AND COMMUNITY HEALING SERVICES. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PROVIDE COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKER WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, MENTAL HEALTH LITERACY TRAINING, TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE, AND STANDARDIZED SCREENING, REFERRAL, AND DATA-SHARING PROTOCOLS TO IMPROVE COORDINATION ACROSS SYSTEMS.  OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, THE INITIATIVE WILL ENGAGE 12,000 RESIDENTS THROUGH COMMUNITY OUTREACH, COMPLETE 4,000 BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENINGS, PROVIDE NAVIGATION SERVICES TO 2,500 INDIVIDUALS, FACILITATE 2,000 REFERRALS, CONNECT 1,500 INDIVIDUALS TO MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES, PROVIDE RECOVERY AND RESILIENCE SUPPORTS TO 2,000 PARTICIPANTS, AND TRAIN 120 COMMUNITY HEALTH WORKERS AND FRONTLINE STAFF. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE IMPROVED BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, REDUCED TRAUMA-RELATED SYMPTOMS, INCREASED ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, STRONGER COLLABORATION AMONG BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, COMMUNITY, AND PUBLIC SAFETY PARTNERS, EXPANDED ORGANIZATIONAL CAPACITY, AND A SUSTAINABLE COMMUNITY INFRASTRUCTURE THAT STRENGTHENS RECOVERY, RESILIENCE, COMMUNITY HEALING, AND COMMUNITY SAFETY BEYOND THE GRANT PERIOD.

description: RESILIENT ROOTS NC: STRENGTHENING SYSTEMS, SUPPORTING FAMILIES - CHILDREN'S HOME SOCIETY OF NORTH CAROLINA (CHSNC) WILL IMPLEMENT RESILIENT ROOTS NC: STRENGTHENING SYSTEMS, SUPPORTING FAMILIES, A FIVE-YEAR INITIATIVE EXPANDING INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) SERVICES FOR CHILDREN IN OR AT RISK OF CHILD WELFARE INVOLVEMENT. CHSNC WILL TRAIN THE EARLY CHILDHOOD WORKFORCE STATEWIDE, EXPAND CHILD FIRST DYADIC TREATMENT FOR CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH FIVE IN SEVEN COUNTIES, AND ADD IECMH CONSULTATION WITH STATEWIDE ACCESS TO IMPROVE EARLY SYSTEMS OF CARE. TRAINING AND CONSULTATION ARE AVAILABLE TO THE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD WORKFORCE, INCLUDING MENTAL HEALTH CLINICIANS AND OTHER ADULTS WHO CARE FOR INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN, ACROSS NORTH CAROLINA'S 100 COUNTIES AND POPULATION OF 11,197,968. DIRECT CLINICAL SERVICES COVER THE MECKLENBURG REGION (MECKLENBURG, CABARRUS, AND ROWAN COUNTIES) AND THE TRIANGLE REGION (DURHAM, WAKE, ORANGE, AND JOHNSTON COUNTIES). FOUR NEW CHILD FIRST TEAMS WILL SERVE 290 UNDUPLICATED CHILDREN WITH AWARD FUNDS.  DIRECT SERVICES REACH CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE FIVE AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. TRAINING AND CONSULTATION EXTEND THE PROJECT'S REACH TO CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE 12 THROUGH THE PROFESSIONALS, CAREGIVERS, AND CLINICIANS WHO SERVE THEM. CHILDREN SERVED EXPERIENCE OR ARE AT RISK FOR SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL AND BEHAVIORAL DIFFICULTIES RANGING FROM EARLY DYSREGULATION IDENTIFIED THROUGH SCREENING TO DIAGNOSABLE CONDITIONS, INCLUDING SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE, REQUIRING EARLY-CHILDHOOD-SPECIFIC ASSESSMENT AND TREATMENT. FAMILIES RECEIVING CHILD FIRST SERVICES DEMONSTRATE MEDICAID ELIGIBILITY AND MEET CLINICAL CRITERIA, INDICATING LOW-INCOME HOUSEHOLDS. CHSNC WILL DELIVER VIRTUAL LIVE TRAINING STATEWIDE USING COMPLEX TRAUMA TRAINING CONSORTIUM (CTTC) CURRICULA, FOR WHICH CHSNC IS NORTH CAROLINA'S SOLE REGIONAL LEAD SITE, AND WILL DEVELOP ORIGINAL IECMH CURRICULA FOR THE CHILD WELFARE-ADJACENT WORKFORCE AND FOR LICENSED CLINICIANS. CHSNC WILL EXPAND CHILD FIRST, AN EVIDENCE-BASED HOME-BASED DYADIC MODEL DELIVERED THROUGH A CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY APPROACH, FROM FOUR TO EIGHT TEAMS. A NEWLY HIRED EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH COACH WILL DELIVER IECMH CONSULTATION TO PROGRAMS, TEAMS, AND INDIVIDUAL CONSULTEES. GOAL 1 EXPANDS THE CAPACITY OF NORTH CAROLINA'S CHILD WELFARE-ADJACENT WORKFORCE AND MENTAL HEALTH CLINICIANS STATEWIDE TO IDENTIFY AND RESPOND TO IECMH NEEDS AMONG CHILDREN AGES 0-12. CHSNC WILL DELIVER A MINIMUM OF 300 VIRTUAL LIVE TRAININGS AND BUILD A PERMANENT ON-DEMAND DIGITAL TRAINING LIBRARY REACHING 25 TRAINING COURSES BY THE END OF YEAR 5. ANNUALLY, 85 PERCENT OF SURVEYED TRAINEES WILL DEMONSTRATE INCREASED KNOWLEDGE, AND 60 PERCENT WILL REPORT IMPLEMENTING TRAINING CONTENT AT THREE MONTHS. GOAL 2 EXPANDS ACCESS TO IECMH INTERVENTION STATEWIDE AND DIRECTLY THROUGH CHILD FIRST. CHSNC WILL HIRE AND TRAIN FOUR NEW TEAMS IN YEAR 1, BUILDING CASELOADS OF 12 TO 16 FAMILIES PER TEAM BY THE END OF YEAR 2. ALL EIGHT TEAMS WILL SERVE 630 UNDUPLICATED FAMILIES BY THE END OF THE PROJECT PERIOD, MEETING MODEL BENCHMARKS OF 60 PERCENT OF FAMILY-IDENTIFIED NEEDS MET AND 75 PERCENT OF DISCHARGED FAMILIES DEMONSTRATING IMPROVEMENT. THE EXPANDED WORKFORCE WILL BE SUSTAINED BY MEDICAID. GOAL 3 ENHANCES THE QUALITY, REACH, AND COORDINATION OF IECMH SERVICE DELIVERY STATEWIDE THROUGH CONSULTATION, STRENGTHENING EARLY SYSTEMS OF CARE. CHSNC WILL HIRE AN EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH COACH BY MONTH 7, WITH CONSULTATION OPERATIONAL BY MONTH 9, AND BOTH THE PROJECT DIRECTOR AND THE COACH WILL COMPLETE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE IECMHC CERTIFICATE TRAINING. CONSULTATION WILL REACH AT LEAST 8 ADULTS WHO CARE FOR INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN IN YEAR 1 AND AT LEAST 20 IN EACH OF YEARS 2 THROUGH 5, FOR AT LEAST 88 OVER THE PROJECT PERIOD.

STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS: METROCARE WILL EMPLOY A MULTIDISCIPLINARY TEAM, INCLUDING A QUALIFIED MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONAL (QMHP) AND FAMILY PARTNER, WITH INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION PROVIDED BY THE PROJECT DIRECTOR, TO IMPLEMENT: • UNIVERSAL SCREENING: STANDARDIZED ASSESSMENT USING THE AGES AND STAGES QUESTIONNAIRE (ASQ) FOR AGES 0-3 AND THE CHILD AND ADOLESCENT NEEDS AND STRENGTHS (CANS) FOR AGES 3-12. • EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES (EBPS): DELIVERY OF CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP) AND PARENT-CHILD INTERACTION THERAPY (PCIT) TO STRENGTHEN CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS. • CAPACITY BUILDING: SPECIALIZED WORKFORCE TRAINING FOR CLINICAL STAFF AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS THROUGH THE COMMUNITY RESOURCE COORDINATION GROUP (CRCG). ENSURE 60% OF REFERRED FAMILIES INITIATE SERVICES WITHIN 14 DAYS AND 40% OF CHILDREN SHOW IMPROVED SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL FUNCTIONING WITHIN SIX MONTHS. • GOAL 3: RELATIONAL HEALTH. PROVIDE DYADIC OR CAREGIVER-FOCUSED INTERVENTIONS TO 85% OF ENROLLEES, AND REDUCE ACTIONABLE CAREGIVER NEEDS ON THE CANS FOR 40% OF PARTICIPANTS. • GOAL 4: WORKFORCE CAPACITY. DELIVER IECMH-FOCUSED TRAINING TO AT LEAST 40 MEMBERS OF THE EARLY CHILDHOOD WORKFORCE ANNUALLY.

description: EARLY CONNECTIONS: EXPANDING INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH IN THE LOWCOUNTRY AND BEYOND - EARLY CONNECTIONS WILL EXPAND ACCESS TO INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) SERVICES ACROSS SOUTH CAROLINA'S LOWCOUNTRY BY INCREASING SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, TREATMENT, CONSULTATION, AND WORKFORCE TRAINING. THROUGH INTEGRATED TRAINING, CLINICAL SERVICES, CONSULTATION, AND COORDINATED REFERRALS, EARLY CONNECTIONS WILL IMPROVE OUTCOMES FOR YOUNG CHILDREN AND FAMILIES WHILE ADVANCING SAMHSA PRIORITIES IN PREVENTION, WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, ACCESS TO CARE, AND RESILIENCE.   OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, SCIMHA EXPECTS TO SERVE APPROXIMATELY 2,529 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS, SPECIFICALLY CHILDREN AGES 0–5 AND THEIR CAREGIVERS ACROSS BERKELEY, BEAUFORT, CHARLESTON, AND DORCHESTER COUNTIES IN SOUTH CAROLINA. IT WILL OFFER WARMLINE CONSULTATION AND WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES STATEWIDE. THE FOCUS IS ON CHILDREN WITH DEVELOPMENTAL, BEHAVIORAL, SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL, OR RELATIONSHIP ISSUES; FAMILIES FACING POVERTY, ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES (ACES), INVOLVEMENT WITH CHILD WELFARE, BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROBLEMS, OR LIMITED SERVICE ACCESS; AND FAMILIES WHO ARE MEDICAID-ENROLLED, UNDERINSURED, RURAL, OR UNDERSERVED.    OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD, SCIMHA EXPECTS TO SERVE APPROXIMATELY 2,529 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS THROUGH WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT, TREATMENT, AND CONSULTATION ACTIVITIES. THIS INCLUDES APPROXIMATELY 440 PROFESSIONALS PARTICIPATING IN WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT ACTIVITIES, 1,661 CHILDREN RECEIVING SCREENING AND ASSESSMENT SERVICES, 68 CHILDREN AND FAMILIES RECEIVING DIRECT IECMH TREATMENT, AND 360 CAREGIVERS AND PROFESSIONALS RECEIVING CONSULTATION SERVICES.   THE PROJECT WILL FOCUS ON FOUR MAIN ACTIVITIES. FIRST, SCIMHA WILL INCREASE WORKFORCE CAPACITY BY PROVIDING TRAINING THROUGH THE IECMH FOUNDATIONS CERTIFICATE, IECMH CLINICAL CERTIFICATE, DC:0–5 TRAINING, AND CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP). SECOND, HELP ME GROW SOUTH CAROLINA (HMG) WILL BE ENHANCED AS THE PRIMARY RESOURCE FOR DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING, CARE COORDINATION, REFERRALS, AND SERVICE NAVIGATION. THIRD, SCIMHA WILL BROADEN DIRECT CLINICAL SERVICES BY ADDING AN IECMH CLINICIAN TO CONDUCT ASSESSMENTS, DYADIC TREATMENT, CAREGIVER SUPPORT, AND BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS. FINALLY, SCIMHA WILL INTRODUCE A STATEWIDE WARMLINE CONSULTATION SERVICE TO OFFER PROMPT SUPPORT TO CAREGIVERS AND PROFESSIONALS CARING FOR YOUNG CHILDREN.    PROJECT GOALS ARE TO: (1) STRENGTHEN WORKFORCE CAPACITY TO IMPLEMENT IECMH BEST PRACTICES; (2) EXPAND ACCESS TO SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, AND REFERRAL SERVICES; (3) EXPAND MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT AND CONSULTATION SERVICES; AND (4) IMPROVE CHILD AND FAMILY OUTCOMES THROUGH COORDINATED, SUSTAINABLE SUPPORTS. KEY OBJECTIVES INCLUDE TRAINING 75 GRANT-SUPPORTED PROFESSIONALS THROUGH THE IECMH FOUNDATIONS CERTIFICATE, TRAINING 100 PROFESSIONALS THROUGH THE IECMH CLINICAL CERTIFICATE, PROVIDING DC:0–5 TRAINING TO APPROXIMATELY 250 ADDITIONAL PROFESSIONALS, INCREASING DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING BY 20% ANNUALLY, EXPANDING ASSESSMENT CAPACITY TO 50 ASSESSMENTS ANNUALLY BY YEAR 4, SERVING AT LEAST 100 CHILDREN AND FAMILIES THROUGH TREATMENT SERVICES, AND PROVIDING STATEWIDE WARMLINE CONSULTATION. OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE IMPROVED CHILD SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL FUNCTIONING, DECREASED CAREGIVER STRESS, INCREASED CAREGIVER CONFIDENCE, AND STRENGTHENED ACCESS TO INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORTS.

description: DEVELOPING RESILIENCE AND WELL-BEING (DRAW) - DEVELOPING RESILIENCE AND WELL-BEING (DRAW), A PROGRAM OF LUK CRISIS CENTER, INC. (LUK), WILL PROVIDE SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, DIAGNOSIS, MENTAL HEALTH PROMOTION AND INTERVENTION SERVICES FOR INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN (IYC), AGES 0-12, AND THEIR FAMILIES. TO RAISE AWARENESS OF MENTAL HEALTH NEEDS OF IYC AND AVAILABLE SERVICES, WE WILL ALSO PROVIDE TRAINING TO THE IYC WORKFORCE INCLUDING MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS, AND SUPPLEMENT TRAINING WITH INDIVIDUALIZED CONSULTATIONS.   DRAW WILL SERVE IYC AND THEIR CAREGIVERS IN WORCESTER COUNTY, MASSACHUSETTS. 113,404 CHILDREN UNDER THE AGE OF 12 RESIDE IN THE SERVICE AREA (US CENSUS, 2020-2024 AMERICAN COMMUNITY SURVEY, 5-YEAR ESTIMATES). CHILD TRENDS (2026) REPORTED THAT 32% OF CHILDREN IN MASSACHUSETTS HAVE EXPERIENCED AT LEAST ONE ACE (AN ESTIMATED 36,289 CHILDREN UNDER AGE 12 IN WORCESTER COUNTY). COMMON CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS OF THE POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDE BEHAVIORAL DISTURBANCES (E.G., NON-COMPLIANCE, AGGRESSION), AND DYSREGULATION (E.G., TANTRUMS, CRYING/WHINING). THE MOST COMMON DIAGNOSES INCLUDE TRAUMA AND STRESSOR-RELATED, ADJUSTMENT, ANXIETY, RELATIONAL, AND REGULATORY DISORDERS.  DRAW’S GOALS ARE: (1) TO INCREASE ADULTS’ (PROFESSIONALS AND FAMILY) KNOWLEDGE OF TRAUMA SYMPTOMS IN IYC AND WHEN TO REFER FOR ADDITIONAL SERVICES, (2) TO INCREASE REFERRALS OF IYC IN NEED OF EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENT, (3) TO IMPROVE THE FUNCTIONING OF IYC IMPACTED BY TRAUMA AND THE FUNCTIONING OF THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND (4) TO IMPROVE THE SKILLS OF EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION (ECE) PROVIDERS TO MANAGE IYC WITH TRAUMA AND OTHER STRESSORS/SYMPTOMS. DRAW WILL UTILIZE THE FOLLOWING EVIDENCE-BASED TRAUMA TREATMENTS: ATTACHMENT, REGULATION, AND COMPETENCY (ARC); A CAREGIVER ADAPTATION OF ARC CALLED ARC GROW; AND PARENT-CHILD INTERACTION THERAPY (PCIT). CONSULTATION COMPETENCIES FROM THE CENTER OF EXCELLENCE FOR INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH WILL ALSO BE UTILIZED.  EACH YEAR, DRAW PLANS TO SCREEN 150 IYC, WITH ADDITIONAL ASSESSMENTS AND DIAGNOSES FOR 75 IYC ANNUALLY. EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT WILL BE PROVIDED TO 50 IYC AND THEIR FAMILIES ANNUALLY. OVER THE 5-YEAR PROJECT, WE WILL SCREEN 750 IYC, PROVIDE ASSESSMENT AND DIAGNOSES TO 375 IYC, AND PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT TO 250 IYC AND THEIR FAMILIES. WE ALSO PLAN TO TRAIN 150 ADULTS WHO CARE FOR IYC EACH YEAR (E.G., MEDICAL PROFESSIONALS, CHILDCARE PROVIDERS, MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS) FOR A TOTAL OF 750 TRAINED OVER THE 5-YEAR PROJECT, WITH CONSULTATION PROVIDED TO 10 EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATORS EACH YEAR, FOR A TOTAL OF 50 OVER THE 5-YEAR PROJECT.  DRAW’S PROPOSED OBJECTIVES INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING:  - BY THE END OF THE 5-YEAR PROJECT, 75% OF TRAINING PARTICIPANTS WILL REPORT INCREASED ABILITY TO IDENTIFY AND REFER THE POPULATION OF FOCUS; - BY DISCHARGE, 75% OF FAMILIES WILL BE STRENGTHENED: TO IMPROVE CHILDREN’S SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SKILLS AND FUNCTIONING, TO ENHANCE CAREGIVER-CHILD INTERACTIONS, AND TO DECREASE CHILDREN’S STRESSORS; AND - BY THE END OF 5-YEAR PROJECT, 75% OF ECE PROVIDERS ENGAGED IN CONSULTATION WILL REPORT AN IMPROVEMENT IN INDIVIDUAL SKILLS.

description: CHILDREN'S RESEARCH TRIANGLE'S STRENGTHENING INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH THROUGH TRAUMA-INFORMED INTEGRATED SERVICES - CHILDREN'S RESEARCH TRIANGLE'S (CRT) STRENGTHENING INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH THROUGH TRAUMA-INFORMED INTEGRATED SERVICES (IECMH) BUILDS SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL DEVELOPMENT, PROVIDING EVIDENCE-BASED SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, EVALUATION, TREATMENT, CRISIS CARE, AND CAREGIVER EDUCATION TO 900+ LOW-INCOME CHICAGO-AREA CHILDREN (BIRTH-12) WITH/AT RISK FOR SED, AND FAMILIES. IECMH WILL TRAIN 500 PROFESSIONALS AND CONSULT FOR 10 COMMUNITY AGENCIES. SERVICE AREA & POPULATION. IECMH PRIMARILY BENEFITS THE CHICAGO METROPOLITAN AREA, WITH 70% OF SERVICES DELIVERED AT NINE SCHOOLS AND SOCIAL SERVICE AGENCIES IN SOUTH AND WEST SIDE NEIGHBORHOODS IMPACTED BY HIGH POVERTY RATES AND WORKFORCE SHORTAGES. IECMH ALSO PROVIDES SERVICES IN ITS LOOP CLINIC AND VIA TELEHEALTH. OF THE 1,166 CLIENTS CRT SERVED IN 2025, 570 WERE AGED BIRTH–12, WITH A PROJECTED GRANT SERVICE DISTRIBUTION OF 35% INFANTS AND PRESCHOOLERS (AGES 0–5) AND 65% SCHOOL-AGED YOUTH (AGES 6–12). CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS. CRT'S POPULATION PRESENTS WITH NEGLECT; PHYSICAL, SEXUAL OR EMOTIONAL ABUSE; CAREGIVER SEPARATION; BEREAVEMENT; DOMESTIC/COMMUNITY VIOLENCE; FOOD/HOUSING INSTABILITY; PRENATAL SUBSTANCE EXPOSURE; PARENTAL INCARCERATION; DISABILITY; AND HOUSEHOLD MENTAL ILLNESS. THE MAJORITY (96%) HAVE EXPERIENCED TRAUMA AND 10% ARE IN THE CHILD WELFARE SYSTEM. DIAGNOSES INCLUDE DEPRESSION, ANXIETY, PTSD, NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DIFFERENCES, DISRUPTIVE BEHAVIOR DISORDERS, AND PSYCHOSIS. STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS. IECMH DELIVERS PREVENTION AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH PROMOTION; EVIDENCE-BASED SCREENING/ASSESSMENT AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY EVALUATION; EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT (CPP, TF-CBT, PCIT, THERAPLAY, EMDR); CRISIS INTERVENTION SERVICES; CAREGIVER EDUCATION (STEP, CIRCLE OF SECURITY PARENTING); CASE MANAGEMENT/FAMILY ENGAGEMENT; INFANT/EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION; AND WORKFORCE TRAINING. IT SUSTAINS GAINS POST-TREATMENT THROUGH ONGOING DEVELOPMENTAL GUIDANCE AND REFLECTIVE CONSULTATION. PROJECT GOALS. (1) INCREASE PROFESSIONAL AWARENESS OF DIAGNOSTIC/TREATMENT ISSUES FOR SED; (2) INCREASE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF CHILDREN AT RISK FOR SED VIA EVIDENCE-BASED SCREENING; (3) INCREASE AVAILABILITY OF COMPREHENSIVE EVALUATIONS TO IDENTIFY CLINICAL NEEDS; (4) DECREASE PARENT-CHILD RELATIONSHIP RISK FACTORS; (5) INCREASE ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT; (6) INCREASE COMPETENCY OF COMMUNITY-BASED CLINICIANS; (7) MAINTAIN A HIGH QUALITY STANDARD OF CARE; AND (8) ENGAGE AND EMPOWER PARENTS/CAREGIVERS IN DECISION-MAKING.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. (1) TRAIN 100 PROFESSIONALS ANNUALLY (500/TERM) TO INCREASE AWARENESS OF DIAGNOSTIC AND TREATMENT ISSUES FOR CHILDREN WITH OR AT RISK FOR SED, WITH 80% ACHIEVING INCREASED KNOWLEDGE. (2) SCREEN 150 CHILDREN/CAREGIVERS ANNUALLY (750/TERM) USING EVIDENCE-BASED TOOLS TO INCREASE IDENTIFICATION OF AT-RISK YOUTH, TRACKING 100% OF REFERRAL SOURCES. (3) COMPLETE COMPREHENSIVE PSYCHOLOGICAL EVALUATIONS FOR 25 CHILDREN ANNUALLY (125/TERM), ENSURING 100% RECEIVE TREATMENT PLANS AND 70% FOLLOW THROUGH WITHIN 9 MONTHS. (4) ENROLL 15 CAREGIVERS ANNUALLY (75/TERM) IN STEP/COSP TO DECREASE PARENT-CHILD RELATIONSHIP RISK FACTORS, WITH 80% DEMONSTRATING IMPROVED PARENTING SKILLS.(5) PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT TO 70 CHILDREN/CAREGIVERS ANNUALLY (350/TERM), INCLUDING CRISIS INTERVENTION SERVICES, WITH 80% IMPROVING ON STANDARDIZED OUTCOME MEASURES. (6) PARTNER WITH TWO AGENCIES ANNUALLY (10/TERM) TO INCREASE COMMUNITY CLINICIAN COMPETENCY, WITH 80% OF STAFF IMPROVING ON THE GOAL ACHIEVEMENT SCALE. (7) MAINTAIN HIGH CARE STANDARDS BY SECURING 80% TREATMENT FIDELITY AND 100% CLINICAL SUPERVISION. (8) ENGAGE AND EMPOWER CAREGIVERS TRANSPARENTLY BY PROTECTING PARENTAL RIGHTS, CONTACTING FAMILIES WITHIN 10 DAYS OF REFERRAL, AND ENSURING 80% REPORT THAT THEIR FEEDBACK IS VALUED.

description: STRONG START MENTAL HEALTH INITIATIVE - MOTIVATION, EDUCATION, AND TRAINING, INC. (MET) PROPOSES STRONG START, A COMPREHENSIVE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) INITIATIVE SERVING CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE 12, THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONALS IN THE CITY OF WALLER IN NORTHEAST HARRIS COUNTY AND THE FOLLOWING ADDITIONAL COUNTIES: AUSTIN, CHAMBERS, HARDIN, JEFFERSON, LIBERTY, MONTGOMERY, POLK, WALLER, AND WALKER. THE PROJECT ADDRESSES DOCUMENTED SHORTAGES OF IECMH-TRAINED PROFESSIONALS, FRAGMENTED REFERRAL PATHWAYS, TRANSPORTATION BARRIERS, AND LIMITED ACCESS TO DEVELOPMENTALLY APPROPRIATE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, CONSULTATION, AND FAMILY SUPPORT SERVICES, PARTICULARLY IN RURAL COMMUNITIES. STRONG START WILL IMPROVE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONCERNS WHILE STRENGTHENING THE REGIONAL IECMH WORKFORCE AND EXPANDING COORDINATED ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-INFORMED MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES.  STRONG STARTT WILL ESTABLISH AN IECMH LEARNING COLLABORATIVE THAT TRAINS 2,000 EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONALS THROUGH A COMPETENCY-BASED CURRICULUM THAT INTEGRATES IECMH INTO MET'S DEPARTMENT OF LABOR REGISTERED EARLY CHILDHOOD EDUCATION APPRENTICESHIP. STRONG START WILL ALSO ESTABLISH A REGIONAL SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, AND REFERRAL HUB TO PROVIDE DEVELOPMENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SCREENING FOR 2,500 CHILDREN, ENSURE TIMELY REFERRAL AND FOLLOW-UP FOR CHILDREN REQUIRING ADDITIONAL SERVICES, AND DELIVER CAREGIVER EDUCATION AND EARLY INTERVENTION THROUGH THE NURTURING PARENTING PROGRAM AND WELLNESS ON WHEELS OUTREACH. LICENSED MENTAL HEALTH PROFESSIONALS WILL PROVIDE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION (IECMHC) TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONALS, PROMOTE HEALTHY CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS, AND IMPROVE ACCESS TO DEVELOPMENTALLY APPROPRIATE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES.  BY LEVERAGING MET'S EXISTING PROGRAMS, STRONG START WILL STRENGTHEN EXISTING SYSTEMS RATHER THAN DUPLICATE SERVICES. THE PROJECT WILL IMPROVE WORKFORCE CAPACITY, INCREASE ACCESS TO EARLY IDENTIFICATION AND REFERRAL, STRENGTHEN CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS, EXPAND ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES, AND CREATE A SUSTAINABLE REGIONAL MODEL THAT IMPROVES BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR CHILDREN AND FAMILIES THROUGHOUT SOUTHEAST TEXAS.

description: INFANT AND CHILD NURTURE PROJECT (ICNP) - INTERBOROUGH DEVELOPMENTAL & CONSULTATION CENTER (IDCC) WILL LAUNCH THE INFANT AND CHILD NURTURE PROJECT (ICNP) WITH AN AWARD UNDER THE SAMHSA INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) SM26020 TO CLOSE A DOCUMENTED GAP IN MENTAL HEALTH IDENTIFICATION AND TREATMENT FOR THE YOUNGEST CHILDREN IN BROOKLYN'S LARGEST BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SYSTEM, WHILE FORMALIZING EXISTING BUT UNDERUTILIZED TREATMENT CAPACITY FOR SCHOOL-AGE CHILDREN. IN 2025, IDCC SERVED 1,593 CHILDREN AGES 6 TO 12 BUT ONLY 59 CHILDREN UNDER AGE 6, DESPITE THE TARGET POPULATION SPLITTING ALMOST EVENLY BY AGE. THIS INITIATIVE WILL BRING VALIDATED DEVELOPMENTAL SCREENING, EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC TREATMENT, AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION TO FIVE IDCC CLINICS AND PARTNERED EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION SITES ACROSS KINGS COUNTY, CLOSING THAT GAP AT ITS SOURCE. SERVICES WILL BE DELIVERED THROUGHOUT KINGS COUNTY, NEW YORK, ANCHORED AT CANARSIE COUNSELING CENTER WITH FOUR SATELLITE CLINICS, FLATBUSH, CROWN HEIGHTS, CONEY ISLAND, AND WILLIAMSBURG, AND EXTENDED THROUGH 24 SCHOOL-BASED SITES AND PARTNERED EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION SETTINGS. AN ESTIMATED 436,097 CHILDREN AGES BIRTH TO 12 RESIDE IN KINGS COUNTY, SPLIT NEARLY EVENLY BETWEEN AGES BIRTH TO 5 (207,882) AND AGES 6 TO 12 (228,215). ICNP WILL SERVE 120 UNDUPLICATED CHILDREN IN YEAR 1, GROWING TO 160 ANNUALLY BY YEAR 2, FOR A FIVE-YEAR TOTAL OF 760 CHILDREN SERVED THROUGH GRANT-FUNDED SCREENING, TREATMENT, AND CONSULTATION PATHWAYS.  CHILDREN AGES 6 TO 12 ALREADY SERVED BY IDCC PRESENT MOST FREQUENTLY WITH ADHD, ANXIETY AND TRAUMA-RELATED CONDITIONS, AND DISRUPTIVE OR MOOD DYSREGULATION PRESENTATIONS. CHILDREN BIRTH TO 5 PRESENT MOST FREQUENTLY WITH SEPARATION ANXIETY, ADJUSTMENT DISORDERS, AND EARLY HYPERACTIVITY OR IMPULSIVITY INDICATORS, AN AGE GROUP SUBSTANTIALLY UNDER-IDENTIFIED DUE TO THE ABSENCE OF VALIDATED SCREENING IN IDCC'S CURRENT INTAKE PROCESS.  IDCC WILL IMPLEMENT VALIDATED DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING (ASQ-3, ASQ:SE-2, M-CHAT-R, AND DECA); CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY, AN EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC TREATMENT MODEL FOR CHILDREN BIRTH TO 5; ATTACHMENT, REGULATION, AND COMPETENCY (ARC), A DYADIC TREATMENT FRAMEWORK ALREADY HELD BY 25 TRAINED IDCC CLINICAL STAFF, FORMALIZED UNDER THIS PROJECT INTO A STRUCTURED 10-PERSON CLINICAL TRACK FOR CHILDREN AGES 6 TO 12; AND WEEKLY PARENTING SUPPORT GROUPS THROUGH THE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION DELIVERED TO PARTNERED EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION SETTINGS. ICNP PURSUES THREE GOALS: INCREASING EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH AND DEVELOPMENTAL CONCERNS AMONG CHILDREN BIRTH TO 5, ACTIVATING EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC TREATMENT CAPACITY FOR CHILDREN BIRTH TO 12 AND THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND ESTABLISHING CONSULTATION CAPACITY CONNECTING IDCC TO EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION SETTINGS ACROSS KINGS COUNTY. BY THE END OF YEAR 1, IDCC WILL SCREEN 100% OF NEWLY INTAKING CHILDREN BIRTH TO 5 AT ALL FIVE CLINICS AND DELIVER CPP TREATMENT DIRECTLY TO AT LEAST 20 CAREGIVER-CHILD DYADS. BY MONTH 6 OF YEAR 1, IDCC WILL FORMALIZE ITS 10-PERSON ARC CLINICAL CADRE, AT LEAST TWO PER CLINIC. BY MONTH 9 OF YEAR 1, IDCC WILL ESTABLISH FORMAL CONSULTATION AGREEMENTS WITH AT LEAST THREE EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS. BY THE END OF YEAR 2, 80% OF CHILDREN WHO SCREEN POSITIVE WILL BE CONNECTED TO TREATMENT WITHIN 30 DAYS. THIS DESIGN REFLECTS SAMHSA'S COMMITMENT TO EVIDENCE-BASED, DATA-DRIVEN PRACTICE AND TO PARENTAL RIGHTS AND FAMILY ENGAGEMENT, WITH TREATMENT PLANS DEVELOPED JOINTLY WITH CAREGIVERS THROUGHOUT.

description: START CORPORATION'S FY26 SAMHSA INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) PROGRAM - PROJECT NAME: START CORPORATION INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH PROGRAM – LOUISIANA REGION 3  START CORPORATION (START) WILL LAUNCH LOUISIANA'S FIRST INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) PROGRAM, SERVING CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE 12 ACROSS REGION 3'S SEVEN-PARISH RIVER AND BAYOU AREA. OVER FIVE YEARS, THE PROJECT WILL SCREEN THOUSANDS OF CHILDREN, DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED MENTAL HEALTH TREATMENT, AND EXTEND CONSULTATION TO THE ADULTS WHO CARE FOR THEM, CLOSING LOUISIANA'S ONLY VALIDATED-CARE GAP FOR ITS YOUNGEST RESIDENTS.  GEOGRAPHIC AREA: THE PROJECT SERVES LOUISIANA DEPARTMENT OF HEALTH REGION 3 IN ITS ENTIRETY – ASSUMPTION, LAFOURCHE, ST. CHARLES, ST. JAMES, ST. JOHN THE BAPTIST, ST. MARY, AND TERREBONNE PARISHES – ANCHORED BY START'S HOUMA AND THIBODAUX CLINICS, WITH TELEHEALTH AND IN-HOME SERVICE EXTENDING REACH REGION-WIDE.  POPULATION SIZE AND INDIVIDUALS TO BE SERVED: THE SEVEN-PARISH CATCHMENT HAS APPROXIMATELY 380,000 RESIDENTS. START PROJECTS SERVING APPROXIMATELY 680 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS IN YEAR 1, SCALING TO APPROXIMATELY 1,040 ANNUALLY BY YEAR 5, FOR A TOTAL OF APPROXIMATELY 4,520 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS OVER THE FIVE-YEAR PROJECT PERIOD.  AGE RANGE AND POPULATION DISTRIBUTION: CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE 12 WHO ARE AT RISK FOR, SHOWING EARLY SIGNS OF, OR DIAGNOSED WITH A MENTAL ILLNESS, INCLUDING SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE (SED), TOGETHER WITH THEIR FAMILIES AND CAREGIVERS, WITH PARTICULAR CONCENTRATION IN THE BIRTH-TO-5 RANGE SERVED THROUGH START'S CLINICS AND HEALTHY START PROGRAM.  CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS: THE POPULATION PRESENTS WITH TRAUMA EXPOSURE, ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES, SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL DELAYS, AND DIAGNOSED OR EMERGING SED, WITH EXTENSIVE DCFS SYSTEM INVOLVEMENT. REGIONAL RISK INDICATORS ARE PRONOUNCED – ELEVATED TEEN BIRTH AND LOW-BIRTHWEIGHT RATES, HIGH CAREGIVER DEPRESSION, AND A SEVERE PROVIDER SHORTAGE – AND NO ORGANIZATION IN REGION 3 CURRENTLY OFFERS IECMH-VALIDATED SCREENING OR BIRTH-5 DYADIC TREATMENT.  STRATEGIES AND INTERVENTIONS: START WILL ADOPT DECA FOR BIRTH-5 SCREENING (COMPLEMENTING SEEK, CPSS, AND CALOCUS FOR OLDER CHILDREN), WITH DC:0–5 DIAGNOSTIC CLASSIFICATION FOR BIRTH-5 CHILDREN. CORE EVIDENCE-BASED PRACTICES ARE TF-CBT, CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP), AND PARENT-CHILD INTERACTION THERAPY (PCIT), WITH DBT FOR OLDER/CO-OCCURRING CASES, PLUS INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION (IECMHC) FOR ADULTS WHO CARE FOR YOUNG CHILDREN – DELIVERED THROUGH START'S CLINICS, HEALTHY START HOME VISITING, AND DCFS/MY COMMUNITY CARES REFERRAL PATHWAYS UNDER A NO WRONG DOOR MODEL, WITH WORKFORCE TRAINED THROUGH THE LSU EVIDENCE TO PRACTICE COHORT.  PROJECT GOALS: (1) INCREASE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF IECMH CONCERNS THROUGH VALIDATED SCREENING; (2) BUILD A WORKFORCE CREDENTIALED IN EVIDENCE-BASED IECMH PROMOTION, INTERVENTION, AND CONSULTATION; (3) DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC/INDIVIDUAL TREATMENT; AND (4) EXTEND IECMHC TO CAREGIVERS OF YOUNG CHILDREN.  MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES: SCREEN 250 CHILDREN VIA DECA WITHIN 6 MONTHS, SCALING TO ~800 ANNUALLY BY YEAR 5; TRAIN 3 CLINICIANS EACH IN CPP/PCIT AND 2 IN DBT WITHIN 4 MONTHS; SERVE 40 CHILDREN IN YEAR 1, REACHING 60-120 ANNUALLY FROM YEAR 2; AND PROVIDE IECMHC TO 80 STAFF WITHIN 9 MONTHS, EXPANDING TO DCFS AND HOME VISITORS THEREAFTER, ALIGNED WITH SAMHSA'S STRATEGIC PRIORITIES OF GOLD-STANDARD SCIENCE/DATA AND ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY SERVICES FOR ALL.

description: PROJECT TEND — TRAINING, ENGAGEMENT, AND NURTURING DEVELOPMENTBUILDING AN IECMH SYSTEM OF CARE AND WORKFORCE INITIATIVE IN MA - PROJECT TEND WILL BUILD AN INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH (IECMH) SYSTEM OF CARE IN MA, UNITING A FRAGMENTED CONTINUUM OF SERVICES INTO ONE COORDINATED PATHWAY FOR YOUNG CHILDREN AND FAMILIES. PROJECT TEND WILL IDENTIFY AND TREAT MENTAL ILLNESS IN THE DEVELOPMENTAL WINDOW WHEN INTERVENTION WORKS BEST—PREVENTING EARLY DIFFICULTIES FROM PROGRESSING INTO SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS, SUBSTANCE USE, AND CHRONIC DISEASE IN ADULTHOOD. GEOGRAPHIC AREA. MASSACHUSETTS, CONCENTRATED IN HIGH-NEED, UNDER-RESOURCED COMMUNITIES—WORCESTER, NEW BEDFORD, LYNN, LAWRENCE, HOLYOKE, CHELSEA, LOWELL, EVERETT, HAVERHILL, AND BOSTON—AND UNDERSERVED RURAL AREAS OF WESTERN MASSACHUSETTS.  POPULATION SIZE & NUMBER SERVED. MASSACHUSETTS HAS A POPULATION OF 7,136,171, OF WHOM 4.9% (APPROXIMATELY 349,700) ARE CHILDREN UNDER AGE FIVE AND 19.2% (APPROXIMATELY 1,370,100) ARE UNDER 18 (U.S. CENSUS BUREAU, QUICKFACTS, V2024). THE PROJECT'S TARGET COMMUNITIES CARRY SUBSTANTIALLY HIGHER CONCENTRATIONS OF YOUNG CHILDREN THAN THE STATE AS A WHOLE—7.8% OF RESIDENTS ARE UNDER FIVE IN CHELSEA AND LAWRENCE. STATEWIDE, 11.1% OF CHILDREN LIVE IN POVERTY AND 8,564 WERE IN FOSTER CARE IN 2024 (U.S. CENSUS BUREAU; ACF CHILD WELFARE OUTCOMES). PROJECT TEND WILL SERVE 3,330 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS OVER FIVE YEARS, COMPRISING 1,450 CHILDREN, 1,080 PARENTS AND CAREGIVERS, AND 800 TRAINED WORKFORCE MEMBERS. AGE RANGE & DISTRIBUTION. CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE 12, WEIGHTED TOWARD BIRTH THROUGH FIVE: PERINATAL AND INFANCY (PREGNANCY–12 MONTHS), TODDLERHOOD (12–36 MONTHS), AND PRESCHOOL (3–5 YEARS); SERVICES REMAIN AVAILABLE THROUGH AGE 12 FOR CHILDREN WITH EMERGING OR IDENTIFIED SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE (SED). BOTH MALE AND FEMALE CHILDREN ARE SERVED. CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS. CHILDREN ARE AT RISK FOR, SHOW EARLY SIGNS OF, OR HAVE A DIAGNOSED MENTAL ILLNESS INCLUDING SED, WITH HIGH EXPOSURE TO ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES AND TOXIC STRESS. NATIONALLY, 19.0% OF CHILDREN AGES 2–8 HAVE A DIAGNOSED MENTAL, BEHAVIORAL, OR DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER (CDC, 2024), YET ONLY ONE IN FOUR WITH A DIAGNOSABLE CONCERN RECEIVES TREATMENT (AAP, 2023). CAREGIVERS FREQUENTLY PRESENT WITH UNTREATED PERINATAL MOOD AND ANXIETY DISORDERS. STRATEGIES & INTERVENTIONS. (1) WORKFORCE TRAINING VIA IECMH LEARNING COLLABORATIVE, INCLUDING CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP), FAN, AND DIR/ FLOORTIME, DC:0-5, A TRAIN-THE-REFLECTIVE-SUPERVISOR PIPELINE, GROUP REFLECTIVE SUPERVISION/CONSULTATION (RS/C), AND MASSAIMH ENDORSEMENT®. (2) SCREENING, ASSESSMENT, AND DIAGNOSIS USING ASQ-3, ASQ:SE-2, SWYC, AND DECA, WITH CAREGIVER DEPRESSION SCREENING (EPDS/PHQ-9) IN THE SAME WORKFLOW AND DC:0-5 DIAGNOSTIC EVALUATION AFTER POSITIVE SCREENS. (3) EVIDENCE-BASED PROMOTION, PREVENTION, AND INTERVENTION SERVICES (4) IECMH CONSULTATION (IECMHC) TO EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS. (5) QUARTERLY COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE TO CREATE A COHESIVE IECMH SYSTEM OF CARE.. GOALS. (1) STRENGTHEN AND SUSTAIN THE IECMH WORKFORCE THROUGH TRAINING AND REFLECTIVE SUPERVISION/CONSULTATION. (2) CONVENE A QUARTERLY COMMUNITY OF PRACTICE TO CREATE A COHESIVE, COORDINATED IECMH SYSTEM OF CARE. (3) DELIVER EVIDENCE-BASED AND EVIDENCE-INFORMED PROMOTION, PREVENTION, AND INTERVENTION SERVICES. (4) PROVIDE IECMH CONSULTATION TO EARLY CARE AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS. MEASURABLE OBJECTIVES. LAUNCH THE LEARNING COLLABORATIVE WITHIN FOUR MONTHS OF AWARD; TRAIN 800 PROFESSIONALS. PROVIDE GROUP RS/C TO 150 WORKFORCE MEMBERS; PREPARE 20 REFLECTIVE SUPERVISORS AND SUPPORT 150 PRACTITIONERS TOWARD ENDORSEMENT®. IMPLEMENT STANDARDIZED SCREENING; COMPLETE DC:0–5 EVALUATION WITHIN 30 DAYS OF POSITIVE SCREEN; ACHIEVE ≥85% LINKAGE TO APPROPRIATE SERVICES. SERVE 500 CHILDREN AND CAREGIVERS IN EVIDENCE-BASED DYADIC INTERVENTION. SCREEN ≥90% OF CAREGIVERS FOR PERINATAL/PARENTAL DEPRESSION AND LINK ≥85% OF POSITIVES TO TREATMENT. DELIVER IECMHC TO 100 ECE PROGRAMS REACHING 150 PROVIDERS. PROJECT TEND WILL PRODUCE A TOOLKIT AS A BLUEPRINT FOR AN IECMH SYSTEM OF CARE.

description: CENTRAL MISSOURI INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CM-IECMH CONTINUUM - THE UNIVERSITY OF MISSOURI CENTER FOR CHILD WELL-BEING (CCWB) WILL IMPLEMENT THE CENTRAL MISSOURI INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CM-IECMH CONTINUUM TO EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES ACROSS CENTRAL MISSOURI. THE PROJECT WILL STRENGTHEN THE REGIONAL WORKFORCE, IMPLEMENT UNIVERSAL DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING, PROVIDE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION (IECMHC), AND EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED PREVENTION, INTERVENTION, AND TREATMENT SERVICES THAT PROMOTE HEALTHY DEVELOPMENT, STRENGTHEN CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS, AND IMPROVE BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR INFANTS AND YOUNG CHILDREN. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE BOONE, AUDRAIN, CALLAWAY, COLE, COOPER, HOWARD, MONITEAU, AND RANDOLPH COUNTIES, REPRESENTING APPROXIMATELY 406,000 RESIDENTS, INCLUDING AN ESTIMATED 26,000 CHILDREN FROM BIRTH THROUGH AGE FIVE. OVER THE PROJECT PERIOD, THE CM-IECMH CONTINUUM WILL SERVE 3,073 UNDUPLICATED INDIVIDUALS, INCLUDING INFANTS, YOUNG CHILDREN, CAREGIVERS, AND EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONALS. ANNUAL ENROLLMENT WILL INCREASE FROM 190 PARTICIPANTS IN YEAR 1 TO APPROXIMATELY 720 PARTICIPANTS ANNUALLY DURING YEARS 2 THROUGH 5.  THE PRIMARY POPULATION OF FOCUS INCLUDES CHILDREN BIRTH THROUGH AGE FIVE AND THEIR CAREGIVERS, WITH SERVICES AVAILABLE FOR CHILDREN THROUGH AGE 12 WHEN CLINICALLY APPROPRIATE. THE PROJECT WILL SERVE CHILDREN WHO ARE AT RISK FOR, DEMONSTRATE EARLY SIGNS OF, OR HAVE BEEN DIAGNOSED WITH DEVELOPMENTAL, SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL, BEHAVIORAL, TRAUMA-RELATED, OR MENTAL HEALTH CONDITIONS, INCLUDING SERIOUS EMOTIONAL DISTURBANCE (SED). PRIORITY POPULATIONS INCLUDE CHILDREN EXPERIENCING ADVERSE CHILDHOOD EXPERIENCES, DEVELOPMENTAL DELAYS, ATTACHMENT DISRUPTIONS, CAREGIVER MENTAL HEALTH CONCERNS, AND LIMITED ACCESS TO BEHAVIORAL HEALTH SERVICES. THE CM-IECMH CONTINUUM WILL IMPLEMENT FOUR INTEGRATED STRATEGIES: (1) ESTABLISH THE CENTRAL MISSOURI EARLY CHILDHOOD PROFESSIONAL LEARNING COLLABORATIVE (ECPLC) TO STRENGTHEN THE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD WORKFORCE THROUGH INTERDISCIPLINARY TRAINING, IMPLEMENTATION COACHING, AND CHILD-PARENT PSYCHOTHERAPY (CPP) AND PARENT-CHILD INTERACTION THERAPY (PCIT) LEARNING COLLABORATIVES; (2) IMPLEMENT UNIVERSAL DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING USING THE SURVEY OF WELL-BEING OF YOUNG CHILDREN (SWYC) FOLLOWED BY COMPREHENSIVE ASSESSMENT, DIAGNOSIS, AND COORDINATED REFERRALS; (3) PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED PROMOTION, PREVENTION, AND TREATMENT THROUGH SHINE, ATTACHMENT VITAMINS, CPP, AND PCIT; AND (4) DELIVER INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH CONSULTATION (IECMHC) USING PREVENT-TEACH-REINFORCE FOR YOUNG CHILDREN (PTR-YC) TO STRENGTHEN THE CAPACITY OF EARLY CHILDHOOD PROGRAMS AND IMPROVE COORDINATED SYSTEMS OF CARE.  THE PROJECT'S GOALS ARE TO STRENGTHEN THE INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH WORKFORCE, INCREASE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF DEVELOPMENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONCERNS, EXPAND ACCESS TO EVIDENCE-BASED SERVICES, AND ESTABLISH A COORDINATED REGIONAL SYSTEM OF CARE. BY THE END OF YEAR 5, THE PROJECT WILL IMPLEMENT UNIVERSAL DEVELOPMENTAL AND SOCIAL-EMOTIONAL SCREENING FOR AT LEAST 1,000 CHILDREN IN PARTICIPATING CHILDCARE PROGRAMS, COMPLETE 1,600 COMMUNITY-BASED SCREENINGS, PROVIDE EVIDENCE-BASED ASSESSMENT AND TREATMENT TO AT LEAST 150 INFANTS, YOUNG CHILDREN, AND CAREGIVERS, AND ESTABLISH FORMAL REFERRAL AND CARE COORDINATION PARTNERSHIPS WITH AT LEAST 26 ORGANIZATIONS ACROSS THE REGION. THROUGH WORKFORCE DEVELOPMENT, EARLY IDENTIFICATION, EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTION, AND COORDINATED SYSTEMS OF CARE, THE CM-IECMH CONTINUUM WILL IMPROVE ACCESS TO HIGH-QUALITY INFANT AND EARLY CHILDHOOD MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES, STRENGTHEN CAREGIVER-CHILD RELATIONSHIPS, AND PROMOTE HEALTHY DEVELOPMENTAL AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR INFANTS, YOUNG CHILDREN, AND FAMILIES ACROSS CENTRAL MISSOURI.
