description: LINKING ADOLESCENT ENVIRONMENTAL ENRICHMENT TO ASSOCIATION CORTEX PLASTICITY AND PSYCHIATRIC RESILIENCY - PROJECT ABSTRACT THE MAJORITY OF LIFETIME PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS ONSET IN ADOLESCENCE, THUS THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR ACTIONABLE, NEUROSCIENCE-INFORMED APPROACHES TO PROMOTING ADOLESCENT WELL-BEING. RISK FOR PSYCHOPATHOLOGY IN ADOLESCENCE IS STRONGLY SHAPED BY INTERACTIONS BETWEEN ENVIRONMENTAL INPUTS AND PLASTICITY IN THE BRAIN’S HIGHER- ORDER ASSOCIATION CORTICES. RESEARCH IN HUMANS HAS FOUND THAT ENVIRONMENTAL ADVERSITY EXPERIENCED IN ADOLESCENCE LIMITS ASSOCIATION CORTEX PLASTICITY, LEADING TO POORER COGNITIVE HEALTH AND GREATER PSYCHOPATHOLOGY. IN CONTRAST, RESEARCH IN RODENTS HAS SHOWN THAT ENVIRONMENTAL ENRICHMENT—ENCOMPASSING PHYSICAL, COGNITIVE, AND SOCIAL STIMULATION—ENHANCES CORTICAL PLASTICITY, IMPROVES COGNITION, AND MITIGATES PHENOTYPES OF PSYCHIATRIC DISEASE. DESPITE THE TRANSFORMATIVE POTENTIAL OF ENRICHMENT, STUDIES IN HUMANS HAVE PRIMARILY EXAMINED THE DETRIMENTAL IMPACT OF NEGATIVE ENVIRONMENTS ON THE YOUTH BRAIN. IT IS THEREFORE NOT KNOWN HOW AND WHEN THE ENVIRONMENT CAN BE OPTIMALLY ENRICHED TO FOSTER HEALTHY DEVELOPMENTAL TRAJECTORIES. THIS PROPOSAL WILL TEST THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT THERE IS A MID-ADOLESCENT CRITICAL PERIOD OF HEIGHTENED ASSOCIATION CORTEX PLASTICITY DURING WHICH ENRICHMENT MAXIMALLY PROMOTES HEALTHY COGNITION AND RESILIENCE TO PSYCHOPATHOLOGY. IT WILL TAKE THE FORM OF A NATIONWIDE, NATURAL EXPERIMENT OF ENRICHMENT IN THE ADOLESCENT BRAIN COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT STUDY (ABCD; N = 11,878). MRI, COGNITIVE, CLINICAL, AND ENVIRONMENTAL DATA COLLECTED FROM YOUTH LONGITUDINALLY AT AGES 9-10, 11-12, 13-14, 15-16, AND 17-18 WILL BE USED. AIM 1 WILL EMPLOY DEEP PHENOTYPING OF POSITIVE ASPECTS OF YOUTHS’ PHYSICAL, COGNITIVE, AND SOCIAL ENVIRONMENTS TO DERIVE AN INDIVIDUALIZED INDEX OF ENRICHMENT AND IDENTIFY WHEN ENRICHMENT HAS THE LARGEST IMPACT ON COMPLEX COGNITION. AIM 2 WILL CHARACTERIZE WHEN NEUROBIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF PLASTICITY HYPOTHESIZED TO CONFER SENSITIVITY TO ENRICHMENT DEVELOP ACROSS THE SENSORIMOTOR- ASSOCIATION CORTICAL HIERARCHY. PRECLINICAL RESEARCH ON CRITICAL PERIODS HAS ESTABLISHED THAT ENVIRONMENT-DRIVEN INCREASES IN THALAMOCORTICAL STRUCTURAL CONNECTIVITY PROMOTE CORTICAL PLASTICITY, WHEREAS INCREASES IN CORTICAL MYELIN CONSOLIDATE PLASTICITY FOLLOWING ENVIRONMENTAL ADAPTATION. BY TRANSLATING THESE NEUROBIOLOGICAL HALLMARKS OF PLASTICITY TO IN VIVO MRI, THIS AIM WILL TEMPORALLY DEMARCATE THE OPENING AND CLOSING OF AN ADOLESCENT CRITICAL PERIOD OF ASSOCIATION CORTEX PLASTICITY. AIM 3 WILL EXAMINE WHEN—BETWEEN THE AGES OF 9 AND 18—ENRICHMENT MOST IMPACTS THALAMIC CONNECTIVITY AND MYELIN IN THE ASSOCIATION CORTEX TO CONFER RESILIENCY TO TRANSDIAGNOSTIC PSYCHIATRIC VULNERABILITY. THE PI, DR. SYDNOR, WILL RECEIVE TRAINING IN DEVELOPMENTAL PSYCHOPATHOLOGY, ENVIRONMENTAL ENRICHMENT, POPULATION NEUROIMAGING INFORMATICS, AND LONGITUDINAL AND CAUSAL MODELING. TRAINING WILL OCCUR WITHIN THE UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH’S WORLD-CLASS RESEARCH ENVIRONMENT WITH THE SUPPORT OF OUTSTANDING MENTORS DRS. LUNA, FORBES, SHERIDAN, FAIR, THOMPSON, AND BARCH. THIS K99/R00 PATHWAY TO INDEPENDENCE AWARD WILL ALLOW THE PI TO ESTABLISH AN INNOVATIVE AND INDEPENDENT RESEARCH LAB STUDYING HOW MENTAL ILLNESS CAN BE PREVENTED BY LEVERAGING THE DEVELOPING BRAIN’S CAPACITY FOR ADAPTIVE, ENVIRONMENT-DRIVEN PLASTICITY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TARGETING HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS BY LIPID NANOPARTICLES TO TREAT HEMATOLOGICAL DISORDERS - PROJECT ABSTRACT – OVERALL THIS PROGRAM PROJECT GRANT (PPG) AIMS TO DEVELOP SAFE, EFFECTIVE, AND SCALABLE CURATIVE THERAPIES FOR HEMOGLOBINOPATHIES (INCLUDING SICKLE CELL DISEASE (SCD), A-THALASSEMIA (AT), AND B-THALASSEMIA (BT)) AND FANCONI ANEMIA (FA) BY TARGETING HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELLS (HSC) IN VIVO. WHILE HEMATOPOIETIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION (HSCT) CAN BE CURATIVE, THE TOXICITIES ASSOCIATED WITH CURRENT CONDITIONING REGIMENS LIMIT ELIGIBILITY AND THREATEN FERTILITY AND LONG-TERM HEALTH. THE HEAVY STRAIN PLACED ON PATIENTS, FAMILIES, AND HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS, SPANNING INPATIENT CARE, EMERGENCY SERVICES, TRANSFUSIONS, AND LONG-TERM COMPLICATION MANAGEMENT, HIGHLIGHTS THE PRESSING NEED FOR INNOVATIVE, SAFER, AND MORE WIDELY ACCESSIBLE CURATIVE TREATMENTS. OUR COMPREHENSIVE AND INTEGRATED RESEARCH STRATEGY BRINGS TOGETHER CUTTING-EDGE TECHNOLOGIES AND INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGIES TO ADDRESS HSC DISORDERS. SPECIFICALLY, WE EMPLOY ANTIBODY-DIRECTED, HSC-TARGETED LIPID NANOPARTICLES (LNP) DESIGNED TO DELIVER MRNA-ENCODED PRO-APOPTOTIC (PA) PAYLOADS OR GENE EDITORS DIRECTLY TO DISEASED STEM CELLS. THIS PRECISE DELIVERY SYSTEM IS COUPLED WITH ADVANCED DISEASE MODELING PLATFORMS, INCLUDING HUMANIZED MOUSE MODELS AND PRECLINICAL LARGE ANIMAL SYSTEMS SUCH AS SHEEP AND NON-HUMAN PRIMATES, TO RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE BOTH SAFETY AND EFFICACY. THE ULTIMATE GOAL IS TO ACHIEVE EITHER THE SELECTIVE DEPLETION OF DISEASED POPULATIONS OR DURABLE GENETIC CORRECTION OF FAULTY HSC, PAVING THE WAY FOR TRANSFORMATIVE THERAPIES. SUPPORTING THIS APPROACH ARE THREE INTERCONNECTED RESEARCH PROJECTS, WHICH ARE REINFORCED BY TWO SPECIALIZED SCIENTIFIC CORES AND A CENTRAL ADMINISTRATIVE CORE. TOGETHER, THESE COMPONENTS ENSURE SCIENTIFIC RIGOR, FOSTER COLLABORATION AND SYNERGY ACROSS TEAMS, AND ENABLE RAPID ITERATIVE CYCLES OF DISCOVERY, REFINEMENT, AND TRANSLATION TOWARD CLINICAL APPLICATION. PROJECT 1 IMPROVES FERTILITY-PRESERVING CONDITIONING THROUGH TARGETED HSC DEPLETION AND DEVELOPS IN VIVO GENE EDITING FOR HEMOGLOBINOPATHIES. PROJECT 2 EXPLORES INTERHOMOLOG RECOMBINATION FOR ALLELE REPAIR AND NON-TOXIC IN VIVO SELECTION IN FA. PROJECT 3 FOCUSES ON PRENATAL LNP-MEDIATED BASE EDITING OF FETAL HSC TO INTERVENE BEFORE DISEASE BEGINS. CORE B (OPTIMIZED NUCLEIC ACID AND CELL-SPECIFIC DELIVERY) DESIGNS AND PRODUCES HSC-TARGETED LNP AND CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVES FORMULATIONS BASED ON PROJECT FEEDBACK. CORE C (GENE EDITING, IPSC, AND HSC) SUPPLIES EDITING PLATFORMS, IPSC-DERIVED HSPCS, AND HUMANIZED XENOGRAFT MODELS; CORE A (ADMINISTRATIVE) MANAGES GOVERNANCE, COMPLIANCE, DATA SHARING, AND EVALUATION. INNOVATION INVOLVES IN SITU HSC EDITING AND CONDITIONING USING ANTIBODY-FUNCTIONALIZED LNP, PRENATAL DELIVERY TO THE FETAL LIVER HSC NICHE, AND CAREFUL MEASUREMENT OF ON- AND OFF-TARGET EFFECTS ACROSS SPECIES. ANTICIPATED OUTCOMES INCLUDE FERTILITY-PRESERVING TRANSPLANT CONDITIONING, EFFECTIVE IN VIVO CORRECTION OF DISEASE ALLELES, AND ROBUST PRECLINICAL EVIDENCE TO MITIGATE RISKS IN TRANSLATION. BY REDUCING TOXICITY, SIMPLIFYING PROCEDURES, AND ENABLING EARLIER INTERVENTION, THIS PROGRAM AIMS TO EXPAND ACCESS TO CURATIVE THERAPIES AND LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR FIRST-IN-HUMAN STUDIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: POLYSUBSTANCE ADDICTION RESEARCH CENTER - ABSTRACT OVERALL SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUDS) REMAIN A MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS, DRIVEN INCREASINGLY BY POLYSUBSTANCE USE. DESPITE DECADES OF RESEARCH, WE STILL LACK AN INTEGRATED FRAMEWORK THAT EXPLAINS HOW GENETIC, CELLULAR, AND PHYSIOLOGICAL VULNERABILITIES CONVERGE TO PROMOTE COMPULSIVE DRUG USE, ABSTINENCE, AND RELAPSE. MOST STUDIES ISOLATE SINGLE DRUGS, NARROW BEHAVIORAL PHENOTYPES, OR INDIVIDUAL BIOLOGICAL LEVELS, PRODUCING FRAGMENTED RESULTS THAT LIMIT PREDICTIVE POWER AND THERAPEUTIC DEVELOPMENT. THE POLYSUBSTANCE ADDICTION RESEARCH CENTER (PARC) DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THIS GAP BY UNITING BEHAVIORAL, MOLECULAR, CIRCUIT, AND IMMUNOMETABOLIC DATA WITHIN THE SAME GENETICALLY DIVERSE HETEROGENEOUS STOCK (HS) RATS AND ALIGNING THESE FINDINGS WITH HUMAN OMICS AND IMAGING DATASETS WITH THREE RESEARCH POJECTS: BRAIN CONNECTOMIC, BRAIN TRANSCRIPTOMIC, AND GUT-VAGUS MULTIOMIC. THIS DESIGN ENABLES SYSTEMATIC COMPARISONS ACROSS DRUGS (COCAINE, OXYCODONE, ALCOHOL, AND THEIR CO-USE), ACROSS SPECIES (HS RATS VERSUS HUMAN SUD/AUD COHORTS AND HEALTHY CONTROLS), AND ACROSS THE SEVERITY SPECTRUM OF ADDICTION-LIKE BEHAVIORS. ALL DATA CONVERGE IN THE ONE-INDIVIDUAL MULTISCALE ATLAS, A CENTER-WIDE MANDATE THAT HARMONIZES MULTIMODAL DATASETS INTO A REUSABLE TRANSLATIONAL RESOURCE. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL IDENTIFY MULTILEVEL BIOMARKERS OF ADDICTION-LIKE BEHAVIORS BY QUANTIFYING BEHAVIORAL, NEURAL, MOLECULAR, AND IMMUNOMETABOLIC SIGNATURES ACROSS SEX, DRUGS, AND SEVERITY OF ADDICTION-LIKE BEHAVIORS. ADVANCED AI/ML APPROACHES WILL INTEGRATE THESE DATA INTO INTERPRETABLE PROFILES OF VULNERABILITY AND RESILIENCE, SPANNING GENES TO BEHAVIOR. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL REVEAL AND VALIDATE DRUGGABLE TARGETS. CANDIDATE TARGETS, INCLUDING OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION STRESS PATHWAYS, CHOLINERGIC AND IMMUNE SIGNALING PATHWAYS, WILL BE TESTED USING PHARMACOLOGICAL AND VIRAL APPROACHES AND TRANSLATIONALLY-RELEVANT MODELS OF RELAPSE. SPECIFIC AIM 3 WILL ACCELERATE DISCOVERY BY DEPLOYING AN INTEGRATED CENTER PLATFORM. THIS INCLUDES EXPANDING THE ADDICTION BIOBANK, CREATING CLOUD-BASED PIPELINES FOR DATA SHARING AND ANALYSIS, PROVIDING PILOT FUNDING FOR INNOVATIVE PROJECTS, AND TRAINING THE NEXT GENERATION OF SCIENTISTS IN MULTISCALE ADDICTION RESEARCH. ALL PROJECTS SHARE HARMONIZED LONGITUDINAL COHORTS, EXPERIMENTAL DESIGNS, AND TIME POINTS, ENSURING CROSS-VALIDATION AND IMMEDIATE BIDIRECTIONAL FEEDBACK. INTEGRATION IS FURTHER SUPPORTED BY FOUR CORES: BEHAVIORAL PHENOTYPING, BIOBANK, COMPUTATIONAL & ANALYTICAL, AND PILOT PROJECTS. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE A VALIDATED BIOMARKER PANEL FOR DIAGNOSIS AND STRATIFICATION, EXPERIMENTALLY CONFIRMED THERAPEUTIC TARGETS, PUBLICLY AVAILABLE DATASETS AND BIOSPECIMENS, AND A TRAINED WORKFORCE FLUENT IN INTEGRATIVE ADDICTION SCIENCE. TOGETHER, PARC WILL TRANSFORM ADDICTION RESEARCH FROM SILOED OBSERVATIONS INTO A PREDICTIVE, MECHANISTIC, AND TRANSLATIONAL ENTERPRISE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADAPTATION OF PATH-PAIN FOR DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS LIVING WITH PERSISTENT PAIN AND NEGATIVE EMOTIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS FREQUENTLY EXPERIENCE PERSISTENT MUSCULOSKELETAL PAIN. PAIN IS OFTEN MADE WORSE BY PERFORMING CAREGIVING TASKS, IMPAIRING DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS’ ABILITY TO PROVIDE CARE. DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS’ WHO HAVE PAIN OFTEN HAVE CO-EXISTING EMOTIONAL AND PSYCHOLOGICAL HEALTH CHALLENGES, SUCH AS HIGH NEGATIVE EMOTIONS AND/OR COMORBID DEPRESSION, WHICH MAKES MANAGING THEIR PAIN AND THEIR CAREGIVING TASKS MORE DIFFICULT. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS K99/R00 PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP DR. SHELBIE TURNER’S CAPACITY TO CONDUCT TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH TO SUPPORT DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS’ HEALTH AND WELL-BEING THROUGH IMPROVED MANAGEMENT OF THEIR OWN PERSISTENT PAIN. DR. TURNER WILL WORK TOWARDS FIVE TRAINING OBJECTIVES IN THE K99 PHASE OF THE PROJECT. DOING SO WILL ALLOW HER TO DEVELOP AND TRANSITION TO AN INDEPENDENT INVESTIGATOR WHO DESIGNS, ADAPTS, EVALUATES, AND DISSEMINATES INNOVATIVE, EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTIONS TO PREVENT OR MITIGATE DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS’ NEGATIVE HEALTH OUTCOMES, WITH A FOCUS ON THE PROBLEM OF PERSISTENT PAIN AND ASSOCIATED SYMPTOMS (E.G., NEGATIVE EMOTIONS) AND COMORBIDITIES (E.G., DEPRESSION). FIRST, SHE WILL ADD TO AND EXTEND HER KNOWLEDGE IN CORE SUBSTANTIVE AREAS TO INCLUDE PAIN, NEGATIVE EMOTIONS, DEMENTIA CAREGIVING, AND HEALTH BEHAVIOR CHANGE. SECOND, SHE WILL IMPROVE HER ABILITY TO DEVELOP, IMPLEMENT, AND DISSEMINATE BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS WITH AN EMPHASIS ON BOTH PAIN MANAGEMENT INTERVENTIONS AND CAREGIVER INTERVENTIONS. THIRD, SHE WILL GAIN EXPERIENCE NEEDED TO DESIGN AND CONDUCT CLINICAL TRIALS, INCLUDING CONVENTIONAL, PRAGMATIC, AND ADAPTIVE CLINICAL TRIALS WITH DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS. FINALLY, SHE WILL PURSUE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN GRANT WRITING (FOURTH TRAINING OBJECTIVE) AND LEADERSHIP AND COLLABORATION (FIFTH TRAINING OBJECTIVE). THE THREE RESEARCH AIMS OF THIS APPLICATION WILL PROGRESS AS FOLLOWS. AIM 1 ADAPTS AN EVIDENCE- BASED PAIN SELF-MANAGEMENT INTERVENTION, PROBLEM ADAPTATION THERAPY FOR PAIN IN PRIMARY CARE (PATH-PAIN), FOR USE BY DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS WITH PERSISTENT PAIN. AIM 2 TESTS THE USABILITY OF THE ADAPTED INTERVENTION WITH DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS, AND AIM 3 EXAMINES THE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OF THE INTERVENTION THROUGH A PILOT RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL. THE ADAPTED INTERVENTION WILL BE THE FIRST EVIDENCE- BASED PAIN SELF-MANAGEMENT PROGRAM CUSTOMIZED SPECIFICALLY FOR DEMENTIA FAMILY CAREGIVERS. THE PROPOSED PROJECT IS CONSISTENT WITH NIA’S MISSION TO CONDUCT BEHAVIORAL RESEARCH ON AGING AND FOSTER THE DEVELOPMENT OF RESEARCH SCIENTISTS IN AGING. IT IS ALIGNED WITH NIA’S SPECIAL INTERESTS IN DEMENTIA CAREGIVER INTERVENTION RESEARCH AND PAIN MANAGEMENT RESEARCH. DR. TURNER PROPOSES TO PURSUE HER DEVELOPMENTAL GOALS AND BEGIN THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WITH THE SUPPORT OF THE DIVISION OF GERIATRICS AND PALLIATIVE MEDICINE AT WEILL CORNELL MEDICAL COLLEGE OF CORNELL UNIVERSITY, WHICH PROVIDES AN IDEAL ENVIRONMENT OF RESEARCH SUPPORT AND RESOURCES TO HELP HER ACHIEVE HER TRAINING AND RESEARCH GOALS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING NOVEL METHODS TO COMBAT URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS - URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (UTIS) AFFECT MORE THAN 150 MILLION PEOPLE ANNUALLY AND ARE BECOMING INCREASINGLY DIFFICULT TO TREAT BECAUSE OF RISING ANTIMICROBIAL RESISTANCE. BACTERIAL ADHESION TO HOST TISSUES AND MEDICAL DEVICES IS THE CRITICAL FIRST STEP IN INFECTION AND IS MEDIATED BY SPECIALIZED SURFACE PROTEINS KNOWN AS ADHESINS. BECAUSE ADHESION IS REQUIRED FOR INFECTION TO BE ESTABLISHED, ADHESINS REPRESENT ATTRACTIVE THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR PREVENTING INFECTION. THE ADHESIN FIMH FROM UROPATHOGENIC ESCHERICHIA COLI HAS VALIDATED ANTI-ADHESION STRATEGIES AS A THERAPEUTIC APPROACH. A KEY OUTSTANDING QUESTION IS WHETHER THIS APPROACH CAN BE GENERALIZED TO OTHER ADHESINS, MANY OF WHICH REMAIN STRUCTURALLY AND MECHANISTICALLY UNCHARACTERIZED. THIS PROJECT FOCUSES ON TWO CLINICALLY IMPORTANT ADHESINS: FMLH FROM UROPATHOGENIC ESCHERICHIA COLI, WHICH PROMOTES PERSISTENT COLONIZATION OF THE URINARY TRACT, AND MRKD FROM MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT KLEBSIELLA PNEUMONIAE, WHICH MEDIATES BIOFILM FORMATION AND IS IMPLICATED IN CATHETER-ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS (CAUTIS). BUILDING ON DISCOVERIES FROM THE K99 PHASE, WHICH ESTABLISHED THE STRUCTURAL AND MECHANISTIC BASIS OF A NOVEL ADHESIN INHIBITORY MECHANISM TERMED PARASTERIC INHIBITION USING THE PROTOTYPICAL ADHESIN FIMH, THIS WORK WILL TEST WHETHER THE CONFORMATIONAL DYNAMICS AND ALLOSTERIC REGULATORY MECHANISMS GOVERNING FIMH FUNCTION ARE CONSERVED IN FMLH AND MRKD, AND WHETHER THEY CAN BE EXPLOITED TO INHIBIT BACTERIAL ADHESION. THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL DEFINE THE CONFORMATIONAL LANDSCAPES OF FMLH AND MRKD USING MUTAGENESIS AND NMR SPECTROSCOPY, CHARACTERIZE THE CONFORMATIONAL DYNAMICS THAT REGULATE LIGAND BINDING AND ADHESION USING NMR AND BIOPHYSICAL TOOLS, AND DEVELOP PEPTIDE INHIBITORS THAT TARGET THESE ADHESINS TO BLOCK BACTERIAL ATTACHMENT. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES GOVERNING ADHESIN STRUCTURE, DYNAMICS, AND FUNCTION WHILE PROVIDING A GENERALIZABLE FRAMEWORK FOR DEVELOPING ANTI-ADHESION THERAPEUTICS AGAINST MULTIDRUG-RESISTANT UROPATHOGENS. THESE STUDIES HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO ADVANCE A NEW CLASS OF NON-ANTIBIOTIC INTERVENTIONS FOR THE PREVENTION AND TREATMENT OF URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF A HOMELESSNESS PREVENTION AND RAPID REHOUSING INITIATIVE FOR HOUSING UNSTABLE VETERANS ON ALCOHOL-RELATED HARMS: ANALYSIS OF LINKED HOUSING PROGRAM AND HEALTH CARE DATA - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT PERSONS WHO LACK STABLE HOUSING EXPERIENCE A DISPROPORTIONATE BURDEN OF ALCOHOL USE DISORDER (AUD). THREE IN FIVE (60%) HOMELESS ADULTS HAVE A HISTORY OF AUD, LEADING TO ELEVATED RATES OF ALCOHOL-RELATED HARMS (E.G., POISONING AND WITHDRAWAL, ALCOHOL-RELATED INJURY, CHRONIC DISEASE, AND PREMATURE MORTALITY). THE LACK OF STABLE HOUSING NEGATIVELY IMPACTS ALCOHOL-RELATED OUTCOMES PRIMARILY BY CAUSING HIGHER STRESS, RUPTURING CONNECTIONS TO HEALTH-PROMOTING SOCIAL SUPPORTS, INCREASING EXPOSURE TO RISKY ENVIRONMENTS, AND CREATING BARRIERS TO ACCESSING BOTH PREVENTATIVE CARE AND AUD TREATMENT. LITTLE IS KNOWN REGARDING WHETHER HOUSING INTERVENTIONS COULD IMPROVE ALCOHOL USE AND RELATED OUTCOMES. THE SUPPORTIVE SERVICES FOR VETERAN FAMILIES (SSVF) PROGRAM IS THE LARGEST PROGRAM TO PREVENT AND END HOMELESSNESS AMONG VETERANS IN THE US. SSVF IS A PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN THE DEPARTMENT OF VETERANS AFFAIRS (VA) AND COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS (REFERRED TO AS GRANTEES). IN THIS PARTNERSHIP, GRANTEES PROVIDE TEMPORARY FINANCIAL ASSISTANCE AND OTHER SUPPORT SERVICES TO VETERANS WHO ARE EITHER CURRENTLY HOMELESS OR FACING IMMINENT RISK OF HOMELESSNESS. IN FY 2023, VA PROVIDED $712 MILLION IN FUNDING TO 249 GRANTEES COVERING EVERY STATE IN THE US WHO DELIVERED SERVICES TO ROUGHLY 80,000 VETERANS NATIONWIDE. OUR PREVIOUS EFFORTS HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT SSVF HAS A POSITIVE IMPACT ON VETERAN HOUSING, HEALTHCARE COSTS, AND ALL- CAUSE MORTALITY OUTCOMES. HOWEVER, THE IMPACTS OF SSVF ON ALCOHOL USE AND ALCOHOL-RELATED TREATMENT AND OUTCOMES HAVE NOT BEEN ESTABLISHED. IN THIS STUDY, OUR TEAM WILL USE A UNIQUE, LONGITUDINAL, PERSON-LEVEL DATASET THAT LINKS BOTH DATA ON PARTICIPATION IN SSVF AND VETERAN ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD DATA FOR MORE THAN A DECADE ALONG WITH INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGICAL APPROACHES INCLUDING TARGET TRIAL EMULATION AND NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING. IN AIM 1, WE WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF THE SSVF PROGRAM ON UNHEALTHY ALCOHOL CONSUMPTION AMONG VETERANS WITH AND WITHOUT A HISTORY OF UNHEALTHY ALCOHOL USE. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ASSESS THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN SSVF AND ALCOHOL-RELATED ADVERSE OUTCOMES—INCLUDING TRAUMATIC INJURY, ALCOHOL POISONING, CIRRHOSIS, SUICIDAL IDEATION, AND MORTALITY—AMONG VETERANS WITH A DIAGNOSIS OF ALCOHOL USE DISORDER. IN AIM 3, WE WILL EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF SSVF ON INITIATION OF MEDICATIONS FOR ALCOHOL USE DISORDER (MAUD) AND BEHAVIORAL HEALTH INTERVENTIONS, AS WELL AS RETENTION ON MAUD. OUR FINDINGS WILL PROVIDE ACTIONABLE INFORMATION TO TAILOR HOMELESSNESS PREVENTION AND RAPID REHOUSING INTERVENTIONS—BOTH WITHIN THE VA AND IN THE COMMUNITY-BASED HOMELESS ASSISTANCE SYSTEM—TO MITIGATE ALCOHOL-RELATED HARMS AMONG PERSONS WITH UNSTABLE HOUSING.

description: BIOMARKERS TO TRACK EFFECTIVE INTERVENTIONS THAT DELAY DEMENTIA ONSET IN PARTICIPANTS OF THE "RISK REDUCTION FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (RRAD)" TRIAL - PROJECT SUMMARY IT IS OFTEN HARD TO DISTINGUISH BETWEEN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND AD-RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRDS), INCLUDING VASCULAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA (VCID), DUE TO A SIMILAR CLINICAL PRESENTATION OF MEMORY LOSS AND THE PRESENCE OF CARDIOVASCULAR (CV) RISK FACTORS (E.G. HYPERTENSION, DYSLIPIDEMIA). WHILE CV RISK FACTORS HAVE AVAILABLE DRUG THERAPIES, INCREASED  PHYSICAL ACTIVITY ALSO SIGNIFICANTLY LOWERS THESE CO-MORBIDITIES. UNFORTUNATELY, EVIDENCE LINKING CV AND EXERCISE INTERVENTIONS TO THE PREVENTION OF COGNITIVE DECLINE IS INCONCLUSIVE, NOR ARE  BIOMARKERS AVAILABLE TO DETERMINE THE EFFICACY OF PRE-DEMENTIA LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS. THIS ANCILLARY R01 WILL USE PLASMA-BASED BIOMARKERS AND NEUROIMAGING FROM SUBJECTS ENROLLED IN OUR  NIH-FUNDED TRIAL “RISK REDUCTION FOR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (RRAD; NCT02913664).” THIS PHASE II RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL WILL DETERMINE THE INDEPENDENT AND COMBINED EFFECTS OF INTENSIVE PHARMACOLOGICAL REDUCTION OF VASCULAR RISK FACTORS (IRVR; I.E. BLOOD PRESSURE, LIPIDS) AND AEROBIC EXERCISE (EX) ON COGNITIVE FUNCTION. PARTICIPANTS WERE RANDOMIZED INTO 2-YEAR INTERVENTIONS (IRVR, EX, IRVR+EX, AND A CONTROL ARM OF STANDARD CARE (SC)) WITH PLASMA AND NEUROIMAGING COLLECTED AT BASELINE AND YEARLY. OF THE 513  INITIAL RRAD SUBJECTS (63% FEMALES; 34% AGED 71-85; 13% AFRICAN-AMERICAN; 4% LATINO), 89% (458 SUBJECTS) HAVE LONGITUDINAL SERUM AND NEUROIMAGING BIOMARKERS AVAILABLE FOR LINEAR MIXED-MODELS ANALYSES. BANKED LONGITUDINAL RRAD PLASMA SAMPLES WILL BE USED TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT 1) BENCHMARK AD, 2) BENCHMARK VCID, AND/OR 3) NOVEL CIRCULATING BRAIN-DERIVED BIOMARKERS CAN BE MODULATED BY POSITIVE LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS. AIM 1 WILL TEST IF THE BENCHMARK AD BIOMARKERS AΒ42/AΒ40 RATIO WILL INCREASE, WHILE PTAU181 AND PTAU 231 WILL DECREASE, THE GREATEST WITH IRVR+EX. HIGHER RATIOS AND LOWER TAU WILL BE ASSOCIATED WITH OUR SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES OF PRESERVED HIPPOCAMPAL VOLUME (T1-WEIGHTED MRI). AIM 2 WILL TEST IF PRIMARY BENCHMARK VCID BIOMARKERS WILL REVEAL EFFECTS OF VASCULAR AND EXERCISE INTERVENTIONS ON CEREBROVASCULAR HEALTH. WE WILL TEST IF LOWER PATHOLOGIC PRO-ANGIOGENIC PROTEINS (I.E. VEGF-D, PLGF, BFGF) MEASURED LONGITUDINALLY DECREASE WITH INTERVENTION. LOWER EXPRESSION WILL COINCIDE WITH SECONDARY OUTCOME MEASURES OF INCREASED REGIONAL CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW (I.E. ARTERIAL SPIN LABELING, MRI) AND FEWER WHITE MATTER HYPERINTENSITIES (I.E. T2 FLAIR, MRI). AIM 3 WILL TEST IF VASCULAR AND EXERCISE INTERVENTIONS ALTER THE NEUROTROPHIC CARGO OF CIRCULATING NEURONAL-ENRICHED EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES (EVS). WE WILL TEST IRVR+EX LOWERS PRO- (I.E. UNCLEAVED) BRAIN-DERIVED NEUROTROPHIC FACTOR (BDNF) AND INCREASES MATURE BDNF IN NEURONAL-ENRICHED EVS. HIGHER BDNF WILL COINCIDE WITH THE SECONDARY OUTCOME OF PRESERVED DEFAULT-MODE NETWORK (DMN) CONNECTIVITY MEASURED BY RESTING-STATE FUNCTIONAL (RS-F)MRI. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AD, VCID, AND EV BIOMARKERS NOT ONLY IDENTIFY INDIVIDUALS WITH HIGH RISK FOR AD/ADRDS BUT CAN ALSO TRACK EFFICACY OF INDEPENDENT AND COMBINED LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS THAT IMPROVE CEREBROVASCULAR HEALTH AND DELAY DEMENTIA ONSET IN SEDENTARY ADULTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AN AI-DRIVEN METABOLIC CLOCK FOR HEALTHY AGING AND AD/ADRD - AGE IS THE GREATEST RISK FACTOR FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND AD-RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRDS). AD PROGRESSION IS CURRENTLY UNDERSTOOD AS PATHOPHYSIOLOGIC PROCESSES THAT BEGIN YEARS, IF NOT UP TO A DECADE AHEAD OF ANY NEUROLOGICAL SYMPTOMS. HOWEVER, THESE PATHOLOGICAL CHANGES ALONE ARE NOT SUFFICIENT FOR THE CLINICAL EXPRESSION OF AD DEMENTIA SYMPTOMS. IN THE BACKGROUND OF AD RISK, AGING IS ASSOCIATED WITH SYSTEMIC CHANGES IN METABOLISM WHICH MAY PROVIDE BIOLOGICAL SIGNALS THAT CAN DISTINGUISH THE SHIFT FROM HEALTHY AGING TO AD INITIATION AND PROGRESSIVE COGNITIVE DECLINE, WHICH IS CRUCIAL FOR DEVELOPING TREATMENT OR PREVENTION STRATEGIES. SYSTEMIC METABOLISM IS MOST COMPREHENSIVELY ASSAYED THROUGH UNTARGETED METABOLOMICS PERFORMED ON A BIOFLUID SAMPLE. TO DATE, THE METABOLIC DRIVERS OF COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT IN AD REMAIN UNKNOWN OUTSIDE OF A FEW PUTATIVE CONNECTIONS BETWEEN INSULIN RESISTANCE AND DEMENTIA RISK. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP IN KNOWLEDGE, THIS PROJECT WILL USE LARGE-SCALE UNTARGETED METABOLOMICS TO REVEAL A MORE COMPLETE CONNECTION BETWEEN METABOLIC STATE, AGING, AND AD/ADRD. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT THE SHIFT FROM HEALTHY AGING TO LATENT (ALSO KNOWN AS PRECLINICAL OR ASYMPTOMATIC) AD AND ULTIMATELY TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE DEMENTIA (ADD) CAN BE UNDERSTOOD THROUGH METABOLIC DEVIATIONS FROM A HEALTHY AGING TRAJECTORY. OUR MAIN RESEARCH DESIGN IS PERFORMING UNTARGETED METABOLOMICS IN TWO MAJOR COHORTS (THE NCRAD COHORT REPRESENTING AD PATIENTS AND HEALTHY CONTROLS (HCS) FROM MULTIPLE SITES, AND THE STANFORD ADRC COHORT THAT REPRESENTS AD PATIENTS AND HC MATCHES WHEREIN THE COMPLETE ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD (EHR) IS AVAILABLE FOR STUDY). IN SPECIFIC AIM 1, TO DEVELOP A METABOLIC “CLOCK” OF HUMAN AGING AND STUDY DEVIATIONS THAT ARE ASSOCIATED WITH AD/ADRD, WE WILL TEST THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS BY FIRST CREATING A DEEP LEARNING-BASED METABOLOMIC SIGNATURE OF CALENDAR AGE AS BASELINE MULTIVARIATE COMPOSITE BIOMARKER (SUB-AIM 1.1). BY STUDYING DEVIATIONS FROM METABOLIC AGE AND ASSOCIATED COMORBIDITIES (SUB-AIM 1.2) AND CHARACTERIZING THE INTERPLAY BETWEEN INSULIN RESISTANCE, THE METABOLOMIC CLOCK, AND AD/ADRD DIAGNOSIS (SUB-AIM 1.3), WE WILL DETERMINE HOW METABOLIC AGE CAN DELINEATE VARIOUS RISK GROUPS IN THE GENERAL ELDERLY POPULATION. SPECIFIC AIM 2 IS TO DEVELOP A METABOLOMICS MODEL TO PROVIDE IN-DEPTH INSIGHTS INTO AD/ADRD. HERE, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT METABOLOMICS CONTAINS A SPECIFIC SIGNATURE OF AD/ADRD PROGRESSION OVER TIME BY DEVELOPING LONGITUDINAL TRANSFORMER MODELS (SUB-AIM 2.1) AND END-TO-END RAW METABOLOMICS MODELS THAT PROVIDE INTERPRETABLE READ-OUTS OF METABOLITE AND METABOLIC PATHWAY IMPORTANCE (SUB-AIM 2.2) TO POWER BIOLOGICAL DISCOVERY. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL EXPLORE THE POTENTIAL OF INTEGRATING THE EHR (SUB-AIM 2.3) TO CREATE MORE POWERFUL MODELS OF AD/ADRD RISK. THE LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP AD/ADRD RISK GROUPS BASED ON AN UNTARGETED METABOLOMICS WHICH TAKE INTO CONTEXT AGING, COGNITIVE STATUS, QUALITY OF LIFE, AND THE PRESENCE OF COMORBIDITIES. ACHIEVING A METABOLIC RISK DIFFERENTIATION STRATEGY AND AD/ADRD-FOCUSED RISK MANAGEMENT WILL HELP ELDERLY PATIENTS LIVE LONGER, MORE ACTIVE LIVES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HEALTH CARE CONTACT DAYS: ASSESSING KEY PERSPECTIVES, THE ROLE OF HEALTH SYSTEMS, AND IMPACT ON PATIENT OUTCOMES - PROJECT SUMMARY FOR OLDER ADULTS, DAYS SPENT OBTAINING HEALTH CARE OUTSIDE THE HOME (“HEALTH CARE CONTACT DAYS”) REPRESENT NOT ONLY ACCESS TO NEEDED CARE, BUT ALSO SUBSTANTIAL TIME, EFFORT, FINANCIAL, AND OTHER OPPORTUNITY COSTS FOR THEMSELVES AND THEIR CARE PARTNERS. CONTACT DAYS REPRESENT A CLAIMS- BASED, PERSON-CENTERED MEASURE THAT INCLUDES DAYS SPENT RECEIVING INSTITUTIONAL CARE (HOSPITAL, EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT, SKILLED NURSING FACILITY, OR INPATIENT HOSPICE) AND AMBULATORY CARE (OFFICE VISITS, PROCEDURES, TREATMENTS, IMAGING, OR TESTS). GIVEN THE TRADEOFFS, AND EARLY EVIDENCE THAT CONTACT DAYS ARE INFLUENCED BY FACTORS BEYOND PATIENTS’ HEALTH NEEDS, THERE IS BOTH NEED AND AMPLE OPPORTUNITY TO UNDERSTAND AND OPTIMIZE CONTACT DAYS. SOME OF THIS EFFORT SHOULD LIKELY COME FROM HEALTH SYSTEMS – WHICH SERVE A LARGE AND GROWING SHARE OF OLDER ADULTS AND HAVE MAJOR INFLUENCE ON THEIR CARE, E.G., THROUGH PAYMENT MODELS AND TECHNOLOGY. YET THERE IS SCANT RESEARCH ON CONTACT DAYS; SPECIFICALLY, THERE ARE NO QUALITATIVE STUDIES OF CONTACT DAYS AND NO QUANTITATIVE EVIDENCE ON THE ROLE OF HEALTH SYSTEMS OR HOW CONTACT DAYS IMPACT PATIENT OUTCOMES THAT MIGHT JUSTIFY, OR BE NEGATIVELY AFFECTED BY, HAVING MORE OF THESE DAYS. THIS PROPOSAL WILL ADDRESS THESE CRITICAL GAPS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL USE SEMI-STRUCTURED INTERVIEWS AND FOCUS GROUPS TO ELICIT AND ANALYZE PATIENT, CARE PARTNER, CLINICIAN, CARE MANAGER, AND OPERATIONAL LEADER PERSPECTIVES ON HEALTH CARE CONTACT DAYS IN TWO LARGE HEALTH SYSTEMS SERVING A RANGE OF POPULATIONS ACROSS 5 STATES. IN AIM 2, WE WILL USE SURVEY AND MEDICARE BILLING DATA TO DETERMINE HOW CONTACT DAYS VARY ACROSS HEALTH SYSTEMS AND TO QUANTIFY THE ASSOCIATION OF MODIFIABLE HEALTH SYSTEM ATTRIBUTES (E.G., LOW-VALUE SERVICE USE, TELEMEDICINE ADOPTION) WITH PATIENT SEVERITY-ADJUSTED CONTACT DAYS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL USE A RIGOROUS NATURAL EXPERIMENT (A “MOVER” ANALYSIS) AND 100% MEDICARE CLAIMS DATA TO DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF QUASI-RANDOMIZING PATIENTS TO HIGHER CONTACT DAY ENVIRONMENTS ON PATIENTS’ OWN CONTACT DAYS AND OTHER OUTCOMES SUCH AS CHRONIC CONDITION CARE QUALITY AND RECEIPT OF POTENTIALLY INAPPROPRIATE MEDICATIONS. THIS PROJECT ADDRESSES THE NIA GOAL TO IDENTIFY INSTITUTIONAL MECHANISMS THAT AFFECT THE HEALTH OF OLDER ADULTS TO INFORM ORGANIZATIONAL INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE THEIR HEALTH. RESULTS WILL ALLOW RESEARCHERS, SYSTEM LEADERS, AND POLICYMAKERS TO CONTEXTUALIZE CONTACT DAYS THROUGH KEY STAKEHOLDER PERSPECTIVES, REPLICATE THE MEASURE ACROSS POPULATIONS AND SETTINGS, AND ULTIMATELY, TAKE PRACTICAL STEPS TO IMPROVE ON CONTACT DAYS, E.G., THROUGH REDUCING UNNEEDED CARE, COORDINATING CARE, AND SHIFTING CARE TO THE HOME.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPACT OF HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE AND TELEMEDICINE USE ON DEMENTIA CARE AMONG MEDICARE ENROLLEES WITH ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS - PROJECT SUMMARY HOME-BASED MEDICAL CARE (HBMC) -  HOUSE CALLS  BY PHYSICIANS AND ADVANCED CARE PROVIDERS - IS ESSENTIAL FOR THE GROWING POPULATION OF COMMUNITY-LIVING PERSONS LIVING WITH ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD). PERSONS WITH ADRD LIVE WITH MULTIPLE CHRONIC CONDITIONS (MCCS), WHICH NECESSITATE COMPLEX CARE REGIMENS, BUT AS FUNCTIONAL IMPAIRMENT WORSENS, THEY MAY STRUGGLE TO ACCESS OFFICE-BASED MEDICAL CARE. HBMC HELPS ALLEVIATE THIS STRUGGLE BY ENABLING CONTINUITY OF PATIENT CARE, TAILORING MEDICAL MANAGEMENT TO EVOLVING PATIENT NEEDS, AND MITIGATING THE CAREGIVING BURDEN FOR PERSONS LIVING WITH ADRD (PLWD). HOWEVER, HBMC IS LIMITED, LARGELY DUE TO LIMITED AVAILABILITY. THE RAPID EXPANSION OF TELEMEDICINE USE SINCE 2020 PROVIDES ANOTHER ALTERNATIVE TO OFFICE-BASED MEDICAL CARE. OUR STUDY AIMS TO EXAMINE HBMC AND TELEMEDICINE USE AMONG PLWD IN TRADITIONAL MEDICARE (TM) AND MEDICARE ADVANTAGE (MA) AND THEIR IMPACT ON PATIENT OUTCOMES. AMONG PLWD, WHILE THE CONCEPTUAL RATIONALE FOR IMPROVED MANAGEMENT AND OUTCOMES FROM HBMC RELATIVE TO OFFICE-BASED MEDICAL CARE IS COMPELLING, THE EVIDENCE IS SCANT. MOST STUDIES OF THE IMPACT OF HBMC ON OLDER ADULTS FOCUS ON THOSE WITH MCCS AND PRESENT A MIXED PICTURE, WITH SOME STUDIES FINDING A SIGNIFICANT REDUCTION IN ACUTE COMPLICATIONS. THE RAPID EXPANSION OF TELEMEDICINE SINCE EARLY 2020 HAS NOT ONLY INTRODUCED ANOTHER ALTERNATIVE TO OFFICE-BASED MEDICAL CARE BUT MAY HAVE INDIRECTLY AFFECTED HBMC USE. PRIOR STUDIES WERE LARGELY LIMITED TO TM ENROLLEES. OVER THE RECENT DECADE, THE PROPORTION OF MEDICARE ENROLLEES IN MA HAS GROWN RAPIDLY, FROM 25% IN 2010 TO 54% IN 2024. EVIDENCE OF HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION IN MA IS NASCENT, WITH VIRTUALLY NO PRIOR WORK ON HBMC OR TELEMEDICINE USE AMONG PLWD. FURTHER, WE WILL EXAMINE USE AND IMPACT OF THESE SERVICES AMONG SUBPOPULATIONS BY SEX, CO-EXISTING SERIOUS ILLNESS, AND HIGH-NEED, AS THEIR NEED FOR THESE SERVICES MAY DIFFER SYSTEMATICALLY. TO FILL THE SIGNIFICANT EVIDENCE GAPS, WE PROPOSE TO USE MEDICARE ADMINISTRATIVE DATA (2017-2026) FOR TM AND MA ENROLLEES WITH ADRD. WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE NATIONAL TRENDS IN HBMC AND TELEMEDICINE - ALONGSIDE OFFICE-BASED CARE - AND RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE THEIR POTENTIAL IMPACT ON THE PATIENT OUTCOMES FOR COMMUNITY LIVING PLWD. OUR MAIN OUTCOMES WILL BE DAYS SPENT AT HOME, POTENTIALLY PREVENTABLE ACUTE COMPLICATIONS (E.G., FALLS AND TRAUMA), MEDICATION DEPRESCRIBING, TIME TO TRANSITION TO LONG-TERM CARE, AND MEDICARE SPENDING. AS SECONDARY OUTCOMES, WE WILL EXAMINE OVERALL HEALTHCARE CONTACT DAYS, CONTINUITY OF CARE, TREATMENT FOR ADRD, AND DEATH. USING QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL CAUSAL INFERENCE MODELS, WE WILL ESTIMATE THE POTENTIAL IMPACT OF HBMC AND TELEMEDICINE ON OUTCOMES FOR TM AND MA ENROLLEES SEPARATELY. WE WILL ESTIMATE THE IMPACT ACROSS SUBGROUPS BY SEX, CO-EXISTING SERIOUS ILLNESS, AND HIGH NEED. OUR FINDINGS AIM TO DEVELOP RIGOROUS AND GENERALIZABLE EVIDENCE ON THE POTENTIAL BENEFITS OF HBMC AND TELEMEDICINE USE FOR DEMENTIA OUTCOMES, PARTICULARLY THOSE WITH SERIOUS ILLNESS AND HIGH-NEED.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: COGNITION AFTER ARMED CONFLICT: CREATION OF A HARMONIZED COGNITIVE ASSESSMENT PROTOCOL (HCAP) AND EXAMINATION OF ADRD RISKS RELATED TO OLDER ADULT ADRD RISKS RELATED TO EARLY LIFE WAR EXPOSURE - PROJECT SUMMARY: CURRENT COHORTS OF OLDER ADULTS, ESPECIALLY MILITARY VETERANS IN THE U.S. AND WORLDWIDE, WERE WIDELY AND DIFFERENTIALLY EXPOSED TO THE VIOLENCE, TRAUMA, AND SUBSEQUENT MENTAL HEALTH PROBLEMS OF TWENTIETH-CENTURY WARS. THESE OLDER ADULTS, EXPOSED TO NUMEROUS, OFTEN SEVERE, WAR-RELATED STRESSORS AT VARIOUS SENSITIVE STAGES IN EARLY LIFE, MAY EXPERIENCE HEIGHTENED RISK OF LATER LIFE COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA. SUCH RAMIFICATIONS NOT ONLY IMPACT DIRECTLY-EXPOSED INDIVIDUALS BUT ALSO PLACE SIGNIFICANT BURDENS UPON FAMILY CAREGIVERS AND HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS. SIGNIFICANT STRIDES IN UNDERSTANDING THE IMPACT OF ADRD HAVE BEEN MADE THROUGH THE HARMONIZED COGNITIVE ASSESSMENT PROTOCOL (HCAP) NETWORK, WHICH HAS GENERATED FLEXIBLE BUT COMPARABLE INSTRUMENTS FOR ASSESSING OLDER ADULTS’ COGNITIVE FUNCTION, ILLUMINATING COMMON AND DIVERGENT ADRD RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS AROUND THE WORLD. THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL ADVANCE UNDERSTANDING OF ADRD RISK AND RESILIENCE RELATED TO EARLY LIFE WAR EXPOSURES BY DESIGNING AND IMPLEMENTING A NEW HCAP IN A COHORT OF OLDER ADULTS AND THEIR MIDDLE-AGED CHILDREN WITHIN AN ONGOING STUDY THAT HAS COLLECTED RARE AND HIGHLY DETAILED DATA ON EARLY LIFE WAR EXPOSURE - THE VIETNAM HEALTH AND AGING STUDY (VHAS). AIM 1 IMPLEMENTS A THIRD ROUND OF DATA COLLECTION WITH ORIGINAL VHAS PARTICIPANTS (N≈1500) AND BASELINE DATA COLLECTION WITH PARTICIPANTS’ SPOUSES (N≈1100) AND TWO RANDOMLY CHOSEN CHILDREN NOW IN MIDLIFE (N≈2500) TO SUPPORT LONGITUDINAL AND LIFE COURSE INVESTIGATION OF WAR-RELATED ADVERSITIES AND ADRD RISK. THIS AIM INCLUDES IN-DEPTH INTERVIEWS ON HEALTH, SOCIAL RELATIONAL, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL CHARACTERISTICS; THE MAP OF LIFE COURSE EVENTS TO ASSESS EARLY-LIFE WAR EXPOSURE TIMING; AND BIOMARKERS OF CARDIOMETABOLIC DISORDER (CMD). AIM 2 DEVELOPS AND IMPLEMENTS A PROTOCOL TO IDENTIFY MILD COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT (MCI) AND DEMENTIA, SPECIFICALLY BY: DESIGNING, PILOTING, AND ADMINISTERING AN HCAP IN THE VHAS SAMPLE; IMPLEMENTING CLINICAL DEMENTIA RATING (CDR) INTERVIEWS AND CONSENSUS DIAGNOSES OF MCI/DEMENTIA IN A RANDOMLY-SELECTED GROUP OF PARTICIPANTS WITH LOW HCAP SCORES (N≈200) AND RANDOMLY-SELECTED CONTROLS (N≈100) FOR HCAP VALIDATION AND DIAGNOSTIC ALGORITHMS; AND ASSAYING PLASMA-BASED BIOMARKERS WITH HIGH DISCRIMINATIVE ACCURACY FOR DETECTING AD PATHOLOGY (AΒ42/40, P-TAU217, GFAP, & NFL) IN A SUBSET OF PARTICIPANTS (N=500) STRATIFIED BY DEGREES OF WAR-RELATED ADVERSITY. AIM 3 ESTIMATES ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN EARLY-LIFE WAR STRESSORS, MEDIATING ADRD RISK FACTORS (E.G., CMD, PTSD), AND HCAP-BASED MEASURES OF MCI/DEMENTIA IN MID-LATE ADULTHOOD. THE PARENT-OFFSPRING AND SIBLING RELATIONAL DATA GENERATED WILL SUPPORT FUTURE ANALYSES OF GENETIC, EPIGENETIC, AND FAMILY ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS INFLUENCING ADRD. IN ADDITION TO ENRICHING THE NIH-SUPPORTED HCAP NETWORK, THIS STUDY FURTHER INFORMS U.S. HEALTH BY EXPANDING KNOWLEDGE ON THE SOCIAL AND BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH EARLY LIFE WARRELATED STRESSORS CONTRIBUTE TO ADRD RISK AND RESILIENCE. SUCH FINDINGS WILL SHED LIGHT ON APPROACHES TO ADRD PREVENTION WITHIN WAR-AFFECTED POPULATIONS, IN PARTICULAR MILITARY VETERANS AND FAMILIES AFFECTED BY WAR.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MENOPAUSE TRANSITION AND CORONARY MICROVASCULAR DISEASE - PROGRAM SUMMARY/ABSTRACT HORMONAL IMBALANCE DURING THE MENOPAUSE TRANSITION SIGNIFICANTLY INCREASES THE RISK OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, INCLUDING CARDIAC ISCHEMIA AND STROKE. RECENT STUDIES HIGHLIGHT THE IMPORTANCE OF CORONARY MICROVASCULAR DISEASE (CMD, ONE TYPE OF NON-OBSTRUCTIVE CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE) IN WOMEN WITH MENOPAUSE. OBSTRUCTIVE CORONARY ARTERY DISEASE (CAD) AND CMD BOTH REDUCE CORONARY BLOOD FLOW AND MAKE THE HEART PRONE TO CARDIAC ISCHEMIA; THE MECHANISMS ARE, HOWEVER, DIFFERENT. OBSTRUCTIVE CAD IS PRIMARILY CAUSED BY LIPID PLAQUE FORMATION IN CORONARY ARTERIES (CAS), WHEREAS THE MECHANISMS RESPONSIBLE FOR CMD ARE ATTENUATED VASODILATATION AND VASCULAR REMODELING IN SMALL CAS AND MICROVASCULAR RAREFACTION. UP TO NOW, THERE HAS BEEN NO TREATMENT SPECIFIC TO CMD, AND PATIENTS WITH CMD ARE COMMONLY TREATED WITH MEDICATIONS FOR OBSTRUCTIVE CAD, RESULTING IN UNSATISFACTORY EFFECTIVENESS. THE GOAL OF THIS STUDY IS TO ELUCIDATE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF MENOPAUSE- INDUCED CMD AND ULTIMATELY DEVELOP NOVEL THERAPIES FOR CMD IN WOMEN WITH MENOPAUSE. TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECT OF MENOPAUSE TRANSITION ON CORONARY MICROVASCULAR FUNCTION, WE UTILIZE THE INDUCIBLE MENOPAUSE MOUSE MODEL GENERATED BY VCD INJECTION, TOGETHER WITH OVARIECTOMIZED MICE. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT I) CORONARY MICROVASCULAR FUNCTION (ASSESSED BY CORONARY FLOW VELOCITY RESERVE [CFVR]) IS SIGNIFICANTLY DECREASED IN PERIMENOPAUSAL AND POSTMENOPAUSAL MICE COMPARED TO THE CONTROL, II) OUR RNA SEQUENCING DATA REVEALED THAT MANY GENES RELATED TO ENDOTHELIUM-DEPENDENT RELAXATION (EDR) ARE DOWNREGULATED, INCLUDING TRPV4 AND SOD2, IN CARDIAC ENDOTHELIAL CELLS (CECS) FROM PERIMENOPAUSAL MICE, III) EDR AND ENDOTHELIUM-DEPENDENT HYPERPOLARIZATION (EDH)-MEDIATED RELAXATION IN CAS ARE SIGNIFICANTLY ATTENUATED IN PERIMENOPAUSAL MICE, IV) CHRONIC ADMINISTRATION OF TRPV4 AGONIST IMPROVES CFVR IN PERIMENOPAUSAL MICE, AND V) FOLLICLE-STIMULATING HORMONE (FSH) ATTENUATES EDR AND TRPV4 AGONIST-MEDIATED RELAXATION IN CAS. DURING THE MENOPAUSE TRANSITION, ESTRADIOL AND PROGESTERONE LEVELS BEGIN TO DECLINE, WHILE FSH AND LUTEINIZING HORMONE LEVELS INCREASE. IN THIS PROJECT, WE INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF FSH IN REGULATING ENDOTHELIAL AND CORONARY MICROVASCULAR FUNCTION DURING MENOPAUSE TRANSITION. TRPV4 IS A NON-SELECTIVE CATION CHANNEL THAT REGULATES VASCULAR TONE VIA EDH-MEDIATED RELAXATION, AND DOWNREGULATION OF ENDOTHELIAL TRPV4 IS IMPLICATED IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF SEVERAL TYPES OF HYPERTENSION. INCREASED MITOCHONDRIAL ROS DUE TO REDUCED SOD2 ACTIVITY IS A HALLMARK OF MANY CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES. BASED ON OUR PRELIMINARY DATA, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT MENOPAUSE LEADS TO CMD VIA FSH-MEDIATED DOWNREGULATION OF TRPV4/SOD2 SIGNALING IN CECS, AND THAT THE FSH/TRPV4/SOD2 AXIS IS A VALID TARGET FOR PREVENTING CMD IN WOMEN UNDERGOING THE MENOPAUSE TRANSITION. THREE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE PROPOSED IN THIS STUDY TO TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS: 1) TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECT OF MENOPAUSE TRANSITION ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF CMD, 2) TO DEFINE THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF CORONARY ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION DURING THE MENOPAUSE TRANSITION, AND 3) TO EXAMINE WHETHER AND HOW FSH CONTRIBUTES TO THE DEVELOPMENT AND/OR PROGRESSION OF CMD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: RESISTANCE EXERCISE TRAINING FOR OLDER ADULTS WITH OBESITY USING GLP- RECEPTOR AGONISTS - PROJECT ABSTRACT THE RAPID ADOPTION AND DIFFUSION OF GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 (GLP-1) RECEPTOR AGONISTS IS TRANSFORMING OBESITY TREATMENT IN THE UNITED STATES. MEDICATIONS IN THIS DRUG CLASS, INITIALLY APPROVED FOR THE TREATMENT OF TYPE 2 DIABETES, HAVE PROVEN TO BE HIGHLY EFFECTIVE AT PROMOTING SUBSTANTIAL WEIGHT LOSS (>15% INITIAL BODY WEIGHT) AMONG ADULTS WITH OBESITY. DESPITE THESE BENEFITS, GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS MAY POSE UNIQUE RISKS FOR OLDER ADULTS DUE TO THE LOSS OF MUSCLE MASS THAT OCCURS WITH SUBSTANTIAL AND RAPID WEIGHT REDUCTION. TO DATE, THERE IS LIMITED INFORMATION ON THE EFFECTS OF THESE MEDICATIONS IN OLDER ADULTS WITH OBESITY AND INTERVENTIONS TO THWART THEIR IMPACT ON MUSCLE. HOWEVER, PRESERVING MUSCLE MASS IN OLDER ADULTS IS CRITICAL BECAUSE LOSS OF MUSCLE IN THIS POPULATION INCREASES THE RISK OF CLINICAL DECOMPENSATION, STRENGTH AND POWER LOSS, DISABILITY, MOBILITY IMPAIRMENT, AND INJURIOUS FALLS—ALL OF WHICH LOWER PHYSICAL FUNCTION AND QUALITY OF LIFE. MUSCLE-SPARING BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS, SUCH AS A PROGRESSIVE INTENSITY RESISTANCE EXERCISE, HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO MITIGATE SKELETAL MUSCLE LOSS AMONG OLDER ADULTS USING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS. WE POSIT THAT PROGRESSIVE, MODERATE TO HIGH-INTENSITY RESISTANCE TRAINING WILL MITIGATE MUSCLE LOSS AND STRENGTH IN OLDER ADULTS WITH OBESITY INITIATING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONIST THERAPY. AS A RESULT, WE ALSO POSIT THAT A MODERATE TO HIGH-INTENSITY RESISTANCE TRAINING PROGRAM WILL IMPROVE MEASURES OF PHYSICAL FUNCTION AND QUALITY OF LIFE TO A GREATER EXTENT THAN CONVENTIONAL CARE ALONE, WHICH WE DEFINE AS HEALTH EDUCATION WORKSHOPS. IN ADDITION, A MODERATE TO HIGH-INTENSITY RESISTANCE TRAINING PROGRAM MAY REDUCE REBOUND WEIGHT GAIN COMMONLY EXPERIENCED AFTER DISCONTINUATION OF GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS, A CLINICAL EVENT THAT AFFECTS MANY PATIENTS AND CONTRIBUTES TO POOR COST-EFFECTIVENESS. TO ASSESS THESE HYPOTHESES, WE PROPOSE TO ENROLL 198 SOCIOECONOMICALLY DIVERSE OLDER ADULTS (≥60 YEARS-OLD) WITH OBESITY WHO ARE INITIATING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONIST THERAPY FOR WEIGHT LOSS. WITHIN 3 WEEKS OF THEIR THERAPY, WE WILL RANDOMLY ASSIGN OLDER ADULTS TO EITHER A SUPERVISED, CENTER-BASED MODERATE-TO-HIGH INTENSITY RESISTANCE TRAINING PROGRAM (RT, 3 DAYS PER WEEK) OR TO AN ENHANCED USUAL CARE GROUP WHO, IN ADDITION TO FOLLOWING PHYSICIAN RECOMMENDATIONS, WILL PARTICIPATE IN WEEKLY HEALTH EDUCATION AS AN “ACTIVE CONTROL” GROUP. THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE CHANGE IN MUSCLE MASS, MEASURED USING DEUTERATED CREATINE (D3CR) DILUTION. OUR AIMS/HYPOTHESES ARE AIM/HYPOTHESIS 1: COMPARED TO EUC, RT WILL ATTENUATE THE LOSS IN MUSCLE MASS AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH OBESITY USING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS; AIM/HYPOTHESIS 2: COMPARED TO EUC, RT WILL IMPROVE OBJECTIVE MEASURES OF PHYSICAL FUNCTION AND STRENGTH AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH OBESITY USING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS; AIM/HYPOTHESIS 3: COMPARED TO EUC, RT WILL IMPROVE SELF-ASSESSED QUALITY OF LIFE AND PHYSICAL FUNCTION AMONG OLDER ADULTS USING GLP-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISMS OF SKELETAL MUSCLE MAINTENANCE RELEVANT TO AD/ADRD - PROJECT SUMMARY A DECLINE OF MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION IS ASSOCIATED WITH AGING AND AGE-RELATED DISORDERS, FROM AGE-RELATED MUSCLE DISEASES SUCH AS SARCOPENIA AND INCLUSION BODY MYOSITIS (IBM) TO ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE (AD) AND AD RELATED DEMENTIA (ADRD). MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION FEATURES PROMINENTLY AMONG THE FUNDAMENTAL HALLMARKS OF AGING, BUT THE PRIMARY MITOCHONDRIAL PROCESSES CONTRIBUTING TO AGING AND AGE-RELATED DISEASES REMAIN POORLY DE?NED. MITOCHONDRIA ARE INTIMATELY INVOLVED IN NAD+/NADH METABOLISM. THE CENTRAL ROLES OF NAD+ AND NADH IN THE TRICARBOXYLIC ACID (TCA) CYCLE AND ELECTRON TRANSPORT CHAIN (ETC) UNDERSCORE THE IMPORTANCE OF BALANCED NAD+/NADH METABOLISM TO CELLULAR HEALTH. NAD+ LEVEL IS KNOWN TO DECLINE WITH AGE AND BOOSTING THE NAD(H) POOL WITH PRECURSORS PROVES TO BE BENE?CIAL IN AGING AND AGE-RELATED DISEASE SETTINGS. HOWEVER, THE CAUSES OF NAD+ DEPLETION DURING AGING ARE NOT WELL DE?NED AND THE LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCE OF BOOSTING THE NAD(H) POOL ON HUMAN HEALTH REMAINS UNCERTAIN. WE HAVE FOUND THAT REVERSE ELECTRON TRANSPORT (RET) ALONG MITOCHONDRIAL COMPLEX I IS A MAJOR MECHANISM OF NAD+ DECLINE ASSOCIATED WITH AGING. DURING NORMAL OXIDATIVE PHOSPHORYLATION, NADH IS OXIDIZED TO NAD+ AT COMPLEX I AND ELECTRONS ARE TRANSFERRED FROM NADH TO UBIQUINONE. UNDER CERTAIN THERMODYNAMIC CONDITIONS, FOR EXAMPLE WHEN FORWARD ELECTRON TRANSPORT (FET) IS BLOCKED WHILE MEMBRANE POTENTIAL IS STILL HIGH, OR WHEN COQH2 LEVEL IS HIGH, RET WILL PREVAIL. RET MOVES ELECTRONS FROM COQH2 BACK TO THE NAD+/NADH BINDING SITE OF COMPLEX I, CONVERTING NAD+ TO NADH AND THUS LOWERING THE NAD+/NADH RATIO WITHOUT CHANGING THE TOTAL NAD(H) POOL, AND GENERATING EXCESS ROS (RET-ROS) IN THE PROCESS. RET HAS BEEN WIDELY CONSIDERED A MAJOR SOURCE OF ROS, AND OUR STUDIES INDICATE THAT IT IS ALSO A MAIN DETERMINANT OF CELLULAR NAD+/NADH RATIO. IN RECENT STUDIES, WE SHOWED THAT RET IS ACTIVATED DURING MUSCLE AND ORGANISMAL AGING IN ANIMAL MODELS. INHIBITION OF RET INCREASES NAD+/NADH RATIO AND IT EXTENDS THE LIFESPAN AND PROMOTES HEALTHSPAN OF NORMAL ANIMALS THROUGH NAD+ REGULATED SIGNALING PATHWAYS. SUPPORTING ITS CLINICAL RELEVANCE, RET WAS FOUND ELEVATED IN NORMALLY AGED SKELETAL MUSCLE AND DISEASED MUSCLE IN HUMANS, AND OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES SUGGEST THAT IT ALSO CONTRIBUTES TO AGING-ASSOCIATED SARCOPENIC PROGRAM. HOW RET IS DEREGULATED IN MUSCLE AGING IS A MAJOR UNANSWERED QUESTION. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES HAVE IDENTI?ED A NEW PROTEIN THAT REGULATES MUSCLE HEALTH AND ORGANISMAL AGING, IS REQUIRED FOR THE BENE?CIAL EFFECT OF RET INHIBITION, AND IS DOWNREGULATED DURING MUSCLE AGING AND IN AGE-RELATED MUSCLE DISEASES IN ANIMAL MODELS AND HUMANS. THIS UNCOVERS FOR THE ?RST TIME A NON-ETC PROTEIN THAT MEDIATES THE EFFECT OF RET ON MUSCLE HEALTH AND LIFESPAN. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THIS NEWLY IDENTI?ED PROTEIN ACTS IN AN UNCONVENTIONAL MANNER TO DIRECTLY INTERACT WITH THE RET MACHINERY INSIDE MITOCHONDRIA, AND THAT RET DEREGULATION IS A CONSERVED MECHANISM AND ACTIONABLE TARGET IN AGE-RELATED MUSCLE DISEASES. UNDERSTANDING THE REGULATION AND FUNCTION OF RET IN MUSCLE AGING AND DISEASE WILL HAVE SIGNI?CANT IMPACT ON OTHER AGE-RELATED DISEASES SUCH AS AD/ADRD, AS KEY AD/ADRD ASSOCIATED GENES WILL BE STUDIED IN THIS CONTEXT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE CHEMICAL LANGUAGE OF HUMAN GUT BACTERIA IN HEALTHY AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT WITH AGE, THE GUT MICROBIOME CHANGES IN COMPOSITION AND BECOMES LESS DIVERSE. RECENT STUDIES IN FISH AND MOUSE MODELS HAVE SHOWN THAT TRANSPLANTING FECAL BACTERIA FROM YOUNG DONORS IMPROVES THE LIFESPAN AND HEALTHSPAN OF OLDER RECIPIENTS. MOREOVER, DIETARY SUPPLEMENTATION WITH HUMAN INFANT-ASSOCIATED BIFIDOBACTERIA EXTENDS THE LIFESPAN OF C. ELEGANS AND MICE AND IMPROVES COGNITIVE FUNCTIONS IN MOUSE MODELS OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD). THEREFORE, THE GUT MICROBIOME REPRESENTS AN ATTRACTIVE THERAPEUTIC TARGET TO PROMOTE HEALTHY AGING. HOWEVER, WE DO NOT FULLY UNDERSTAND THE UNDERLYING MOLECULAR MECHANISMS BY WHICH IMPLICATED MICROBES SUCH AS BIFIDOBACTERIA MODULATE AGING PHYSIOLOGY. ONE KEY WAY THAT HUMAN GUT BACTERIA IMPACT HOST BIOLOGY IS THROUGH METABOLITE PRODUCTION. THESE MICROBIOME-DERIVED METABOLITES (MDMS) HAVE THE POTENTIAL TO INTERACT WITH THE INTESTINAL TISSUES AND INFLUENCE SYSTEMIC AGING AFTER ENTERING THE HOST CIRCULATION. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT BIFIDOBACTERIA PRODUCE A COLLECTION OF BENEFICIAL MDMS, WHICH IN TURN FUNCTIONALLY CONTRIBUTE TO AGING PHYSIOLOGY BY INTERACTING WITH CONSERVED HOST PATHWAYS. OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO USE A NOVEL EXPERIMENTAL STRATEGY TO IDENTIFY BIOACTIVE MDMS FROM BENEFICIAL GUT BACTERIA AND TO DETERMINE THEIR MECHANISMS OF ACTION ON HOST AGING. PURSUING THE BIOLOGY OF DIVERSE MDMS HAS BEEN A SCIENTIFIC CHALLENGE. THIS IS LARGELY DUE TO DIFFICULTIES IN IDENTIFYING THEIR BIOCHEMICAL STRUCTURES AND BACTERIAL BIOSYNTHETIC PATHWAYS, AS WELL AS THEIR FUNCTIONS AND MECHANISMS IN THE HOST. TO ADDRESS THESE KNOWLEDGE GAPS, WE HAVE DEVELOPED A HIGH-THROUGHPUT, MASS SPECTROMETRY-BASED PIPELINE TO CONSTRUCT STRAIN-SPECIFIC METABOLIC PROFILES OF HUMAN ANAEROBIC GUT BACTERIA. THIS HAS ENABLED THE PRELIMINARY IDENTIFICATION OF A PANEL OF PROMISING MDMS THAT ARE BOTH HIGHLY PRODUCED BY PRO-LONGEVITY BIFIDOBACTERIA GROWN IN BACTERIAL CULTURE AND DETECTED IN HUMAN BIOFLUIDS. TO TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS ON THEIR FUNCTIONAL ROLES IN AGING, WE WILL EXPLOIT A HUMAN GUT BACTERIA-C. ELEGANS AGING PLATFORM THAT WE HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED AND TRANSLATE THESE FINDINGS TO RELEVANT MAMMALIAN MODELS. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE THE ROLES OF BIFIDOBACTERIA MDMS IN LIFESPAN AND STRESS RESISTANCE IN GENETICALLY TRACTABLE IN VIVO MODELS. AIM 2 WILL IDENTIFY THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH BIFIDOBACTERIA MDMS CONFER NEUROPROTECTION IN C. ELEGANS AND HUMAN CELL MODELS OF NEUROPATHOGENESIS. THIS PROPOSED WORK IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE IT UNIQUELY LEVERAGES 1) A GUT MICROBE-FOCUSED, HIGH-RESOLUTION MASS SPECTROMETRY TO IDENTIFY LONGEVITY-ASSOCIATED MDMS IN VITRO AND IN VIVO, AND 2) TRACTABLE BACTERIAL AND HOST MODELS (C. ELEGANS, MICE, HUMAN CELLS) TO DISSECT CONSERVED INTRA-ORGANISMAL PATHWAYS UNDERLYING LIFESPAN, STRESS RESISTANCE, AND NEUROPROTECTION. IT IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT MOVES BEYOND ASSOCIATION TO MECHANISM, ADDRESSING A KEY KNOWLEDGE GAP IN HOW BENEFICIAL HUMAN GUT MICROBES CONTRIBUTE TO HOST AGING BIOLOGY AND IDENTIFYING NEW MOLECULAR TARGETS TO DELAY AGE-RELATED DECLINE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ABETA BETA-HAIRPIN PEPTIDES AND OLIGOMERS AS TREATMENTS FOR ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT. ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS CHARACTERIZED BY PROGRESSIVE SYNAPTIC AND NEURONAL LOSS DRIVEN IN PART BY THE AGGREGATION OF Β-AMYLOID (AΒ) INTO SOLUBLE OLIGOMERS AND FIBRILS. PASSIVE ADMINISTRATION OF ANTIBODIES TARGETING AΒ HAS EMERGED AS A LEADING DISEASE-MODIFYING APPROACH AIMED AT REDUCING PATHOGENIC AΒ ASSEMBLIES AND SLOWING COGNITIVE DECLINE. CLINICAL SUCCESS WITH ANTIBODIES SUCH AS LECANEMAB AND DONANEMAB DEMONSTRATES THAT AMYLOID REDUCTION CAN ALTER DISEASE TRAJECTORY BUT ALSO EXPOSES KEY CHALLENGES, INCLUDING MODEST COGNITIVE BENEFIT AND AMYLOID-RELATED IMAGING ABNORMALITIES (ARIA) ASSOCIATED WITH VASCULAR AΒ CLEARANCE. ACTIVE AΒ VACCINATION, WHICH ELICITS ENDOGENOUS ANTIBODY RESPONSES, OFFERS A COMPLEMENTARY AND PREVENTIVE APPROACH BUT HAS SHOWN INCONSISTENT EFFICACY IN HUMANS DESPITE PROMISING PRECLINICAL AND EARLY CLINICAL RESULTS. BOTH ACTIVE AND PASSIVE STRATEGIES HAVE PREDOMINANTLY TARGETED PROTOFIBRILLAR AND FIBRILLAR AΒ SPECIES, LEAVING EARLY, SOLUBLE ASSEMBLIES—THE CONFORMATIONS MOST STRONGLY ASSOCIATED WITH SYNAPTIC DYSFUNCTION AND NEUROINFLAMMATION—INSUFFICIENTLY EXPLORED.  THIS PROJECT DEVELOPS AND EVALUATES STRUCTURE-GUIDED ACTIVE AND PASSIVE AΒ IMMUNOTHERAPIES THAT TARGET CONFORMATIONAL EPITOPES WITHIN EARLY, NON-FIBRILLAR AΒ ASSEMBLIES. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT VACCINES AND MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES (MABS) DIRECTED AGAINST STRUCTURALLY DEFINED Β-HAIRPIN AND OLIGOMER-MIMETIC ANTIGENS CAN SAFELY ENGAGE EARLY AΒ CONFORMATIONS TO PREVENT OR REVERSE AD-LIKE PATHOLOGY WHILE MINIMIZING VASCULAR COMPLICATIONS SUCH AS ARIA. PRELIMINARY STUDIES SHOW THAT THE Β-HAIRPIN PEPTIDE 2AM-L AND THE COVALENTLY STABILIZED OLIGOMER MIMETIC 2AT-L REPRODUCE STRUCTURAL FEATURES OF EARLY AΒ ASSEMBLIES AND ELICIT ANTIBODIES THAT SELECTIVELY BIND DISEASE-RELEVANT AΒ PATHOLOGY. CORRESPONDING MABS, F20-5 AND F20-12, RECOGNIZE CONFORMATIONAL EPITOPES ON THESE ANTIGENS AND LABEL DISTINCT PATTERNS OF AΒ PATHOLOGY IN HUMAN AD BRAIN TISSUE.  AIM 1 EVALUATES THE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF 2AM-L AND 2AT-L PEPTIDE VACCINES IN MAD2 KNOCK- IN MICE, A MODEL EXPRESSING HUMAN APP, TAU, AND APOE Ε4. VACCINES DISPLAYING THESE ANTIGENS ON LUMAZINE SYNTHASE VIRUS-LIKE PARTICLES WILL BE TESTED UNDER PREVENTIVE AND DISEASE-MODIFYING REGIMENS AND BENCHMARKED AGAINST THE CLINICAL VACCINE CAD106. AIM 2 ASSESSES THE CORRESPONDING MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES F20-5 AND F20- 12 IN THE SAME MODEL AND USING IDENTICAL ENDPOINTS, BENCHMARKED AGAINST MAB158, THE MURINE PRECURSOR OF LECANEMAB. OUTCOMES FOR BOTH AIMS INCLUDE AΒ DEPOSITION, COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE, TAU PATHOLOGY, NEUROINFLAMMATION, SYNAPTIC INTEGRITY, AND ARIA-LIKE MICROHEMORRHAGE.  COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL DETERMINE WHETHER STRUCTURE-GUIDED AΒ IMMUNOTHERAPIES BASED ON 2AM-L, 2AT-L, F20-5, AND F20-12 CAN SAFELY AND EFFECTIVELY MODIFY AD PATHOLOGY. BY INTEGRATING STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY, IMMUNOLOGY, AND PRECLINICAL MODELING, THE RESEARCH ESTABLISHES A MECHANISTIC FRAMEWORK FOR DESIGNING NEXT- GENERATION AΒ IMMUNOTHERAPIES INTENDED TO TARGET EARLY, PATHOGENIC AΒ CONFORMATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH - OF THE COMMONWEALTH SYSTEM OF HIGHER EDUCATION

description: STATISTICAL METHODS FOR SPATIAL PROTEOGENOMICS DATA IN ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY  ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) IS A LEADING CAUSE OF DISABILITY AND MORTALITY AMONG OLDER ADULTS, YET ITS UNDERLY- ING MECHANISMS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. SPATIAL PROTEOGENOMICS (SPG) INTEGRATES SPATIALLY RESOLVED PROTEIN AND TRANSCRIPT INFORMATION TO PROVIDE UNPRECEDENTED INSIGHTS INTO CELLULAR ORGANIZATION AND INTERACTIONS. RECENT ADVANCEMENTS IN SPATIAL PROTEOMICS, NAMED METHOD OF THE YEAR 2024 BY NATURE METHODS, HIGHLIGHT THE NEED FOR ROBUST DATASETS, INNOVATIVE COMPUTATIONAL METHODS, AND ADVANCED SPATIAL ANALYSES TO FULLY LEVERAGE SPG’S POTENTIAL IN AD RESEARCH. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ADVANCE SPG DATA ANALYSIS BY ADDRESSING KEY GAPS IN IMAGE ANNOTATION, STATISTICAL METHODOLOGY, AND BIOLOGICAL INFERENCE. IN AIM 1, WE WILL FIRST GENERATE LARGE-SCALE, MANUALLY ANNOTATED BRAIN CELL IMAGES TO BENCHMARK SEGMENTATION METHODS. THESE HIGH-QUALITY ANNOTATIONS WILL PROVIDE ESSENTIAL TRAINING DATA FOR COMPUTATIONAL MODELS AND RIGOROUS VALIDATION OF SEGMENTATION METHODS. THEN WE WILL DEVELOP STATISTICAL METHODS FOR BRAIN CELL SEGMENTATION, INCLUDING A DEEP-LEARNING-BASED ALGORITHM ADAPTED FOR IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE IMAGES AND A STATISTICAL FRAMEWORK FOR DELINEATING CELL BOUNDARIES IN MULTIPLEXED SPATIAL PRO- TEOMICS DATA WITH CORRESPONDING SPOT-LEVEL SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS. THESE APPROACHES WILL IMPROVE SEGMENTATION AND CLASSIFICATION ACCURACY ACROSS DIVERSE CELL MORPHOLOGIES. AIM 2 WILL DEVELOP SPATIAL INFERENCE METHODS TO INVESTIGATE CELL-CELL CO-LOCALIZATION USING SPATIAL PROTEOMICS OR IMAGE-BASED SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS. AIM 3 WILL INFER SPATIAL GENE CO-EXPRESSION NETWORKS IN AD AND CONTROLS USING IMAGE-BASED SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS. BY AD- DRESSING CRITICAL GAPS IN SPG ANALYSIS, THIS RESEARCH WILL ADVANCE THE UNDERSTANDING OF AD AND UNCOVER POTENTIAL NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS. THE RESULTS, INCLUDING ANNOTATED DATASETS AND OPEN-SOURCE SOFTWARE, WILL BE SHARED PUBLICLY, FOSTERING COLLABORATION AND ACCELERATING PROGRESS IN THE FIELD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCE CARE PLANNING FOR OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME EXPERIENCING EARLY ONSET AND ACCELERATED DEMENTIA: A MECHANISTIC EVALUATION - PROJECT SUMMARY OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME ARE DISPROPORTIONALLY AFFECTED BY DEMENTIA. DOWN SYNDROME IS THE MOST COMMON GENETIC ETIOLOGY OF INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY AFFECTING >400,000 INDIVIDUALS NATIONALLY, AND ITS PREVALENCE IS HISTORICALLY INCREASING, WITH ~5,300 BABIES BORN ANNUALLY IN THE U.S. IN THE LAST 25 YEARS, THE AVERAGE LIFE EXPECTANCY FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME HAS MORE THAN DOUBLED FROM 25 TO 60 YEARS. THOUGH INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME ARE BORN WITH SERIOUS, LIFE-LIMITING ILLNESSES, THEY FACE THE ADDITIONAL HARDSHIP OF EARLY-ONSET AND ACCELERATED DEMENTIA, RESULTING IN THE #1 CONTRIBUTOR OF DEATH IN THIS POPULATION. DESPITE THE PRESSING NEED, NO STANDARDIZED METHODS EXIST TO PREPARE OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME AND THEIR CAREGIVERS FOR END-OF- LIFE CARE ANTICIPATED TO BE COMPLICATED BY EARLY-ONSET AND ACCELERATED DEMENTIA. CONVERSATIONS BETWEEN PATIENTS WITH SERIOUS ILLNESS AND THEIR CLINICIANS ABOUT VALUES, GOALS, AND PROGNOSIS (I.E., SERIOUS ILLNESS CONVERSATIONS, SICS) CAN LEAD TO WELL-INFORMED SHARED DECISION-MAKING AND IMPROVED QUALITY OF LIFE. THE SERIOUS ILLNESS CARE PROGRAM (SICP, A MULTI-MODAL INTERVENTION THAT INCLUDES A STRUCTURED CONVERSATION GUIDE AND CLINICIAN TRAINING, DESIGNED TO SUPPORT CLINICIANS TO HAVE EARLIER, PERSON-CENTERED SICS), HAS DEMONSTRATED SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENTS IN ACCESS TO AND TIMING OF SICS, POSITIVE PATIENT AND CLINICIAN EXPERIENCES, AND LOWER RATES OF ANXIETY AND DEPRESSION FOR PATIENTS IN VARIOUS SETTINGS. SICP IS DISSEMINATED WIDELY IN 87 COUNTRIES WITH >28,000 CLINICIANS REACHING >378,000 PATIENTS. HOWEVER, SICP IS NOT TAILORED TO OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME EXPERIENCING DEMENTIA. THIS VULNERABLE POPULATION FACES INTELLECTUAL, COMMUNICATION, BEHAVIORAL, AND COGNITIVE CHALLENGES THAT OFTEN RESULT IN MISTREATMENT DURING CLINICAL ENCOUNTERS, WHICH LEADS TO LOWER RATES OF TRUST, RESPECT, AND FAIRNESS BY CLINICIANS. AT THE SAME TIME, CLINICIANS EXPRESS CHALLENGES IN NOT KNOWING HOW TO ENGAGE WITH THESE PATIENTS AND FOCUS ON CAREGIVERS FOR CONVERSATIONS, RESULTING IN SUBOPTIMAL CARE. THUS, OUR OBJECTIVE IS TO TAILOR SICP FOR OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME AND THEIR CAREGIVERS AND DETERMINE THE MECHANISM OF THE REFINED SICP (I.E., SICPDOWN) TO LEAD TO PATIENT-CENTERED CARE IN A SINGLE CENTER, MECHANISTIC RANDOMIZED TRIAL OF 100 OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT SICPDOWN WILL LEAD TO SIMILAR IMPROVEMENT IN PATIENT-CENTERED OUTCOMES. WE WILL REFINE SICP TO MEET THE NEEDS OF OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME (AIM 1) AND CLINICIANS IN VARIOUS CARE SETTINGS (AIM 2), THEN DETERMINE THE MECHANISM OF SICP ON PATIENT-CENTERED ADVANCE CARE PLANNING (AIM 3). THE PRIMARY OUTCOME WILL BE MECHANISTIC: ANXIETY, PROGNOSTIC UNDERSTANDING, AND FEELING HEARD AND UNDERSTOOD ABOUT VALUES AND GOALS. OUR STUDY RESULTS WILL DEEPEN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW SICS, TAILORED TO OLDER INDIVIDUALS WITH DOWN SYNDROME, LEAD TO PATIENT- CENTERED CARE AND SERVE AS A RICH RESOURCE TO DEVELOP EVIDENCE-BASED STRATEGIES TO TAILOR SICS FOR OTHER 2.3 MILLION AGING ADULTS WITH INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY, MEETING PRIORITIES OF THE NIH INCLUDE PROJECT AND ITS NIA GOALS, AND THE NATIONAL ALZHEIMER’S PROJECT ACT (PUBLIC LAW 111-375).

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PROTEOMIC INTERROGATION OF N-TERMINAL ACETYLATION ON MISFOLDED PROTEINS IN EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES, SUCH AS ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD), CLOSELY RELATE TO THE AGGREGATION OF INTRINSICALLY DISORDERED PROTEINS (IDPS), PATHOGENIC POST-TRANSLATIONAL MODIFICATIONS (PTMS), AND IMPAIRED CLEARANCE MECHANISMS. HERE IN THIS R01 APPLICATION, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP INNOVATIVE MASS SPECTROMETRY- BASED STRATEGIES TO EXAMINE PTMS RELATED TO IDP AGGREGATION AND EXTRACELLULAR VESICLE (EV)-MEDIATED PROPAGATION. OUR HYPOTHESIS POSITS THAT SPECIFIC COVALENT MODIFICATIONS AND CELLULAR STRESS CONDITIONS FACILITATE IDP MISFOLDING AND ABNORMAL PTMS, CONTRIBUTING TO THEIR AGGREGATION AND PROPAGATION IN DISEASE STATES. WE WILL FOCUS ON N-TERMINAL ACETYLATION (NT-ACETYLATION), ONE OF THE MOST ABUNDANT, WHILE UNDERSTUDIED AND UNDERAPPRECIATED, PROTEIN MODIFICATIONS IN EUKARYOTES, WHICH INFLUENCE PROTEIN STABILITY, LOCALIZATION, AND INTERACTIONS. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES INDICATE THAT QUANTIFYING BOTH CANONICAL NT-ACETYLATION AND NEO NT- ACETYLATION STOICHIOMETRY MAY SERVE AS INDICATORS FOR DISEASE ONSET AND PROGRESSION, PARTICULARLY IN AD PATIENTS EXPERIENCING INCREASED PROTEIN MISFOLDING AND AGGREGATION. TO CORRELATE ALTERATIONS IN THE EV PROTEOME WITH AD PROGRESSION, WE WILL PROFILE BOTH CANONICAL AND NEO NT-ACETYLATION IN NEURON CELLS AND CIRCULATING EVS, REVEALING SIGNIFICANT LINKS TO AD. WE PROPOSE ESTABLISHING A NOVEL PROTEOMICS PLATFORM TO PROFILE THE NT- ACETYLATION LANDSCAPE IN PRIMARY NEURON CELLS, IPSCS, BRAIN TISSUES FROM AD PATIENTS, AND THEIR SECRETED EVS. ACCORDINGLY, OUR INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM WILL PURSUE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) MEASUREMENT OF CANONICAL AND NEO TERMINAL ACETYLATION STOICHIOMETRY OF MISFOLDED PROTEINS IN CELLS AND EVS; 2) INVESTIGATE HOW IMPAIRED AUTOPHAGY-LYSOSOMAL PATHWAY AFFECTS PROTEIN NT-ACETYLATION IN PRIMARY NEURON-SECRETED EVS; AND 3) CORRELATE NT-ACETYLATION STOICHIOMETRY OF MISFOLDED PROTEINS IN EVS WITH THE STAGES OF AD PROGRESSION. BY THE COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT, WE WILL ESTABLISH CORRELATIONS BETWEEN PROTEIN MISFOLDING, COVALENT MODIFICATIONS, AND EV- MEDIATED CLEARANCE, PROVIDING A NOVEL BIOMARKER PLATFORM FOR EARLY DETECTION, DISEASE MONITORING, AND POTENTIALLY GUIDING THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS IN NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ABERRANT NUCLEAR MATERIAL PROPERTIES IN AGING CELLS - THE NUCLEUS UNDERGOES DRAMATIC ORGANIZATIONAL CHANGES DURING SENESCENCE, INCLUDING CHROMATIN REDISTRIBUTION AND ALTERED LAMIN NETWORKS, BUT WHETHER THESE STRUCTURAL ALTERATIONS AFFECT THE PHYSICAL PROPERTIES OF THE NUCLEAR INTERIOR REMAINS UNKNOWN. THIS REPRESENTS A CRITICAL GAP BECAUSE TRANSCRIPTION AND SPLICING DEPEND ON LARGE MACROMOLECULAR COMPLEXES OPERATING AT THE MESOSCALE (10-200 NM), WHERE PHYSICAL PROPERTIES LIKE MOLECULAR CROWDING AND VISCOELASTICITY PROFOUNDLY INFLUENCE BIOCHEMICAL REACTIONS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS PROPOSAL IS THAT AGE-RELATED ALTERATIONS IN NUCLEAR PHYSICAL PROPERTIES DIRECTLY CONTRIBUTE TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND SPLICING DYSREGULATION CHARACTERISTIC OF CELLULAR AGING. UNTIL NOW, IT WAS EXTREMELY LABOR INTENSIVE TO CHARACTERIZE NUCLEAR PHYSICAL PROPERTIES. WE HAVE OVERCOME THIS BARRIER BY INNOVATION OF MULTIPLE TOOLS INCLUDING NUCLEAR GENETICALLY ENCODED MULTIMERIC NANOPARTICLES (GEMS), A TRANSFORMATIVE TECHNOLOGY ENABLING HIGH-THROUGHPUT CHARACTERIZATION OF NUCLEAR BIOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES FOR THE FIRST TIME. USING GEMS, WE DISCOVERED THAT NUCLEAR FLUIDITY INCREASES DRAMATICALLY DURING BOTH CDK4/6 INHIBITION AND REPLICATIVE SENESCENCE—CONTRARY TO PRIOR EXPECTATIONS OF CHROMATIN RIGIDIFICATION. REMARKABLY, INHIBITING H3K27 TRIMETHYLATION NOT ONLY SUPPRESSES THESE PHYSICAL CHANGES BUT INCREASES REPLICATIVE LIFESPAN AFTER CDK4/6 INHIBITOR TREATMENT, SUGGESTING THAT PHYSICAL CHANGES MAY BE THERAPEUTICALLY TARGETABLE. AIM 1 WILL COMPREHENSIVELY MEASURE NUCLEAR MATERIAL PROPERTIES ACROSS BIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT LENGTHSCALES USING OUR COMPLETE TOOLKIT: NUCGEMS (40-50 NM), NEWLY DEVELOPED LARGER GEMS (140 NM), SYNTHETIC PROTEIN CRYSTALS (200-500 NM), AND SYNDROP CONDENSATES (50 NM-3 ΜM). WE WILL PERFORM MICRORHEOLOGY TO QUANTIFY NUCLEAR FLUIDITY, VISCOSITY, AND DYNAMICS IN YOUNG VERSUS AGED CELLS ACROSS MULTIPLE SENESCENCE MODELS. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE MECHANISMS DRIVING BIOPHYSICAL CHANGES BY SYSTEMATICALLY PERTURBING HISTONE MODIFICATIONS, REMODELING FACTORS, NUCLEAR PERIPHERY COMPONENTS (LAMINS, LINC COMPLEX, NUCLEAR PORES), AND PROTEINS THAT HAVE BEEN REPORTED TO SUBSCALE OR SUPERSCALE WITH CELL SIZE PERTURBATIONS. WE WILL IDENTIFY PERTURBATIONS THAT EITHER RECAPITULATE SENESCENCE-ASSOCIATED NUCLEAR FLUIDITY IN YOUNG CELLS OR RESCUE NORMAL PHYSICAL PROPERTIES IN SENESCENT CELLS. AIM 3 WILL ESTABLISH CAUSAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN NUCLEAR PHYSICAL PROPERTIES AND GENE EXPRESSION BY INTEGRATING RNA-SEQ, SINGLE-MOLECULE TRACKING OF TRANSCRIPTIONAL MACHINERY, AND CHROMATIN CONFORMATION ANALYSIS. WE WILL EXPERIMENTALLY MANIPULATE NUCLEAR PHYSICAL PROPERTIES THROUGH OSMOTIC PERTURBATIONS, SYNTHETIC CONDENSATE EXPRESSION, AND TARGETED GENETIC INTERVENTIONS TO DETERMINE WHETHER PHYSICAL MANIPULATIONS CAN RESCUE SENESCENCE-RELATED TRANSCRIPTIONAL SIGNATURES. THIS WORK WILL ESTABLISH NUCLEAR BIOPHYSICS AS A FUNDAMENTAL AGING MECHANISM, PROVIDE A NEW CONCEPTUAL FRAMEWORK FOR MAINTAINING NUCLEAR FUNCTION DURING AGING, AND IDENTIFY NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS TO REVERSE CELLULAR SENESCENCE PHENOTYPES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENFORCED HIV-1 SILENCING AT THE TIME OF ART INITIATION TO CONTROL VIREMIA, RESERVOIR PERSISTENCE, AND VIRAL REBOUND - PROJECT SUMMARY ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART) SUPPRESSES HIV-1 REPLICATION TO UNDETECTABLE LEVELS. HOWEVER, INTERRUPTION OF ART ALMOST INEVITABLY RESULTS IN RESURGENCE OF VIRAL REPLICATION. THAT IS BECAUSE ART DOES NOT PREVENT THE ESTABLISH- MENT OF LONG-LIVED VIRAL RESERVOIRS THAT REKINDLE VIRAL REPLICATION AFTER TREATMENT INTERRUPTION. FURTHER, ART DOES NOT PREVENT SPONTANEOUS REVERSAL OF LATENCY AND RESIDUAL VIRAL EXPRESSION, WHICH CONTRIBUTE TO PERSISTENT INFLAM- MATION. THESE LIMITATIONS MAY BE COMPENSATED BY NEW INTERVENTIONS TARGETING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND MAINTE- NANCE OF LATENCY. THEIR IMPLEMENTATION AROUND THE TIME OF ART INITIATION/RESTART MAY ACCELERATE THE DECAY OF VIREMIA BEFORE ART, REDUCE VIRAL EXPRESSION DURING ART, AND BLOCK, DELAY, OR MITIGATE VIRAL REBOUND AFTER ART. THE AIM OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP A NEW INTERVENTION DELIVERED BEFORE INITIATION/RESTART OF ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART) THAT (1) SILENCES HIV-1 AND ACCELERATES DECAY OF VIREMIA; (2) REDUCES RESIDUAL HIV-1 EXPRESSION DURING ART; AND (3) BLOCKS OR DELAYS VIRAL REBOUND IMPROVING POST-TREATMENT CONTROL. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT THESE GOALS CAN BE ACHIEVED VIA ECTOPIC EXPRESSION OF AN HIV-1-ENCODED ANTISENSE TRANSCRIPT (AST), WHICH WE HAVE SHOWN TO SILENCE HIV-1 EXPRESSION VIA HETEROCHROMATIZATION OF THE HIV-1 5’ LONG TERMINAL REPEAT (LTR), PROMOTING THE ESTABLISHMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF VIRAL LATENCY. THE APPLICATION IS CENTERED AROUND THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. IN SPECIFIC AIM 1, WE PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE THE MOLEC- ULAR MECHANISMS THROUGH WHICH AST SILENCES HIV-1 TRANSCRIPTION. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT AST PROMOTES THE FORMATION OF BIOMOLECULAR CONDENSATES AT THE 5’ LTR. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL UTILIZE A CD4-SPECIFIC ENGINEERED LENTIVIRAL (ELV) AST DELIVERY PLATFORM TO TEST ITS EFFICACY USING IN-VITRO AND EX-VIVO CULTURE SYSTEMS, INCLUDING A NOVEL LYMPH NODE ON-A-CHIP ORGANOID MODEL. FINALLY, SPECIFIC AIM 3 WILL TEST THE EFFICACY OF THE NEW AST-BASED INTERVENTION IN A PRECLINICAL HUMANIZED MOUSE MODEL. WE WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER ECTOPIC EXPRESSION OF AST ACCELERATES THE DECLINE OF VIREMIA AT ART INITIATION, REDUCE VIRAL EXPRESSION DURING ART, AND INCREASE CONTROL OF VIRAL REPLICATION AFTER INTERRUPTION OF ART. THE INNOVATIVE ASPECTS OF THE PROPOSAL INCLUDE: (1) A NEW STRATEGY TO BLOCK RESIDUAL VIRAL EXPRESSION DURING ART AND TO ACHIEVE POST-TREATMENT CONTROL; (2) AN HIV-SPECIFIC BIOLOGICAL MOLECULE TO INDUCE VIRAL SILENCING VIA BIO- MOLECULAR CONSENSATES; (3) A CD4-SPECIFIC LENTIVIRAL DELIVERY PLATFORM; (4) A NOVEL LYMPH NODE ORGANOID SYSTEM; AND (5) THE TRIPLE KNOCKOUT HUMANIZED MOUSE MODEL THAT EXHIBITS SIGNIFICANTLY DELAYED GRAFT VERSUS HOST DISEASE. THESE STUDIES WILL BE LED BY A TEAM OF INVESTIGATORS WITH COMPLEMENTARY SETS OF EXPERTISE THAT WILL ENSURE THE SUCCESS OF THIS APPLICATION. DR. ROMERIO’S WORK HAS FOCUSED ON HIV-1 REGULATION BY AST; DR. CAI SPECIALIZES ON THE ROLE OF BIOMOLECULAR CONDENSATES IN CHROMATIN ORGANIZATION; DR. FERRARI HAS PIONEERED THE DEVELOPMENT OF ORGANOID MODELS; DR. SIMONETTI FOCUSES ON MONITORING VIRAL DYNAMICS AND RESERVOIR PERSISTENCE; AND DR. HEREDIA IS AN EXPERT OF HUMANIZED MOUSE MODELS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTEGRATED ROLE OF NASAL AIRWAY & GUT MICROBIOME DYNAMICS IN ALLERGIC RHINITIS - PROJECT ABSTRACT THE MAJOR CHALLENGES FOR DEVELOPING PRIMARY PREVENTION STRATEGIES FOR ALLERGIC RHINITIS (AR) ARE THE EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF MODIFIABLE RISK FACTORS (E.G., AIRWAY AND GUT MICROBIOME) AND THE HETEROGENEITY OF AR. OUR GROUP HAS APPLIED INTEGRATED OMICS (E.G., AIRWAY METAGENOME, HOST GENOME AND TRANSCRIPTOME) APPROACHES TO INFANCY DATA, AND IDENTIFIED ENDOTYPES AT HIGH RISK FOR AR AND ASTHMA. TO DATE, NO STUDY HAS EXAMINED THE DYNAMIC ROLE OF AIRWAY-GUT MICROBIOME IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF AR AND ITS PHENO/ENDOTYPES. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT AN INTERRELATION BETWEEN LONGITUDINAL CHANGES IN THE DUAL NASAL AIRWAY-GUT MICROBIOME (BOTH COMPOSITION AND FUNCTIONAL POTENTIAL) AND HOST AR GENETIC RISK CONTRIBUTES TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF AR. WE WILL LEVERAGE LONGITUDINAL SAMPLES AND COMPREHENSIVE CLINICAL AND OMICS DATA FROM OUR ONGOING NIH-FUNDED COHORTS. THE 43RD MULTICENTER AIRWAY RESEARCH COLLABORATION (MARC-43) STUDY (UH3 OD023253) IS AN ONGOING MULTICENTER COHORT STUDY OF 599 HEALTHY INFANTS. THE PROPOSED R01 PROJECT WOULD EXTEND THIS WELL-CHARACTERIZED COHORT BY LONGITUDINALLY SEQUENCING BOTH NASAL AIRWAY AND GUT METAGENOME, AND THEN EXAMINING THEIR RELATIONS TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF AR AND ITS PHENOTYPES BY AGE 7 YEARS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL IDENTIFY INTEGRATED LONGITUDINAL NASAL AIRWAY METAGENOME (AGES 0, 1, AND 2 YEARS) AND HOST GENOME SIGNATURES OF DEVELOPING AR (AND ITS PHENOTYPES). IN AIM 2, WE WILL IDENTIFY INTEGRATED LONGITUDINAL GUT METAGENOME (AGES 0, 1, AND 2 YEARS) AND HOST GENOME SIGNATURES OF DEVELOPING AR (AND ITS PHENOTYPES). IN AIM 3, WE WILL USE NOVEL MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES TO INTEGRATE THE DUAL NASAL-GUT METAGENOME DATA WITH AVAILABLE MULTI-OMICS DATA TO DETERMINE LONGITUDINAL ENDOTYPES RELATED TO AR RISK. WE WILL VALIDATE OUR FINDINGS IN CHILDREN FROM TWO ALREADY-HARMONIZED COHORTS UNDERGOING SIMILAR PROCEDURES AND TESTING AT SIMILAR AGES. THE LONGITUDINAL DUAL AIRWAY-GUT METAGENOME DATA GENERATED BY THIS R01 PROJECT—ALONG WITH PARALLEL, ALREADY AVAILABLE MULTI-LEVEL OMICS (E.G., GENOME, TRANSCRIPTOME) AND IMMUNOLOGICAL DATA—OFFER AN UNPRECEDENTED OPPORTUNITY TO DEVELOP DATA-DRIVEN MECHANISTIC MODELS FOR AR. RESULTS WILL INCLUDE THE FIRST DATA ON THE LONGITUDINAL AIRWAY-GUT METAGENOME IN AR DEVELOPMENT. THIS R01 PROJECT PROVIDES A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO ELUCIDATE THE MECHANISMS OF AR AND TO HIGHLIGHT MOLECULAR TARGETS FOR THE PREVENTION OF AR.

description: HIGH AVIDITY MULTIEPITOPE TARGETING OF RNA-INDUCED CELL SURFACE HIV ENV - PROJECT SUMMARY DESPITE THE SUCCESS OF ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART), HIV-1 PERSISTS IN LONG-LIVED CELLULAR RESERVOIRS THAT EVADE IMMUNE CLEARANCE. THESE LATENT PROVIRUSES REMAIN THE MAJOR BARRIER TO CURE, AS THEY RE- EMERGE WHEN ART IS WITHDRAWN. THE HIV-1 ENVELOPE GLYCOPROTEIN (ENV), EXPRESSED ON THE SURFACE OF INFECTED CELLS, PROVIDES A LOGICAL TARGET FOR IMMUNE CLEARANCE BUT IS IMMUNOLOGICALLY ELUSIVE. LATENT CELLS EXPRESS LITTLE TO NO ENV, AND ACTIVELY INFECTED CELLS DISPLAY ENV AT LOW DENSITY AND IN HETEROGENEOUS CONFORMATIONS, REDUCING SENSITIVITY TO ANTIBODY-MEDIATED RESPONSES. THIS PROPOSAL INTEGRATES TWO TRANSFORMATIVE TECHNOLOGIES—RNA-BASED LATENCY REVERSAL AND ENGINEERED HIGH-AVIDITY ANTIBODIES—TO OVERCOME THESE BARRIERS AND ADVANCE A RATIONAL “INDUCE-AND-CLEAR” THERAPEUTIC FRAMEWORK. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES SHOW THAT LIPID NANOPARTICLE (LNP) DELIVERY OF TAT MRNA AND CRISPRA MRNA CAN POTENTLY AND SYNERGISTICALLY REACTIVATE LATENT PROVIRUSES, IN SOME CASES EXCEEDING THE ACTIVITY OF STRONG MITOGEN STIMULATION WHILE AVOIDING BROAD T CELL ACTIVATION. FURTHER ENHANCEMENT IS ACHIEVED WITH DNA METHYLATION INHIBITORS SUCH AS 5-AZACYTIDINE OR WITH CAS9-TETHERED TET1, PROVIDING SITE- SPECIFIC EPIGENETIC REPROGRAMMING TO AWAKEN REFRACTORY PROVIRUSES. AT THE SAME TIME, OUR WORK DEMONSTRATES THAT ENV DISPLAYED ON INFECTED CELLS IS STRUCTURALLY DISTINCT FROM VIRION-ASSOCIATED ENV, OFTEN UNCLEAVED AND DYNAMICALLY SAMPLING CONFORMATIONS POORLY RECOGNIZED BY MANY BROADLY NEUTRALIZING ANTIBODIES (BNABS). THIS HETEROGENEITY UNDERLIES INCOMPLETE NEUTRALIZATION OF CELL-TO-CELL TRANSMISSION, EMPHASIZING THE NEED FOR NEW ANTIBODY DESIGNS. WE PROPOSE TO TEST A STRATEGY THAT MAXIMIZES ENV EXPRESSION AND OPTIMIZES ITS RECOGNITION BY ENGINEERED ANTIBODIES. IN AIM 1, WE WILL ENHANCE RESERVOIR CLEARANCE BY COMBINING TAT, CRISPRA, AND CAS9-TETHERED TET1 MRNAS IN TARGETED LNPS, DEFINING CONDITIONS THAT YIELD ROBUST ENV INDUCTION IN VITRO AND IN HUMANIZED MICE. IN AIM 2, WE WILL IDENTIFY MAXIMALLY SYNERGISTIC BNAB COMBINATIONS THAT ACHIEVE HIGH CELL-SURFACE BINDING AND POTENT FCΓRIIIA CROSSLINKING, ENGINEERING BISPECIFIC ANTIBODIES THAT RECRUIT NK CELLS FOR ANTIBODY-DEPENDENT CELLULAR CYTOTOXICITY (ADCC). IN AIM 3, WE WILL ADAPT THE ADAPTIVE MULTI-EPITOPE TARGETING WITH ENHANCED AVIDITY (AMETA) PLATFORM PIONEERED BY MPI YI SHI TO HIV ENV, CREATING MULTIVALENT IGM-SCAFFOLDED ANTIBODIES WITH ULTRAHIGH AVIDITY AND ENGINEERED FC DOMAINS THAT DRIVE NK CELL RECRUITMENT AND CLEARANCE OF ENV-EXPRESSING CELLS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INDUCTION OF ACQUIRED FETAL TOLERANCE THROUGH AN EPO-DEPENDENT PATHWAY - PROJECT SUMMARY  ACQUIRED TOLERANCE PLAYS A CENTRAL ROLE ACROSS A BROAD SPECTRUM OF HUMAN BIOLOGY SPANNING ORGAN TRANSPLANTATION AND PREGNANCY. THE WORK PROPOSED HERE DRAWS INSPIRATION FROM OUR WORK EXAMINING EPOR SIGNALING IN CONVENTIONAL TYPE 1 DENDRITIC CELLS (CDC1S) IN SOLID ORGAN TRANSPLANTATION TO UNDERSTAND HOW T-CELL MEDIATED TOLERANCE IS INITIATED AND MAINTAINED IN HUMAN PREGNANCY. TISSUE HYPOXIA AT THE MATERNAL-FETAL INTERFACE IS A KEY REGULATOR OF PLACENTAL INVASION, SPIRAL ARTERY REMODELING, AND EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX REMODELING THAT TRIGGERS EPO PRODUCTION BY THE PLACENTA. ADDITIONALLY, PLACENTAL TROPHOBLASTS UNDERGO EXTENSIVE APOPTOSIS THROUGHOUT GESTATION. OUR HYPOTHESIS IS THAT THE CONVERGENCE OF PLACENTAL EPO AND TROPHOBLAST APOPTOSIS DRIVE FETAL AG-SPECIFIC TREG INDUCTION AND CD8 T-CELL EXHAUSTION THROUGH A CDC1-DEPENDENT MECHANISM. TO TEST THIS, WE WILL USE A STRATEGY THAT LEVERAGES PRIMARY HUMAN TISSUE, ANIMAL MODELS, AND NEXT-GENERATION ASSAYS IN SPATIAL BIOLOGY TO UNDERSTAND THIS PROCESS. WE WILL USE TRANSGENIC MOUSE MODELS TO ELUCIDATE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH EPOR SIGNALING IN CDC1S PROMOTES FETAL TOLERANCE DURING SUCCESSIVE PREGNANCIES. USING NEXT GENERATION TOOLS FOR SPATIAL BIOLOGY, WE WILL ANALYZE CDC1S IN HUMAN TISSUE TO DETERMINE IF THE COMPOSITION AND STRUCTURE OF DECIDUA AND UTERINE DRAINING LYMPH NODES ALIGN WITH OUR PROPOSED MODEL AND THE RESULTS OF OUR TRANSGENIC MOUSE EXPERIMENTS. THESE RESULTS WILL BE COMPARED WITH SAMPLES FROM WOMEN WITH A HISTORY OF RECURRENT PREGNANCY LOSS TO IDENTIFY DIFFERENCES IN DECIDUAL DCS, TREGS, AND CD8 T-CELLS THAT COULD EXPLAIN THIS DISORDER. LASTLY, WE WILL CULTURE HUMAN CDC1S AND DECIDUAL EXPLANTS WITH TROPHOBLASTS OR TROPHOBLAST CONDITIONED MEDIA (CM) TO DETERMINE IF THE PLACENTAL SECRETOME IS SUFFICIENT FOR INDUCING CDC1 TOLEROGENIC PHENOTYPES. TOGETHER, THIS COMBINATION OF MURINE FUNCTIONAL MODELS, DEEP SPATIAL ANALYSIS OF HUMAN TISSUES, AND IN VITRO STUDIES OF HUMAN DECIDUA, PLACENTA, AND IMMUNE CELLS WILL ALLOW US TO TEST OUR MODEL, TO ASSESS ITS RELEVANCE IN HUMANS, AND TO PROVIDE NEW DIRECTIONS FOR TREATING PREGNANCY DISORDERS.

description: THE ROLE OF DYNAMIC JOINT STABILITY IN GENERALIZED JOINT HYPERMOBILITY: ACOMPREHENSIVE ANALYSIS OF BIOMECHANICAL CONTRIBUTIONS TO CHRONIC PAIN - PROJECT SUMMARY HYPERMOBILE EHLERS-DANLOS SYNDROME (HEDS) AND HYPERMOBILITY SPECTRUM DISORDER (HSD) ARE UNDERRECOGNIZED CONNECTIVE TISSUE DISORDERS CHARACTERIZED BY GENERALIZED JOINT HYPERMOBILITY (GJH) AND CHRONIC MUSCULOSKELETAL PAIN. CLINICAL MANAGEMENT REMAINS CHALLENGING DUE TO A LACK OF MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING AND EVIDENCE-BASED TREATMENT STRATEGIES. ALTHOUGH GJH AFFECTS UP TO 35% OF WOMEN UNDER AGE 40, ONLY A SUBSET DEVELOPS CHRONIC PAIN, SUGGESTING THAT HYPERMOBILITY ALONE IS INSUFFICIENT TO EXPLAIN SYMPTOM ONSET. INCREASING EVIDENCE IMPLICATES BIOMECHANICAL JOINT INSTABILITY AS A KEY CONTRIBUTOR TO PAIN AND DISABILITY IN HEDS/HSD, YET CERVICAL SPINE INSTABILITY HAS NEVER BEEN DIRECTLY MEASURED IN THIS POPULATION. DYNAMIC JOINT STABILITY IS MAINTAINED BY THE COORDINATED FUNCTION OF THREE INTERDEPENDENT SUBSYSTEMS: PASSIVE (LIGAMENTOUS STRUCTURES), ACTIVE (MUSCULATURE), AND NEURAL (PROPRIOCEPTION AND MOTOR CONTROL). WE PROPOSE THAT JOINT INSTABILITY IN HEDS/HSD ARISES FROM SUBSYSTEM-SPECIFIC IMPAIRMENTS, AND THAT ASYMPTOMATIC INDIVIDUALS WITH GJH MAY MITIGATE SYMPTOMS BY COMPENSATING FOR PASSIVE LAXITY WITH STRONGER ACTIVE AND/OR NEURAL CONTROL. THIS FRAMEWORK IS QUANTIFIED USING A NOVEL METRIC—THE DYNAMIC JOINT STABILITY INDEX (DJSI)—THAT INTEGRATES MEASURES FROM ALL THREE SUBSYSTEMS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUPPORT THIS HYPOTHESIS, REVEALING ABERRANT CERVICAL SPINE MOTION IN SYMPTOMATIC INDIVIDUALS AND ELEVATED STRENGTH IN ASYMPTOMATIC GJH PARTICIPANTS. THIS STUDY WILL ENROLL 120 BIOLOGICAL FEMALES (AGES 18–39), STRATIFIED INTO SYMPTOMATIC GJH (S-GJH; HEDS/HSD WITH CHRONIC NECK PAIN), ASYMPTOMATIC GJH (A-GJH), AND NON-GJH CONTROLS. PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE STANDARDIZED ASSESSMENTS AT BASELINE AND TWO-YEAR FOLLOW-UP. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE GROUP DIFFERENCES AND LONGITUDINAL CHANGES IN DJSI SUBSYSTEM PERFORMANCE AND CLINICAL OUTCOMES. AIM 2 WILL DIRECTLY ASSESS CERVICAL SEGMENTAL INSTABILITY USING BIPLANE VIDEORADIOGRAPHY AND EVALUATE ITS RELATIONSHIP WITH DJSI AND TISSUE HEALTH VIA QUANTITATIVE MRI. AIM 3 WILL USE MULTIVARIABLE MODELING TO IDENTIFY PREDICTORS OF INSTABILITY, PAIN, AND DISABILITY, INTEGRATING BIOMECHANICAL, IMAGING, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL DATA. FINDINGS WILL DEFINE BIOMECHANICAL PHENOTYPES ACROSS THE GJH SPECTRUM AND IDENTIFY MECHANISM-INFORMED TARGETS FOR FUTURE INTERVENTIONS. THIS WORK ADDRESSES A CRITICAL GAP IN THE CARE OF INDIVIDUALS WITH HEDS/HSD AND HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM CLINICAL MANAGEMENT OF HYPERMOBILITY-RELATED NECK PAIN.

description: MECHANISTIC-BASED THERAPEUTIC TO AMELIORATE CELLULAR SENESCENCE AND REVERSE QUADRICEPS MUSCLE ATROPHY IN HUMANS FOLLOWING ACL INJURY - PROJECT SUMMARY ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT (ACL) INJURY AND SUBSEQUENT RECONSTRUCTION RESULT IN LOCALIZED INFLAMMATION AND ALTERATIONS WITHIN THE EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX WHICH HAVE BEEN LINKED TO PROTRACTED QUADRICEPS WEAKNESS AND ATROPHY. THERE IS A SIGNIFICANT GAP IN KNOWLEDGE CONCERNING THE SIGNALING CASCADES AND INTERCELLULAR COMMUNICATION AMONG IMMUNE CELLS (E.G., MACROPHAGES), FIBRO-ADIPOGENIC PROGENITORS (FAPS), AND SATELLITE CELLS THAT DIRECTLY REGULATE EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX REMODELING WITHIN THE QUADRICEPS, LIMITING PROGRESS IN THE FIELD TO ADDRESS THE INCEPTIVE EVENTS UNDERLYING POOR FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY. COMPELLING PRELIMINARY DATA IDENTIFY A SUBSET OF IMMUNE CELLS AND FAPS THAT UNDERGO CELLULAR SENESCENCE THAT MAY UNDERLIE A FIBROTIC AND INFLAMMATORY MUSCLE PHENOTYPE THROUGH THE INDUCTION OF SENESCENCE ASSOCIATED SECRETORY PHENOTYPE (SASP) SIGNALING WITHIN THE ACL-INJURY QUADRICEPS. METFORMIN HAS BEEN IMPLICATED TO HAVE POSITIVE EFFECTS ON MUSCLE SIZE AND FUNCTION IN AGED INDIVIDUALS FOLLOWING A PERIOD OF DISUSE BY ENHANCING MACROPHAGE FUNCTION AND AN ATTENUATED CELLULAR SENESCENT BURDEN BY TARGETING SASP IN A VARIETY OF MUSCLE INTERSTITIAL CELL TYPES. WHETHER METFORMIN IS CAPABLE OF MODULATING EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX REMODELING AND IMMUNE CELL PROFILE FOLLOWING ACUTE LIGAMENT INJURY AND RECONSTRUCTION IS UNKNOWN. THE OVERARCHING OBJECTIVE OF THE CURRENT PROPOSAL IS TO DEFINE CELLULAR SENESCENCE AS A MODIFIABLE TARGET TO IMPROVE QUADRICEPS HEALTH AND FUNCTION IN PATIENTS FOLLOWING ACL RECONSTRUCTION. IN THIS RANDOMIZED, DOUBLE BLIND, PLACEBO-CONTROLLED CLINICAL TRIAL, THE HYPOTHESIS IS THAT TREATMENT WITH METFORMIN (VS PLACEBO) WILL MITIGATE QUADRICEPS CELLULAR SENESCENCE AND THIS WILL ENHANCE ECM REMODELING, MUSCLE STRENGTH AND SIZE FOLLOWING ACL RECONSTRUCTION. TWO INTERCONNECTED BUT INDEPENDENT AIMS WILL ADDRESS THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS AND PROVIDE CRITICAL MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO THE ETIOLOGY OF MUSCLE CELLULAR SENESCENCE FOLLOWING INJURY. SPECIFICALLY, INNOVATIVE IMAGING AND SINGE CELL ANALYSES WILL REVEAL THE IMPACT OF METFORMIN TREATMENT ON MACROPHAGE AND FAP CELLULAR SENESCENCE AND SASP, COLLAGEN ORGANIZATION, AND MUSCLE RECOVERY FOLLOWING ACL RECONSTRUCTION. RESULTS FROM THIS WORK WILL DIRECTLY SUPPORT THE REPURPOSING OF METFORMIN TO ACCELERATE FUNCTIONAL RECOVERY IN PATIENTS WHO HAVE SUSTAINED ACL INJURIES.
