description: THE ROLE OF ERNA M6A MODIFICATION IN LIGAND-INDEPENDENT ER ACTIVATION AND BREAST CANCER PROGRESSION - SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE ROLE OF ERNA M6A MODIFICATION IN LIGAND-INDEPENDENT ER ACTIVATION AND BREAST CANCER PROGRESSION ESTROGENS (E2) AND ESTROGEN RECEPTOR (ERΑ) ARE ESSENTIAL FOR THE NORMAL FUNCTION OF THE MAMMARY GLAND. ABERRANT REGULATION OF ERΑ SIGNALING IS CLOSELY LINKED TO BREAST CANCER PROGRESSION, MAKING ENDOCRINE THERAPIES USING AROMATASE INHIBITORS, TAMOXIFEN, AND FULVESTRANT CRUCIAL FOR TREATING ER+ BREAST CANCER. HOWEVER, DESPITE INITIAL EFFICACY, MANY TUMORS DEVELOP RESISTANCE AND ADVANCE TO A LETHAL METASTATIC STATE. RECENT FINDINGS HIGHLIGHT MUTATIONS IN THE LIGAND-BINDING DOMAIN (LBD) OF THE ERΑ GENE AS SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTORS TO ENDOCRINE RESISTANCE AND METASTATIC PROGRESSION. UNDERSTANDING THE IMPACT OF THESE ERΑ LBD MUTATIONS IS VITAL FOR DEVELOPING NEW THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES FOR AGGRESSIVE BREAST CANCER. N6- METHYLADENOSINE (M6A) MODIFICATION, A COMMON RNA MODIFICATION, PLAYS SIGNIFICANT ROLES IN NORMAL BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES AND CANCER. ALTHOUGH METTL3-CATALYZED M6A MODIFICATION IS KNOWN TO HAVE ONCOGENIC ROLES IN BREAST CANCER, ITS IMPACT ON ERΑ SIGNALING, PARTICULARLY IN ENDOCRINE-RESISTANT BREAST CANCER, REMAINS UNCLEAR. OUR DATA REVEAL THAT PHASE-SEPARATED CONDENSATION OF HORMONE RECEPTORS IS CRITICAL FOR ASSEMBLING ENHANCER TRANSCRIPTIONAL MACHINERY, WITH ERΑ CONDENSATE FORMATION FACILITATED BY M6A MODIFICATION ON ENHANCER RNAS (ERNAS) AND THE NUCLEAR M6A READER YTHDC1. INHIBITING M6A MODIFICATION OR DISRUPTING M6A BINDING TO YTHDC1 LEADS TO THE DISSOLUTION OF ERΑ CONDENSATES, DECREASED CHROMATIN BINDING OF ERΑ AND ITS COFACTORS, AND REDUCED TRANSCRIPTIONAL ACTIVITY. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES ON ENDOCRINE-RESISTANT ERΑ MUTANTS (Y537S AND D538G) SHOW THAT THESE MUTATIONS ENABLE CHROMATIN BINDING AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL ACTIVATION INDEPENDENT OF E2. UNLIKE WILD-TYPE ERΑ, WHICH ONLY FORMS CONDENSATES UPON E2 STIMULATION, THESE CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVE ERΑ MUTANTS FORM CONDENSATES WITHOUT E2. OUR FINDINGS FURTHER DEMONSTRATE THAT INHIBITING M6A MODIFICATION AND DISRUPTING CONDENSATION COULD SUPPRESS THE LIGAND-INDEPENDENT ACTIVATION OF ERΑ MUTANTS, SUGGESTING THAT M6A-MEDIATED ERΑ CONDENSATION DRIVES THE CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVE SIGNALING OBSERVED IN ADVANCED BREAST CANCER. THUS, THESE FINDINGS LEAD US TO PROPOSE AN ERΑ SIGNALING ACTIVATION MODEL LINKING M6A MODIFICATION OF ERNA, ERΑ CONDENSATION, ENHANCER ASSEMBLY, AND TRANSACTIVATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TARGETING M6A MODIFICATION COULD INHIBIT THE CONSTITUTIVE ACTIVATION OF THESE ERΑ MUTANTS AND OVERCOME BREAST CANCER PROGRESSION. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE PROPOSE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: 1). DETERMINE THE ROLE OF M6A-ERNAS IN E2-INDEPENDENT ACTIVATION OF ENDOCRINE-RESISTANT ERΑ MUTANTS. 2). ELUCIDATE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH M6A- ERNAS PROMOTE E2-INDPENDENT ENHANCER ACTIVATION. 3). EVALUATE THE POTENTIAL OF TARGETING M6A MODIFICATION AS A THERAPEUTIC APPROACH TO COMBAT CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVE ERΑ SIGNALING AND TUMOR PROGRESSION. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THESE STUDIES WILL HAVE A BROAD IMPACT BY ELUCIDATING THE ROLE OF ERNA M6A MODIFICATION IN ERΑ SIGNALING ACTIVATION AND OFFERING A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY TO TREAT AGGRESSIVE BREAST CANCER BY TARGETING M6A MODIFICATION AND MUTANT ER ENHANCER CONDENSATES TO INHIBIT CONSTITUTIVE ACTIVATION OF MUTANT ERΑ.

description: UNDERSTANDING THE CONTRIBUTION OF TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR 4 ACTIVITY IN MESENCHYMAL STROMAL CELLS TO CANCER TREATMENT INDUCED SKELETAL MUSCLE DECLINE AND FIBROSIS - SUMMARY ONE OF THE GREAT ACHIEVEMENTS IN MEDICAL SCIENCES IS THE IMPROVED SURVIVAL RATE AMONG CHILDREN DIAGNOSED WITH CANCER. ALTHOUGH ESTIMATES INDICATE THE 5-YEAR SURVIVAL RATE OF CHILDREN DIAGNOSED WITH A MALIGNANCY IS NEAR 80%, MOST OF THESE INDIVIDUALS PRIOR TO THE AGE OF 40 DEMONSTRATE INDICES OF PHYSICAL LIMITATION NORMALLY ASSOCIATED WITH THE ELDERLY POPULATION. AMONG THE INDUCTION REMISSION TREATMENTS RECEIVED BY PEDIATRIC CANCER PATIENTS IS FRACTIONATED X-RAY IRRADIATION, WHICH INDUCES GENOTOXIC STRESS THAT ELIMINATES PROLIFERATIVE CANCER CELLS. HOWEVER, MULTIFARIOUS DIRECT AND INDIRECT EFFECTS OF RADIATION CAN NEGATIVELY IMPACT NORMAL TISSUE GROWTH AND MAINTENANCE ESPECIALLY IN ACTIVELY GROWING POPULATIONS. PHENOTYPES OBSERVED EARLIER IN PEDIATRIC CANCER SURVIVORS IS THE ACCELERATED ONSET OF FRAILTY INDICES SUCH AS MUSCULAR DECLINE. IN A MURINE MODEL, WE FIND WEEKS AFTER IMAGE GUIDED PEDIATRIC FRACTIONATED X-RAY IRRADIATION OF HINDLIMBS DECREASES IN MUSCLE FORCE PRODUCTION, MYOFIBER SIZE, MYONUCLEAR CONTENT AND SKELETAL MUSCLE STEM CELL (SATELLITE CELL) NUMBER. WE ALSO FIND OTHER PHENOTYPES CONSISTENT WITH SKELETAL MUSCLE DECLINE SUCH AS INTRAMUSCULAR FIBROSIS AND AN ELEVATION OF C-C CHEMOKINE RECEPTOR 2 (CCR2) EXPRESSING MONOCYTE/MACROPHAGE CONTENT. THROUGH SCRNASEQ ANALYSIS WE OBSERVE WEEKS AFTER PEDIATRIC FRACTIONATED RADIATION AN INCREASE IN THE EXPRESSION OF THE TOLL-LIKE RECEPTOR 4 (TLR4) LIGAND TENASCIN C (TNC), AND THE TLR4 EFFECTOR MYELOID DIFFERENTIATION PRIMARY RESPONSE 88 (MYD88) IN MESENCHYMAL STROMAL CELLS (MSCS). THIS IS ACCOMPANIED BY ELEVATIONS IN THE EXPRESSION OF TLR4 TARGET GENES MONOCYTE CHEMOATTRACTANT PROTEIN-1/C-C MOTIF CHEMOKINE LIGAND 2 (MCP-1/CCL2) AND THROMBOSPONDIN 1 (THBS1), WHICH RESPECTIVELY CONTRIBUTE TO MONOCYTE/MACROPHAGE RECRUITMENT AND TRANSFORMING GROWTH FACTOR BETA (TGFΒ) SIGNALING AN INHIBITOR OF SATELLITE CELL ACTIVITY, REGULATOR OF VASCULAR ADAPTATION AND EXPRESSION OF ECM FACTORS FROM MSCS. FINALLY, WE FIND OUR MURINE MODEL OF PEDIATRIC RADIATION EFFECTIVELY INDUCES TUMOR REMISSION, HOWEVER, IN THE CONTEXT OF TUMOR TREATMENT EXACERBATES SKELETAL MUSCLE PHENOTYPES. THEREFORE, OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO RIGOROUSLY CHARACTERIZE THE MECHANISMS WHEREBY TREATMENT RELATED EXPRESSION OF THE TLR4 TARGET CCL2, AND TLR4 ACTIVITY IN MSCS CONTRIBUTE TO PEDIATRIC RADIATION RELATED INHIBITION OF SKELETAL MUSCLE GROWTH, FIBROSIS AND INFLAMMATION. IDEALLY, SUCH INSIGHT WOULD BE USED TO UNCOVER INTERVENTIONS TO ATTENUATE PEDIATRIC RADIATION RELATED MUSCULAR DECLINE THAT INCREASES MORBIDITY AND BURDENS SURVIVORS. TO ACCOMPLISH OUR OBJECTIVES, WE WILL UTILIZE, ASSESSMENT OF SKELETAL MUSCLE INTEGRITY, MUSCULAR FUNCTION, IMAGING ANALYSIS, MOUSE GENETICS, SCRNASEQ ANALYSIS, FLOW CYTOMETRY, PROTEIN ANALYSIS, AND PHARMACOLOGICAL TREATMENTS. THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THIS PROPOSAL ARE 1) DETERMINE IF CELL-SPECIFIC LOSS OF CCL2 OR CCR2, AND 2) EXAMINE WHETHER TLR4 ACTIVITY IN MSCS IMPACTS PEDIATRIC RADIATION AND CANCER TREATMENT RELATED SKELETAL MUSCLE ALTERATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPROVING CANCER AND TOBACCO CESSATION CARE FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS - SERIOUS MENTAL ILLNESS (SMI) INCLUDING SCHIZOPHRENIA, BIPOLAR DISORDER, AND SEVERE MAJOR DEPRESSION AFFECTS MORE THAN 15 MILLION U.S. ADULTS WHO DIE 15-25 YEARS EARLIER THAN THE GENERAL POPULATION. MORE THAN 50% OF ADULTS WITH SMI SMOKE4; SMOKING-RELATED ILLNESSES ACCOUNT FOR >70% OF THAT MORTALITY GAP. ADULTS WITH SMI ARE LESS LIKELY TO RECEIVE TOBACCO CESSATION TREATMENT AND GUIDELINE-CONCORDANT CANCER CARE AND 2-4 TIMES MORE LIKELY TO DIE FROM MANY COMMON CANCERS. DIAGNOSTIC DELAYS AND DIFFERENCES IN CANCER TREATMENT CONTRIBUTE TO POOR CANCER SURVIVAL. PATIENT, CLINICIAN, AND SYSTEMS FACTORS IMPACT CANCER OUTCOMES: HIGH SMOKING RATES CAN INCREASE CANCER RECURRENCE; UNTREATED PSYCHIATRIC ILLNESS CAN IMPAIR PROGNOSTIC UNDERSTANDING, AND INADEQUATE ACCESS TO CARE. CLINICIANS LACK CROSS-DISCIPLINARY TRAINING, PSYCHO-ONCOLOGY SERVICES REMAIN INADEQUATE, AND CLINICAL TRIALS EXCLUDE PATIENTS WITH SMI. THE TIME OF CANCER DIAGNOSIS IS A CRITICAL OPPORTUNITY TO IMPROVE CANCER CARE DELIVERY AND OUTCOMES FOR ALL PATIENTS WITH SMI. EARLY, INTEGRATED MENTAL HEALTH CARE PROTECTS AGAINST CANCER CARE DISRUPTIONS FOR PEOPLE WITH SMI, HOWEVER, MANY PATIENTS WITH SMI LACK MENTAL HEALTH CARE. COLLABORATIVE CARE IMPROVES DEPRESSION COST-EFFECTIVELY FOR PATIENTS WITH CANCER BUT HAS EXCLUDED PATIENTS WITH SMI. WE DEVELOPED AND PILOTED BRIDGE, PERSON-CENTERED COLLABORATIVE CARE FOR SMI AND CANCER. WE COMPLETED THE FIRST RANDOMIZED TRIAL (N=120) FOR SMI AND A NEW CANCER. BRIDGE WAS FEASIBLE (85% CONSENTED) AND DELIVERED REMOTELY DURING THE PANDEMIC. COMPARED TO ENHANCED USUAL CARE (EUC), PATIENTS ON BRIDGE HAD FEWER CANCER CARE DISRUPTIONS (TREATMENT DELAYS, DEVIATIONS FROM GUIDELINE-CONCORDANT CANCER CARE, TREATMENT INTERRUPTIONS; 17% VS. 35%, P<.035) AND DECREASED PSYCHIATRIC ILLNESS SEVERITY. WE CONDUCTED A 2-SITE RCT THAT FOUND THAT ADULTS WITH SMI CAN BENEFIT FROM VIRTUAL TOBACCO CESSATION COUNSELING BEGINNING AT CANCER DIAGNOSIS. ONE CRITICAL NEXT STEP IS INCREASING REACH TO COMMUNITY SETTINGS. GUIDED BY A STAKEHOLDER COALITION, WE NOW PROPOSE A HYBRID TYPE I EFFECTIVENESS-IMPLEMENTATION TRIAL OF BRIDGE-FREE WHICH INTEGRATES TOBACCO CESSATION INTO PERSON-CENTERED COLLABORATIVE CARE ACROSS THE MGH AND DANA-FARBER NETWORKS (N=248). WE WILL DETERMINE THE IMPACT ON CANCER CARE DISRUPTIONS, TOBACCO CESSATION, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL OUTCOMES AND IDENTIFY BARRIERS TO IMPLEMENTATION. THE OVERARCHING GOAL IS TO INFORM SCALABLE APPROACHES THAT ADDRESS MODIFIABLE CAUSES OF PREMATURE CANCER MORTALITY.

description: MUTATIONAL EPIDEMIOLOGY OF CHILDHOOD ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKEMIA IN CALIFORNIA - ABSTRACT ACUTE LYMPHOBLASTIC LEUKEMIA (ALL) IS THE MOST COMMON CHILDHOOD MALIGNANCY AND, DESPITE HIGH CURE RATES IN DEVELOPED COUNTRIES, IT REMAINS A LEADING CAUSE OF CHILDHOOD MORTALITY. MOREOVER, SURVIVORS OF CHILDHOOD ALL FACE LONG-TERM TREATMENT-RELATED MORBIDITIES. THUS, PREVENTION OF ALL REMAINS AN IMPORTANT GOAL; HOWEVER, THERE ARE FEW KNOWN MODIFIABLE RISK FACTORS. THE RISING INCIDENCE OF CHILDHOOD ALL, PARTICULARLY AMONG HISPANIC/LATINO CHILDREN, SUGGESTS A ROLE FOR COMMON ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES. CASE-CONTROL STUDIES HAVE IDENTIFIED SEVERAL ENVIRONMENTAL RISK FACTORS FOR CHILDHOOD ALL, BUT THESE HAVE LARGELY RELIED ON QUESTIONNAIRE DATA AND, THUS, MAY BE PRONE TO RECALL BIAS. RECENT POPULATION-BASED GEOSPATIAL STUDIES REPORTED SIGNIFICANT ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES TO AIR POLLUTION, PESTICIDES, AND ULTRAVIOLET (UV) RADIATION AND RISK OF ALL, ALTHOUGH THEY PROVIDE NO INSIGHTS INTO BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS. WE PROPOSE TO ADDRESS THESE SHORTCOMINGS THROUGH “MUTATIONAL EPIDEMIOLOGY”, A PROMISING APPROACH THAT COMBINES STUDYING PATTERNS OF TUMOR MUTATIONS WITH EPIDEMIOLOGICAL ANALYSES TO ELUCIDATE THE CAUSES OF CANCER. WHILE MUTATIONAL EPIDEMIOLOGY STUDIES OF ADULT CANCERS HAVE LED TO NOVEL DISCOVERIES, THIS APPROACH HAS YET TO BE APPLIED TO CHILDHOOD LEUKEMIA. TWO MAJOR PATTERNS OF SOMATIC MUTATIONS ARE DETECTABLE IN CHILDHOOD ALL: I) SINGLE-BASE SUBSTITUTION (SBS) MUTATIONAL SIGNATURES RELATED TO APOBEC MUTAGENESIS, REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES (ROS), AND UV RADIATION; AND II) DELETIONS MEDIATED BY “OFF- TARGET” RECOMBINATION-ACTIVATING GENE (RAG) RECOMBINATION; YET THE ETIOLOGIES OF THESE PATTERNS ARE LARGELY UNKNOWN. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE CALIFORNIA CHILDHOOD LEUKEMIA STUDY (CCLS), IN WHICH WE HAVE ACCESS TO AVAILABLE DIAGNOSTIC LEUKEMIA (TUMOR) AND GERMLINE SAMPLES AS WELL AS RICH EPIDEMIOLOGICAL DATA, INCLUDING RESIDENTIAL HISTORY, QUESTIONNAIRE DATA, AND OMICS DATA, FROM 630 CHILDHOOD ALL PATIENTS OF WHICH ~50% ARE HISPANIC/LATINO. THROUGH OUR INNOVATIVE AND COLLABORATIVE APPROACH, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT WE WILL IDENTIFY RISK FACTORS FOR THE SOMATIC MUTATIONAL PATTERNS IN CHILDHOOD ALL. IN OUR FIRST AIM, WE WILL INVESTIGATE RISK FACTORS FOR OFF-TARGET RAG RECOMBINATION THROUGH TUMOR-NORMAL WHOLE-GENOME SEQUENCING (WGS) OF 630 CHILDHOOD ALL PATIENTS. WE WILL EXPAND UPON OUR PRIOR DISCOVERY OF AN ASSOCIATION BETWEEN EARLY-LIFE TOBACCO SMOKE EXPOSURE AND RAG-MEDIATED DELETIONS IN ALL TO A LARGER SET OF PATIENTS AND EXAMINE THE POTENTIAL ROLE OF AIR POLLUTION (FROM GEOSPATIAL MODELS) AND EARLY-LIFE INFECTIONS. IN OUR SECOND AIM, WE WILL ANALYZE TUMOR MUTATIONAL SIGNATURES IN THE 630 PATIENTS, FOCUSING ON THE APOBEC, ROS, AND UV SBS SIGNATURES, AND INVESTIGATE ASSOCIATIONS WITH SPECIFIC EXPOSURES OF INTEREST, INCLUDING EARLY-LIFE INFECTIONS, AIR POLLUTION, PESTICIDES OF INTEREST, AND UV RADIATION. FINALLY, IN OUR THIRD AIM, WE WILL INVESTIGATE WHETHER GENETIC VARIATION IS ASSOCIATED WITH RAG-MEDIATED DELETIONS AND MUTATIONAL SIGNATURES AND IF GENETIC VARIANTS MODERATE THE EFFECTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES ON SOMATIC MUTATIONAL PATTERNS. OUR INNOVATIVE MUTATIONAL EPIDEMIOLOGY STUDY OF CHILDHOOD ALL WILL FURTHER OUR UNDERSTANDING OF ITS CAUSES, HIGHLIGHT NOVEL AVENUES OF PREVENTION, AND INFORM FUTURE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL STUDIES.

description: NEURAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL MECHANISMS OF CISPLATIN OTOTOXICITY - PROJECT SUMMARY CISPLATIN IS A WIDELY USED AND POTENTIALLY LIFE-SAVING CHEMOTHERAPY, HOWEVER, CISPLATIN ACCUMULATES IN THE COCHLEA WITH CONTINUED TREATMENT LEADING TO IRREVERSIBLE HEARING LOSS. CISPLATIN-INDUCED HEARING LOSS IMPOSES SIGNIFICANT MEDICAL, PSYCHOLOGICAL, FINANCIAL, AND LIFESTYLE BURDENS ON MANY CANCER SURVIVORS. ALTHOUGH SODIUM THIOSULFATE OTOPROTECTIVE THERAPY PROVIDES PARTIAL PROTECTION IN ELIGIBLE YOUNG PATIENTS, COMPROMISED CHEMOTHERAPEUTIC ACTIVITY REMAINS A MAJOR LIMITATION. TARGETED OTOPROTECTIVE THERAPIES THAT DO NOT INTERFERE WITH CISPLATIN ANTICANCER ACTIVITY ARE NEEDED. TO REALIZE THIS GOAL, WE SEEK TO BETTER DEFINE THE MOST CRITICAL CELLULAR TARGETS OF CISPLATIN IN THE COCHLEA, WHICH IS COMPLICATED DUE TO ITS BROAD GENOTOXIC EFFECTS. RECENT FINDINGS, INCLUDING OUR PRELIMINARY DATA, DEMONSTRATE THAT CISPLATIN OTOTOXICITY EXTENDS BEYOND THE WELL-CHARACTERIZED LOSS OF OUTER HAIR CELLS (OHC), AND MAY RELATE TO DAMAGE IN NEURAL AND OTHER CELL TYPES. NOTABLY, WE FIND SIGNIFICANT CHANGES IN LOW-FREQUENCY AUDITORY BRAINSTEM RESPONSES (ABR) THAT ARE NOT EXPLAINED BY OHC LOSS IN CORRESPONDING COCHLEAR REGIONS. COMPLEMENTARY FUNCTIONAL, TRANSCRIPTIONAL, AND PATHOLOGICAL FINDINGS INDICATE NEURAL INJURY PROCESSES IN THESE REGIONS AND WE THEREFORE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CISPLATIN DISRUPTS CHROMATIN ACCESSIBILITY AND GENE EXPRESSION IN COCHLEAR CELLS, LEADING TO DISRUPTED AUDITORY NEURAL FUNCTION INDEPENDENT OF SENSORY LOSS ALONE. TO TEST THIS, WE WILL EVALUATE CISPLATIN’S EFFECTS ON NEW ASPECTS OF AUDITORY NERVE FUNCTION ALONGSIDE HISTOPATHOLOGY AND EPIGENETIC AND TRANSCRIPTOMIC STUDIES. MOUSE MODELS PROVIDE ACCESS TO INNER EAR TISSUES, A FUNCTIONAL HEARING SYSTEM, AND CAREFULLY CONTROLLED CONDITIONS FOR RIGOROUS MECHANISTIC STUDIES, CAPABILITIES NOT AVAILABLE IN HUMAN AND ALTERNATIVE MODELS. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE CELL-SPECIFIC CISPLATIN INSULTS AT THE GENOMIC LEVEL BY SINGLE-NUCLEUS MULTIOMIC PROFILING. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS AUDITORY FUNCTION DURING THE COURSE OF CISPLATIN TREATMENT AND STUDY THE PROGRESSION OF PATHOLOGICAL CHANGES. THESE STUDIES WILL IDENTIFY CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR TARGETS OF CISPLATIN IN THE COCHLEA, WITH A FOCUS ON NEURAL INJURY. FINDINGS WILL SUPPORT THE DEVELOPMENT OF TARGETED OTOPROTECTIVE THERAPIES TO FURTHER PREVENT HEARING LOSS WITHOUT INTERFERING WITH CHEMOTHERAPEUTIC ACTIVITY.

description: CHARACTERIZING THE ROLE OF AIR POLLUTION IN BREAST CANCER PROGNOSIS AND SURVIVORSHIP - PROJECT SUMMARY BLACK WOMEN DIAGNOSED WITH BREAST CANCER (BC) EXPERIENCE HIGHER MORTALITY RATES, GREATER CARDIOMETABOLIC BURDEN, AND WORSE SURVIVORSHIP OUTCOMES COMPARED TO WHITE WOMEN. THEY ARE ALSO MORE LIKELY TO LIVE IN AREAS WITH HIGHER EXPOSURE TO OUTDOOR AIR POLLUTION, WHICH HAS BEEN CLASSIFIED AS CARCINOGENIC IN HUMANS BY THE INTERNATIONAL AGENCY FOR RESEARCH ON CANCER AND IS LINKED TO INFLAMMATION, CARDIOTOXICITY, IMPAIRED QUALITY OF LIFE, CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, AND MORTALITY. BECAUSE EXPOSURE TO AIR POLLUTION IS UBIQUITOUS, UNAVOIDABLE, AND MORE PREVALENT IN SOCIOECONOMICALLY DISADVANTAGED COMMUNITIES, IT REPRESENTS AN IMPORTANT YET UNDERSTUDIED CONTRIBUTOR TO DIFFERENCES IN BC OUTCOMES. DESPITE BIOLOGICAL PLAUSIBILITY AND EMERGING EVIDENCE, THE LONG-TERM ASSOCIATIONS OF AIR POLLUTION WITH SURVIVAL, PATIENT-REPORTED OUTCOMES (PROS), AND BIOMARKERS OF SYSTEMIC HEALTH IN BLACK BC SURVIVORS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS, WE WILL LEVERAGE THE WOMEN’S CIRCLE OF HEALTH FOLLOW-UP STUDY (WCHFS), A WELL-CHARACTERIZED, POPULATION-BASED COHORT OF 1,900 BLACK BC SURVIVORS IN NEW JERSEY WITH DETAILED DATA ON CLINICAL CHARACTERISTICS, LIFESTYLE, AREA-BASED FACTORS, STRUCTURAL FACTORS,, AND BIOSPECIMENS. THIS PROJECT WILL EVALUATE WHETHER LONG-TERM RESIDENTIAL OUTDOOR AIR POLLUTION EXPOSURE ADVERSELY IMPACTS SURVIVAL, PROS, AND BIOMARKERS OF INFLAMMATION AND CARDIAC INJURY IN THIS DISPROPORTIONATELY AFFECTED POPULATION. THIS STUDY IS DESIGNED TO PURSUE THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) ASSESS ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN CUMULATIVE RESIDENTIAL AIR POLLUTION EXPOSURE AND BC-SPECIFIC AND ALL-CAUSE SURVIVAL; (2) EVALUATE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN AIR POLLUTION AND PROS, INCLUDING HEALTH-RELATED QUALITY OF LIFE (HRQOL), FATIGUE, AND SLEEP DISTURBANCE, MEASURED APPROXIMATELY TWO YEARS POST-DIAGNOSIS; AND (3) EXAMINE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN AIR POLLUTION AND BIOMARKERS OF SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION (HSCRP, IL-6, IL-1Β, TNF-Α) AND CARDIAC INJURY (HS-CTNT, NT-PROBNP) MEASURED TWO TO THREE YEARS POST-DIAGNOSIS. OUTDOOR AIR POLLUTION WILL BE ESTIMATED FROM SPATIOTEMPORAL MODELS YIELDING PREDICTIONS IN 1KM GRIDS (PARTICULATE MATTER WITHIN 2.5 MICRONS IN DIAMETER (PM2.5), NITROGEN DIOXIDE (NO2), PARTICULATE MATTER TRACE ELEMENTS, AND PARTICULATE MATTER COMPONENTS). THESE GRIDDED ESTIMATES WILL BE LINKED TO RESIDENTIAL ADDRESS HISTORIES OF STUDY PARTICIPANTS TO EXAMINE TIME-VARYING EXPOSURE WINDOWS. WE WILL APPLY ADVANCED MIXTURES-BASED STATISTICAL APPROACHES TO EVALUATE THE JOINT IMPACTS OF MULTIPLE POLLUTANTS AND WILL EVALUATE EFFECT MODIFICATION OF PRIMARY ANALYSES BY INDIVIDUAL AND NEIGHBORHOOD- LEVEL STRUCTURAL AND AREA-BASED FACTORS. BY INTEGRATING AIR POLLUTION EXPOSURES WITH CLINICAL, EPIDEMIOLOGIC, PRO, AND BIOMARKER INFORMATION IN A LARGE, WELL-CHARACTERIZED COHORT OF BLACK BC SURVIVORS, THIS PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY MODIFIABLE ENVIRONMENTAL CONTRIBUTORS TO DIFFERENCES IN CANCER OUTCOMES. FINDINGS WILL PROVIDE AN EVIDENCE BASE TO INFORM SURVIVORSHIP CARE, CLINICAL GUIDELINES, AND PUBLIC HEALTH STRATEGIES, WITH THE LONG-TERM GOAL OF IMPROVING OUTCOMES FOR CANCER SURVIVORS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INTEGRATING TOBACCO AND ALCOHOL COUNSELING AND TREATMENT INTO HIV CARE IN KISUMU COUNTY, KENYA- INTACT STUDY - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT ADVANCES IN HIV TREATMENT HAVE SUBSTANTIALLY INCREASED LIFE EXPECTANCY AMONG PEOPLE WITH HIV (PWH), BUT HAVE ALSO HIGHLIGHTED A GROWING BURDEN OF NON-COMMUNICABLE DISEASES (NCDS). HIGHER RATES OF TOBACCO AND ALCOHOL USE AMONG PWH INCREASE THE RISK OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, CANCER, AND OTHER CHRONIC CONDITIONS. THIS STUDY WILL EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS, IMPLEMENTATION, AND COSTEFFECTIVENESS OF INTEGRATING PHARMACOLOGIC AND BEHAVIORAL INTERVENTIONS FOR TOBACCO AND ALCOHOL USE INTO ROUTINE HIV PRIMARY CARE. IN THE UNITED STATES, HIV CARE REMAINS FRAGMENTED, WITH LIMITED INTEGRATION OF BEHAVIORAL HEALTH, SUBSTANCE USE TREATMENT, ALCOHOL USE DISORDER SERVICES, AND OTHER NCD CARE. THIS FRAGMENTATION CREATES BARRIERS TO PROVIDER ADOPTION, PARTICIPANT RECRUITMENT AND RETENTION, AND EVALUATION OF INTEGRATED INTERVENTIONS IN REAL-WORLD SETTINGS. KENYA PROVIDES A STRONG IMPLEMENTATION SETTING BECAUSE INTEGRATED HIV AND NCD SERVICES ARE ALREADY EMBEDDED WITHIN PRIMARY HEALTHCARE, OFFERING ESTABLISHED INFRASTRUCTURE FOR INTEGRATING TOBACCO AND ALCOHOL DEPENDENCE TREATMENT. LEVERAGING THIS PLATFORM WILL ENABLE EFFICIENT RECRUITMENT AND RIGOROUS EVALUATION OF INTERVENTION EFFECTIVENESS, COST-EFFECTIVENESS, FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND SCALABILITY, WHILE GENERATING IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE THAT WOULD BE MORE DIFFICULT AND COSTLY TO OBTAIN IN THE FRAGMENTED U.S. HEALTHCARE SYSTEM. BUPROPION AND NALTREXONE ARE FDA-APPROVED TREATMENTS FOR TOBACCO DEPENDENCE AND ALCOHOL USE DISORDER, RESPECTIVELY, BUT EVIDENCE SUPPORTING THEIR COMBINED USE AMONG PWH WITH CONCURRENT TOBACCO AND HEAVY ALCOHOL USE REMAINS LIMITED. FINDINGS FROM THIS STUDY COULD INFORM INTEGRATED TREATMENT APPROACHES IN U.S. HIV CARE SETTINGS, INCLUDING FEDERALLY QUALIFIED HEALTH CENTERS AND RYAN WHITE HIV/AIDS PROGRAM CLINICS. WE WILL CONDUCT A 2×2 FACTORIAL CLUSTER-RANDOMIZED TRIAL IN 12 PRIMARY CARE CLINICS IN KISUMU, KENYA, ENROLLING 600 PWH WHO USE TOBACCO AND ALCOHOL. AIM 1: CONDUCT FORMATIVE RESEARCH TO DEVELOP AND ADAPT INTERVENTIONS AND ONLINE PROVIDER TRAINING FOR INTEGRATING MEDICATION MANAGEMENT AND MOTIVATIONAL INTERVIEWING-BASED COUNSELING INTO HIV PRIMARY CARE. AIM 2: EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF BUPROPION PLUS NALTREXONE AND/OR INTENSIVE COUNSELING ON BIOCHEMICALLY VERIFIED TOBACCO CESSATION AND ALCOHOL REDUCTION AT 6 MONTHS. AIM 3: ESTIMATE THE INCREMENTAL COST-EFFECTIVENESS OF THE INTERVENTION STRATEGIES. AIM 4: ASSESS IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES AND CONTEXTUAL DETERMINANTS USING THE PRISM FRAMEWORK.

description: OPIOID USE DISORDER COUNTY AREA PREVALENCE THROUGH USE OF RECAPTURE ESTIMATES (OUD CAPTURE) - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT OPIOID USE DISORDER (OUD) REMAINS A CRITICAL PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN IN THE UNITED STATES WITH AN ESTIMATED 2.08% PREVALENCE AMONG INDIVIDUALS AGED 12 AND OLDER. THIS ESTIMATE IS WIDELY RECOGNIZED AS AN UNDERESTIMATE ARISING FROM INHERENT LIMITATIONS OF DIRECT MEASURES SUCH AS SURVEYS FROM THE NATIONAL SURVEY ON DRUG USE AND HEALTH. COMPOUNDING THESE LIMITATIONS IS THE LACK OF COUNTY-LEVEL PREVALENCE ESTIMATES, WHICH ARE ESSENTIAL FOR TARGETED TREATMENT, RESOURCE ALLOCATION, AND POLICY DEVELOPMENT. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO CHANGE THIS STATUS QUO BY USING CAPTURE-RECAPTURE (CRC) ANALYSIS AND TWO STATE-OF-THE-ART BAYESIAN MODELING TECHNIQUES TO ESTIMATE OUD PREVALENCE FOR THE LARGEST NUMBER OF COUNTIES EVER ATTEMPTED WITH PROJECTIONS TO ALL U.S. COUNTIES ONCE RECRUITMENT AIMS ARE ACHIEVED. IN AIM 1, WE GENERATE ESTIMATES OF OUD PREVALENCE USING CRC, THE BEST AVAILABLE METHOD FOR ESTIMATING THE UNKNOWN COMPONENT OF THE POPULATION WITH OUD, BY COUNTY AND YEAR (MOST RECENT AVAILABLE) WITH LINKED DATA FROM MULTIPLE PARTICIPATING STATES AND COMPARE RESULTS TO BAYESIAN BENCHMARK MULTIPLIER (BBM) AND BAYESIAN INTEGRATED ABUNDANCE (BIA) MODELS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL CONDUCT BAYESIAN SPATIAL REGRESSION ANALYSES TO ASSOCIATE OUD PREVALENCE ESTIMATES FROM CRC WITH PUBLICLY AVAILABLE COVARIATES AT THE COUNTY-LEVEL TO EVENTUALLY USE THOSE COEFFICIENTS FOR ITERATIVELY PROJECTING OUD PREVALENCE TO MISSING COUNTIES. IN AIM 3, WE FOCUS ON RECRUITMENT OF ADDITIONAL STATES PRIMARILY PARTICIPATING IN THE U.S. CENTERS FOR DISEASE CONTROL AND PREVENTION'S OVERDOSE TO ACTION PROJECT. THE FINDINGS FROM THIS PROJECT, CALLED OPIOID USE DISORDER COUNTY AREA PREVALENCE THROUGH USE OF RECAPTURE ESTIMATES (OUD CAPTURE), WILL INFORM TARGETED PUBLIC HEALTH RESPONSES, PROVIDE A TRANSFERABLE AND ADAPTABLE FRAMEWORK FOR ESTIMATING “HIDDEN” AND VULNERABLE POPULATIONS UNDER VARIOUS STATE RESOURCE ENVIRONMENTS, AND OPTIMIZE THE NATION'S CONSIDERABLE STATE AND FEDERAL INVESTMENTS IN LINKING ADMINISTRATIVE DATASETS.

description: NATIONAL LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF VIOLENCE AND SUBSTANCE USE IN THE UNITED STATES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT VIOLENCE REMAINS A SIGNIFICANT AND PREVENTABLE CAUSE OF INJURY, MORTALITY, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, SUBSTANCE USE DISORDERS (SUDS), AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH BURDEN IN THE UNITED STATES. DESPITE THIS, MAJOR PUBLIC HEALTH DATA SYSTEMS FREQUENTLY HAVE OMITTED VARIABLES, CONTRIBUTING TO SURVEILLANCE GAPS IN HOW VIOLENCE IS TRACKED AND UNDERSTOOD. THESE OMISSIONS LIMIT OUR ABILITY TO ASSESS SAFETY RISKS, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, SUDS, AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH IMPACTS THAT INFLUENCE THE ONSET AND PROGRESSION OF HARM. EXISTING LIMITATIONS IN NATIONAL DATA COLLECTION AND COHORT DESIGN MAKE IT DIFFICULT TO ACCURATELY ESTIMATE PREVALENCE, UNDERSTAND RISK TRAJECTORIES, OR IDENTIFY PROTECTIVE FACTORS ACROSS AFFECTED POPULATIONS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A NATIONWIDE PROSPECTIVE DIGITAL COHORT OF 1,200 ADULTS AT INCREASED RISK OF EXPOSURE TO VIOLENCE. PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE STRUCTURED SURVEYS EVERY SIX MONTHS OVER A 24-MONTH PERIOD, AND A SUBSET WILL PARTICIPATE IN LONGITUDINAL QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS TO PROVIDE CONTEXTUAL DEPTH ON EXPERIENCES OF VIOLENCE, PERCEIVED SAFETY, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, SUDS, AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CHALLENGES. THE STUDY’S OBJECTIVES ARE TO: (1) ESTIMATE THE PREVALENCE AND PATTERNS OF VIOLENCE AND CO- OCCURRING SUBSTANCE MISUSE AND SUDS; (2) EXAMINE INDIVIDUAL, RELATIONAL, COMMUNITY, AND SOCIETAL FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH RISK AND PROTECTION; AND (3) ASSESS ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN VIOLENCE EXPOSURE, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, SUDS, AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS. BY LEVERAGING A FLEXIBLE DIGITAL COHORT MODEL, THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE TIMELY, ACTIONABLE DATA TO ENHANCE PUBLIC HEALTH SURVEILLANCE, INFORM PREVENTION STRATEGIES, AND GUIDE RESOURCE ALLOCATION FOR INDIVIDUALS AFFECTED BY VIOLENCE, SUBSTANCE MISUSE, SUDS, AND OTHER BEHAVIORAL HEALTH CONDITIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISMS OF RENAL DISEASE PROGRESSION IN OFFSPRING FROM OBESE PARENTS - OBESITY IS A MAJOR RISK FACTOR FOR HYPERTENSION AND CHRONIC KIDNEY DISEASE (CKD), AND ACCUMULATING EVIDENCE INDICATES THAT PARENTAL OBESITY INCREASES THE SUSCEPTIBILITY OF OFFSPRING TO CARDIORENAL DISEASE. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES DEMONSTRATE THAT OFFSPRING FROM OBESE PARENTS EXHIBIT EARLY RENAL DYSFUNCTION, HEIGHTENED KIDNEY INFLAMMATION, INCREASED EXPRESSION OF THE PURINERGIC RECEPTOR P2X7 (P2X7R), AND ALTERED MACROPHAGE IMMUNOMETABOLISM, EVEN WHEN MAINTAINED ON A NORMAL DIET. WE ALSO FOUND THAT GENETIC DELETION OF P2X7R, INCLUDING IN MACROPHAGES, ATTENUATES RENAL INFLAMMATION AND INJURY FOLLOWING ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY (AKI), SUGGESTING THAT EXCESSIVE P2X7R ACTIVATION CONTRIBUTES TO MALADAPTIVE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES IN OFFSPRING FROM OBESE PARENTS. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DETERMINE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH PARENTAL OBESITY PROGRAMS MACROPHAGE IMMUNOMETABOLISM TO INCREASE SUSCEPTIBILITY TO ACUTE KIDNEY INJURY (AKI) AND AGING-RELATED CKD. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT EXCESSIVE P2X7R ACTIVATION AND ALTERED MACROPHAGE METABOLISM PROMOTE A PRO-INFLAMMATORY MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPE THAT IMPAIRS KIDNEY REPAIR FOLLOWING AKI AND ACCELERATES PROGRESSION TO CKD. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL (1) DETERMINE HOW PARENTAL OBESITY ALTERS MACROPHAGE PHENOTYPE AND METABOLISM DURING AKI AND AGING-RELATED KIDNEY DYSFUNCTION; (2) DETERMINE THE CONTRIBUTION OF MACROPHAGE P2X7R ACTIVATION TO RENAL INFLAMMATION AND INJURY; AND (3) DETERMINE WHETHER TARGETING MACROPHAGE METABOLISM BY REDUCING GLYCOLYSIS AND PROMOTING OXIDATIVE METABOLISM IMPROVES KIDNEY REPAIR AND LIMITS CKD PROGRESSION.

description: ROLE OF AHR IN SIV-ASSOCIATED INTESTINAL DYSFUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY  DESPITE EFFECTIVE VIRAL CONTROL WITH ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART), PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV EXPERIENCE A HIGH PREVALENCE OF NONINFECTIOUS COMORBIDITIES INCLUDING METABOLIC, CARDIOVASCULAR, KIDNEY, & LIVER DISEASES, DRIVEN BY INCOMPLETE IMMUNE RESTORATION AND CHRONIC INFLAMMATION. INTESTINAL EPITHELIAL BARRIER DISRUPTION (IEBD) AND MICROBIAL TRANSLOCATION (MT) ARE CENTRAL TO THIS INFLAMMATORY STATE, YET THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS LINKING CHRONIC VIRAL INFECTION, GUT BARRIER DYSFUNCTION, AND SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. RECENT FINDINGS FROM OUR RHESUS MACAQUE MODEL OF ART-SUPPRESSED SIMIAN IMMUNODEFICIENCY VIRUS (SIV) INFECTION DEMONSTRATE THAT LOSS OF IL-17/IL-22 (TYPE-3) CYTOKINE FUNCTION IN GUT ΓΔ T CELLS CORRELATES WITH INCREASED IEBD, SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION, AND DISRUPTION OF THE GUT MICROBIOME. THESE DEFECTS ARE LINKED TO DYSREGULATION OF THE ARYL HYDROCARBON RECEPTOR (AHR)–RORΓT SIGNALING PATHWAY, CRITICAL REGULATORS OF MUCOSAL IMMUNE HOMEOSTASIS AND EPITHELIAL INTEGRITY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SIV-INDUCED AHR DYSREGULATION IMPAIRS TYPE-3 CYTOKINE RESPONSES, DISRUPTS GUT EPITHELIAL TIGHT JUNCTIONS, AND PROMOTES CHRONIC INFLAMMATION. WE FURTHER POSIT THAT THERAPEUTIC ACTIVATION OF AHR SIGNALING, COMBINED WITH IN VIVO ΓΔ T CELL MODULATION, CAN RESTORE EPITHELIAL INTEGRITY AND REDUCE INFLAMMATION.  THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEFINE THE ROLE OF AHR SIGNALING IN REGULATING INTESTINAL BARRIER INTEGRITY AND INFLAMMATION DURING ART-SUPPRESSED INFECTION. THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THIS STUDY ARE: (1) TO DEFINE HOW GUT AHR SIGNALING PRESERVES EPITHELIAL BARRIER INTEGRITY AND RESTRAINS SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION DURING CHRONIC SIV+ART INFECTION; AND (2) TO DETERMINE WHETHER THERAPEUTIC ACTIVATION OF AHR SIGNALING—VIA EXOGENOUS AHR LIGANDS AND IN VIVO ΓΔ T CELL STIMULATION—CAN RESTORE GUT BARRIER FUNCTION BY ENHANCING THE AHR–IL-22 IMMUNE AXIS. TO ACHIEVE THESE AIMS, WE WILL INTEGRATE MULTIOMICS PROFILING (TRANSCRIPTOMICS, METABOLOMICS, MICROBIOMICS) WITH MECHANISTIC STUDIES IN A PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT MODEL OF CHRONIC SIV+ART INFECTION, INCLUDING MACAQUES ON A HIGH-FAT, HIGH-CALORIE WESTERN DIET. OUR STUDIES WILL DISSECT THE INTERRELATIONSHIP BETWEEN AHR SIGNALING, TYPE-3 IMMUNITY, AND THE GUT MICROBIOME, AND PROVIDE MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO HOW GUT DYSFUNCTION SUSTAINS CHRONIC INFLAMMATION DESPITE ART.  SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TARGETING AHR PATHWAYS TO RESTORE INTESTINAL BARRIER FUNCTION, LIMIT SYSTEMIC INFLAMMATION, AND REDUCE THE LONG-TERM BURDEN OF COMORBIDITIES IN PLWH.

description: NON-INVASIVE RISK STRATIFICATION OF NEUROGENIC LOWER URINARY TRACT DYSFUNCTION WITH MAGNETIC RESONANCE FINGERPRINTING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  NEUROGENIC LOWER URINARY TRACT DYSFUNCTION (NLUTD) AFFECTS >80% OF THE 300,000 AMERICANS WITH SPINAL CORD INJURY (SCI), SIGNIFICANTLY IMPAIRING QUALITY OF LIFE AND POTENTIALLY LEADING TO RENAL FAILURE AND DEATH. CURRENT AMERICAN UROLOGICAL ASSOCIATION (AUA) GUIDELINES RECOMMEND STRATIFYING PATIENTS BY THEIR RISK OF DAMAGE TO THE UPPER URINARY TRACT. ALTHOUGH RISK STRATIFICATION CURRENTLY RELIES ON URODYNAMIC STUDIES (UDS) TO EVALUATE BLADDER FUNCTION, THESE TESTS ARE INVASIVE (INVOLVING URETHRAL AND RECTAL CATHETERIZATION), SUFFER FROM POOR REPRODUCIBILITY, ASSESS THE BLADDER UNDER NON-PHYSIOLOGIC CONDITIONS, AND CAN PROVOKE SEVERE REACTIONS (E.G., AUTONOMIC DYSREFLEXIA) IN SOME SCI PATIENTS. MOREOVER, NEITHER UDS NOR CONVENTIONAL DIAGNOSTIC IMAGING (ULTRASOUND OR CT) PROVIDE INFORMATION ABOUT UNDERLYING TISSUE-LEVEL BLADDER WALL REMODELING THAT DRIVES DISEASE PROGRESSION. WE PROPOSE A QUANTITATIVE MAGNETIC RESONANCE FINGERPRINTING (MRF) SOLUTION TO NON-INVASIVELY ASSESS BLADDER WALL TISSUE CHARACTERISTICS. THIS TECHNOLOGY WILL IMPROVE BIOLOGICAL UNDERSTANDING OF PATHOLOGICAL BLADDER WALL REMODELING IN NLUTD, ENABLE EARLIER INTERVENTION AND IMPROVED RISK STRATIFICATION, AND SUPPORT PERSONALIZED MANAGEMENT GUIDED BY DISCRETE PHENOTYPES (DEFINED BY QUANTITATIVE IMAGING BIOMARKERS). MRF IS AN INNOVATIVE MRI FRAMEWORK THAT PRODUCES CO-REGISTERED, QUANTITATIVE MAPS OF MULTIPLE TISSUE PROPERTIES FROM A SINGLE RAPID SCAN. ALTHOUGH MRF HAS BEEN DEMONSTRATED IN OTHER ORGANS, QUANTITATIVE MRI OF THE BLADDER REMAINS NASCENT DUE TO CHALLENGES OF IMAGING THE THIN BLADDER WALL. WE WILL OPTIMIZE MRF FOR SIMULTANEOUS, HIGH-RESOLUTION, 3D ISOTROPIC WHOLE-BLADDER MAPPING OF TISSUE PROPERTIES RELEVANT TO NLUTD, INCLUDING T1 (TO ASSESS CHRONIC INFLAMMATION AND FIBROSIS), T2 (TO EVALUATE ACUTE INFLAMMATION AND EDEMA), AND EXTRACELLULAR VOLUME FRACTION (ECV, A MARKER OF INTERSTITIAL EXPANSION AND FIBROSIS). IN AIM 1, WE WILL OPTIMIZE MRF FOR HIGH-RESOLUTION TISSUE CHARACTERIZATION WITH 3D WHOLE-BLADDER COVERAGE AND ESTABLISH NORMATIVE RANGES FOR BLADDER T1, T2, AND ECV VALUES IN HEALTHY ADULTS ACROSS THE AGE SPAN. IN AIM 2, WE WILL SCAN PATIENTS WITH SCI-RELATED NLUTD UNDERGOING CLINICAL UDS TO DEVELOP A PREDICTIVE MODEL THAT INCORPORATES QUANTITATIVE MRF BIOMARKERS AND LIMITED CLINICAL VARIABLES TO NON-INVASIVELY IDENTIFY PATIENTS WITH HIGH-RISK URODYNAMIC PROFILES, YIELDING A COMPOSITE RISK SCORE TERMED THE MRF VESICAL SCI (MIVESCI) SCORE. IN AIM 3, WE WILL PROSPECTIVELY EVALUATE THE MIVESCI SCORE IN A BLINDED STUDY, COMPARING DIAGNOSTIC ACCURACY AGAINST STANDARD AUA RISK STRATIFICATION BASED ON UDS. IN ADDITION, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE PROGNOSTIC UTILITY OF THE MIVESCI SCORE TO PREDICT CLINICAL PROGRESSION OF NLUTD OVER ONE YEAR. THIS RESEARCH HAS THE POTENTIAL TO USHER A SEISMIC SHIFT IN NLUTD MANAGEMENT. THE OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE A RAPID (≤30-MIN), NON-INVASIVE, PUSH-BUTTON MRF EXAM YIELDING QUANTITATIVE BLADDER WALL BIOMARKERS FOR NLUTD RISK STRATIFICATION AND PROGNOSTICATION. THIS WORK ALIGNS WITH CURRENT PRIORITIES IN NEUROUROLOGY, SEEKING TO SHIFT NLUTD CARE TOWARD OBJECTIVE, TISSUE-BASED PHENOTYPING TO PRESERVE LONG-TERM HEALTH OF THE URINARY TRACT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: METABOLOMICS-DRIVEN INSIGHTS INTO ULTRA-PROCESSED FOODS: IDENTIFYING HIGH-RISK UPF SUBTYPES FOR T2D PREVENTION - TYPE 2 DIABETES (T2D) IS A SIGNIFICANT PUBLIC HEALTH CONCERN, AFFECTING OVER 38 MILLION ADULTS IN THE U.S. AND COSTING THE ECONOMY NEARLY $413 BILLION ANNUALLY. DESPITE THE ESTABLISHED ROLE OF DIET IN T2D RISK, THE SPECIFIC CONTRIBUTIONS OF ULTRA-PROCESSED FOODS (UPFS) REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. UPFS, CHARACTERIZED BY INDUSTRIAL PROCESSING AND THE USE OF COSMETIC ADDITIVES FOR ENHANCED PALATABILITY AND EXTENDED SHELF-LIFE, ACCOUNT FOR APPROXIMATELY 58% OF CALORIC INTAKE IN THE U.S. POPULATION. ALTHOUGH SOME UPF SUBTYPES HAVE BEEN IMPLICATED IN INCREASING T2D RISK, OTHERS MAY BE RELATIVELY INERT OR EVEN BENEFICIAL, UNDERSCORING THE NEED FOR DISCERNING THEIR DISTINCT HEALTH EFFECTS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO CLARIFY THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN UPF CONSUMPTION AND T2D BY INTEGRATING A NOVEL CONTROLLED FEEDING TRIAL WITH LARGE-SCALE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL ANALYSES. IN A CROSSOVER FEEDING TRIAL DESIGN, 40 HEALTHY ADULTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN FOUR ISOCALORIC DIET PHASES: ONE CONTROL DIET AND THREE DIETS FOCUSED ON DIFFERENT UPF SUBTYPES-STARCHY AND REFINED GRAINS, MEATS AND FISH, AND DAIRY-BASED PRODUCTS. FOODS AND BEVERAGES WILL BE PROVIDED DURING THE STUDY, AND PARTICIPANTS WILL ATTEND WEEKLY CLINIC VISITS FOR IN-PERSON ASSESSMENTS AND BIOSPECIMEN COLLECTIONS. WE WILL OBTAIN METABOLOMIC PROFILING OF THE FASTING PLASMA SAMPLES AND CONDUCT DATA ANALYSES TO ISOLATE BIOMARKERS OF THE SPECIFIC UPF SUBTYPES, INDUSTRIAL ADDITIVES, OR PROCESSES. THESE BIOMARKERS WILL BE VALIDATED AGAINST DIETARY DATA IN WELL-CHARACTERIZED, CONTEMPORARY U.S.-BASED COHORTS. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE ASSOCIATION BETWEEN THESE MARKERS AND T2D RISK IN LONGITUDINAL OBSERVATIONAL STUDIES TO COST-EFFECTIVELY LEVERAGE EXISTING DATA FOR PLASMA METABOLOMIC PROFILES COLLECTED AT THE COHORTS' BASELINES, WITH FOLLOW-UP FOR INCIDENT T2D CASES, TO EVALUATE UPF-DERIVED METABOLITES WITH T2D RISK, CONTROLLING FOR OTHER DIETARY AND LIFESTYLE FACTORS. LEADING THIS RIGOROUS AND FEASIBLE EFFORT IS A TEAM OF MULTIPLE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS (MPLS) WHO BRING TOGETHER COMPLEMENTARY EXPERTISE. THIS INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM COMBINES PROFICIENCY IN NUTRITION SCIENCE, METABOLOMICS, EPIDEMIOLOGY, AND NUTRI-KINETIC FEEDING STUDIES, ENSURING A ROBUST APPROACH CRUCIAL FOR ACHIEVING THE PROJECT GOALS. BY IDENTIFYING METABOLOMICS ASSOCIATED WITH HIGH-RISK UPF SUBTYPES THIS RESEARCH WILL ENHANCE UNDERSTANDING OF THE BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS LINKING DIET TO T2D. THE FINDINGS ARE EXPECTED TO INFORM TARGETED DIETARY RECOMMENDATIONS AND POLICY INTERVENTIONS, FACILITATING HEALTHIER FOOD CHOICES AND PROMOTING EFFECTIVE REFORMULATIONS IN THE FOOD INDUSTRY. THROUGH THIS METHODOLOGICAL FRAMEWORK, OUR STUDY STRIVES TO ADDRESS CRITICAL GAPS IN THE EVIDENCE-BASE, ULTIMATELY REDUCING THE BURDEN OF T2D AND IMPROVED PUBLIC HEALTH OUTCOMES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TESTING STRATEGIES TO INCREASE THE IMPACT OF AN OBESITY PREVENTION INTERVENTION IN A COMMUNITY SETTING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AMONG YOUNG ADULT WOMEN 40% AND 12% HAD OBESITY AND SEVERE OBESITY IN 2017-2020, RESPECTIVELY, ELEVATING THEIR RISK OF CHRONIC DISEASE SUCH AS DIABETES AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. YET YOUNG ADULT WOMEN FACE BARRIERS TO PARTICIPATING IN INTERVENTIONS THAT PROMOTE HEALTHY WEIGHT AND PREVENT CHRONIC DISEASES SUCH AS DIABETES. TO ADDRESS THIS, OUR TEAM DEVELOPED AND TESTED THE EVIDENCE-BASED HEALTHY EATING AND ACTIVE LIVING TAUGHT AT HOME (HEALTH) INTERVENTION, DEMONSTRATING HEALTH’S EFFECTIVENESS TO REDUCE WEIGHT GAIN AMONG MOTHERS OF YOUNG CHILDREN AND TO PROMOTE HEALTHY GESTATIONAL WEIGHT GAIN AND POSTPARTUM WEIGHT LOSS, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH PARENTS AS TEACHERS (PAT). PAT IS A NATIONAL, EVIDENCE-BASED HOME VISITING ORGANIZATION WITH EXPERTISE IN ENGAGING AND SUPPORTING FAMILIES, ESPECIALLY THOSE NOT WELL REACHED BY THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM. PAT REACHES 73,283 FAMILIES NATIONWIDE THROUGH A NETWORK OF 4,300 PARENT EDUCATORS ACROSS 920 AFFILIATES. PAT HAS DECIDED TO DELIVER HEALTH AT SCALE, WHICH PRESENTS A UNIQUE AND TIMELY OPPORTUNITY TO DEVELOP AND TEST STRATEGIES TO SUPPORT SYSTEM-WIDE HEALTH IMPLEMENTATION. OUR PREVIOUS STUDIES DEMONSTRATED POSITIVE PERCEPTIONS OF HEALTH AMONG PARENT EDUCATORS AND MOTHERS AND IDENTIFIED POTENTIAL IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGIES TO SUPPORT ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND REACH. THE CURRENT STUDY WILL USE IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE, PARTICIPATORY SYSTEMS SCIENCE MODELING, PAT NATIONAL CENTER EXPERTISE AND ADMINISTRATIVE DATA, AND ADAPTIVE STRATEGY METHODS TO: 1) REFINE IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY BUNDLES TO PROMOTE HEALTH ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND REACH; 2) EVALUATE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THE STRATEGY BUNDLES REFINED IN AIM 1 ON HEALTH ADOPTION, IMPLEMENTATION, AND REACH AT 12- MONTHS USING A SEQUENTIAL MULTIPLE ASSIGNMENT RANDOMIZED TRIAL (SMART) DESIGN WITH 627 PAT AFFILIATES; AND 3) CHARACTERIZE THE MECHANISMS BEHIND IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY BUNDLES. THIS STUDY IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT AIMS TO EXPAND ACCESS TO AN EVIDENCE-BASED INTERVENTION TO PREVENT WEIGHT GAIN AND CHRONIC DISEASE SUCH AS DIABETES FOR MOTHERS THROUGH A NATIONAL HOME VISITING ORGANIZATION'S EXISTING NATIONAL SYSTEM AND INFRASTRUCTURE. IT BUILDS ON OUR TEAM’S EXTENSIVE EXPERIENCE IN APPLYING IMPLEMENTATION AND SYSTEM SCIENCE TO LEVERAGE THE STRENGTHS OF COMMUNITY-BASED ORGANIZATIONS TO REACH AND ENGAGE COMMUNITIES OFTEN NOT REACHED BY THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM. THIS INNOVATIVE RESEARCH 1) OPTIMIZES AND TESTS STRATEGY BUNDLES USING A SMART DESIGN IN REAL-WORLD SITES AND 2) EXPLORES MECHANISMS FOR BUNDLE EFFECTIVENESS. OUR RESULTS WILL IMPACT PUBLIC HEALTH BY REACHING MOTHERS NATIONWIDE WITH HEALTH AND EXPANDING IMPLEMENTATION STRATEGY AND MECHANISM EVIDENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE EFFECT OF VERAPAMIL ON BETA CELL FUNCTION IN ADOLESCENTS AND ADULTS WITH CYSTIC FIBROSIS-RELATED DYSGLYCEMIA - ABSTRACT CYSTIC FIBROSIS-RELATED DIABETES (CFRD) IS INCREASINGLY PREVALENT COMORBIDITY IN PEOPLE WITH CYSTIC FIBROSIS (PWCF). CFRD AND ITS PRECURSOR STATE, ABNORMAL GLUCOSE TOLERANCE (AGT), ARE ASSOCIATED WITH PROGRESSIVE PULMONARY DECLINE AND NUTRITIONAL DETERIORATION. INSULIN IS THE MAINSTAY OF TREATMENT FOR CFRD AND IS KNOWN TO IMPROVE LONG-TERM CLINICAL OUTCOMES. HOWEVER NO THERAPIES, INCLUDING INSULIN, CURRENTLY EXIST TO IMPROVE CLINICAL OUTCOMES IN AGT, LIMIT BETA CELL DYSFUNCTION, OR HALT PROGRESSION FROM AGT TO CFRD. OXIDATIVE STRESS IS KNOWN TO CONTRIBUTE TO BOTH TYPE 1 (T1D) AND TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS (T2D). THIOREDOXIN- INTERACTING PROTEIN (TXNIP), A KEY REGULATOR OF OXIDATIVE STRESS, IS UPREGULATED IN HYPERGLYCEMIC STATES AND CONTRIBUTES TO BETA CELL APOPTOSIS AND IMPAIRED INSULIN SECRETION. VERAPAMIL, A WIDELY USED CALCIUM CHANNEL BLOCKER, DOWNREGULATES TXNIP AND HAS SHOWN PROMISE IN PRESERVING BETA CELL FUNCTION IN T1D AND T2D. EMERGING DATA IMPLICATES OXIDATIVE STRESS AS A CENTRAL COMPONENT OF CYSTIC FIBROSIS PATHOLOGY, INCLUDING WITHIN THE CF PANCREATIC ISLETS. OXIDATIVE STRESS IN PWCF IS LIKELY EXACERBATED BY CHRONIC INFLAMMATION, IMPAIRED ANTIOXIDANT DEFENSES, AND CFTR-RELATED CELLULAR DYSFUNCTION. THE EFFECTS OF VERAPAMIL ON BETA CELL FUNCTION AND DYSGLYCEMIA IN PEOPLE WITH CF-RELATED DYSGLYCEMIA ARE CURRENTLY UNKNOWN. WE PROPOSE A PILOT PRE/POST INTERVENTIONAL CLINICAL TRIAL TO ASSESS THE EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF VERAPAMIL IN 30 ADOLESCENTS (>14 YEARS) AND ADULTS WITH CF AND AGT OR EARLY CFRD (NOT YET ON INSULIN). AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER VERAPAMIL (A) IMPROVES BETA CELL FUNCTION, MEASURED BY MIXED MEAL TOLERANCE TEST (MMTT)-STIMULATED C-PEPTIDE AREA UNDER THE CURVE (AUC), AND (B) REDUCES DYSGLYCEMIA, ASSESSED VIA CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORING (CGM), OVER A 6-MONTH TREATMENT PERIOD. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE THE SAFETY, TOLERABILITY, AND ADHERENCE TO VERAPAMIL IN THIS POPULATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT VERAPAMIL WILL IMPROVE BETA CELL FUNCTION AND GLYCEMIC CONTROL, WHILE DEMONSTRATING A FAVORABLE SAFETY PROFILE. THIS STUDY WILL ADDRESS A PRESSING UNMET NEED IN THE MANAGEMENT OF AGT AND EARLY CFRD AND PROVIDE FURTHER INSIGHT INTO THE MECHANISM OF CF-RELATED DYSGLYCEMIA. THIS PROPOSAL HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM THE MANAGEMENT OF AGT AND CFRD THROUGH A TARGETED, LOW RISK, LOW-COST INTERVENTION AIMED AT PRESERVING BETA CELL FUNCTION AND IMPROVING DYSGLYCEMIA, PROVIDING KEY PRELIMINARY DATA TO INFORM A LARGER PHASE 3 TRIAL IN THIS PATIENT POPULATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE ROLE OF MACROPHAGES IN STEATOTIC LIVER DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MACROPHAGES PLAY CRITICAL ROLES IN THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF STEATOTIC LIVER DISEASE (SLD), CONTRIBUTING TO TISSUE DAMAGE THROUGH INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES THAT PROMOTE HEPATOTOXICITY, RECRUIT ADDITIONAL PRO-INFLAMMATORY IMMUNE CELLS, AND DRIVE PROGRESSION TO FIBROSIS. PARADOXICALLY, MACROPHAGES CAN ALSO PROMOTE DISEASE RESOLUTION THROUGH THEIR IMMUNOREGULATORY FUNCTIONS, SUCH AS CLEARANCE OF DEAD OR DYING CELLS, PRODUCTION OF ANTI-INFLAMMATORY MEDIATORS, AND DEGRADATION OF EXCESS EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX. UNDERSTANDING HOW MACROPHAGES BALANCE THESE OPPOSING BEHAVIORS IS ESSENTIAL FOR DEVELOPING TARGETED THERAPIES FOR SLD. A KEY FACTOR IS THE EXPANSION OF LIVER MACROPHAGE HETEROGENEITY—BOTH IN POPULATION AND PHENOTYPE—DRIVEN IN PART BY RECRUITMENT AND DIFFERENTIATION OF PERIPHERAL BLOOD MONOCYTES. THIS EXPANDING HETEROGENEITY CORRELATES WITH SLD PROGRESSION AND CLINICAL SEVERITY. WHILE BLOCKING MACROPHAGE EXPANSION HAS SHOWN BENEFIT IN SOME EXPERIMENTAL MODELS, IT HAS PROVEN DETRIMENTAL IN OTHERS AND FAILED TO MEET EFFICACY ENDPOINTS IN A RECENT PHASE III TRIAL. THESE FINDINGS SUGGEST THAT THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES MUST SELECTIVELY INHIBIT INFLAMMATORY MACROPHAGES WHILE HARNESSING IMMUNOREGULATORY SUBSETS. HOWEVER, WE LACK A FUNDAMENTAL UNDERSTANDING OF HOW SPECIFIC MACROPHAGE POPULATIONS CONTRIBUTE TO SLD PROGRESSION. THIS PROPOSAL WILL USE EXPERIMENTAL MODELS TO DEFINE POPULATION-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS FOR THE TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR ATF3 IN REPRESSING SLD PROGRESSION. GIVEN THE LARGE-SCALE TRANSCRIPTIONAL DIFFERENCES AMONG LIVER MACROPHAGE SUBSETS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT ATF3 REGULATES DISTINCT FUNCTIONS IN SPECIFIC POPULATIONS. THIS HYPOTHESIS IS RELEVANT TO HUMAN HEALTH BECAUSE ATF3 EXPRESSION IN HUMAN LIVER BIOPSIES CORRELATES STRONGLY WITH SLD PROGRESSION TO STEATOHEPATITIS, AND ATF3 ACTIVITY IN GLOBAL MACROPHAGE POPULATIONS SUPPRESSES INFLAMMATION, ATHEROSCLEROSIS, AND SLD IN MURINE MODELS. HOWEVER, THE SUBSET-SPECIFIC REQUIREMENTS FOR TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS LIKE ATF3 REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THIS KNOWLEDGE IS CRITICAL, AS TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATORY MECHANISMS DIFFER ACROSS LIVER MACROPHAGE POPULATIONS AND DICTATE THEIR CONTRIBUTIONS TO SLD. SPECIFIC AIM 1 WILL INVESTIGATE THE ROLES OF ATF3 IN KUPFFER CELLS VERSUS OTHER LIVER MACROPHAGE SUBSETS IN PROTECTING AGAINST EXPERIMENTAL SLD AND STEATOHEPATITIS. SPECIFIC AIM 2 WILL DEFINE CONTRASTING REQUIREMENTS FOR ATF3 IN KUPFFER CELLS AND/OR OTHER LIVER MACROPHAGE SUBSETS IN ASSEMBLING A MULTI-LAYERED TRANSCRIPTIONAL PLATFORM THAT GOVERNS IMMUNOREGULATORY AND INFLAMMATORY GENE EXPRESSION. THESE GOALS WILL BE AIDED BY COMBINATIONS OF ESTABLISHED CRE DRIVERS, AS WELL AS A NOVEL INDUCIBLE CRE STRAIN PERMITTING TARGETED GENE ACTIVATION WITH IMPROVED SUBSET SPECIFICITY. FILLING THESE KNOWLEDGE GAPS WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HUMAN HEALTH BY IDENTIFYING TRANSCRIPTIONAL PATHWAYS SPECIFIC TO SLD-RELEVANT MACROPHAGE POPULATIONS THAT MAY BE TARGETED TO PROMOTE BENEFICIAL BEHAVIORS AND LIMIT DETRIMENTAL ONES.

description: BIOFILM-HOST DEFENSE MECHANISM UNDERLYING DIABETIC WOUND CHRONICITY - ABSTRACT BIOFILM INFECTIONS, STRUCTURED COMMUNITIES OF BACTERIA THAT ADHERE TO SURFACES AND ARE ENCASED IN A SELF-PRODUCED EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX EMBEDDED IN HOST TISSUE, ARE AN EMERGING AND INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED THREAT TO HUMAN HEALTH. THEY ARE COMMONLY ASSOCIATED WITH MEDICAL DEVICES SUCH AS CATHETERS AND IMPLANTS, AND DISEASES LIKE CYSTIC FIBROSIS AND CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE (COPD). UNDERSTANDING THE COMPLEX BIOLOGY OF BIOFILMS, THEIR FORMATION, AND THEIR ROLE IN PERSISTENT INFECTIONS IS CRUCIAL FOR ADVANCING MEDICAL PRACTICES AND IMPROVING PATIENT OUTCOMES. NON-HEALING DIABETIC ULCERS ARE COMPLICATED BY BIOFILM INFECTION. THE IMBALANCE BETWEEN THE THREAT OF BFI AND HOST DEFENSES IN FAVOR OF THE FORMER MAY DETERMINE WOUND CHRONICITY. BFI DIRECTLY CONTRIBUTES TO CHRONIC INFLAMMATION IN A WIDE RANGE OF DISORDERS SUCH AS CYSTIC FIBROSIS, IMPLANTS ETC. IN DIABETIC WOUNDS, BFI AND CHRONIC INFLAMMATION CO-EXIST. HOWEVER, UNDERLYING MECHANISMS REMAIN UNCLEAR. MACROPHAGES (MPH) ARE CENTRAL PLAYERS IN WOUND HOST DEFENSE AND SUBSEQUENT HEALING. THIS PROPOSAL RESTS ON OUR NOVEL OBSERVATION USING SCRNASEQ AND SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS THAT MPH, EXPOSED TO BFI, ACQUIRE A UNIQUE PHENOTYPE AND ARE FUNCTIONALLY COMPROMISED IN A WAY THAT LIMIT THE HEALING PROCESS. PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT THIS UNIQUE BIOFILM RESPONSIVE MPH AKA MPH-BFR (MARCOHI/PLIN2HI) IS ABUNDANT IN HUMAN CHRONIC WOUNDS WITH BFI. WE PROPOSE TO TEST THE OVERALL HYPOTHESIS THAT IN DFU, BFI LEADS TO EMERGENCE OF A UNIQUE BIOFILM RESPONSIVE MPH-BFR THAT IS DYSFUNCTIONAL LEADING TO PERSISTENT INFECTION, INFLAMMATION AND POOR DFU HEALING OUTCOMES. THE FOLLOWING AIMS ARE PROPOSED: AIM 1: DETERMINE MECHANISMS OF STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS (SA) BIOFILM INFECTION (BFI) IMPAIRMENT OF WOUND MACROPHAGE (MPH) EFFEROCYTOSIS THAT CAUSES CHRONIC INFLAMMATION AND IMPAIRED HEALING IN DIABETIC WOUNDS. AIM 2: TEST THE SIGNIFICANCE OF SA BIOFILM-INDUCED IMPAIRMENT OF LYSOSOMAL MATURATION, COMPROMISING MACROPHAGE BACTERIAL CLEARANCE, THUS ENABLING PERSISTENCE OF INTRACELLULAR BACTERIA WITH BIOFILM PHENOTYPE. AIM 3: STUDY IN DFU PATIENTS WHETHER THE PROPORTIONATE ABUNDANCE OF BIOFILM- RESPONSIVE: TOTAL MACROPHAGE (MPH-BFR: TOTAL MPH) IS HIGHER IN: (A) RESPONSE TO BIOFILM SEVERITY, AND (B) NON- HEALING OUTCOMES. UNDERSTANDING THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING BIOFILM-MEDIATED HOST DYSFUNCTIONS IN DFU IS CRUCIAL FOR EFFECTIVE MANAGEMENT AND TREATMENT STRATEGIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GLIAL NEURONAL CROSSTALK IN NEUROPATHIC PAIN AND DIABETES - NEUROPATHIC PAIN IS A CHRONIC, DEBILITATING CONDITION THAT AFFECTS MILLIONS OF AMERICANS AND REMAINS CHALLENGING TO TREAT DUE TO LIMITED THERAPEUTIC OPTIONS. EMERGING RESEARCH IMPLICATES GLIAL CELLS INCLUDING MICROGLIA, ASTROCYTES, AND SATELLITE GLIAL CELLS (SGCS) AS CRITICAL PLAYERS IN NEUROPATHIC PAIN PATHOGENESIS AND RESOLUTION. SGCS, WHICH TIGHTLY SURROUND SENSORY NEURONS IN THE DORSAL ROOT GANGLIA (DRG), BECOME REACTIVE UNDER NEUROPATHIC PAIN CONDITIONS SUCH AS NERVE INJURY, CHEMOTHERAPY-INDUCED PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY (CIPN), AND DIABETIC NEUROPATHY (DPN). THESE GLIAL-NEURONAL INTERACTIONS INFLUENCE BOTH PAIN SENSITIVITY AND NEURONAL RECOVERY. MITOCHONDRIA ARE THE POWERHOUSE OF THE CELL DUE TO THEIR CRUCIAL ROLE IN ENERGY PRODUCTION. MITOCHONDRIAL DYSREGULATION AND LIPID OXIDATIVE STRESS HAVE BEEN IMPLICATED IN NEURODEGENERATION, CELL DEATH (E.G., FERROPTOSIS), AND NEUROPATHIC PAIN. THE LONG AXONS OF PRIMARY SENSORY NEURONS FACE EXCEPTIONAL CHALLENGES IN MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSPORT AND DELIVERY. HOW SENSORY NEURONS SUSTAIN MITOCHONDRIAL HOMEOSTASIS IS UNCLEAR. ACCUMULATING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT MITOCHONDRIA CAN BE TRANSFERRED BETWEEN CELLS. THE GOAL OF THIS STUDY IS TO INVESTIGATE HOW MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSFER FROM SATELLITE GLIAL CELLS TO SENSORY NEURONS PROTECTS AGAINST NEUROPATHIC PAIN AND HOW DYSFUNCTION OF THIS PROCESS CONTRIBUTES TO DIABETIC PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY IN MOUSE AND HUMAN DISEASE MODELS. OUR GOAL WILL BE ACHIEVED BY ACCOMPLISHING THE FOLLOWING TWO SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 WILL EXAMINE THE ROLE OF SGC-NEURON MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSFER IN HEALTH AND NEUROPATHIC PAIN AFTER NERVE INJURY AND DIABETES IN MICE. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE MITOCHONDRIAL TRANSFER FROM SATELLITE GLIAL CELLS TO SENSORY NEURONS IN HUMAN DRG IN HEALTH AND DIABETES. WE WILL EMPLOY HIGH-RESOLUTION SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO DELINEATE GENE REGULATORY NETWORKS IN HUMAN DRG NEURONS AND GLIAL CELLS AND TO IDENTIFY DYSREGULATED PATHWAYS ASSOCIATED WITH DIABETIC NEUROPATHY. WE PROPOSE A MULTI-DISCIPLINARY APPROACH THAT COMBINES SCANNING AND TRANSMISSION ELECTRON MICROSCOPY, CALCIUM IMAGING, ADOPTIVE TRANSFER OF GLIAL CELLS AND MITOCHONDRIA, AND MEASUREMENTS OF EVOKED AND SPONTANEOUS PAIN. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL YIELD NOVEL MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO NEUROGLIAL INTERACTIONS IN NEUROPATHIC PAIN AND IDENTIFY POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR NEUROPATHIC PAIN AND DIABETIC NEUROPATHY.

description: THE IMPACT OF ADDING RESTRICTIONS AND INCENTIVES TO A MONTHLY FOOD BENEFIT PROGRAM TO IMPROVE DIET QUALITY: A LONGITUDINAL RCT - PROJECT SUMMARY UNHEALTHY DIET IS ONE OF THE LEADING MODIFIABLE CAUSES OF DEATH IN THE U.S. AND CONTRIBUTES TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF DIET-RELATED CHRONIC CONDITIONS LIKE TYPE 2 DIABETES AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. CRITICS HAVE LONG ARGUED THAT GIVEN THE POOR DIET QUALITY OF THE AVERAGE AMERICAN, FEDERAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS SHOULD PROHIBIT PURCHASES OF UNHEALTHY FOODS WITH PROGRAM BENEFITS. THE SUPPLEMENTAL NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM (SNAP) IS THE NATION'S LARGEST FOOD ASSISTANCE PROGRAM, SERVING ABOUT 42 MILLION LOW-INCOME AMERICANS MONTHLY. THIS PROGRAM HAS BEEN SHOWN TO HELP REDUCE FOOD INSECURITY. WITH A FEDERAL PRIORITY TO IMPROVE THE DIETS OF AMERICANS, USDA HAS GRANTED WAIVERS TO MANY STATES THAT PLACE RESTRICTIONS ON THE PURCHASE OF UNHEALTHY FOODS WITH SNAP BENEFITS. EVIDENCE IS LACKING ON HOW SUCH A CHANGE WOULD AFFECT PROGRAM RECIPIENTS, WHETHER THEY WOULD IMPROVE DIET QUALITY, OR HOW IT WOULD AFFECT PEOPLE'S EXPERIENCES WITH THE PROGRAM. TO ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING ON THE IMPACTS OF A MONTHLY FOOD BENEFIT PROGRAM WITH RESTRICTIONS AND INCENTIVES, OUR OVERALL OBJECTIVE IS TO EXAMINE THE DEGREE TO WHICH A MONTHLY FOOD BENEFIT INTERVENTION THAT HAS UNHEALTHY FOOD RESTRICTIONS ALONE OR IS PAIRED WITH HEALTHY FOOD INCENTIVES IMPROVES THE QUALITY OF FOOD AND BEVERAGE PURCHASES, QUALITY OF DIETARY INTAKE, AND PROGRAM EXPERIENCES. THE PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS IS THAT RESTRICTIONS WITH INCENTIVES WILL LEAD TO THE GREATEST IMPROVEMENTS IN HEALTHY FOOD PURCHASES AND INTAKE AND THE LARGEST REDUCTIONS IN SUGARY FOOD PURCHASES AND INTAKE, FOLLOWED BY THE RESTRICTIONS ALONE WHEN COMPARED TO THE CONTROL GROUP. STUDY PARTICIPANTS (N=357) WILL BE INCOME-ELIGIBLE FOR SNAP BUT NOT CURRENTLY ENROLLED. PARTICIPANTS IN THIS 12-WEEK STUDY (4 WEEKS BASELINE + 8 WEEKS INTERVENTION) WILL RECEIVE A MONTHLY FOOD BENEFIT FOR GROCERY SHOPPING EVERY FOUR WEEKS FOR 8 WEEKS. THEY WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO ONE OF THREE ARMS: 1) CONTROL; 2) UNHEALTHY FOOD RESTRICTIONS ALONE; OR 3) RESTRICTIONS WITH HEALTHY FOOD INCENTIVES. PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE A SURVEY AND TWO 24-HOUR DIETARY RECALLS AT BASELINE AND AGAIN AT THE END-OF-STUDY. THEY WILL TEXT THE STUDY TEAM RECEIPTS FROM ALL FOOD AND BEVERAGE PURCHASES FOR THE DURATION OF THE STUDY. A SUBSET (N=30) WILL COMPLETE QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS. THE FIRST AIM IS TO ASSESS HOW A MONTHLY FOOD BENEFIT PROGRAM AFFECTS THE NUTRITIONAL QUALITY OF FOOD AND BEVERAGE PURCHASES BY COMPARING (A) RESTRICTING BENEFITS FROM BUYING SWEETENED DRINKS, CANDY, AND PREPARED DESSERTS, AND (B) THE SAME RESTRICTIONS PLUS A HEALTHY FOOD INCENTIVE FOR A RANGE OF HEALTHY FOODS WITH (C) NO INCENTIVES OR RESTRICTIONS. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE SUCH A PROGRAM ON DIETARY QUALITY. THE THIRD AIM WILL EXPLORE THE ACCEPTABILITY AND EXPERIENCE OF SUCH A PROGRAM USING SEMI-STRUCTURED INTERVIEWS. THE INTERVIEWS WILL ANSWER HOW RECIPIENTS OF A MONTHLY FOOD BENEFIT PROGRAM WITH RESTRICTIONS AND/OR INCENTIVES EXPERIENCE THE MODEL AND HOW IT AFFECTS THEIR LIKELIHOOD OF APPLYING FOR THE PROGRAM. THE CONTRIBUTIONS FROM THESE AIMS WILL BE SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE THEY ARE EXPECTED TO PROVIDE STRONG EVIDENCE ON HOW PROPOSED CHANGES TO A NUTRITION ASSISTANCE PROGRAM AIMED AT IMPROVING DIET WOULD HAVE ON PURCHASING, INTAKE, AND PROGRAMMATIC EXPERIENCES AMONG A LOW-INCOME POPULATION.

recipient.name: RECTOR & VISITORS OF THE UNIVERSITY OF VIRGINIA

description: TARGETING CELL VOLUME REGULATORY MECHANISMS TO RESTRAIN ALDOSTERONE PRODUCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY SIGNIFICANCE: PRIMARY ALDOSTERONISM (PA) IS CHARACTERIZED BY EXCESSIVE ALDOSTERONE PRODUCTION THAT OCCURS INDEPENDENTLY OF THE RENIN-ANGIOTENSIN SYSTEM. IT STANDS AS THE MOST PREVALENT FORM OF ENDOCRINE-RELATED HYPERTENSION AND SIGNIFICANTLY ELEVATES THE RISK FOR CARDIOVASCULAR COMPLICATIONS AND STROKE. OFTEN DRIVEN BY GENETIC MUTATIONS THAT DISRUPT ION TRANSPORT AND INTRACELLULAR CALCIUM DYNAMICS, PA PRESENTS AN URGENT NEED FOR THERAPIES THAT DIRECTLY TARGET ITS MOLECULAR UNDERPINNINGS. RELEVANCE: BUILDING ON PRELIMINARY FINDINGS, THIS PROJECT EXPLORES VOLUME REGULATORY EFFECTORS (VRES) AS KEY MODULATORS OF CALCIUM OSCILLATIONS IN ZONA GLOMERULOSA (ZG) CELLS—THE CENTRAL SIGNAL INITIATING ALDOSTERONE SYNTHESIS. BY HARNESSING THE PHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESS OF CELL VOLUME REGULATION, WE AIM TO ATTENUATE ALDOSTERONE SECRETION THAT OCCURS INDEPENDENTLY OF RENIN SIGNALING. HYPOTHESIS: WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT ZG CELLULAR MACHINERY MAINTAINING CELL VOLUME HOMEOSTASIS REGULATES AUTONOMOUS AND STIMULI-EVOKED CALCIUM SIGNALING, AND THUS ALDOSTERONE PRODUCTION. SPECIFICALLY, WE PROPOSE THAT TWO WELL-ESTABLISHED CELL VOLUME REGULATORS, THE NA+-K+-CL- COTRANSPORTER 1 (NKCC1) AND THE VOLUME- REGULATED ANION CHANNEL (VRAC), ARE CO-EXPRESSED IN BOTH MOUSE AND HUMAN ZG CELLS AND CAN BE TARGETED TO MEDIATE ZG CELL STEROIDOGENESIS. INNOVATION: OUR APPROACH UTILIZES CHANGES IN EXTRACELLULAR OSMOLARITY TO TRIGGER VOLUME REGULATORY RESPONSES, COMBINED WITH PHARMACOLOGICAL AND GENETIC MANIPULATION OF NKCC1 AND VRAC IN ZG CELLS, BOTH EX VIVO AND IN VIVO. WE UTILIZE INNOVATIVE MOUSE MODELS OF PA AND IMAGING TECHNIQUES TO VALIDATE OUR HYPOTHESIS. AIMS: (1) DETERMINE WHETHER OSMOTIC PERTURBATION ALTERS SPECIFIC ALDOSTERONE SIGNALING PATHWAYS. (2) TO RESOLVE THE ROLE OF VRES IN CONTROLLING THE STEADY-STATE RESPONSIVENESS OF ZG CELLS TO AUTONOMOUS AND STIMULI-EVOKED CALCIUM ACTIVITY AND ALDOSTERONE PRODUCTION, (3) TO ASSESS THE IN VIVO EFFICACY OF TARGETING VRES TO SUPPRESS ALDOSTERONE AUTONOMY. LONG-TERM GOALS: THIS RESEARCH AIMS TO IDENTIFY A NOVEL MECHANISM TO SUPPRESS ALDOSTERONE PRODUCTION AND IDENTIFY NOVEL MOLECULAR TARGETS TO RESTRAIN ALDO-AUTONOMY FOR TREATMENT OF PA-ASSOCIATED HYPERTENSION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SCH: ADVANCING AI FAIRNESS FOR TRUSTWORTHY LIVER ORGAN ALLOCATION - PROJECT SUMMARY (SEE INSTRUCTIONS):  LIVER DISEASES, INCLUDING CIRRHOSIS AND LIVER CANCER, AFFECT MORE THAN 100 MILLION INDIVIDUALS IN THE UNITED STATES AND CONTRIBUTE TO  APPROXIMATELY 50,000 DEATHS ANNUALLY. LIVER TRANSPLANTATION REMAINS THE MOST EFFECTIVE TREATMENT FOR MANY PATIENTS WITH END-STAGE  LIVER DISEASE; HOWEVER, THE PERSISTENT SHORTAGE OF DONOR ORGANS LEAVES THOUSANDS OF PATIENTS ON TRANSPLANT WAITING LISTS EACH YEAR.  CURRENT LIVER ALLOCATION SYSTEMS ARE LARGELY DRIVEN BY MEDICAL URGENCY BUT DO NOT FULLY ACCOUNT FOR FACTORS BEYOND MEDICAL URGENCY  THAT INFLUENCE ACCESS TO TRANSPLANTATION AND TRANSPLANT OUTCOMES. AS AI IS INCREASINGLY ADOPTED TO SUPPORT ORGAN ALLOCATION DECISIONS,  THERE IS GROWING INTEREST IN LEVERAGING AI FAIRNESS METHODOLOGIES TO ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES. HOWEVER, EXISTING AI FAIRNESS  APPROACHES FACE IMPORTANT LIMITATIONS. MOST METHODS ASSUME COMPLETE OUTCOME INFORMATION, DESPITE TRANSPLANT DATA BEING INHERENTLY  CENSORED BECAUSE MANY PATIENT OUTCOMES ARE ONLY PARTIALLY OBSERVED. IN ADDITION, THEY OFTEN FOCUS EITHER ON ENSURING CONSISTENT  TREATMENT OF SIMILAR PATIENTS OR ON MAINTAINING FAIRNESS ACROSS PATIENT GROUPS, WITHOUT ACCOUNTING FOR THE INTERACTION BETWEEN THESE  OBJECTIVES. THEY ALSO PROVIDE LIMITED SUPPORT FOR UNDERSTANDING FAIRNESS–UTILITY TRADE-OFFS IN A MANNER THAT CLINICIANS CAN READILY  INTERPRET. TO ADDRESS THESE CHALLENGES, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ADVANCE AI FAIRNESS FOR TRUSTWORTHY LIVER ORGAN ALLOCATION UNDER CENSORED  OUTCOMES. SPECIFICALLY, AIM 1 WILL DEVELOP METHODOLOGIES FOR INDIVIDUAL FAIRNESS WITH GROUP AWARENESS UNDER CENSORING, ENABLING THE  IDENTIFICATION AND MITIGATION OF PATIENT-LEVEL UNFAIRNESS WHILE QUANTIFYING ASSOCIATED GROUP-LEVEL EFFECTS. AIM 2 WILL DEVELOP  METHODOLOGIES FOR GROUP FAIRNESS WITH INDIVIDUAL CONSTRAINTS UNDER CENSORING, QUANTIFYING GROUP-LEVEL FAIRNESS OUTCOMES WHILE LIMITING  EXCESSIVE FAIRNESS LOSSES EXPERIENCED BY INDIVIDUAL PATIENTS. AIM 3 WILL DEVELOP A UNIFIED FRAMEWORK THAT INTEGRATES INDIVIDUAL  FAIRNESS, GROUP FAIRNESS, AND CLINICAL UTILITY, TOGETHER WITH INTERPRETABLE TOOLS THAT ENABLE CLINICIANS TO UNDERSTAND FAIRNESS–UTILITY TRADE OFFS AND ALLOCATION DECISIONS. THE PROPOSED METHODS WILL BE EVALUATED USING DATA FROM THE SCIENTIFIC REGISTRY OF TRANSPLANT RECIPIENTS  (SRTR) AND VALIDATED THROUGH COLLABORATION WITH THE UNIVERSITY OF PITTSBURGH MEDICAL CENTER (UPMC), ONE OF THE NATION'S LEADING  TRANSPLANT CENTERS. BY ADVANCING FAIRNESS-AWARE AND INTERPRETABLE AI METHODS FOR CENSORED CLINICAL DATA, THIS PROJECT HAS THE POTENTIAL  TO IMPROVE ORGAN ALLOCATION DECISIONS, SUPPORT PATIENT SURVIVAL, AND ESTABLISH A FOUNDATION FOR THE BROADER DEPLOYMENT OF AI FAIRNESS  METHODOLOGIES IN HIGH-STAKES HEALTHCARE SETTINGS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PRENATAL EXPOSURE TO AMBIENT BTEX AND BIRTH OUTCOMES: MODEL DEVELOPMENT AND EPIDEMIOLOGIC ANALYSIS - ABSTRACT  THE GOAL OF THIS STUDY IS TO INVESTIGATE THE IMPACT OF PRENATAL EXPOSURE TO BTEX COMPOUNDS (BENZENE, TOLUENE, ETHYLBENZENE, AND XYLENE ISOMERS) AND THEIR MIXTURE ON BIRTH OUTCOMES, INCLUDING BIRTH WEIGHT, LOW BIRTH WEIGHT, PRETERM BIRTH AND PRETERM BIRTH SUBTYPES. BTEX COMPOUNDS ARE HAZARDOUS AIR POLLUTANTS KNOWN TO ORIGINATE FROM TRAFFIC AND INDUSTRIAL EMISSIONS. COMPARED TO CRITERIA POLLUTANTS LIKE PARTICULATE MATTERS, FEWER EPIDEMIOLOGIC STUDIES HAVE BEEN DEDICATED TO ANALYZING THE EFFECTS OF BTEX. WHILE LABORATORY STUDIES HAVE FOUND THAT LOW-LEVEL EXPOSURE CAN ADVERSELY IMPACT FETAL DEVELOPMENT, HISTORIC EPIDEMIOLOGIC EXPOSURE METRICS HAVE NOT POSSESSED ADEQUATE SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL RESOLUTION TO UNDERSTAND HOW THESE CHEMICALS AFFECT INFANT BIRTH OUTCOMES ON A POPULATION LEVEL. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, WE PROPOSE TO DEVELOP A HIGH-RESOLUTION EXPOSURE MODEL FOR BTEX COMPOUNDS ACROSS THE SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES FROM 2011 TO 2023. THIS MODEL WILL INTEGRATE A NUMBER OF STATE-OF-THE-ART MODELING APPROACHES, INCLUDING DISPERSION MODELS, CHEMICAL TRANSPORT MODELS, LAND- USE DATA, AND MACHINE LEARNING TECHNIQUES. THE BTEX EXPOSURE METRICS GENERATED FROM THIS MODEL WILL BE LINKED TO A LARGE ADMINISTRATIVE BIRTH DATASET RECORDED AND RETAINED BY THE TEXAS DEPARTMENT OF STATE HEALTH SERVICES FOR SUBSEQUENT EPIDEMIOLOGIC ANALYSIS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL ASSIGN TRIMESTER-SPECIFIC AVERAGE EXPOSURES BASED ON GEOCODED MATERNAL RESIDENTIAL ADDRESSES AND DATES OF BIRTH FOR ALL LIVE BIRTHS IN TEXAS BETWEEN 2020 AND 2022, AN ESTIMATED COHORT OF APPROXIMATELY 1 MILLION BIRTHS. GIVEN TEXAS’S LARGE AND DIVERSE POPULATION, ALONG WITH ITS ABUNDANT BTEX EMISSION SOURCES (E.G., REFINERIES AND HIGHWAYS), THIS DATASET WILL PROVIDE ROBUST RESULTS. MULTIVARIABLE LINEAR, LOGISTIC REGRESSION, AND GEOGRAPHICALLY WEIGHTED MODELS WILL BE USED TO ESTIMATE THE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN INDIVIDUAL BTEX COMPOUND EXPOSURES AND BIRTH OUTCOMES OF INTEREST. TO EVALUATE THE JOINT EFFECTS OF BTEX MIXTURES AND IDENTIFY CRITICAL EXPOSURE WINDOWS, WE WILL APPLY A NEWLY DEVELOPED EXTENSION OF THE QUANTILE G-COMPUTATION METHOD, WHICH ENABLES SIMULTANEOUS ASSESSMENT OF MULTIPLE CORRELATED POLLUTANTS AND THEIR TIME-SPECIFIC EFFECTS. OVERALL, BY LEVERAGING HIGH-RESOLUTION EXPOSURE ESTIMATES, LARGE BIRTH DATA, AND ADVANCED STATISTICS TOOLS, THIS STUDY WILL GENERATE NOVEL EVIDENCE ON THE CHILD HEALTH RISKS OF AMBIENT BTEX EXPOSURE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXAMINING PATHWAYS OF PFAS EXPOSURE AND THEIR IMPACTS ON HYPERLIPIDEMIA IN A RURAL COMMUNITY IMPACTED BY LAND SPREADING - ABSTRACT PER- AND POLYFLUOROALKYL SUBSTANCES (PFAS) ARE A LARGE CLASS OF SYNTHETIC “FOREVER CHEMICALS” THAT PERSIST IN THE ENVIRONMENT AND HUMAN BODY, AND ARE LINKED TO KIDNEY AND LIVER CANCERS, THYROID DISEASE, LIVER DISEASE, AND HYPERLIPIDEMIA. AN UNDER-RECOGNIZED SOURCE OF PFAS EXPOSURE IS FROM SLUDGE AND BIOSOLIDS FROM WASTEWATER TREATMENT AND INDUSTRIAL PROCESSES, WHICH CAN BE APPLIED ON AGRICULTURAL FIELDS AS FERTILIZER. AS A RESULT, RURAL AMERICANS IN AGRICULTURAL SETTINGS ARE DISPROPORTIONATELY AT RISK OF CONTAMINATED FOOD AND WATER FROM LAND SPREADING. ABOUT 60% OF BIOSOLIDS GENERATED IN THE UNITED STATES ARE LAND- APPLIED, YET THE HEALTH IMPLICATIONS FOR RURAL RESIDENTS REMAIN LARGELY UNKNOWN. THREE BARRIERS LIMIT PROGRESS. FIRST, LIPID METABOLISM IS A KEY MECHANISM BY WHICH PFAS EXPOSURE MAY LEAD TO DOWNSTREAM HEALTH OUTCOMES. YET PRIOR HUMAN HEALTH STUDIES HAVE EXAMINED ONLY A HANDFUL OF LEGACY PFAS, DESPITE >10,000 PFAS EXISTING. SECOND, INDUSTRY HAS REPLACED LEGACY PFAS WITH PRECURSOR COMPOUNDS SUCH AS POLYFLUOROALKYL PHOSPHATE ESTERS (PAPS), WHICH CAN BIO-TRANSFORM INTO PERFLUOROOCTANOIC ACID (PFOA), A CLASSIFIED CARCINOGENIC. SOME INTERMEDIATES ARE ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE MORE TOXIC THAN THEIR END PRODUCTS, YET LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THEIR REAL-WORLD CONTRIBUTION TO HUMAN EXPOSURE. THIRD, BIOMONITORING DATA ARE LARGELY FROM OCCUPATIONAL OR URBAN SETTINGS, OVERLOOKING RURAL PATHWAYS OF EXPOSURE WHERE PFAS ACCUMULATE IN SOIL, GROUNDWATER, SURFACE WATER, AND LOCALLY PRODUCED FOOD. WISCONSIN PROVIDES A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS AS IT HAS SOME OF THE NATION’S HIGHEST PFAS LEVELS IN PRIVATE WELLS (>36,000 PPT), WITH CONTAMINATION LINKED TO BIOSOLID AND PAPERMILL SLUDGE LAND SPREADING. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT PRECURSOR PFAS SIGNIFICANTLY CONTRIBUTE TO THE PERSISTENCE AND BURDEN OF PFAS EXPOSURE, AND THAT ONGOING EXPOSURE VIA LOCAL FOOD, WATER, AIR, AND DUST CONTRIBUTES TO ELEVATED LIPID LEVELS. AIM 1 WILL IDENTIFY ONGOING ROUTES OF EXPOSURE TO PFAS IN AN IMPACTED RURAL COMMUNITY BY ENROLLING 400 RESIDENTS, COLLECTING ENVIRONMENTAL AND BLOOD SAMPLES, QUANTIFYING TARGETED AND UNTARGETED PFAS, AND APPLYING TOXICOKINETIC MODELING. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PFAS MIXTURES AND LIPID PROFILES, TESTING WHETHER INCLUSION OF PREVIOUSLY UNIDENTIFIED PFAS STRENGTHENS ASSOCIATIONS WITH CHOLESTEROL, TRIGLYCERIDES, AND SPECIFIC LIPOPROTEIN SUBFRACTIONS. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS OF HIGH IMPACT AND WILL SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCE THE FIELD BY CLARIFYING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HUMAN EXPOSURE TO PFAS FROM CONTAMINATED LAND SPREADING AND KEY RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN PFAS AND HYPERLIPIDEMIA. FINDINGS WILL INFORM INTERVENTIONS AIMED AT REDUCING EXPOSURE AMONG RURAL RESIDENTS IMPACTED BY PFAS EXPOSURE FROM LAND SPREADING, AND INTERVENTIONS AIMED AT PREVENTING OR TREATING ELEVATED CHOLESTEROL FROM HISTORIC OR CURRENT PFAS EXPOSURE – THEREBY REDUCING RISKS OF DOWNSTREAM CHRONIC HEALTH CONDITIONS.

description: OXIDATIVE STRESS AND NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME ACTIVATION IN EYE LENS PATHOBIOLOGY DURING AGING - ABSTRACT: DESPITE A WEALTH OF REPORTS DEMONSTRATING A LINK BETWEEN INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE AND AGE-RELATED DISEASES (ARDS), THE FACTORS THAT CAUSALLY LINK TO AGING PATHOLOGIES ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. RECENTLY, INCREASING LEVELS OF OXIDATIVE STRESS-DRIVEN NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME ACTIVATION HAS BEEN IMPLICATED AS A MAJOR RISK FACTOR FOR AGING- RELATED DISEASES. THE DYSREGULATION OF ANTIOXIDANT PATHWAY AND REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES (ROS) AMPLIFICATION IN AGING HAVE NOW BEEN FOUND TO EXACERBATE NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME ACTIVATION-MEDIATED INFLAMMATORY RESPONSES AND DEVELOPMENT OF AGE-RELATED BLINDING DISORDERS. THE DETAILED MOLECULAR PATHWAYS UNDERLYING THIS ADVERSE SIGNALING AND CAUSES FOR ROS AMPLIFICATION AND RELATED OCULAR PATHOLOGIES WITH ADVANCING AGE, HOWEVER, REMAIN ELUSIVE. RECENTLY, USING EYE LENS/LENS EPITHELIAL CELLS (LECS) AS A MODEL, I FOUND THAT AGING LECS UNDER CONDITIONS OF OXIDATIVE STRESS REVEAL A DRAMATIC INCREASE IN TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR KLF9 (KRUPPEL-LIKE FACTOR 9) EXPRESSION, RESULTING IN KLF9-DEPENDENT ANTIOXIDANT GENES SUPPRESSION WITH ROS AMPLIFICATION AND CELL DAMAGE. HOWEVER, THIS ADVERSE SIGNALING ENSUES IN AGING LENSES/LECS, CAUSING ABERRANT TXNIP (THIOREDOXIN INTERACTING PROTEIN) EXPRESSION AND NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME ACTIVATION-DRIVEN AGING PATHOLOGIES OR CELL DEATH-TYPE ARE NOT EXPLORED. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA USING EACH OF THESE FACTORS SHOW THAT: 1) INCREASED ROS LEVEL IS ASSOCIATED WITH NF-ΚB ACTIVATION-DEPENDENT INCREASED KLF9 EXPRESSION IN AGING; 2) LIKE OXIDATIVE STRESS OR AGING LECS, LECS OVEREXPRESSING KLF9 DISPLAY EXCESSIVE ROS AND NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME ACTIVATION-EVOKED SIGNALING; 3) AGING LECS SHOW INCREASED TXNIP EXPRESSION WITH REDUCED LEVELS OF THIOREDOXIN (TRX1) AND NRF2 (NFE2-RELATED FACTOR 2), A REPRESSOR OF TXNIP; 4) IN CONTRAST TO AGING LECS AND LECS OVEREXPRESSING KLF9, THESE LECS WHEN TREATED WITH AN ANTIOXIDANT, LIKE PRDX6 (PEROXIREDOXIN 6) DO NOT SHOW NF-ΚB/KLF9/NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME AXIS- MEDIATED INFLAMMATORY SIGNALING. BACKED WITH THESE OBSERVATIONS, THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS PROPOSAL IS THAT AGING/OXIDATIVE STRESS CAUSES ABERRANT EXPRESSION OF KLF9 VIA NF-ΚB, AND THAT SUBSEQUENTLY RESULTS IN KLF9- MEDIATED ANTIOXIDANT SUPPRESSION AND ROS AMPLIFICATION, LEADING TO NLRP3 ACTIVATION-MEDIATED PATHOLOGIES VIA THE FEED-FORWARD VICIOUS CYCLES WITHIN LENS MICROENVIRONMENT (THAT ARE OPERATIVE DURING AGING AND OXIDATIVE STRESS WITH INCREASE TXNIP). USING IN-VITRO AND IN-VIVO APPROACHES, WE WILL TEST OUR HYPOTHESIS VIA THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) EXPLORE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING NF-ΚB-KLF9-ANTIOXIDANT AXIS MEDIATED INDUCTION OF NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME INFLAMMATORY PATHWAY IN AGING/OXIDATIVE STRESS IN-VITRO; 2) DETERMINE THAT KLF9’S ABERRANT EXPRESSION ALTERS ITS TRANSCRIPTIONAL REPROGRAMMING, LEADING TO NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME ACTIVATION PATHWAY; 3) DETERMINE THE MECHANISM(S) INVOLVED IN THE PROGRESSION OF NF-ΚB-KLF9-AND NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME-MEDIATED SIGNALING IN VIVO IN A MOUSE MODEL OF AGE-RELATED CATARACT. UNDERSTANDING THE MECHANISMS RESPONSIBLE FOR OXIDATIVE/AGING-INDUCED NLRP3 INFLAMMASOME ACTIVATION-MEDIATED LENS PATHOBIOLOGY WILL SET THE STAGE FOR FUTURE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL THERAPEUTICS AIMED AT DAMPING OXIDATIVE/AGING/NLRP3-ASSOCIATED CATARACT FORMATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DECODING CURVATURE-DEPENDENT KERATOCONUS PATHOLOGY USING AN ENGINEERED HUMAN CORNEA CHIP - PROJECT SUMMARY KERATOCONUS (KC) IS A PROGRESSIVE CORNEAL DISORDER AFFECTING MILLIONS WORLDWIDE, CHARACTERIZED BY CORNEAL THINNING, PROTUSION, AND IRREGULAR ASTIGMATISM. DESPITE ITS PREVALENCE, THE PRECISE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING KC REMAIN UNCLEAR, HINDERING THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS BEYOND CORNEAL CROSS-LINKING AND TRANSPLANTATION. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP AN ADVANCED IN VITRO KC MODEL USING A MICROFABRICATED ORGAN CHIP PLATFORM, ADDRESSING THE LIMITATIONS OF CURRENT ANIMAL MODELS AND PROVIDING A MORE ACCURATE, ETHICALLY SOUND, AND CONTROLLABLE PLATFORM FOR STUDYING KC PATHOGENESIS. OUR APPROACH WILL ESTABLISH AN ANATOMICALLY AND PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT CORNEA CHIP, PROVIDING EXPERIMENTAL ACCESS TO MECHANISTIC INVESTIGATIONS OF INTERACTIONS BETWEEN CORNEAL EPITHELIAL, STROMAL, AND ENDOTHELIAL CELLS IN THE CONTEXT OF KC.  THE PROJECT CONSISTS OF THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) INVESTIGATE CURVATURE-DEPENDENT CELLULAR RESPONSES IN EPITHELIAL, STROMAL, AND ENDOTHELIAL CELLS USING A CURVATURE ARRAY CHIP, IDENTIFYING MECHANOTRANSDUCTION PATHWAYS DRIVING PATHOLOGICAL REPROGRAMMING AND VALIDATING THERAPEUTIC TARGETS THROUGH GENE KNOCKOUT STUDIES; 2) ENGINEER BIOMIMETIC INTERFACIAL MEMBRANES (EPITHELIAL BASEMENT MEMBRANE AND DESCEMET'S MEMBRANE) USING CO-CULTURE APPROACHES TO INVESTIGATE HOW GEOMETRIC STRESS CONCENTRATIONS DISRUPT MEMBRANE INTEGRITY AND DISTINGUISH ACTIVE PATHWAY-MEDIATED FROM PASSIVE MECHANICAL DAMAGE; AND 3) DEVELOP AN INTEGRATED MULTI-LAYER CORNEA CHIP WITH CONTROLLABLE CURVATURE TO INVESTIGATE MECHANOBIOLOGICAL CROSSTALK, VALIDATE THE PLATFORM COMPREHENSIVELY, AND TEST THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS TARGETING MECHANOTRANSDUCTION AND MATRIX DEGRADATION PATHWAYS AT DIFFERENT DISEASE STAGES. BY COMBINING EXPERTISE IN BIOENGINEERING, OPHTHALMOLOGY, AND CORNEAL BIOLOGY, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO CREATE A PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT KC MODEL THAT WILL ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE PERPETUATION CYCLE MECHANISMS, IDENTIFY MECHANOBIOLOGICAL TIPPING POINTS, AND FACILITATE THE DISCOVERY OF THERAPEUTIC TARGETS FOR INTERRUPTING THIS PROGRESSIVE CORNEAL DISORDER.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MACHINE LEARNING-DRIVEN MULTIFUNCTIONAL PEPTIDE ENGINEERING FOR SUSTAINED INTRAOCULAR PRESSURE LOWERING - PROJECT SUMMARY GLAUCOMA IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF IRREVERSIBLE VISION LOSS WORLDWIDE. INTRAOCULAR PRESSURE (IOP) REDUCTION IS THE ONLY CLINICALLY PROVEN APPROACH TO PREVENT GLAUCOMATOUS VISION LOSS, AND EYE DROPS ARE THE MOST COMMON MODALITY FOR IOP LOWERING. HOWEVER, POOR PATIENT ADHERENCE TO EYE DROP REGIMENS IS A SIGNIFICANT BARRIER TO EFFECTIVE IOP REDUCTION AND PREVENTION OF DISEASE PROGRESSION. AS GLAUCOMA IS A CHRONIC DISEASE THAT TYPICALLY REQUIRES TREATMENT FOR YEARS OR EVEN DECADES, THERE IS CONSIDERABLE INTEREST IN SUSTAINED DRUG DELIVERY PLATFORMS FOR GLAUCOMA TREATMENT. THE MOST COMMON APPROACH FOR DEVELOPING SUSTAINED DELIVERY SYSTEMS IS TO EMPLOY A DEGRADABLE OR NON-DEGRADABLE MATRIX THAT BOTH CONTAINS THE DRUG AND CONTROLS THE RATE AT WHICH DRUG EXITS THE DEVICE. EVEN FOR A BIODEGRADABLE MATRIX, THE RATE OF MATRIX DEGRADATION MAY BE MUCH SLOWER THAN THE DURATION OF DRUG RELEASE, RESULTING IN ACCUMULATION OF EXCIPIENTS AND OCULAR SIDE EFFECTS. OUR APPROACH UTILIZES PEPTIDE ENGINEERING TO IMPART MELANIN BINDING PROPERTIES TO PEPTIDE-DRUG CONJUGATES, AND ALLOWS FOR INJECTION IN LIQUID FORM WITH A SMALL GAUGE NEEDLE WITHOUT THE NEED FOR AN IMPLANT. WE DEVELOPED AN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) METHODOLOGY THAT ADAPTS THE SUPER LEARNING (SL) APPROACH TO ENGINEER MULTIFUNCTIONAL PEPTIDES THAT EFFICIENTLY ENTER CELLS, BIND TO MELANIN, AND HAVE LOW CYTOTOXICITY. WE DEMONSTRATE HERE THAT HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING FOR MELANIN BINDING COMBINED WITH THE SL MODEL IDENTIFIED 780 PEPTIDES THAT OUT-PERFORMED PEPTIDES REPORTED IN THE LITERATURE. WHEN A PROMISING 12-MER PEPTIDE WAS CONJUGATED TO BRIMONIDINE (AVAILABLE AS A TOPICAL DROP THAT MUST BE ADMINISTERED 3X/DAY), THE RESULT WAS IOP LOWERING FOR UP TO 18 DAYS WITH A SINGLE INJECTION. HERE, WE WILL USE OUR HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING/SL METHODOLOGY TO FURTHER IMPROVE THE PHYSICOCHEMICAL PROPERTIES OF THE ENGINEERED PEPTIDES TO PRODUCE PEPTIDE-DRUG CONJUGATES THAT LAST UP TO A FEW MONTHS WITH A SINGLE INJECTION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT INCREASING THE PEPTIDE LENGTH TO 18- AND 24-MERS WILL ALLOW FOR INCREASED MELANIN BINDING CAPACITY AND PEPTIDE-DRUG CONJUGATE SOLUBILITY, FURTHER INCREASING THE INTRAOCULAR LOADING AND DURATION OF THERAPEUTIC EFFECT COMPARED TO THE 12-MER. WE ANTICIPATE THAT SUSTAINED IOP LOWERING WILL BE ACHIEVED WITH IMPROVED OCULAR SAFETY. AIM 1 WILL INCLUDE DEVELOPING A GENERATIVE MACHINE LEARNING MODEL THAT WILL BE USED TO EXPAND THE PEPTIDE LIBRARY TO 18- AND 24-MERS WITH FURTHER IMPROVED PROPERTIES. WE WILL IDENTIFY AT LEAST 3 NEW PEPTIDE-DRUG CONJUGATES USING A VARIETY OF IN VITRO AND COMPUTATION METHODS TO THEN TEST IN AIM 2 FOR PHARMACOKINETICS AND PHARMACODYNAMICS IN RABBITS. TWO OF THESE PEPTIDE- DRUG CONJUGATES WILL THEN BE TESTED HEAD-TO-HEAD WITH THE 12-MER PEPTIDE-DRUG CONJUGATE IN AIM 3 FOR PHARMACODYNAMICS AND SAFETY WITH REPEATED INJECTION FOR A TOTAL OF 1 YEAR.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENABLING TECHNOLOGIES FOR PRE-CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH USING 3-DIMENSIONAL ADULT RETINA TISSUE CULTURE - ABSTRACT: 3-DIMENSIONAL (3D) CULTURES OF ANIMAL- OR HUMAN-DERIVED ADULT RETINAL TISSUES OFFER PHYSIOLOGICAL COMPLEXITY AND MATURITY IN AN EXPERIMENTALLY APPROACHABLE FORMAT, WHICH IS ESSENTIAL FOR DISEASE MODELING, DRUG TESTING, AND REGENERATIVE MEDICINE. HOWEVER, THEIR WIDESPREAD ADOPTION HAS BEEN HINDERED BY THE CHALLENGES IN MAINTAINING ADULT TISSUES IN CULTURE BECAUSE OF CELL LOSS, TISSUE REMODELING, AND ULTIMATELY, DETERIORATION. BARRIERS OF CURRENT- GENERATION 3D RETINA CULTURES INCLUDE 1) UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS DUE TO METABOLITE FLUCTUATIONS AND WASTE ACCUMULATION, 2) SLOW AND CUMBERSOME ITERATION OF TEST CONDITIONS, 3) A HEAVY RELIANCE ON ENDPOINT ANALYSIS (CROSS-SECTIONAL DATA), WHICH REQUIRES LARGE NUMBERS OF SAMPLES THAT LACK CONNECTIVITY ACROSS TIMEPOINTS, 4) CHALLENGES IN MONITORING CELL AND TISSUE VIABILITY IN THE ABSENCE OF LABELS, AND (5) THE CHALLENGE OF TRACKING LIVE CELLS IN THE ABSENCE OF GENETICALLY-ENCODED FLUORESCENT PROTEIN REPORTERS. IN THIS TECHNOLOGY FOCUSED PROJECT, WE WILL DEVELOP, IN AIM 1, A CUSTOM SCALABLE MICROFLUIDIC PLATFORM THAT WILL BE INTEGRATED INTO THE AIR-LIQUID INTERFACE CULTURE FORMAT FOR RETINAL TISSUE THAT WILL STABILIZE CULTURE CONDITIONS OVER EXISTING METHODOLOGY. THIS PLATFORM WILL FEATURE PROGRAMMABLE CONTROL OF FACTOR DELIVERY AND WITHDRAWAL, ENABLE MULTIPLEXING OF TEST CONDITIONS, AND WILL BE COMPATIBLE WITH IMAGING MODALITIES. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DEVELOP DYNAMIC CONTRAST-OPTICAL COHERENCE MICROSCOPY FOR CELLULAR-RESOLUTION LABEL-FREE IMAGING OF CULTURED RETINA. THIS WILL ENABLE LONGITUDINAL IMAGE CAPTURE TO ASSESS CELL AND TISSUE VIABILITY AND TRACK CHANGES IN CELL MORPHOLOGY WITHOUT THE NEED FOR LABELS SUCH AS FLUORESCENT REPORTERS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL DEVELOP GENE-SPECIFIC FLUORESCENT BIOSENSORS FOR CELL TRACKING BASED ON ADAR RNA EDITING. THIS APPROACH WILL NOT REQUIRE CELL-SPECIFIC PROMOTERS AND WILL ENABLE LONGITUDINAL FLUORESCENCE-BASED IMAGING IN THE ABSENCE OF GENETICALLY ENCODED REPORTERS. EACH OF THESE TECHNOLOGIES WILL BE DEVELOPED AND BENCHMARKED USING EXPERIMENTALLY AMENABLE MOUSE MODELS. IN AIM 4, THE TECHNOLOGIES WILL BE TRANSLATED TO ADULT HUMAN RETINA CULTURE. THESE TECHNOLOGIES, WHEN INTEGRATED, WILL UNIQUELY OVERCOME BOTTLENECKS IN THE EFFICIENCY AND VARIABILITY OF PRE-CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH USING 3D CULTURES OF ADULT RETINAL TISSUES AND PROVIDES, FOR THE FIRST TIME, ACCESS TO QUANTITATIVE LONGITUDINAL DATA ON CELL/TISSUE STRUCTURE, STATE, AND FUNCTIONAL CHANGES, TO ALLOW FOR MORE ROBUST AND REPRODUCIBLE APPLICATIONS OF 3D RETINA CULTURE OF MURINE OR HUMAN ORIGIN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NOVEL ULTRAHIGH RESOLUTION OCT BIOMARKERS IN AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION - AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION (AMD) CURRENTLY AFFECTS ~20 MILLION ELDERLY PEOPLE IN THE US ALONE, WITH THE NUMBER PROJECTED TO RISE RAPIDLY DUE TO THE AGING POPULATION. LATE DISEASE VISION LOSS OFTEN RESULTS FROM PHOTORECEPTOR CELL DEATH; AND TREATMENT OPTIONS REMAIN LIMITED. DETECTING AND UNDERSTANDING IMPAIRMENTS AT EARLIER STAGES CAN GREATLY BENEFIT CLINICAL MANAGEMENT AND FACILITATE THERAPEUTIC DISCOVERY, WHEN THE DAMAGE MAY BE REVERSIBLE. THIS PROGRAM WILL DEVELOP AND APPLY NOVEL OPTICAL COHERENCE TOMOGRAPHY (OCT) METHODS FOR DETECTING AND MONITORING OF AMD ASSOCIATED PHOTORECEPTOR CHANGES. AIM 1 WILL INVESTIGATE CONE PHOTORECEPTOR FUNCTION IMPAIRMENTS IN AMD. CONES ARE ESSENTIAL FOR FINE CENTRAL VISION, THE UNDERSTANDING AND PRESERVATION OF WHICH HAVE MEANINGFUL QUALITY OF LIFE IMPACTS. WE WILL ADVANCE OCT SPLIT-SPECTRUM AMPLITUDE-DECORRELATION OPTORETINOGRAPHY (SSADOR) AND VALIDATE OBJECTIVE, QUANTITATIVE SSADOR METRICS AS SURROGATE MARKERS OF CONE VISUAL FUNCTION. THE CLINICAL STUDIES HAVE BOTH CROSS-SECTIONAL AND LONGITUDINAL COMPONENTS, WHICH WILL ENROLL TWO INDEPENDENT COHORTS OF EARLY AND INTERMEDIATE AMD PATIENTS AND AGE MATCHED NORMAL CONTROLS. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT A REDUCTION IN CONE LIGHT RESPONSES DIFFERENTIATES BETWEEN NORMAL AGING VERSUS AMD EYES AND AMONG DISEASE SEVERITY CATEGORIES. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT WORSE RESPONSES CONFER A HIGHER PROGRESSION RISK. THE STUDY WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE SPATIOTEMPORAL CORRELATION BETWEEN CONE IMPAIRMENT AND AMD LESIONS INCLUDING DRUSEN, SUBRETINAL DRUSENOID DEPOSITS (SDD), PIGMENTARY ABNORMALITIES, ETC. AIM 2 WILL INVESTIGATE ROD FUNCTION IMPAIRMENTS IN AMD. RODS MEDIATE LOW LIGHT VISION; AND ONE OF THE EARLIEST SYMPTOMS OF AMD IS IMPAIRED TRANSITION FROM BRIGHT TO DIMLY LIT ENVIRONMENTS. SSADOR TESTS CAN BE ADAPTED TO ROD PHYSIOLOGY TO ISOLATE THEIR RESPONSES. WE WILL MONITOR ROD RESPONSE RECOVERY AFTER AN INTENSE BLEACHING FLASH, A PROCESS KNOWN AS DARK ADAPTATION. USING THE SAME AMD AND CONTROL COHORTS, THE PLANNED STUDIES WILL TEST IF ROD SPECIFIC SSADOR METHODS CAN MEASURE A DELAY IN DARK ADAPTATION THAT SIGNIFIES AMD PATHOLOGY AND CORRESPONDS TO DISEASE SEVERITY. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT PROFOUND DELAYS INDICATE INCREASED RISK OF DISEASE PROGRESSION. AIM 3 WILL EMPLOY ULTRAHIGH RESOLUTION DIRECTIONAL OCT FOR ASSESSING OUTER RETINAL MORPHOLOGICAL ALTERATIONS. DIRECTIONAL OCT INTERROGATES THE DEPENDENCE OF RETINAL LAYER APPEARANCE (E.G., INTENSITY) ON THE IMAGING LIGHT ANGLE. WHEN COMBINED WITH ULTRAHIGH IMAGING RESOLUTION, IT PROMISES TO OFFER INSIGHTS INTO THE BANDS’ ANATOMICAL ORIGINS, AS WELL AS ENABLE EARLY DETECTION AND MONITOR SUBTLE CHANGES OVER A SHORT PERIOD OF TIME. IN A SERIES OF PILOT CLINICAL STUDIES, WE WILL INVESTIGATE IF “MISDIRECTED” PHOTORECEPTORS, E.G., A CHANGE OR LOSS IN THE ELLIPSOID ZONE (EZ) DIRECTIONAL REFLECTIVITY, INDICATE AMD DAMAGE AND PRECEDES ONSET OF ATROPHY. FINALLY, WE WILL COMBINE CONE AND ROD FUNCTIONAL METRICS TOGETHER WITH OCT MORPHOLOGICAL MARKERS TO DEVELOP A COMPUTATIONAL MODEL FOR PREDICTING RETINA HEALTH, WITH THE LONG TERM GOAL OF IMPROVING DISEASE DIAGNOSIS, FURTHERING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF AMD PATHOGENESIS, AND HELPING AMD PATIENTS ACHIEVE BETTER VISUAL OUTCOMES.
