description: MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF OUTER SEGMENT RENEWAL. - PROJECT SUMMARY MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF OUTER SEGMENT RENEWAL THIS PROPOSAL UNCOVERS FUNDAMENTAL MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERPINNING THE CONSTANT RENEWAL OF PHOTORECEPTOR OUTER SEGMENTS – A NEVER-ENDING PROCESS THAT IS CRUCIAL FOR OUR VISION. DEFECTS IN OUTER SEGMENT RENEWAL UNDERLIE MANY INHERITED RETINAL DEGENERATIVE DISEASES THAT LEAD TO COMPLETE BLINDNESS IN HUMANS. ELUCIDATING HOW OUTER SEGMENTS ARE RENEWED AT THE MOLECULAR LEVEL IS THE KEY TO DEVELOPING NOVEL THERAPIES. HERE, WE INVESTIGATE UNANSWERED QUESTIONS ABOUT HOW THE OUTER SEGMENT’S LIGHT SENSITIVE MEMBRANE MATERIAL IS SHAPED INTO FLATTENED MEMBRANE DISCS, HOW THESE DISCS ARE STRUCTURALLY STABILIZED AND HOW THEIR MOLECULAR COMPOSITION IS CONTROLLED. EVERY DAY, DOZENS OF NEW DISC MEMBRANES ARE BUILT AT THE BASE OF EACH OUTER SEGMENT AND AN EQUAL NUMBER OF OLD DISCS ARE DISCARDED FROM THE TIP. THE TREMENDOUS NEVER-ENDING FLUX OF DISC PROTEINS AND LIPIDS INTO THE OUTER SEGMENT INITIALLY MUST PASS THROUGH THE NARROW CONNECTING CILIUM THAT PHYSICALLY LINKS THE NEWLY FORMING DISCS AND PHOTORECEPTOR CELL BODY. THE CONNECTING CILIUM ALSO ACTS AS A CILIARY GATE REGULATING PROTEIN ENTRY INTO THE DISCS. ONCE PROTEIN AND MEMBRANE MATERIAL PASS THROUGH THE CONNECTING CILIUM, THE CILIARY PLASMA MEMBRANE EVAGINATES INTO LARGE MEMBRANE PROTRUSIONS THAT SUBSEQUENTLY FLATTEN INTO NEWLY FORMING DISC LAMELLAE. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE ELUCIDATE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT DRIVE THE FLATTENING OF THE NEWLY FORMING DISCS, THEIR STABILIZATION AND HOW THEIR CONTENT IS REGULATED. WE FOCUS ON TWO OUTER SEGMENT PROTEINS CRITICAL FOR THESE PROCESSES, PRCD AND KIAA1549, BOTH OF WHICH ARE LINKED TO RETINITIS PIGMENTOSA IN HUMANS. IN AIM 1, WE INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF THE DISC-SPECIFIC PROTEIN PRCD. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT IN THE ABSENCE OF PRCD, THE NEWLY FORMING DISCS DELAMINATE AND BLEB AS EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES, WHICH ACCUMULATE IN THE INTERPHOTORECEPTOR SPACE. WE WILL ADDRESS THE MOLECULAR MECHANISM BY WHICH PRCD SUPPORTS THE STRUCTURE OF NEWLY FORMING DISCS AS THEY PROTRUDE FROM THE CILIUM. IN AIM 2, WE FOCUS ON KIAA1549 AND ITS ROLE IN DISC FORMATION. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA INCLUDE A NEWLY GENERATED KIAA1549-/- MOUSE AND SUGGEST THIS PROTEIN MAY PARTICIPATE IN REGULATING PROTEIN FLUX INTO THE DISC MEMBRANES AND/OR IN THE STRUCTURAL CONNECTION THAT SUPPORTS THE CILIARY POCKET. OUR PROPOSED EXPERIMENTS LEVERAGE INNOVATIVE BIOCHEMICAL, PROTEOMICS AND ADVANCED ELECTRON MICROSCOPY TECHNIQUES TO ELUCIDATE THESE BASIC MOLECULAR MECHANISMS. BY DISCOVERING HOW DISCS ARE BUILT AND STABILIZED WE WILL ANSWER LONG-STANDING QUESTIONS ABOUT HOW OUR VISION WORKS AT THE MOLECULAR LEVEL AND PROVIDE NEW MOLECULAR ENTRY POINTS FOR TREATING RETINAL DISEASE.

description: MAKING HEALTHY BABIES: HOLISTIC EVALUATION AND OPTIMIZATION OF TARGETED NANOMEDICINES TO TREAT PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION IN COMMON PREGNANCY COMPLICATIONS - PROJECT SUMMARY PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION IS THE MAJOR UNDERLYING CAUSE OF THE SERIOUS PREGNANCY COMPLICATIONS PREECLAMPSIA (PE), INTRAUTERINE GROWTH RESTRICTION (IUGR) AND STILLBIRTH, WHICH AFFECT UP TO 15% OF PREGNANCIES IN THE US. NO TREATMENTS ARE AVAILABLE, LEAVING CLINICIANS RELIANT ON PRENATAL MONITORING AND EARLY DELIVERY, WHICH CAN FURTHER EXACERBATE ADVERSE MATERNAL AND INFANT OUTCOMES. DEVELOPING NEW THERAPEUTICS FOR USE IN PREGNANCY IS HAMPERED BY THE POTENTIAL RISK OF HARMFUL SIDE EFFECTS AND TERATOGENESIS, SEVERELY LIMITING INVESTMENT AND PROGRESS IN THIS AREA. TO ADDRESS THIS ROADBLOCK, WE HAVE CREATED TARGETED NANOPARTICLES DECORATED WITH PLACENTAL HOMING PEPTIDES, WHICH CAN SELECTIVELY DELIVER A WIDE RANGE OF DRUGS DIRECTLY TO THE PLACENTA, BUT DO NOT CROSS TO THE BABY. THE OVERARCHING AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO CONDUCT ROBUST PHARMACOKINETIC/ PHARMACODYNAMIC (PK/PD), SAFETY AND EFFICACY STUDIES TO QUANTIFY, OPTIMIZE AND MODEL THE TRUE BENEFITS OF THIS PLACENTAL-SPECIFIC DRUG DELIVERY APPROACH. USING WELL-CHARACTERIZED MOUSE MODELS OF HEALTHY PREGNANCY AND DIET-INDUCED PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION, HUMAN PLACENTAL EXPLANT CULTURES AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING, WE WILL COMPREHENSIVELY ASSESS THE BIODISTRIBUTION AND ACTIONS OF THREE DRUGS WITH PROVEN EFFICACY TO TREAT PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION: ASPIRIN, MELATONIN AND SE175. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT ADMINISTRATION OF THESE DRUGS IN TARGETED LIPOSOMES DECORATED WITH THE WELL-CHARACTERIZED PLACENTAL HOMING PEPTIDE IRGD WILL INCREASE THEIR SAFETY, EFFICACY AND UTEROPLACENTAL-SPECIFIC DELIVERY, COMPARED TO ADMINISTRATION OF THE FREE DRUG. WE WILL PERFORM BIODISTRIBUTION STUDIES IN MICE TO QUANTIFY AND MODEL CHANGES IN THE DRUG CONCENTRATIONS IN MATERNAL, PLACENTAL AND PUP TISSUES OVER TIME. WE WILL ALSO PERFORM A TREATMENT STUDY TO COMPARE THE EFFECTS OF SYSTEMIC VERSUS TARGETED DELIVERY OF DRUGS ON (I) PLACENTAL STRUCTURE, GENE AND PROTEIN EXPRESSION, AND LEVELS OF PLACENTAL INFLAMMATION AND OXIDATIVE STRESS, (II) PUP OUTCOMES AND ANTHROPOMETRIC MEASUREMENTS, AND (III) INFLAMMATORY BIOMARKERS IN MATERNAL AND PUP PLASMA, TO ASSESS THE EXTENT OF RESCUE OF PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION. USING DATA FROM OUR IN VIVO STUDIES, WE WILL BUILD COMPUTATIONAL MODELS OF DRUG/LIPOSOME TISSUE DISTRIBUTION AND CLEARANCE OVER TIME, THEN INCORPORATE UPTAKE DATA FROM HUMAN PLACENTAL EXPLANT CULTURES TO CREATE PHYSIOLOGICAL-BASED PHARMACOKINETIC (PBPK) MODELS, WHICH WILL PREDICT THE LIPOSOME CONCENTRATIONS AND DOSING STRATEGIES REQUIRED TO ACHIEVE OPTIMAL THERAPEUTIC RESPONSES IN RODENTS, NON-HUMAN PRIMATES AND HUMANS. THIS RESEARCH SUPPORTS THE MISSION OF NICHD TO DEVELOP SAFE AND EFFECTIVE PLACENTAL-SPECIFIC THERAPEUTICS FOR THE TREATMENT OF PLACENTAL DYSFUNCTION. ACCURATE QUANTITATION OF MATERNAL, PLACENTAL AND PUP DRUG DISTRIBUTION AND CLEARANCE, AS WELL AS THE GLOBAL AND PLACENTAL-SPECIFIC DRUG EFFECTS OBSERVED, IS IMPERATIVE TO FACILITATE DATA-DRIVEN APPROACHES TO BETTER INFORM THE DESIGN AND SUCCESS OF FUTURE PRE-CLINICAL AND CLINICAL PREGNANCY STUDIES, A KEY HURDLE THAT CURRENTLY IMPEDES CLINICAL TRANSLATION OF OBSTETRIC THERAPEUTICS.

description: CHILDHOOD MALTREATMENT, ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING AND COGNITIVE FUNCTION AT MIDLIFE: A BIOPSYCHOSOCIAL STUDY ACROSS THE LIFESPAN - PROJECT SUMMARY EMERGING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT CHILDHOOD ABUSE AND TRAUMA INCREASE THE RISK OF ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT IN ADULTHOOD. YET, THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THESE ASSOCIATIONS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD, PARTICULARLY IN MIDLIFE, A CRITICAL PERIOD WHEN AGING PROCESSES AND CUMULATIVE LIFE EXPOSURES MAY CONVERGE TO SHAPE LONG-TERM HEALTH, INCLUDING ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD). THIS PROJECT USES A DEVELOPMENTAL LIFESPAN PERSPECTIVE TO EXAMINE PATHWAYS THROUGH WHICH CHILDHOOD MALTREATMENT (CM) MAY BE ASSOCIATED WITH ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING AND COGNITIVE OUTCOMES, INCLUDING PSYCHOSOCIAL AND INFLAMMATORY PATHWAYS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT CM ALTERS THE EARLY ENVIRONMENT IN WAYS THAT DISRUPT HEALTHY DEVELOPMENT ACROSS THE LIFESPAN, INITIATING A CASCADE OF RISK THAT MAY INCREASE THE LIKELIHOOD OF ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING AND COGNITIVE DECLINE. WE FURTHER HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE MANIFESTATION OF THESE DISRUPTIONS DIFFERS BY SEX, DUE TO WELL-ESTABLISHED DIFFERENCES IN STRESS-RESPONSE BIOLOGY. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL INVESTIGATE HOW ADVERSE PSYCHOSOCIAL FACTORS IN EMERGING ADULTHOOD, INCLUDING ELEVATED STRESS, DEPRESSION, AND POOR RELATIONSHIP QUALITY WITH PARENTS, FREQUENTLY OBSERVED AMONG CM SURVIVORS—CONTRIBUTE TO INCREASED INFLAMMATION DURING EARLY ADULTHOOD, THEREBY HEIGHTENING THE RISK FOR ACCELERATED BIOLOGICAL AGING AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT IN MIDLIFE. LEVERAGING DATA FROM THE NATIONAL LONGITUDINAL STUDY OF ADOLESCENT TO ADULT HEALTH (ADD HEALTH), A NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE COHORT FOLLOWED FROM ADOLESCENCE (AGES 12-19) INTO MIDLIFE (AGES 39-51), WE WILL USE STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELING TO TEST THESE PATHWAYS AND EVALUATE SEX-SPECIFIC PATTERNS. THIS RESEARCH SUPPORTS THE GROWING FOCUS ON MIDLIFE AS A CRITICAL OPPORTUNITY TO IDENTIFY MODIFIABLE FACTORS AND INTERVENTION TARGETS BEFORE THE ONSET OF AGE-RELATED DISEASE, INCLUDING ADRD. FINDINGS WILL DEEPEN UNDERSTANDING OF HOW EARLY ADVERSITY SHAPES AGING AND UNCOVER POTENTIAL SEX-SPECIFIC PATHWAY DIFFERENCES, WHILE INFORMING FUTURE RESEARCH, CLINICAL PRACTICE, AND PUBLIC POLICY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: PRECISE CHARACTERIZATION OF SELECTIVE MOTOR CONTROL IN CEREBRAL PALSY - CEREBRAL PALSY (CP) IS THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF PHYSICAL DISABILITY IN CHILDREN AND VARIABILITY IN TREATMENT RESPONSE IS UNACCEPTABLY HIGH. MUCH OF THIS VARIABILITY MAY BE EXPLAINED BY THE FAILURE OF CURRENT PRACTICE TO MATCH TREATMENTS TO INDIVIDUAL PATTERNS OF MOTOR CONTROL IMPAIRMENT. DESPITE BEING THE UNIVERSAL DEFICIT IN CP, IMPAIRMENT IN SELECTIVE MOTOR CONTROL (SMC) IS NOT ROUTINELY MEASURED AND EVEN WHEN MEASURED, EXISTING SCALES LACK PRECISION TO CHARACTERIZE INDIVIDUAL VARIABILITY AND GUIDE TREATMENT. PERSONALIZED TREATMENT APPROACHES FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH CP WILL REMAIN UNATTAINABLE WITHOUT THE ABILITY TO PRECISELY CHARACTERIZE THE TYPES AND DEGREES OF IMPAIRMENTS IN SMC. IMPAIRED NEUROMOTOR CONTROL IN CP CAUSES EXCESS ACTIVATION OF MUSCLES NOT NEEDED FOR THE TASK, OFTEN CALLED OVERFLOW, WHICH DISRUPTS THE COORDINATION OF MOVEMENT AND IMPAIRS PHYSICAL FUNCTION. SOME OF THIS EXCESS MUSCLE ACTIVATION CAN BE FURTHER DESCRIBED (DEPENDING ON ITS LOCATION AND LATERALITY) AS CO-ACTIVATION, MIRRORING, OR SYNERGISTIC MOVEMENT – AND THESE DISTINCTIONS MAY BE CRITICAL TO GUIDE TREATMENT PRESCRIPTIONS. THIS WORK IS PARTICULARLY IMPORTANT FOR YOUNG CHILDREN WITH CP WHOSE IMPAIRMENTS IN MOTOR CONTROL MAY BE MORE AMENABLE TO TREATMENT THAN IN OLDER CHILDREN. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DEVELOP PERSONALIZED MEASURES THAT PREDICT TREATMENT RESPONSE AND GUIDE PERSONALIZED TREATMENT DECISIONS FOR CHILDREN WITH CP. WE HAVE ESTABLISHED THE FEASIBILITY OF A NEW METHODOLOGICAL APPROACH THAT QUANTIFIES MUSCLE ACTIVATION PATTERNS USING ELECTROMYOGRAPHY PAIRED WITH BIOFEEDBACK DURING SINGLE-JOINT MOVEMENT. THE APPROACH RESULTS IN FOUR INDEX VALUES OF SMC (COACTIVATION, MIRRORING, SYNERGY AND TOTAL OVERFLOW) FOR EACH OF SIX LOWER LIMB JOINT ACTIONS (HIP EXTENSION, HIP ABDUCTION, KNEE EXTENSION, KNEE FLEXION, ANKLE DORSIFLEXION AND ANKLE PLANTARFLEXION). THE BIOFEEDBACK GAME MAINTAINS THE CHILD'S ENGAGEMENT WHILE PROVIDING RIGOROUS STANDARDIZATION OF SUB-MAXIMAL EFFORT ON EACH OF THE SIX TASKS. OUR PRELIMINARY OBSERVATIONS SUGGEST LARGE DIFFERENCES BETWEEN CHILDREN WITH CP AND THEIR TYPICALLY DEVELOPING PEERS AND STRONG RELATIONS TO MOTOR FUNCTION FOR SEVERAL SMC INDICES, BUT AS EXPECTED, WITH WIDE VARIATION BETWEEN INDIVIDUAL CHILDREN WITH CP. THE NEXT PHASE OF THE WORK IS TO IDENTIFY WHICH MEASURES ARE MOST REPEATABLE AND INFORMATIVE, AND THUS MOST LIKELY TO PREDICT TREATMENT RESPONSE. THE OBJECTIVE OF THE PROPOSED WORK IS TO PRECISELY CHARACTERIZE SMC IN YOUNG CHILDREN WITH AND WITHOUT CP AGED 2-7 YEARS AND EVALUATE THE METRICS FOR REPEATABILITY, INTERNAL CONSISTENCY (AIM 1) AND DISCRIMINATIVE VALIDITY (AIM 2). WE WILL ALSO IDENTIFY PATTERNS OF MOTOR PERFORMANCE BASED ON TYPE, LOCATION, AND DEGREE OF SMC IMPAIRMENT WITHIN THE CP COHORT USING A MACHINE LEARNING CLUSTERING APPROACH AND INTERPRETED IN RELATION TO THE NORMATIVE DATASET AND TO EXISTING CLINICAL MEASURES (AIM 3). CHARACTERIZING THE TYPE, LOCATION AND DEGREE OF INDIVIDUAL SMC IMPAIRMENT IN CHILDREN WITH CP, ACCOMPANIED BY A NORMATIVE DATABASE FROM AGE-MATCHED PEERS, WILL ESTABLISH A FOUNDATION FOR PERSONALIZED MEASUREMENT TO GUIDE INDIVIDUALIZED TREATMENT PLANNING FOR CP AND SUPPORTS THE NICHD MISSION TO OPTIMIZE ABILITIES FOR ALL PEOPLE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NON-INVASIVE SPINAL STIMULATION TO REDUCE SPASTICITY AND IMPROVE MOBILITY FOR CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL PALSY - PROJECT SUMMARY CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL PALSY EXPERIENCE SPASTICITY AND OTHER NEUROMUSCULAR IMPAIRMENTS WHICH NEGATIVELY AFFECT MOBILITY AND ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING. CURRENT SPASTICITY MANAGEMENT APPROACHES REQUIRE INVASIVE SURGERIES LIKE SELECTIVE DORSAL RHIZOTOMY THAT PERMANENTLY SEVERS SENSORY PATHWAYS, OR MEDICATIONS LIKE BACLOFEN THAT CAN HAVE SUBSTANTIAL SIDE-EFFECTS. THESE INTERVENTIONS DISRUPT SENSORY FEEDBACK AND WEAKEN MUSCLES, SOMETIMES REQUIRING MONTHS OF REHABILITATION TO REGAIN PRE-INTERVENTION LEVELS OF FUNCTION. THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR NON-INVASIVE INTERVENTIONS TO REDUCE SPASTICITY FOR CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL PALSY. HERE WE PROPOSE TO CONDUCT A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL TO EVALUATE THE INDIVIDUAL AND COMBINED EFFECTS OF SPINAL CORD STIMULATION AND INTENSIVE TREADMILL TRAINING SPECIFICALLY DESIGNED FOR CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL PALSY. OUR NEUROMODULATION APPROACH IS DELIVERED THROUGH THE SKIN OVER THE LUMBAR SPINAL CORD TO TARGET PRIMARY SENSORY AFFERENTS, WHICH OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES HAVE FOUND RESULTS IN SUBSTANTIAL AND LASTING REDUCTIONS IN SPASTICITY. IN THE PROPOSED RESEARCH, WE WILL RIGOROUSLY EVALUATE THE IMPACT OF COMBINING SPINAL CORD STIMULATION WITH SHORT- BURST LOCOMOTOR TREADMILL TRAINING ON SPASTICITY THROUGH A RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL FOR CHILDREN WITH CEREBRAL PALSY. WE WILL QUANTIFY CHANGES IN SPASTICITY AND GAIT FOR CHILDREN THAT UNDERGO 24-SESSIONS (3X/WEEK FOR 8 WEEKS) OF EITHER WITH OR WITHOUT SPINAL STIMULATION. WE WILL ALSO EVALUATE SUSTAINED EFFECTS FOR 6-MONTHS OF FOLLOW-UP. WE WILL MEASURE CHANGES IN MOBILITY THROUGH BOTH QUANTITATIVE GAIT ANALYSIS AND WEARABLE SENSORS TO MONITOR COMMUNITY WALKING. FINALLY, WE WILL EXAMINE THE LIVED EXPERIENCES OF CHILDREN AND CAREGIVERS THROUGH SEMI-STRUCTURED INTERVIEWS TO UNDERSTAND HOW NEUROMODULATION AND TREADMILL TRAINING MAY SUPPORT THEIR GOALS FOR MOBILITY AND PARTICIPATION. TOGETHER, THIS RESEARCH WILL TEST NOVEL INTERVENTIONS FOR REDUCING SPASTICITY, WITH THE GOAL OF TRANSLATING NON-INVASIVE TREATMENT STRATEGIES TO IMPROVE QUALITY OF LIFE FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH CEREBRAL PALSY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISTIC INVESTIGATION OF TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENOME DYSREGULATION IN LEIOMYOMAS/UTERINE FIBROIDS - ABSTRACT UTERINE LEIOMYOMATA (UTERINE FIBROIDS OR LEIOMYOMAS) IS A MAJOR GYNECOLOGIC DISEASE AFFECTING UP TO 70% OF WOMEN, CAUSING SIGNIFICANT MORBIDITY SUCH AS BLEEDING, UTERINE STIFFNESS, PELVIC PAIN, AND INFERTILITY. THIS CONDITION IMPOSES SUBSTANTIAL CLINICAL, SOCIAL, EMOTIONAL, AND FINANCIAL BURDENS ON WOMEN AND THEIR FAMILIES. LEIOMYOMAS ARE BENIGN TUMORS CHARACTERIZED BY EXCESSIVE EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX (ECM) DEPOSITION. DESPITE THEIR PREVALENCE AND ASSOCIATED HEALTHCARE COSTS, THIS DISEASE REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD AND UNDERFUNDED. CURRENT NON-SURGICAL TREATMENTS HAVE SIGNIFICANT SIDE EFFECTS THAT LIMIT THEIR USE. WHILE GENETIC EVENTS DRIVE MANY DISEASES INCLUDING LEIOMYOMAS, THE EPIGENOME HAS RECENTLY EMERGED AS A CRUCIAL REGULATOR OF DISEASE MANIFESTATION. OUR PREVIOUS RESEARCH SHOWED THAT LEIOMYOMA SAMPLES WHEN COMPARED TO MYOMETRIAL TISSUES HAVE SIGNIFICANTLY HIGHER HISTONE H3 LYSINE 27 ACETYLATION (H3K27AC EPIGENOMIC MARK) ON GENE PROMOTERS AND ENHANCERS, POTENTIALLY LEADING TO ALTERED EXPRESSION OF ECM GENES AND TUMORIGENESIS. TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE ROLE OF H3K27AC WHICH IS MEDIATED BY THE EP300/CBP COACTIVATORS, WE HAVE ESTABLISHED A REPRODUCIBLE LEIOMYOMA PATIENT-DERIVED PRECISION-CUT EX VIVO TISSUE EXPLANT CULTURE SYSTEM THAT CLOSELY MIMICS IN VIVO HUMAN CONDITIONS AND REPRESENTS A NON-ANIMAL ASSAY MODEL SYSTEM. PRELIMINARY EXPERIMENTS USING A SPECIFIC EPIGENOMIC INHIBITOR TARGETING EP300/CBP SHOWED PROFOUND EFFECTS ON LEIOMYOMA-ASSOCIATED GENES AND SIGNALING PATHWAYS. WE WILL INTEGRATE ADVANCED MOLECULAR AND GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES WITH BIOINFORMATICS AND THIS NOVEL EX VIVO TISSUE PLATFORM AND RECENTLY ENGINEERED HUMAN CELL- BASED STUDIES TO FURTHER EXPLORE EPIGENOME DYSREGULATION IN LEIOMYOMAS. THESE STUDIES ARE HIGHLY SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE THEY WILL IDENTIFY THE EPIGENOME AS A KEY DRIVER OF UTERINE TUMORIGENESIS AND FIBROSIS, WILL ADVANCE KNOWLEDGE, AND HELP ESTABLISH A FRAMEWORK TO ASSESS EPIGENOME- TARGETING DRUGS AND DEVELOP FUTURE THERAPEUTICS FOR LEIOMYOMAS. CONDUCTING THIS RESEARCH IN AN EXCEPTIONAL ENVIRONMENT WITH SCIENTIFIC LEADERS IN GYNECOLOGIC DISEASES WILL FURTHER ENHANCE THE IMPACT OF OUR WORK.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LOWER LIMB HETERONYMOUS SPINAL REFLEXES AND MOTOR IMPAIRMENT AFTER STROKE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AFTER A STROKE, IMPAIRED COORDINATION AND WEAKNESS OF LOWER LIMB MUSCLES ARE KEY BARRIERS TO RECOVERY OF WALKING AND BALANCE. CURRENT THERAPIES STRUGGLE TO IMPROVE THESE IMPAIRMENTS BECAUSE WE LACK A CLEAR NEURAL MECHANISM TO TARGET. TO ADDRESS THIS GAP, WE WILL INVESTIGATE ALTERED CORTICAL CONTROL OF HETERONYMOUS REFLEX PATHWAYS AS A PLAUSIBLE, YET UNDERSTUDIED, MECHANISM CAPABLE OF CAUSING ABNORMAL COORDINATION AND FUNCTIONAL WEAKNESS AFTER STROKE. HETERONYMOUS SPINAL REFLEXES HAVE A UNIQUE ABILITY TO PROMOTE, OR IMPAIR, MOTOR COORDINATION ACROSS JOINTS AS EXCITATORY LENGTH AND INHIBITORY FORCE-RELATED FEEDBACK FROM A MUSCLE CAN ENHANCE (EXCITE) AND SUPPRESS (INHIBIT) MOTOR OUTPUT OF OTHER MUSCLES. NORMALLY, THE MOTOR CORTEX ADJUSTS THE MAGNITUDES OF THESE REFLEXES TO ENSURE TASK-APPROPRIATE COORDINATION. THUS, WE HYPOTHESIZE, SUPPORTED BY STRONG PRELIMINARY DATA, THAT AFTER CORTICAL DAMAGE, MODULATORY CONTROL IS IMPAIRED, CAUSING REFLEXES TO BECOME EXCESSIVE AND POORLY REGULATED. WE FOCUS ON REFLEXES FROM QUADRICEPS (Q) ONTO SOLEUS (SOL) BECAUSE, IN NEUROTYPICAL ADULTS, THESE REFLEXES ARE CORTICALLY MODULATED TO ENSURE THE MUSCLES ARE COORDINATED DURING STANDING AND WALKING. AFTER STROKE, HOWEVER, Q AND SOL ARE OFTEN COACTIVE AT THE WRONG TIME, AND SOL IS POORLY RECRUITED DURING BALANCE REACTIONS AND PROPULSION, DIRECTLY LIMITING BALANCE AND WALKING ABILITY. PI LYLE AND CO-IS KESAR AND TING WILL LEVERAGE THEIR EXPERTISE SPANNING SPINAL CIRCUITS AND NEUROMECHANICS TO TEST WHETHER THESE PERSISTENT IMPAIRMENTS POST-STROKE ARE DUE TO POORLY REGULATED HETERONYMOUS REFLEXES. WE WILL RIGOROUSLY EXAMINE Q TO SOL REFLEX MODULATION ACROSS STRATEGICALLY CHOSEN FUNCTIONAL CONTEXTS TO ESTABLISH MECHANISTIC LINKS TO CLINICALLY RELEVANT BEHAVIOR. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE HOW LIMB LOADING AND POSTURAL ORIENTATION INFLUENCE REFLEX MAGNITUDES TO CLARIFY MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE COMMON CLINICAL OBSERVATION OF INCREASED MOTOR IMPAIRMENT WHEN STANDING. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS IF STROKE DISRUPTS THE BRAIN’S CAPACITY TO MODULATE REFLEXES BASED ON TASK CONTEXT, ESSENTIAL FOR FUNCTIONING IN REAL-WORLD ENVIRONMENTS. AIM 3 WILL PROVIDE NOVEL MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO TWO DIFFICULT-TO-TREAT GAIT DEFICITS BY DETERMINING WHETHER ABNORMAL Q–SOL COACTIVATION IN EARLY STANCE POST-STROKE REFLECTS EXCESSIVE EXCITATION, AND WHETHER REDUCED PROPULSION AND GAIT SPEED REFLECT EXCESSIVE INHIBITION OF SOL IN LATE STANCE. ACROSS AIMS, WE WILL CORRELATE REFLEX MAGNITUDES WITH CLINICAL MEASURES OF DYNAMIC BALANCE AND WALKING SPEED TO ASSESS THEIR FUNCTIONAL RELEVANCE. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA PROVIDES STRONG SUPPORT FOR ALTERED REFLEX MODULATION IN STROKE SURVIVORS AS A NEURAL MECHANISM UNDERLYING POORER DYNAMIC BALANCE AND SLOWER GAIT. WE ANTICIPATE THIS WORK WILL GENERATE NEW OPPORTUNITIES FOR PERSONALIZED TREATMENT OF A NEURAL MECHANISM LINKED TO IMPAIRMENT (TOO MUCH EXCITATION/INHIBITION) VIA TARGETED NEUROMODULATION APPROACHES TO RESTORE FUNCTION AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR STROKE SURVIVORS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: ANN & ROBERT H LURIE CHILDRENS HOSPITAL OF CHICAGO

description: ULTRAFAST ULTRASOUND IN PEDIATRIC PULMONARY HYPERTENSION - PROJECT SUMMARY PEDIATRIC PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION (PAH) IS A PROGRESSIVE DISEASE ASSOCIATED WITH HIGH MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY, LEADING TO EVENTUAL RIGHT VENTRICULAR (RV) FAILURE. THE HYPERTROPHIC RESPONSE OF THE RV LEADS TO RV DIASTOLIC DYSFUNCTION (DD) CHARACTERIZED BY A VARIABLE COMBINATION OF IMPAIRED RELAXATION AND INCREASED MYOCARDIAL STIFFNESS. RV DD HAS BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH OUTCOME PREDICTION IN PEDIATRIC PAH AND A POTENTIAL TO GUIDE THERAPEUTIC MANAGEMENT. THE GOLD STANDARD OF DIASTOLIC ASSESSMENT IS FILLING PRESSURE BY INVASIVE CARDIAC CATHETERIZATION, WHICH HAS INTRINSIC LIMITATIONS. THUS, A CLINICAL NEED FOR DEVELOPMENT OF NONINVASIVE TECHNOLOGY SUCH AS ECHOCARDIOGRAPHY AND CARDIAC MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (MRI) IS NECESSARY TO DETECT, AND RISK STRATIFY DD IN CHILDREN WITH PAH. IN THE PRESENT PROSPECTIVE TWO-CENTER OBSERVATIONAL COHORT STUDY, NOVEL ULTRASOUND TECHNIQUES WILL BE EVALUATED FOR THE DIFFERENT PHASES OF DIASTOLE RELATED TO PAH. THIS INCLUDES EARLY RELAXATION, EARLY FILLING DETERMINED BY DIASTOLIC SUCTION, AND LATE FILLING DURING ATRIAL CONTRACTION. WE WILL USE BOTH CONVENTIONAL AND ULTRAFAST ULTRASOUND (UFUS) WHICH IS A NOVEL ULTRASOUND TECHNIQUE CAPABLE OF RECORDING SHORT-LIVED AND FAST OCCURRING CARDIAC EVENTS. WHILE CONVENTIONAL ULTRASOUND TECHNIQUES CAPTURE IMAGES BETWEEN 25-100 FRAMES/SEC, UFUS IS CAPABLE OF IMAGING THE HEART AT 5000-10000 FRAMES/SEC. THREE DIFFERENT PHASES OF DIASTOLE WILL BE STUDIED USING NOVEL ULTRASOUND TECHNIQUES TO UNDERSTAND AND CHARACTERIZE RV DD. NON-INVASIVE ULTRASOUND MEASUREMENTS WILL BE VALIDATE WITH INVASIVE DIASTOLIC PRESSURE MEASUREMENTS. MYOCARDIAL TISSUE PROPERTIES (FIBROSIS) AND BLOOD FLOW WILL BE STUDIED BY MRI T1 MAPPING AND RV 4D FLOW. A NONINVASIVE RISK SCORE COMBINING UFUS AND MRI MEASUREMENTS WILL HELP PREDICT OUTCOMES IN THIS PATIENT POPULATION. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT BY COMBINING DIFFERENT METHODS OF STUDYING RV DD, THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF RV DD AND ITS RELATIONSHIP TO DISEASE PROGRESSION AND OUTCOMES WILL BE ELUCIDATED.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ENHANCING LAMELLAR BODY FUNCTION VIA LRRK2 INHIBITION TO REDUCE RESPIRATORY DISTRESS SYNDROME (RDS) SEVERITY - PROJECT SUMMARY  RESPIRATORY DISTRESS SYNDROME (RDS) IS A SIGNIFICANT CAUSE OF MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY IN PRETERM NEWBORNS DUE TO INSUFFICIENT SURFACTANT PRODUCTION AND LUNG IMMATURITY. LAMELLAR BODIES (LBS), WHICH STORE AND SECRETE SURFACTANT, ARE OFTEN UNDERDEVELOPED IN PRETERM LUNGS. CURRENT THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES FOR RDS INCLUDE EXOGENOUS SURFACTANT THERAPY, MECHANICAL VENTILATION, AND STEROIDS, WHICH ARE ASSOCIATED WITH LUNG INJURY, BRONCHOPULMONARY DYSPLASIA (BPD) AND POOR NEURODEVELOPMENTAL OUTCOMES. THEREFORE, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR NOVEL THERAPEUTICS THAT CAN ENHANCE ENDOGENOUS SURFACTANT PRODUCTION AND REDUCE RELIANCE ON INVASIVE INTERVENTIONS. LEUCINE-RICH REPEAT KINASE 2 (LRRK2) IS A PROTEIN INVOLVED IN THE REGULATION OF AUTOPHAGY AND VESICLE TRAFFICKING WITHIN LUNG CELLS. ITS ROLE IN LB DEVELOPMENT HAS NOT BEEN FULLY ELUCIDATED, BUT RESEARCH ON ADULT ANIMAL MODELS WITH THE LRRK2 KINASE KNOCKED OUT (KO) DEMONSTRATED ENLARGED LBS WITH NORMAL BASAL SECRETION UNDER UNSTRESSED CONDITIONS. PHARMACOLOGICAL INHIBITION OF THE LRRK2 KINASE WITH GNE-7915 RESULTED IN REVERSIBLE LB ENLARGEMENT WITHOUT LUNG INJURY. HOWEVER, NO STUDIES HAVE TESTED WHETHER LRRK2 INHIBITION ENHANCES SURFACTANT PRODUCTION DURING PERINATAL DEVELOPMENT OR UNDER STRESS CONDITIONS RELEVANT TO RDS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA IN IPSC-DERIVED LUNG ORGANOIDS SHOW THAT LRRK2 KINASE KNOCKOUT ENHANCES AUTOPHAGY (INCREASED LC3B-II), ENLARGES LBS (TEM), UPREGULATES SURFACTANT GENES (RNA-SEQ), AND INCREASES SURFACTANT SECRETION BY 20% (ELISA). WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT ACUTE LRRK2 INHIBITION DURING AT2 MATURATION ENHANCES AUTOPHAGY-DRIVEN LB BIOGENESIS, PROVIDING SURFACTANT RESERVE CAPACITY THAT BECOMES CRITICAL DURING HIGH-DEMAND STRESS OF PRETERM BIRTH. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT TIMED LRRK2 INHIBITION DURING THE CRITICAL POSTNATAL WINDOW ENHANCES SURFACTANT PRODUCTION AND PROVIDES INCREASED RESERVE CAPACITY THAT IMPROVES RESPIRATORY FUNCTION UNDER STRESS CONDITIONS. THE OUTCOMES OF THIS RESEARCH COULD LEAD TO SIGNIFICANT IMPROVEMENTS IN THE TREATMENT OF RDS, OFFERING A NOVEL STRATEGY TO MITIGATE THE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY ASSOCIATED WITH THIS CONDITION IN PRETERM INFANTS. AIM 1 WILL DEFINE THE AUTOPHAGY-ABCA3 MECHANISM REGULATING LB BIOGENESIS USING IPSC ORGANOIDS, MEASURING AUTOPHAGY FLUX, TESTING CAUSALITY VIA AUTOPHAGY INHIBITION, ASSESSING ABCA3 LIPID TRANSPORT, AND DISTINGUISHING BASAL VERSUS STIMULATED SECRETION CAPACITY. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER LRRK2 INHIBITION IMPROVES RESPIRATORY FUNCTION IN PRETERM LAMBS UNDER STRESS CONDITIONS. LAMBS (127-130D GESTATION, EQUIVALENT TO 26-28WK HUMAN) WILL RECEIVE VEHICLE OR GNE-7915; WE WILL ASSESS GAS EXCHANGE, LUNG MECHANICS, SURFACTANT BIOCHEMISTRY, LB ULTRASTRUCTURE, AND AT2 TRANSCRIPTOMICS. AIM 3 WILL ASSESS MULTI-ORGAN SAFETY IN DEVELOPING NEONATES (KIDNEY, BRAIN, PHARMACOKINETICS, REVERSIBILITY), ADDRESSING THE CRITICAL DATA GAP AS NO NEONATAL SAFETY STUDIES EXIST. THIS RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE THE COMPLETE PRECLINICAL FOUNDATION FOR FIRST-IN-HUMAN TRIALS. GIVEN THAT LRRK2 INHIBITORS ARE DEVELOPED FOR PARKINSON'S DISEASE, REPURPOSING FOR RDS OFFERS RAPID TRANSLATION, POTENTIALLY PROVIDING A SAFER ALTERNATIVE TO STEROIDS AND TRANSFORMING OUTCOMES FOR PRETERM INFANTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MECHANISMS OF SEX-SPECIFIC RESPONSES TO OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEA THERAPIES (MOST) - PROJECT SUMMARY OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEA (OSA) — A CHRONIC DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY INTERMITTENT HYPOXEMIA AND RECURRENT AROUSAL — DELETERIOUSLY AFFECTS HEALTH VIA OXIDATIVE STRESS, WHICH IN TURN TRIGGERS INFLAMMATION AND DECREASES NITRIC OXIDE BIOAVAILABILITY. ACCORDINGLY, OXIDATIVE STRESS IS A KEY INTERMEDIARY THROUGH WHICH OSA ERODES VASCULAR FUNCTION. ACROSS YOUNG- TO LATE-ADULTHOOD, MEN EXPERIENCE A STEADY, LINEAR INCREASE IN CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE (CVD). IN CONTRAST, THE RELATIVELY ABRUPT LOSS OF ESTROGEN—A POWERFUL ANTIOXIDANT DEFENSE SYSTEM—WITH MENOPAUSE APPEARS TO HEIGHTEN WOMEN’S MODIFIABLE CVD RISK FACTORS, CVD PREVALENCE, AND CARDIOVASCULAR- ASSOCIATED DEATHS, ALL OF WHICH ARE HIGHER COMPARED WITH SAME-AGE MEN. NOTABLY, OSA PREVALENCE ALSO RISES SHARPLY AFTER MENOPAUSE, APPROACHING THAT OF MEN. CONCURRENTLY, IN POSTMENOPAUSAL WOMEN THE VASCULATURE BECOMES VULNERABLE TO SHARP RISES IN ACUTE OXIDATIVE STRESS, POSSIBLY EXPLAINING THEIR INCREASED OSA-BASED SEQUELAE. IN PARTICULAR, THE CRITICAL, ENDOGENOUS GLUTATHIONE (GSH)-BASED ANTIOXIDANT DEFENSE SYSTEM IS DIMINISHED IN BOTH OSA AND IN WOMEN AGES 50–55, CORRESPONDING WITH MENOPAUSE ONSET. GIVEN THAT OSA IS A MODIFIABLE CVD RISK FACTOR BUT ADHERENCE TO FIRST-LINE OSA THERAPY (I.E., POSITIVE AIRWAY PRESSURE [PAP] THERAPY), IS KNOWN TO BE DIFFICULT AND INADEQUATE, IDENTIFYING SAFE ALTERNATIVE THERAPIES FOR OSA IS CRITICAL. N-ACETYLCYSTEINE (NAC) IS A READILY AVAILABLE, SAFE, PRECURSOR ANTIOXIDANT THAT BOOSTS THE INTRACELLULAR GSH POOL. NAC IS A PRIME CANDIDATE FOR MITIGATING MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OSA-ASSOCIATED OXIDATIVE STRESS AND RESULTANT CVD GIVEN THE PROFILE OF OXIDATIVE STRESS, OSA, AND ASSOCIATED MORBIDITIES. HOWEVER, AND IMPORTANTLY, WOMEN AND MEN MAY RESPOND DIFFERENTLY TO THIS POTENTIAL THERAPY. THUS, IN MIDDLE- AND OLDER-AGED WOMEN AND MEN (AGED 52–70 YEARS WHO HAVE BEEN DIAGNOSED WITH MODERATE-TO-SEVERE OSA), THIS RANDOMIZED, CROSSOVER CLINICAL TRIAL, WILL ADDRESS BOTH THE UNIQUE IMPACTS OF OSA ON VASCULAR FUNCTION, AND THE CRITICAL NEED FOR SEX-SPECIFIC PREVENTATIVE THERAPIES. THE STUDY IS EXPECTED TO REVEAL THAT: 1) WOMEN AND MEN EXPERIENCE DISTINCT PROFILES OF ADVERSE, INTERMEDIARY CARDIOVASCULAR CONSEQUENCES WITH OSA — REVEALED BY OXIDATIVE STRESS, INFLAMMATION, AND ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION; 2) PAP THERAPY DIFFERENTIALLY IMPACTS OVERNIGHT OXIDATIVE STRESS, INFLAMMATION, AND ENDOTHELIAL FUNCTION IN WOMEN AND MEN; AND 3) NAC DECREASES OXIDATIVE STRESS IN OSA BUT MAY DO SO UNEQUALLY IN MEN VERSUS WOMEN, WITH WOMEN EXPERIENCING GREATER IMPROVEMENTS IN OXIDATIVE STRESS WITH NAC THERAPY COMPARED TO AGE-MATCHED MEN. ACCOMPLISHING THE STUDY AIMS WILL LEAD TO PIONEERING, TRANSLATABLE INSIGHTS ABOUT OSA- INDUCED CHANGES AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE TO INTRACELLULAR ANTIOXIDANT CAPACITY. THIS WILL ALSO FACILITATE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF TARGETED, SEX-BASED INTERVENTIONS. GIVEN THE STAGGERING PUBLIC HEALTH BURDEN OF CVD IN BOTH MEN AND WOMEN, TARGETING OSA AS A TREATABLE RISK FACTOR—AND USING THE OPTIMAL TREATMENT APPROACHES FOR BOTH WOMEN AND MEN—IS ESSENTIAL.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: IMPROVING ENDOTHELIAL REPAIR IN PEDIATRIC ARDS - PROJECT SUMMARY. ACUTE RESPIRATORY DISTRESS SYNDROME (ARDS) IS A LIFE-THREATENING COMPLICATION OF SEPSIS AND ACUTE LUNG INJURY (ALI). COMPARED TO ADULT ARDS, LUNG REPAIR AFTER PEDIATRIC ARDS (PARDS) IS DEPENDENT UPON RE-ESTABLISHMENT OF POSTNATAL ANGIOGENESIS WHICH IS REQUIRED TO CONTINUE NORMAL ALVEOLARIZATION IN CHILDHOOD. DISRUPTION OF NORMAL ALVEOLARIZATION AND ANGIOGENESIS AFTER PARDS REPRESENTS A RISK FACTOR FOR SEVERE CHRONIC LUNG DISEASES, SUCH AS BRONCHOPULMONARY DYSPLASIA IN CHILDREN AND CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE IN ADULTS. GIVEN THE LACK OF MAJOR IMPROVEMENTS IN PARDS CLINICAL MANAGEMENT, THERE IS A COMPELLING NEED FOR INNOVATIVE MOLECULAR APPROACHES TO COMPLEMENT EXISTING THERAPIES. ONE APPROACH IS THE DEVELOPMENT OF NANOPARTICLE (NP) CARRIERS THAT CAN DELIVER EITHER DRUGS OR NUCLEIC ACIDS (ENCODING THERAPEUTIC TARGETS) TO LUNG ENDOTHELIAL CELLS (ECS) WITH HIGH EFFICIENCY AND PRECISION. WHILE SEVERAL EC-SPECIFIC NP DELIVERY SYSTEMS HAVE BEEN RECENTLY DEVELOPED, NONE OF THESE NANOCARRIERS ARE SPECIFIC TO LUNG ECS WITHOUT TARGETING ECS OF OTHER ORGANS. FURTHERMORE, MANY TYPES OF NPS BECOME TOXIC IN DISEASE SETTINGS, ESPECIALLY DURING INFLAMMATORY CONDITIONS LIKE ALI/ARDS, HIGHLIGHTING THE NEED FOR INNOVATIVE AND NON-TOXIC NP SYSTEMS FOR FUTURE THERAPIES. FOXF1 IS A TRANSCRIPTION FACTOR CRITICAL FOR LUNG DEVELOPMENT AND LUNG REPAIR AFTER INJURY. MY LAB PREVIOUSLY FOUND THAT FOXF1 IS DECREASED IN LUNGS OF PATIENTS WITH ARDS AND THAT EC-SPECIFIC INACTIVATION OF THE FOXF1 GENE IN MICE EXACERBATES ALI AND CAUSES ARDS. WHILE THESE STUDIES INDICATE AN IMPORTANT ROLE FOR FOXF1 IN LUNG REPAIR, IT IS UNCLEAR WHETHER FOXF1 IS A “DRUGGABLE” TARGET IN PARDS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL TEST THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF LUNG EC-SPECIFIC P22-F1 PBAE/PEI/PEG NANOPARTICLES COMPLEXED WITH FOXF1 MRNA TO INHIBIT EC APOPTOSIS AND STIMULATE VASCULAR REPAIR IN 2 MODELS OF PEDIATRIC SEPSIS-INDUCED ARDS (I.P. ADMINISTRATION OF LPS AND THE CECAL LIGATION AND PUNCTURE). WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER FOXF1 PROTECTS ACAP CAPILLARY ECS FROM APOPTOSIS THROUGH TRANSCRIPTIONAL ACTIVATION OF THE BCL2 GENE. MOLECULAR MECHANISMS AND FOXF1 TARGET GENES FOUND IN ANIMAL MODELS WILL BE ALSO TESTED USING HUMAN LUNG TISSUES AND PRECISION-CUT LUNG SLICES (PCLS) FROM DONORS AND PARDS PATIENTS. RECENTLY, WE IDENTIFIED THE TANFE SMALL MOLECULE COMPOUND, WHICH DISRUPTS THE INTERACTION OF THE FOXF1 PROTEIN WITH HECTD1 E3 UBIQUITIN LIGASE, PROTECTING THE FOXF1 PROTEIN FROM DEGRADATION. IN OUR PRELIMINARY DATA FOR AIM 2, WE CHEMICALLY MODIFIED THIS COMPOUND TO PRODUCE A NON-TOXIC DERIVATIVE, TANFE[F], WHICH CAN BE DELIVERED USING PBAE-1.4DA-PEG4X NANOPARTICLES TO LUNG ECS IN A MOUSE PARDS MODEL. WE ALSO FOUND THAT NP DELIVERY OF A KNOWN HECTD1 INHIBITOR, I3C, A PLANT-DERIVED SMALL MOLECULE COMPOUND WHICH IS CURRENTLY IN CLINICAL TRIALS FOR CANCER PATIENTS, INCREASES FOXF1 PROTEIN LEVELS IN INJURED NEONATAL MOUSE LUNGS AND IN HUMAN PCLS. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER NP DELIVERY OF FOXF1-STABILIZING COMPOUNDS PRECISELY TO LUNG ECS WILL INCREASE VASCULAR REPAIR IN PARDS MODELS. ALTOGETHER, WE AIM TO DEVELOP NEW THERAPIES FOR PEDIATRIC ARDS THAT ARE BASED ON SPECIFIC ACTIVATION OF FOXF1 SIGNALING IN PULMONARY ECS.

description: DECODING NEUTROPHIL MEMBRANES IN ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID SYNDROME - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID SYNDROME (APS) IS AN INCURABLE AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE AND A LEADING ACQUIRED CAUSE OF THROMBOSIS. THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF APS IS PROPELLED BY CIRCULATING ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID ANTIBODIES THAT ENGAGE PHOSPHOLIPID-BINDING PROTEINS AT CELL SURFACES TO ACTIVATE NEUTROPHILS, PLATELETS, AND ENDOTHELIAL CELLS—THEREBY TIPPING CIRCULATING BLOOD TOWARD THROMBOSIS. ALTHOUGH MEMBRANE PHOSPHOLIPIDS HAVE A CENTRAL ROLE IN APS PATHOPHYSIOLOGY, FEW MODERN STUDIES HAVE ASSESSED POTENTIALLY CORRECTABLE DISTORTIONS IN MEMBRANE PERMEABILITY OR THE CHARACTERISTICS OF THE PHOSPHOLIPIDS THEMSELVES. WE PROPOSE A REINVIGORATED FOCUS ON APS MEMBRANES, WHICH WE ANTICIPATE WILL OPEN NEW AVENUES TO APS DIAGNOSIS, SUBPHENOTYPING, AND TREATMENT. GASDERMIN D (GSDMD)—A SUBSTRATE OF INFLAMMATORY CASPASES THAT FORMS MEMBRANE PORES UPON CLEAVAGE AND OLIGOMERIZATION—WAS RECENTLY SHOWN TO HAVE A KEY ROLE IN THE MEMBRANE RUPTURE REQUIRED FOR NEUTROPHIL EXTRACELLULAR TRAP RELEASE (I.E., NETOSIS). OUR PRELIMINARY DATA NOW DEMONSTRATE: (I) GSDMD CLEAVAGE AND LIKELY PALMITOYLATION IN THE CONTEXT OF APS IGG-MEDIATED NETOSIS, (II) REDUCED NETOSIS AND THROMBOSIS IN GSDMD-KNOCKOUT MICE, (III) UPREGULATION OF GSDMD-REGULATING GENES LIKE CASP1 AND CASP4 IN APS PATIENT NEUTROPHILS, AND (IV) ACCUMULATION OF CLEAVED GSDMD ON THE CIRCULATING NEUTROPHILS OF MANY APS PATIENTS. INSPIRED BY THE RECENTLY RECOGNIZED ROLE OF MYELOPEROXIDASE (MPO)-DEPENDENT LIPID PEROXIDATION IN NETOSIS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LIPID PEROXIDATION OF NEUTROPHIL MEMBRANES IS ALSO A KEY DRIVER OF APS PATHOPHYSIOLOGY. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA NOW DEMONSTRATE: (I) THE REQUIREMENT OF MPO'S ENZYMATIC ACTIVITY FOR NETOSIS TRIGGERED BY APS IGG, (II) INHIBITION OF THIS NETOSIS BY LIPID PEROXIDATION-QUENCHING VITAMIN E ANALOGS, (III) SMOLDERING LIPID PEROXIDATION IN THE CIRCULATING NEUTROPHILS OF MANY PATIENTS WITH APS, AND (IV) ACCUMULATION OF Β2GPI (POSSIBLY AS AN ALDEHYDE-DERIVED COVALENT ADDUCT) ON THE SURFACES OF PATIENT NEUTROPHILS. HOW TO COMBAT THE INFLAMMATORY, ANTICOAGULANT-RESISTANT MANIFESTATIONS OF APS IS UNKNOWN. THIS PROJECT'S AIMS WILL DEEPEN OUR UNDERSTANDING OF APS NEUTROPHIL MEMBRANES BY SYNERGISTICALLY LEVERAGING WELL-DEFINED AUTOANTIBODIES, UNIQUE MOUSE MODELS, AND A ROBUST, HIGHLY MOTIVATED PATIENT COHORT. AIM 1 WILL CHARACTERIZE THE MOLECULAR PATHWAYS IN ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID ANTIBODY-ACTIVATED NEUTROPHILS THAT TRIGGER GSDMD CLEAVAGE AND DOWNSTREAM THROMBO-INFLAMMATORY EFFECTOR FUNCTIONS. AIM 2 WILL ELUCIDATE THE ROLE OF PHOSPHOLIPID OXIDATION IN ANTIPHOSPHOLIPID ANTIBODY-MEDIATED NEUTROPHIL ACTIVATION AND THROMBO-INFLAMMATORY NETOSIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ROLE OF THE ENDOCANNABINOID SYSTEM, METABOLIC DISEASE PROGRESSION, AND ASSOCIATED CARDIOVASCULAR RISK - PROJECT SUMMARY INDIVIDUALS WHO PROGRESS FROM HAVING OBESITY TO DEVELOPING OVERT DIABETES WILL EXPERIENCE, IN PARALLEL, A STEADY TWO- TO THREE-FOLD RISE IN THEIR RISK FOR CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. THE DYNAMIC AND COMPLEX DRIVERS OF BOTH ADVANCING METABOLIC DISEASE AND ITS ASSOCIATED CARDIOVASCULAR RISK REMAIN UNCLEAR. THE ENDOCANNABINOID SYSTEM IS AN ENDOGENOUS NETWORK OF SMALL LIPID SIGNALING MOLECULES INCLUDING CIRCULATING ENDOCANNABINOID SPECIES, SUCH AS ANANDAMIDE AND 2-ARACHIDONOYLGLYCEROL, WHICH NORMALLY INTERACT WITH CANNABINOID RECEPTORS TO REGULATE ENERGY BALANCE, APPETITE, AND LIPID METABOLISM. OVERACTIVATION OF THE ENDOCANNABINOID SYSTEM IS KNOWN TO CONTRIBUTE TO THE PROGRESSION OF METABOLIC DISEASES WHILE CONCURRENTLY INTERFACING WITH PRO-ATHEROGENIC VASCULAR MECHANISMS. PHARMACOLOGICAL INTERVENTIONS DESIGNED TO TARGET THE ENDOGENOUS ENDOCANNABINOID SYSTEM HAVE DEMONSTRATED THE POTENTIAL TO MITIGATE THESE METABOLIC DISTURBANCES IN CLINICAL STUDIES. DESPITE THESE ADVANCES, HOWEVER, PROGRESS HAS BEEN STYMIED BY A STILL LIMITED UNDERSTANDING OF THE COMPLEX INTERRELATIONS AMONG CIRCULATING ENDOCANNABINOIDS AND THEIR ROLE IN CONTRIBUTING TO HUMAN METABOLIC PHYSIOLOGICAL AND PATHOPHYSIOLOGICAL PROCESSES. IN PRELIMINARY WORK, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED A NUMBER OF DISTINCT ENDOCANNABINOIDS AND RELATED SPECIES THAT APPEAR CONCORDANTLY RELATED TO RISK FOR BOTH INCIDENT DIABETES AND INCIDENT CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE. OUR MOST RECENT FINDINGS NOW INDICATE THAT A SUBSET OF THESE BIOACTIVE LIPIDS IS ASSOCIATED WITH METABOLIC RELATED CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE IN A CONTEXT DEPENDENT MANNER – OFFERING A POTENTIAL EXPLANATION FOR THE MIXED RESULTS SEEN IN PRIOR CLINICAL TRIALS OF CANNABINOID RECEPTOR INHIBITORS OR INVERSE AGONISTS. TO INFORM ONGOING EFFORTS TO DEVELOP NEW AND TAILOR EXISTING METABOLIC THERAPIES, WE NOW PROPOSE A COMPREHENSIVE PROSPECTIVE INVESTIGATION DESIGNED TO MORE PRECISELY IDENTIFY THE KEY ENDOCANNABINOID PATHWAYS THAT UNDERLIE PROGRESSIVE METABOLIC DISEASE AND ITS ASSOCIATED CARDIOVASCULAR RISK. WE ANTICIPATE THIS WORK WILL PROVIDE THE CRITICAL INSIGHTS NEEDED TO EFFECTIVELY DEVELOP AND TAILOR INTERVENTIONS, INCLUDING EXISTING AND NOVEL THERAPIES, AIMED AT MITIGATING EXCESS CARDIOVASCULAR RISKS FOR ALL PERSONS WITH METABOLIC DISEASE INCLUDING THOSE WITH OBESITY AND/OR DIABETES.

description: A MULTISCALE MODELING APPROACH TO UNCOVER MECHANISMS BY WHICH PROCOAGULANT AGENTS RESTORE HEMOSTASIS IN PLATELET INTEGRIN DISORDERS - PROJECT SUMMARY GLANZMANN'S THROMBASTHENIA (GT) IS A RARE CONGENITAL BLEEDING DISORDER CAUSED BY DEFICIENCY OR DYSFUNCTION OF THE PLATELET INTEGRIN ΩIIBΕ3, WHICH MEDIATES PLATELET-PLATELET COHESION ESSENTIAL FOR STABLE CLOT FORMATION. THE STANDARD OF CARE FOR SEVERE BLEEDING IN GT AND OTHER PLATELET INTEGRIN DISORDERS (PIDS) IS PLATELET TRANSFUSION. WHEN PLATELETS ARE NOT AVAILABLE, PROCOAGULANT AGENTS SUCH AS RECOMBINANT ACTIVATED FACTOR VII (RFVIIA) ARE USED. HOWEVER, TREATMENT REMAINS LARGELY EMPIRICAL BECAUSE THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH RFVIIA AND TRANSFUSED PLATELETS RESTORE HEMOSTASIS IN THE PRESENCE OF DYSFUNCTIONAL ENDOGENOUS PLATELETS ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. IT IS UNCLEAR WHETHER GT PLATELETS CAN ADOPT A PROCOAGULANT PHENOTYPE, WHETHER PROCOAGULANT PLATELETS ARE REQUIRED FOR RFVIIA EFFICACY, AND HOW ΩIIBΕ3-DEFICIENT PLATELETS INTERACT WITH FIBRIN. EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES ALONE CANNOT RESOLVE THESE QUESTIONS DUE TO THE COMPLEXITY OF PLATELET FUNCTIONS, THE INABILITY TO SELECTIVELY BLOCK SPECIFIC INTERACTIONS IN VIVO, AND THE LOW THROUGHPUT OF ANIMAL MODELS. THIS GAP IN MECHANISTIC UNDER- STANDING LIMITS THE DEVELOPMENT OF TARGETED, DURABLE THERAPIES FOR GT AND RELATED DISORDERS. COMPUTATIONAL APPROACHES, USED ALONGSIDE EXPERIMENTAL ONES, OFFER MECHANISTIC HYPOTHESIS GENERATION, OPTIMIZATION IN SE- LECTING TARGETED EXPERIMENTS, AND VISUALIZATION THAT EXPERIMENTS ALONE CANNOT ACHIEVE. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO DEVELOP A COMPUTATIONAL MODELING FRAMEWORK THAT INTEGRATES THE BIOCHEMISTRY, BIOPHYSICS, AND BIOME- CHANICS OF CLOTTING WITH EXPERIMENTAL DATA TO PROVIDE ACCURATE MECHANISTIC PREDICTIONS FOR BLEEDING AND CLOTTING DISORDERS. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS APPLICATION IS TO DEVELOP SPARKS-DCM, AN EXPERIMENTALLY VALIDATED MULTISCALE COMPUTATIONAL MODELING FRAMEWORK THAT INCLUDES SINGLE-PLATELET RESOLUTION AND ON-PLATELET BIOCHEM- ISTRY TO ENABLE MECHANISTIC STUDIES OF PIDS. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT GPVI ENABLES ΩIIBΕ3-INDEPENDENT HEMOSTASIS BY (1) ENHANCING PLATELET PROCOAGULANT ACTIVITY UPON ACTIVATION BY COLLAGEN OR FIBRIN AND (2) ANCHOR- ING ΩIIBΕ3-DEFICIENT PLATELETS TO THE FIBRIN NETWORK. THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO 1) DEVELOP A MICROSCALE MODEL OF PLATELET BONDING AND SURFACE-DEPENDENT COAGULATION REACTIONS (SPARKS-D), 2) DEVELOP THE MESOSCALE MODEL AND CREATE SPARKS-DCM THROUGH TWO-WAY COUPLING OF FLUID DYNAMICS AND PLATELET REACTIONS, AND 3) DETER- MINE THE ROLE OF GPVI IN THE PROHEMOSTATIC EFFECTS OF RFVIIA AND PLATELET TRANSFUSION IN PIDS. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE, BY INTEGRATING COMPUTATIONAL MODELS AND EXPERIMENTS, IT WILL REVEAL THE MECH- ANISMS THAT RESTORE HEMOSTASIS IN PIDS AND OFFER A FREELY-AVAILABLE COMPUTATIONAL TOOL TO STUDY AND TEST NOVEL PROHEMOSTATICS IN PIDS. THESE OUTCOMES ARE EXPECTED TO POSITIVELY IMPACT TREATMENT STRATEGIES FOR PIDS AND BLEEDING DISORDERS MORE BROADLY BY PROVIDING EVIDENCE-BASED SELECTION OF PROHEMOSTATIC AGENTS WITH PLATELET TRANSFUSION.

description: STATE MODULATION OF HIPPOCAMPAL MEDIATED MEMORY FORMATION IN THE HUMAN BRAIN - PROJECT SUMMARY EVERY MOMENT OF OUR DAILY EXPERIENCE SETS THE STARTING POINT FOR A NEW MEMORY TO POTENTIALLY FORM. HOWEVER, A HOST OF NEURAL EVENTS MUST CONSPIRE TOGETHER FOR ANY GIVEN EXPERIENCE TO FIND A PERSISTENT PLACE IN OUR MEMORIES. HOW AND WHEN ARE MEMORIES STRENGTHENED OVER TIME TO SUPPORT THEIR LONG-TERM CONSOLIDATION? ONE MECHANISM FOR STRENGTHENING PUTATIVE MEMORY TRACES IS THOUGHT TO BE THE REPEATED “REPLAY” OR “REACTIVATION” OF NEURAL ACTIVITY PATTERNS FROM THE PAST, WHICH OCCURS IN THE HIPPOCAMPUS DURING SHARP WAVE RIPPLE EVENTS. A PREVAILING VIEW IS THAT “OFFLINE” PERIODS OF REST, PARTICULARLY SLEEP, ARE CRUCIAL FOR PROMOTING THESE HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLE EVENTS IN THE SERVICE OF PROGRESSIVELY STRENGTHENING AND CONSOLIDATING LONG-TERM MEMORIES. HOWEVER, A NUMBER OF RECENT FINDINGS FROM THE HUMAN HAVE SUGGESTED HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLE EVENTS OCCUR READILY DURING AWAKE “ONLINE” MEMORY PROCESSING STAGES, SUCH AS ENCODING AND RETRIEVAL. IF FURTHER SUPPORTED, THESE DATA ARGUE FOR A POTENTIAL RECONSIDERATION OF WHAT STATES ARE ASSOCIATED WITH HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLE GENESIS, PROMOTING A BROADER FUNCTIONAL ROLE, BUT SUCH FINDINGS ARE HIGHLY VARIABLE ACROSS HUMAN STUDIES AND SHOW DIVERGENCE FROM THE RODENT. THEREFORE, A CENTRAL QUESTION THAT REMAINS TO BE RESOLVED IN THE FIELD IS: WHEN DO AWAKE HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLES OCCUR IN HUMANS? IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE SEEK TO TEST A PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL STATE MODEL TO ANSWER THIS QUESTION, WHICH WE ARGUE BETTER ACCOUNTS FOR RECENT FINDINGS IN THE HUMAN AND IS CLOSELY BASED ON THE MECHANISMS OF RIPPLE GENESIS DERIVED FROM ANIMAL MODELS. SPECIFICALLY, WE ARGUE IN SUPPORT OF HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLES BEING ASSOCIATED WITH OFFLINE STATES, BUT THAT SUCH STATES OCCUR TRANSIENTLY AND DYNAMICALLY WITH NATURAL FLUCTUATIONS IN AWAKE AROUSAL. MECHANISTICALLY, THIS STATE MODEL LINKS THE CAUSAL ROLE OF ACETYLCHOLINE IN MODULATING BOTH AROUSAL STATES AS WELL AS HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLE GENESIS. TO TRACK THIS INFLUENCE, WE WILL USE PUPILLOMETRY, TOGETHER WITH INVASIVE RECORDINGS FROM THE HUMAN HIPPOCAMPUS. ACROSS TWO AIMS WE WILL CORRELATE AND CAUSALLY TEST I) THE INFLUENCE OF AROUSAL STATE ON HIPPOCAMPAL RIPPLE GENESIS (AIM 1); II) THE INFLUENCE OF AROUSAL STATE MODULATION OF RIPPLE EVENTS ON LONG-TERM MEMORY BEHAVIOR (AIM 2). THROUGH THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS, WE WILL PROVIDE IMPORTANT EVIDENCE TOWARDS UNDERSTANDING HOW AND WHEN MEMORIES ARE FORMED AND CONSOLIDATED OVER TIME AND THE ROLE PLAYED BY AROUSAL IN THIS PROCESS, WHICH HAS BROAD LINKS TO THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF AROUSAL DYSREGULATION COMMON TO MANY PSYCHIATRIC DISORDERS. FURTHERMORE, THE PROPOSED PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL MODEL MAY PROVIDE IMPORTANT TEMPORAL INFORMATION FOR TARGETING NEUROMODULATORY INTERVENTIONS TO IMPROVE MEMORY AND RELATED DYSFUNCTIONS IN DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A MULTI-LEVEL INTERVENTION TO UPSCALE HIV TESTING AND PREP UPTAKE FOR MEN WITH HIGH HIV EXPOSURE VIA COMMUNITY PHARMACIES IN RESOURCE-LIMITED SETTINGS - COMMUNITY PHARMACIES (CPS) ARE A PROMISING BUT UNDERUSED HIV PREVENTION PLATFORM. PHARMACISTS ARE OFTEN THE FIRST POINT OF CONTACT FOR HEALTHCARE IN COMMUNITIES WHERE FORMAL HEALTH FACILITIES MAY BE LESS ACCESSIBLE. WE HAVE A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO EFFICIENTLY STUDY THE POTENTIAL BENEFITS OF PHARMACIES FOR HIV PREVENTION IN GHANA. MEN WITH INCREASED HIV EXPOSURE IN GHANA EXPERIENCE A DISPROPORTIONATE HIV BURDEN, WITH RECENT DATA SHOWING HIV PREVALENCE OF 26.1% IN 2024, UP FROM 18% IN 2017, COMPARED WITH APPROXIMATELY 2% IN THE GENERAL POPULATION. ITS ESPECIALLY HIGH IN URBAN INFORMAL CENTERS, WHERE BEHAVIORAL EXPOSURE, LIMITED HIV KNOWLEDGE, CONFIDENTIALITY CONCERNS, AND CONSTRAINED ACCESS TO PREVENTION SERVICES REDUCE HIV TESTING AND PREP UPTAKE. GHANA, , HAS ADOPTED NATIONAL GUIDELINES FOR HIV SELF-TESTING (HIVST) AND PREP AND PRIORITIZED COMMUNITY-BASED PREVENTION ACCESS. HOWEVER, IMPLEMENTATION REMAINS LIMITED, AND EXISTING APPROACHES OFTEN EMPHASIZE ENROLLMENT AND DISTRIBUTION TARGETS RATHER THAN THE BEHAVIORAL, SOCIAL, AND SERVICE-ACCESS DETERMINANTS THAT SHAPE HIVST, PREP INITIATION, AND PREP ADHERENCE. OUR PILOTS SHOW THAT MEN ARE WILLING TO RECEIVE HIVST AND ORAL OR LONG-ACTING INJECTABLE (LAI) PREP THROUGH CPS AND THAT PHARMACISTS IN CPS ARE WILLING TO PROVIDE THESE SERVICES. YET CP-BASED IMPLEMENTATION HAS NOT BEEN SYSTEMATICALLY TESTED. TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS, WE DEVELOPED LAFIYA PHARMACY, A MULTILEVEL INTERVENTION THAT COMBINES AN EVIDENCE-BASED U.S. PHARMACY PREP DELIVERY MODEL WITH BEHAVIORAL COMPONENTS FROM LAFIYA, AN INTERVENTION DEVELOPED FOR URBAN INFORMAL SETTLEMENT CONTEXTS. LAFIYA PHARMACY IS DESIGNED TO ADDRESS PREVENTION KNOWLEDGE, SERVICE NAVIGATION, LINKAGE TO CARE, IMPLEMENTATION CAPACITY, AND ORAL OR LAI PREP ADHERENCE WHILE EXPANDING CONFIDENTIAL ACCESS TO HIV PREVENTION THROUGH CPS. THIS WORK TESTS WHETHER AN ENHANCED U.S. CP-BASED MODEL CAN FUNCTION UNDER CONDITIONS WHERE SOCIAL DETERRENTS, INFORMAL SETTLEMENT CONDITIONS, AND LIMITED FACILITY ENGAGEMENT SHAPE PREVENTION DECISIONS. GUIDED BY IMPLEMENTATION SCIENCE FRAMEWORKS, THIS STUDY WILL FINALIZE AND EVALUATE LAFIYA PHARMACY TO INCREASE HIVST AND ORAL OR LAI PREP UPTAKE AMONG MEN WITH INCREASED HIV EXPOSURE. AIM 1 WILL FINALIZE THE INTERVENTION PROTOCOL THROUGH FOCUS GROUP DISCUSSIONS WITH MEN, COMMUNITY PHARMACISTS, AND HIV/PHARMACY POLICY STAKEHOLDERS, FOLLOWED BY EXPERT AND COMMUNITY ADVISORY BOARD REVIEW AND PILOT TESTING. AIM 2 WILL EVALUATE EFFECTIVENESS USING A STEPPED-WEDGE DESIGN WITH 12 RETAIL PHARMACIES, 60 PHARMACISTS, AND 240 MEN ACROSS SIX COMMUNITY CLUSTERS, WITH PRIMARY OUTCOMES OF HIVST UPTAKE AND ORAL OR LAI PREP UPTAKE. AIM 3 WILL CONDUCT FOLLOW-UP QUALITATIVE INTERVIEWS TO EXPLAIN TRIAL FINDINGS AND INFORM SCALABILITY, SUSTAINABILITY, AND INTEGRATION INTO NATIONAL HIV PREVENTION SYSTEMS. THIS STUDY WILL GENERATE IMPLEMENTATION EVIDENCE ON WHETHER CPS CAN DELIVER CONFIDENTIAL, DECENTRALIZED HIV TESTING AND PREP SERVICES WHERE FACILITY-BASED ACCESS IS CONSTRAINED. GIVEN THE HEAVY BURDEN OF HIV IN THESE POPULATIONS IN GHANA, CONDUCT OF THE STUDY THERE WILL PROVIDE TIME- AND COST-EFFICIENIES RELATIVE TO US-BASED CONDUCT. FINDINGS WILL INFORM PHARMACY-BASED HIV PREVENTION IN GHANA AND PROVIDE TRANSFERABLE EVIDENCE FOR U.S. COMMUNITIES WHERE SIMILAR DETERMINANTS LIMIT HIV TESTING, PREP INITIATION, AND PREP PERSISTENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THE ASSEMBLY OF AXO-AXONIC SYNAPSES IN THE CEREBRAL CORTEX - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE PROPER FUNCTIONING OF CORTICAL CIRCUITS DEPENDS ON THE PRECISE FORMATION OF SYNAPTIC CONNECTIONS BETWEEN EXCITATORY PYRAMIDAL NEURONS (PYNS) AND A DIVERSE ARRAY OF INHIBITORY GABAERGIC INTERNEURONS (INS), EACH WITH DISTINCT AXONAL ARBORS THAT TARGET SPECIFIC SUBCELLULAR COMPARTMENTS OF PYNS AND SHAPE THEIR OUTPUT PROPERTIES. AMONG THESE INS, CHANDELIER CELLS (CHCS), ALSO KNOWN AS AXO-AXONIC CELLS, ARE ARGUABLY THE MOST DISTINCTIVE DUE TO THEIR EXQUISITE AXONAL MORPHOLOGY AND UNIQUE SUBCELLULAR INNERVATION. THESE CELLS POSSESS A HIGHLY BRANCHED AXON WITH MULTIPLE TERMINAL ARRAYS OF PRESYNAPTIC BOUTONS, REFERRED TO AS CARTRIDGES, ALLOWING ONE CHC TO CONNECT WITH A LARGE POPULATION OF PYNS. MOREOVER, CHCS ARE THE ONLY IN TYPE THAT FORMS SYNAPSES EXCLUSIVELY AT THE AXON INITIAL SEGMENT (AIS) OF PYNS, THE SITE OF ACTION POTENTIAL INITIATION. THESE FEATURES ENABLE CHCS TO EXERT DECISIVE YET PRECISE CONTROL OVER PYN FIRING AND POPULATION OUTPUT. CONSISTENT WITH THEIR FUNCTIONAL SIGNIFICANCE, DEFECTS IN CHC SYNAPTIC CONNECTIVITY HAVE BEEN IMPLICATED IN NEURAL DISORDERS, SUCH AS SCHIZOPHRENIA, AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER, AND EPILEPSY. DESPITE THEIR IMPORTANCE, THE MOLECULAR PROCESSES UNDERLYING THE SUBCELLULAR FORMATION OF CHC SYNAPSES ON PYN AISS REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD, REPRESENTING A SIGNIFICANT KNOWLEDGE GAP. SYNAPSE FORMATION IS A COMPLEX, MULTISTEP PROCESS THAT INCLUDES SYNAPTIC TARGET RECOGNITION, THE FORMATION OF PRE- AND POST-SYNAPTIC CONTACTS, AND THE DIFFERENTIATION AND STABILIZATION OF SYNAPSES. BEYOND NEURON-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS, MICROGLIA, THE BRAIN'S IMMUNE CELLS, HAVE ALSO EMERGED AS KEY CONTRIBUTORS TO SYNAPSE DEVELOPMENT. WHILE WE AND OTHERS HAVE IDENTIFIED CHC-EXPRESSED SIGNALING AND CYTOSKELETAL REMODELING PROTEINS INVOLVED IN THE LATER STAGES OF SYNAPSE FORMATION, THE MOLECULAR COMPONENTS DRIVING THE SUBCELLULAR INNERVATION OF PYN AISS BY CHCS, AS WELL AS MICROGLIA'S ROLE IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THESE AXO-AXONIC SYNAPSES, REMAIN LARGELY ELUSIVE. IN RECENT STUDIES SCREENING FOR PYN-EXPRESSED CELL ADHESION MOLECULES (CAMS) ENRICHED AT THE AIS, WE IDENTIFIED L1CAM AND CNTN1 AS KEY MOLECULES REQUIRED FOR PROPER CHC/PYN AIS INNERVATION. ADDITIONALLY, WE FOUND THAT MICROGLIA PROMOTE CHC CARTRIDGE/BOUTON DEVELOPMENT AND AIS SYNAPTOGENESIS, UNCOVERING FOR THE FIRST TIME A SYNAPTOGENIC ROLE FOR THESE CELLS IN REGULATING INHIBITORY SYNAPSES. BUILDING ON THESE DISCOVERIES, WE PROPOSE HERE TO IDENTIFY THE PRESYNAPTIC BINDING PARTNERS OF L1CAM AND CNTN1 ON CHCS, CRUCIAL FOR UNDERSTANDING CHC TARGETING OF PYN AISS AT THE SUBCELLULAR LEVEL. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL DEFINE HOW MICROGLIA ARE RECRUITED TO CHC-INNERVATED PYN AISS AND HOW THEY PROMOTE SYNAPTOGENESIS AND MODULATE CHC/PYN SYNAPTIC FUNCTION, REVEALING THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THEIR PREVIOUSLY UNRECOGNIZED ROLE IN INHIBITORY SYNAPSE FORMATION. TO ACHIEVE THESE GOALS, WE WILL USE A MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPROACH THAT COMBINES CUTTING-EDGE TECHNIQUES SUCH AS TARGETED IN UTERO ELECTROPORATION, TWO-PHOTON LIVE IMAGING IN AWAKE MICE, AND ADVANCED GENETIC, MOLECULAR, AND ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL METHODS. TOGETHER, OUR STUDIES WILL PROVIDE PIONEERING INSIGHTS INTO THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF CHC/PYN AIS SYNAPTIC CONNECTIVITY, WITH IMPLICATIONS FOR HEALTH AND DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SYNAPTIC MECHANISMS OF INTERMITTENT THETA BURST STIMULATION FOR MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER IS ASSOCIATED WITH DEFICITS IN NEUROPLASTICITY. RESCUE OF THIS PLASTICITY IS THE PUTATIVE MECHANISM OF ACTION OF AN FDA-CLEARED TREATMENT FOR DEPRESSION CALLED INTERMITTENT THETA BURST STIMULATION (ITBS), A PATTERNED FORM OF TRANSCRANIAL MAGNETIC STIMULATION (TMS). WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY FOUND THAT AGONISM OF THE N-METHYL-D-ASPARTATE RECEPTOR (NMDAR), WHICH ACTS AS A GATEKEEPER FOR SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY, IS SUFFICIENT TO ENHANCE THE FACILITATION PRODUCED BY TMS TO THE MOTOR CORTEX OF HEALTHY SUBJECTS. THIS SUGGESTING THAT LONG- TERM POTENTIATION (LTP) IS THE UNDERLYING CAUSE OF TMS-INDUCED FACILITATION. WE FURTHER FOUND A PARTIAL RESCUE OF MDD PLASTICITY DEFICITS IN THE MOTOR CORTEX, AND IN A CLINICAL TRIAL FOR DEPRESSION, HAVE OBSERVED AN UNPRECE- DENTED IMPROVEMENT IN CLINICAL SYMPTOMS WITH NMDAR AGONIST, D-CYCLOSERINE (DCS) COMBINED WITH ITBS. IT IS ESSENTIAL NOW THAT THIS PROMISING NEW TREATMENT APPROACH WHICH IS BASED ON THE PREMISE OF PROMOTING SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY BE DIRECTLY TESTED TO VALIDATE THE THEORETICAL UNDERPINNINGS ENABLING OPTIMIZATION AND GUIDANCE OF PO- TENT PLASTICITY INDUCERS FOR THE TREATMENT OF DEPRESSION AND OTHER DISORDERS. WE PROPOSE TO DETERMINE WHETHER ITBS, AS DELIVERED CLINICALLY, WORKS THROUGH ENHANCING SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY, AND TO VALIDATE OUR THEORY THAT DCS PHARMACOLOGIC AUGMENTATION OF ITBS INDEED WORKS THROUGH THIS MECHANISM OF ACTION. WE PROPOSE TO EXAMINE SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY INDUCED BY ITBS USING CONCURRENT PHARMACOLOGY TO BLOCK (AIM 1) AND ACTIVATE (AIM 2) THE NMDAR DURING ITBS IN 40 DEPRESSED PATIENTS COMPARED TO 40 HEALTHY CONTROLS. FOR THE FIRST TIME, THIS PHARMACOLOGIC AUGMENTATION STRATEGY WILL BE USED TO ASSESS LTP-ASSOCIATED CHANGES IN THE DORSOLATERAL PREFRONTAL CORTEX (DLPFC), WHERE CLINICAL ITBS TREATMENTS ARE DELIVERED, USING ELECTROENCEPHALOG- RAPHY (EEG)-BASED TMS-EVOKED POTENTIALS (TEPS). IN A DOUBLE-BLIND, RANDOMIZED, CROSSOVER DESIGN, EACH SUBJECT WILL RECEIVE A SINGLE SESSION OF 1) ITBS + NMDAR ANTAGONIST, DEXTROMETHORPHAN, 2) ITBS + NMDAR AGONIST, DCS, 3) ITBS + PLACEBO, 4) SHAM ITBS + PLACEBO. IN AN EXPLORATORY AND INDEPENDENT AIM 3, WE WILL TEST EACH DRUG, INCLUDING PLACEBO, OVER 30 DAILY (ACTIVE) ITBS SESSIONS IN A PARALLEL DESIGN WITH ONLY MDD SUB- JECTS. TOGETHER, THESE AIMS WILL TEST THE LTP-LIKE MECHANISMS OF A SESSION OF ITBS AS WELL AS A COURSE OF ITBS, WHICH CAN, AND LIKELY DOES, INVOLVE HOMEOSTATIC CHANGES WHEREBY NEURONS GLOBALLY SCALE RECEPTOR LEVELS TO MAINTAIN THE ABILITY TO RECEIVE ADDITIONAL INPUTS. WE WILL THEN UNDERSTAND HOW PLASTICITY CHANGES OVER THE COURSE OF ITBS, AS WELL AS PHARMACOLOGICALLY AUGMENTED ITBS. WITHIN EACH SESSION, TEP ASSESSMENTS WILL BE GIVEN AT BASELINE, AFTER DRUG, AND THEN AFTER ITBS + DRUG. THIS DESIGN WILL CONTROL FOR THE EFFECTS OF ITBS AND DRUG, AND WILL DEMONSTRATE THE NECESSITY AND SUFFICIENCY OF NMDAR ACTIVITY FOR ITBS-INDUCED PLASTICITY, BOTH ESSENTIAL EVIDENCES FOR LTP, AND WILL DIRECTLY TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT OUR PROMISING CLINICAL TRIAL RESULTS WERE DUE TO EN- HANCED PLASTICITY, VALIDATING AND PAVING THE WAY TO TRANSFORMATIVE TREATMENT APPROACHES IN THE BRAIN THAT MAY TRIPLE CURRENT EFFICACY RATES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SOCIAL PERCEPTION AND COGNITION IN A MARMOSET MODEL OF PHELAN MCDERMID SYNDROME - PROJECT SUMMARY AND ABSTRACT PHELAN-MCDERMID SYNDROME (PMS) IN HUMANS IS CAUSED BY MUTATIONS IN THE SHANK3 GENE, LEADING TO SEVERE INTELLECTUAL IMPAIRMENT AND SOCIAL AND EMOTIONAL DIFFICULTIES THAT ARE OFTEN FOUND IN AUTISM. TO IDENTIFY POSSIBLE NEURAL IMPAIRMENTS IN SOCIAL PERCEPTION AND COGNITION IN A MARMOSET MODEL OF PMS, AND HOW THEY MIGHT BE CORRECTED WITH GENE THERAPY, WE PROPOSE TO STUDY MARMOSETS WITH IMPLANTED ELECTROCORTICOGRAPHY ARRAYS OVER THE VISUAL CORTEX, INFERIOR TEMPORAL CORTEX, AUDITORY CORTEX, AND PREFRONTAL CORTEX, WITH NEURAL RECORDINGS TAKEN BEFORE AND AFTER GENE THERAPY. OUR HYPOTHESES ARE GUIDED BY EXTENSIVE PRELIMINARY DATA. IN AIM 1, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THE CORTICAL SYSTEMS FOR SOCIAL INFORMATION PROCESSING ARE IMPAIRED IN MARMOSETS WITH SHANK3 MUTATIONS COMPARED TO WILD-TYPE ANIMALS, PRIOR TO GENE THERAPY. RECORDINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED BOTH UNDER HIGHLY CONTROLLED EXPERIMENTAL CONDITIONS WHILE ANIMALS VIEW STATIC IMAGES AND VIDEO CLIPS, AND IN THE HOME CAGE WITH THE CAGE-MATE, WITH MORE NATURALISTIC BEHAVIOR THAT IS ANALYZED WITH AUTOMATED VIDEO METHODS. PRELIMINARY RESULTS SUGGEST THAT WHILE LOW-LEVEL VISUAL INFORMATION IS PROCESSED NORMALLY IN SHANK3 MUTANTS, SOCIAL INFORMATION REPRESENTED IN RELEVANT NEURAL CIRCUITS IS DEGRADED, ESPECIALLY IN THE PREFRONTAL CORTEX. THIS IMPAIRMENT IN NEURAL PROCESSING IS FOUND EVEN WHEN THEIR GAZE AND OTHER BEHAVIOR ARE RELATIVELY NORMAL. IN THE RECORDINGS OF AIM 2, WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THESE SAME CIRCUITS ARE IMPAIRED WHEN THE ANIMALS ARE TESTED IN DIFFICULT COGNITIVE TASKS. PRELIMINARY RESULTS FROM REVERSAL LEARNING AND WORKING MEMORY SUGGEST THAT WHILE REVERSAL LEARNING IS NORMAL, WORKING MEMORY PERFORMANCE IS IMPAIRED IN SHANK3 MUTANT ANIMALS, AND THIS IMPAIRMENT SEEMS TO BE ASSOCIATED WITH ABNORMAL ACTIVITY IN PREFRONTAL CORTEX. THUS, PREFRONTAL CORTEX IS EMERGING IN THE PRELIMINARY DATA AS A KEY REGION WHERE NEURAL CIRCUITS MAY BE AFFECTED IN BOTH SOCIAL PERCEPTION AND GENERAL COGNITION IN PMS. IN AIM 3, WE WILL REPEAT ALL OF THESE MEASUREMENTS AFTER THE ANIMALS HAVE RECEIVED A TYPE OF GENE THERAPY, CONSISTING OF GENE REPLACEMENT WITH A SHANK3 MINI-GENE. THE BEFORE-AND-AFTER MEASUREMENTS IN THE SAME ANIMALS WILL HELP NARROW DOWN THE CIRCUIT ABNORMALITIES IN PMS AND HELP IDENTIFY WHICH ABNORMALITIES MIGHT BE AMELIORATED BY GENE THERAPY. BECAUSE PMS SHARES MANY FEATURES WITH SEVERE FORMS OF AUTISM, THE RESULTS MAY HAVE GENERAL IMPLICATIONS FOR UNDERSTANDING SOME OF THE CIRCUIT ABNORMALITIES UNDERLYING THE SOCIAL AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENTS FOUND IN MORE COMMON FORMS OF AUTISM.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NOVEL APPROACHES TO SUPPORTING STUDENTS WITH ADHD IN MULTI-TIERED SYSTEMS OF SUPPORT (MTSS) - ABSTRACT  CHILDREN WITH ADHD ARE LIKELY TO EXHIBIT BEHAVIORAL DIFFICULTIES IN THE CLASSROOM THAT INHIBIT LEARNING (DALEY & BIRCHWOOD, 2010; DUPAUL & STONER, 2003; FABIANO ET AL., 2006; FRIEDMAN & PFIFFNER, 2020; LOE & FELDMAN, 2007; RAGGI & CHRONIS, 2006; RAPPORT, CHUNG, SHORE, & ISAACS, 2001). THESE ISSUES MAKE ADDRESSING ADHD AN AREA IN NEED OF CONTINUOUS AND CONTEMPORARY SUPPORT, PARTICULARLY DURING EARLY ELEMENTARY SCHOOL (BITSKO ET AL., 2022), IN ORDER TO PREVENT THE WORSENING, LIFE-LONG ISSUES THAT INDIVIDUALS WITH ADHD MAY CONFRONT THROUGHOUT THE LIFESPAN. THE PRESENT APPLICATION FOCUSES ON SUPPORTS AND INTERVENTIONS FOR STUDENTS IN ELEMENTARY SCHOOL, AS THAT IS WHERE INITIAL IDENTIFICATION AND INTERVENTION TYPICALLY OCCURS (VISSER ET AL., 2014). WITH THE ADVENT OF MULTI-TIERED SYSTEMS OF SUPPORT (MTSS) WITHIN SCHOOL SETTINGS, A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH TO THE DELIVERY OF UNIVERSAL, TARGETED, AND INDICATED SCHOOL MENTAL HEALTH AND EDUCATIONAL SUPPORTS MAY BE ENHANCED. THE MOST INTENSIVE TIER OF THE MTSS (I.E., TIER 3) IS CURRENTLY THE MOST UNDER-DEVELOPED. THE CREATION OF A POSITIVE BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT CLASSROOM THROUGH TIER 3 OF THE MTSS WILL ASSIST TEACHERS IN IMPROVING THE POSITIVE BEHAVIORAL SUPPORT PROVIDED TO THE STUDENT WITH ADHD. THUS, THE PRESENT INVESTIGATION WILL BE SITUATED WITHIN EVERYDAY SCHOOL PROCEDURES FOR SUPPORTING A STUDENT WITH BEHAVIORS CONSISTENT WITH ADHD. PARTICIPANTS WILL BE 288 ELEMENTARY SCHOOL CHILDREN RECRUITED FROM PARTICIPATING SCHOOL DISTRICTS WITHIN THE EXISTING SCHOOL-BASED PROBLEM SOLVING TEAMS. WE WILL WORK WITH GRADES FIRST TO FOURTH. REFERRED CHILDREN WILL THEN ALL RECEIVE A LEAD-IN, TIER 2 INTERVENTION TO INCLUDE A DAILY REPORT CARD (DRC) INTERVENTION. THOSE WHO CONTINUE TO NEED ADDITIONAL BEHAVIOR SUPPORTS IN THE SPRING -- TIER 3 INTERVENTION -- WILL BE ALLOCATED THROUGH RANDOM ASSIGNMENT TO SCHOOL AS USUAL OR ACADEMIC/BEHAVIOR COMPETENCY (ACE) CLASSROOM IN A HYBRID TYPE 1 DESIGN. THE ACE CLASSROOM IS AN APPROACH BASED ON DECADES OF RESEARCH IN SUMMER TREATMENT PROGRAM CLASSROOMS (FABIANO ET AL., 2007; PELHAM ET AL., 2025). AIM 1 EVALUATES THE OUTCOMES OF THE APPROACH RELATIVE TO SCHOOL AS USUAL. AIM 2 EVALUATES THE IMPLEMENTATION OF THE APPROACH AND EXPLORES COMPONENTS OF USER IMPLEMENTATION THAT PROMOTE FIDELITY. AIM 3 EXPLORES MODERATORS OF THE INTERVENTION OUTCOMES (E.G., COMORBID OPPOSITIONAL/AGGRESSIVE BEHAVIOR OR LEARNING DISABILITIES).

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BIDIRECTIONAL INFLUENCES BETWEEN SOCIAL MEDIA USE AND ADOLESCENT DEPRESSION: TESTING THE ROLE OF FRONTOPARIETAL CONNECTIVITY - ABSTRACT SOCIAL MEDIA IS NOW A MAJOR SOURCE OF ENVIRONMENTAL INPUT FOR ADOLESCENTS. OVER 90% OF U.S. ADOLESCENTS ARE REGULARLY USING SOCIAL MEDIA, WITH 45% REPORTING THAT THEY ARE ONLINE “NEARLY CONSTANTLY”. WHILE 80% OF ADOLESCENTS REPORT THAT SOCIAL MEDIA USE (SMU) MAKES THEM FEEL “MORE CONNECTED” WITH THEIR PEERS, THERE ARE NONETHELESS GROWING CONCERNS THAT PATHOLOGICALLY HEAVY USE IS IMPACTING ATTENTIONAL FOCUS, EXECUTIVE FUNCTIONING, AND SOCIAL COGNITION, AND DRIVING INCREASES IN DEPRESSION AMONG YOUTH, PARTICULARLY AMONG GIRLS. MANY OF THE BRAIN REGIONS CONSTITUTING FRONTOPARIETAL NETWORKS (FPNS) THAT SUPPORT ATTENTIONAL FOCUS, EXECUTIVE FUNCTION, AND SOCIAL COGNITION HAVE ALSO BEEN IMPLICATED IN DEPRESSION. HOWEVER, THERE IS LIMITED DATA LINKING SMU WITH ALTERATIONS IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF FPNS IN THE CONTEXT OF PSYCHOPATHOLOGY RISK. WE HAVE PREVIOUSLY DEMONSTRATED THAT GREATER USE OF NEGATIVE EMOTIONAL WORDS ON SOCIAL MEDIA APPS IS ASSOCIATED WITH GREATER WITHIN-NETWORK FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY OF BOTH MEDIAL AND DORSAL FPNS; A DIAGNOSIS OF DEPRESSION HAS ALSO BEEN ASSOCIATED WITH GREATER FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY OF THE MEDIAL FPN BUT LOWER FUNCTIONAL CONNECTIVITY OF THE DORSAL FPN WITH MIDCINGULO-INSULAR NETWORKS. HOWEVER, NO STUDIES TO DATE HAVE EXAMINED WHETHER PATHOLOGICAL SMU POTENTIATES DEPRESSION RISK (OR VICE-VERSA), AND THE EXTENT TO WHICH FPN DEVELOPMENT IS IMPACTED BY SMU. TOWARD THIS END, WE PROPOSE TO LEVERAGE FIVE WAVES OF LONGITUDINAL DATA FROM THE ADOLESCENT BRAIN COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT (ABCD) STUDY (N>10,000, AGES 13–18) TO TEST ASSOCIATIONS AMONG PROBLEMATIC (V. NORMATIVE) SMU, RISK FOR ADOLESCENT DEPRESSION, AND FPN DEVELOPMENT. UNLIKE PREVIOUS STUDIES IN THIS AREA WHICH FOCUS ON SELF-REPORTED SMU, WE WILL LEVERAGE SMARTPHONE-BASED PASSIVE SENSING TECHNOLOGY TO ASCERTAIN OBJECTIVE MEASURES OF TOTAL EXPOSURE (I.E., AMOUNT OF TIME SPENT) AND NATURE OF ENGAGEMENT (E.G., APPLYING SENTIMENT ANALYSES TO DETERMINE FREQUENCY OF NEGATIVE EMOTIONAL CONTENT) WITH SOCIAL MEDIA APPS. THESE METRICS OF SOCIAL MEDIA EXPOSURE AND ENGAGEMENT WILL BE COMBINED WITH CLINICAL AND SELF-REPORTED ASSESSMENTS OF DEPRESSION AND MULTIMODAL (RESTING-STATE FMRI, DIFFUSION MRI) MEASURES OF DORSAL, LATERAL, AND MEDIAL FPN CONNECTIVITY TO TEST THREE INDEPENDENT AIMS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL TEST WHETHER AND HOW SMU SHAPES ADOLESCENT DEVELOPMENT OF FPN CONNECTIVITY (AIM 1), WHETHER TRAJECTORIES OF FPN CONNECTIVITY MEDIATE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN SMU AND DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS AND VICE-VERSA (AIM 2), AND ADOPT A DATA-DRIVEN MACHINE LEARNING STRATEGY TO TEST WHETHER SMU AND FPN CONNECTIVITY OUTPERFORM OTHER FACTORS IN PREDICTING ADOLESCENT-ONSET DEPRESSION (AIM 3). THE RESULTS OF THIS INNOVATIVE AND SCIENTIFICALLY RIGOROUS STUDY WILL ANSWER CRITICAL QUESTIONS ON WHAT CONSTITUTES POTENTIALLY PATHOLOGICAL SMU, WHO MAY BE DISPROPORTIONATELY IMPACTED BY SMU IN THE CONTEXT OF DEPRESSION RISK, AND IDENTIFY MODIFIABLE NEURODEVELOPMENTAL MECHANISMS BY WHICH SMU MAY LEAD TO DEPRESSION. ALL RESEARCH FINDINGS WILL BE DISSEMINATED RESPONSIBLY TO INFORM GUIDANCE FOR YOUTH AND THEIR FAMILIES, CLINICIANS, EDUCATORS, TECHNOLOGY-BASED STAKEHOLDERS, AND POLICYMAKERS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: BIOPHYSICAL MECHANISMS OF CORTICAL MICROSTIMULATION - DIRECT LOCAL ELECTRICAL STIMULATION (DLES) IS AN INCREASINGLY IMPORTANT THERAPEUTIC TOOL FOR TREATING BRAIN DISORDERS SUCH AS PARKINSON’S, EPILEPSY, AND OCD. THERE IS CONSIDERABLE DISAGREEMENT, HOWEVER, AS TO HOW NEURAL STIMULATION, ESPECIALLY AT THE SCALE OF NEURONS, AFFECTS HUMAN BRAIN FUNCTION. THIS LACK OF UNDERSTANDING HAMPERS THE DESIGN AND IMPLEMENTATION OF MORE EFFECTIVE STIMULATION APPROACHES, PARTICULARLY IN THE CORTEX. TO DELIVER ON THE PRECISE, INCLUSIVE, AND EFFECTIVE THERAPEUTIC PROMISE OF DLES, A MORE MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE BIOPHYSICS OF CORTICAL STIMULATION IS REQUIRED. THIS PROJECT COMBINES SINGLE-CELL ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY IN BOTH HUMAN AND MOUSE CORTEX, BOTH EX-VIVO AND IN VIVO WITH PHARMACOLOGY, OPTICAL PHYSIOLOGY, AND SOPHISTICATED COMPUTATIONAL MODELING TO IDENTIFY THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING ELECTRICAL STIMULATION. IN A TRULY TRANSLATIONAL APPROACH, THESE MULTIPLE RESEARCH ANGLES WILL ALLOW US TO TEST IN-DEPTH MECHANISTIC HYPOTHESES IN THE MOUSE AND WHETHER THESE RESULTS HOLD TRUE IN THE HUMAN. WE WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT DLES INDUCES A DYNAMIC SEQUENCE OF EXCITATORY (E) NEURON OUTPUT COUNTERED BY SUBSEQUENT INHIBITORY (I) NEURON. WE WILL EVALUATE STIMULATION INTENSITY, FREQUENCY, PHASE, DISTANCE, AND SPECIES AS KEY PARAMETERS IN MODULATING THE TIMING AND STRENGTH OF THIS E-I DYNAMIC SEQUENCE. THESE DATA ON NEURONAL DYNAMICS WILL BE LEVERAGED INTO ACTIONABLE KNOWLEDGE THROUGH AN INTEGRATE-AND-FIRE BASED RECURRENT NEURONAL NETWORK MODEL WHICH WE WILL USE TO PREDICT CORTICAL RESPONSES TO NOVEL STIMULI AND DEVELOP SPECIFIC STIMULATION PATTERNS TO EVOKE DESIRED NEURAL OUTPUTS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL IDENTIFY THE BIOPHYSICAL MECHANISMS BY WHICH DLES RECRUITS DIFFERENT NEURONAL POPULATIONS IN ACUTE BRAIN SLICES OF HUMAN AND MOUSE CORTEX USING WHOLE-CELL ELECTROPHYSIOLOGY AND PHARMACOLOGY (AIM 1). WE WILL THEN CHARACTERIZE NEURON AND POPULATION RESPONSES TO DLES IN VIVO, USING NEUROPIXELS PROBES IN AWAKE HUMAN AND MOUSE CORTEX, COMPLEMENTED BY OPTICAL RECORDINGS IN THE AWAKE MOUSE (AIM 2). THIS EXTENSIVE AND DETAILED DATA SET WILL BE USED TO REFINE AND VALIDATE A TRAINABLE NEURAL NETWORK MODEL WE HAVE DEVELOPED TO ASSESS STIMULATION EFFECTS ON E AND I CELL TYPES (AIM 3). THE MODEL WILL BE THE TESTING GROUND TO DEVELOP SPECIFIC PATTERNS OF STIMULATION BASED ON DESIRED OUTPUTS SUCH AS TARGETING EITHER E OR I CELLS. THE MODEL WILL ALSO BE USED TO TEST NOVEL INPUT STIMULI INCLUDING AMPLITUDE AND FREQUENCY RAMPS, CHIRPS, AND STEP FUNCTIONS TO PREDICT NEURAL RESPONSES. TESTING THESE MODEL-PREDICTED OUTPUTS, OR RESPONSES, WILL THEN BE CARRIED OUT THROUGH FURTHER EX- AND IN-VIVO PHYSIOLOGY. NOT ONLY WILL WE CONNECT DYNAMICS OF A PRIMARY MODEL SYSTEM TO ACTIVITY IN THE HUMAN BRAIN, BUT THIS WORK WILL ALSO PROVIDE A UNIQUE ROUTE TOWARD PREDICTABLE MODULATION OF ACTIVITY IN INDIVIDUAL NEURONS AND LOCAL CIRCUITS TO DESIGN TAILORED NEUROMODULATION THERAPIES. OUR MULTI-SCALE ANALYSES OF THE NEURAL MECHANISMS OF ELECTRICAL STIMULATION WILL CATALYZE NOVEL, TARGETED, AND MECHANISTICALLY DRIVEN THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES THAT COULD REVOLUTIONIZE STIMULATION-BASED TREATMENT FOR MEMORY DISORDERS, DEPRESSION, STROKE RECOVERY, AND A HOST OF OTHER NEUROPSYCHIATRIC AILMENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE YOUNG GUT MICROBIOME: A FOUNTAIN OF YOUTH FOR BRAIN INJURY IN THE AGED? - TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY (TBI) IS A LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH AND DISABILITY WORLDWIDE. PATIENTS AGED 65 YEARS AND OLDER ACCOUNT FOR AN INCREASING PROPORTION OF PATIENTS WITH TBI AND LESS THAN HALF OF AGED TBI PATIENTS BECOME FUNCTIONALLY INDEPENDENT AFTER INJURY. IN FACT, TBI IS ONE OF THE GREATEST NON-GENETIC RISK FACTORS FOR THE SUBSEQUENT DEVELOPMENT OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD) AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE-RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD). CHRONIC NEUROINFLAMMATION RESULTING FROM THE CONSTITUTIVE ACTIVATION OF MICROGLIA IS COMPLICIT IN AD, ADRD AND RELATED DISEASE PROCESSES, AND REPRESENTS A COMPLEX INTERPLAY BETWEEN AGED MICROGLIA AND THE STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION OF THE AGED GUT MICROBIOME. HOWEVER, THE MECHANISM(S) UNDERLYING GUT MICROBIOTA-MICROGLIA INTERACTION IN AD, ADRD, AND AGING HAVE YET TO BE ELUCIDATED. PUBLISHED DATA FROM OUR LABORATORY SHOWS THAT AGED MICROGLIA ADOPT A CONSTITUTIVELY ACTIVATED STATE. THESE “PRIMED” MICROGLIA ARE THEN CAPABLE PRODUCING AN EXAGGERATED INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE AND MAY REPRESENT ONE OF THE MECHANISMS LEADING TO THE INCREASED INCIDENCE OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE-RELATED DEMENTIA IN AGED PATIENTS AFTER TBI. PUBLISHED AND PRELIMINARY DATA FROM OUR LABORATORY FURTHER DEMONSTRATES THAT POST-INJURY GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY STRUCTURE IS A CONTRIBUTING FACTOR IN THE DEGREE OF NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT INCLUDING IN AD AND ADRD DIAGNOSES AFTER TBI. OUR DATA SHOWS THAT RESTORATION OF A PREINJURY GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY MARKEDLY IMPROVED NEUROCOGNITIVE INCLUDING AD/ADRD-RELATED OUTCOMES AND ATTENUATED THE CONSTITUTIVE ACTIVATION OF MICROGLIA AFTER TBI IN MICE. WE PUBLISHED SIMILAR FINDINGS WITHIN THE GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY ASSOCIATED WITH NORMAL AGING WITH AN INCREASE IN THE RELATIVE ABUNDANCE OF SEVERAL MICROBIAL TAXA STRONGLY ASSOCIATED WITH AD AND ADRD. NONETHELESS, MECHANISM(S) LINKING ALTERATIONS IN THE AGED GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUBSEQUENT AD AND ADRD HAVE YET TO BE FULLY ELUCIDATED. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT RESTORATION OF A YOUTHFUL GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY BEFORE OR AFTER TBI WILL ATTENUATE THE CONSTITUTIVE ACTIVATION OF MICROGLIA AND IMPROVE NEUROCOGNITIVE AND AD/ADRD-RELATED OUTCOMES IN AGED TBI MICE. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER RESTORING A YOUTHFUL GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY STRUCTURE VIA FECAL MICROBIOTA TRANSPLANT WITH STOOL FROM YOUNG MICE WILL ATTENUATE THE ACTIVATION OF MICROGLIA IN AGED MICE. WE WILL UTILIZE BOTH A PRE-INJURY “PREBIOTIC” MODEL AS WELL AS A POST-INJURY TREATMENT PARADIGM. WE WILL USE BULK POPULATION CELL SORTING (FACSORTING) OF MICROGLIA FOLLOWED BY SINGLE CELL RNA SEQUENCING (SCRNASEQ). WE WILL COMPARE CANDIDATE GENES TO MICROBIAL ACTIVITY VIA FECAL 16S RRNA GENE AMPLICON SEQUENCING AND FECAL METABOLITE ANALYSIS. HARMONIZED WITH THE TRANSCRIPTOMIC AND GUT MICROBIAL COMMUNITY PROFILING, WE WILL UTILIZE LONGITUDINAL PET/CT IMAGING OF THE 18-KDA TRANSLOCATOR PROTEIN (TSPO) WITH A NOVEL FLUORINE-BASED RADIOTRACER DEVELOPED BY OUR GROUP TO TRACK AND COMPARE THE ONSET, PROGRESSION, AND DEGREE OF MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION BEFORE, DURING, AND AFTER GUT MICROBIAL INTERVENTION AFTER TBI. COLLECTIVELY, THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL IDENTIFY THE KEY ROLE OF AN AGED GUT MICROBIOME IN THE ONSET AND PROGRESSION OF CONSTITUTIVE MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION OVER THE COURSE OF TBI, THUS RAISING THE POTENTIAL FOR NOVEL THERAPEUTIC AND BIOMARKER DEVELOPMENT IN AGED TBI, AD, AND ADRD PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SINGLE-PULSE ELECTRICAL STIMULATION TO IMPROVE SURGICAL OUTCOMES IN DRUG-RESISTANT EPILEPSY - PROJECT SUMMARY  EPILEPSY IS A NEUROLOGICAL DISORDER AFFECTING NEARLY 1% OF THE GLOBAL POPULATION, WITH A SUBSTANTIAL PORTION OF PATIENTS EXPERIENCING PERSISTENT SEIZURES DESPITE TREATMENT WITH ANTI-EPILEPTIC MEDICATIONS. FOR PATIENTS WITH FOCAL SEIZURES, SURGICAL RESECTION OF EPILEPTOGENIC REGIONS CAN BE POTENTIALLY CURATIVE, BUT SUCCESS HEAVILY DEPENDS ON ACCURATE LOCALIZATION OF THE EPILEPTOGENIC NETWORKS RESPONSIBLE FOR SEIZURE GENERATION. SINGLE-PULSE ELECTRICAL STIMULATION (SPES) HAS EMERGED AS A TOOL FOR IDENTIFYING EPILEPTOGENIC NETWORKS BY ELICITING CORTICO- CORTICAL EVOKED POTENTIALS (CCEPS), WHICH REVEAL EFFECTIVE CONNECTIVITY BETWEEN BRAIN REGIONS. HOWEVER, SPES IS NOT YET WIDELY USED IN CLINICAL SETTINGS DUE TO THREE KEY LIMITATIONS: A LACK OF STANDARDIZED STIMULATION PROTOCOLS AND COMPARISON WITH ESTABLISHED INTERICTAL BIOMARKERS OF SEIZURE-GENERATING BRAIN REGIONS, AN INCOMPLETE CLINICAL INTUITION FOR CCEPS DUE TO SPARSE SAMPLING OF INTRACRANIAL EEG, AND THERE HAS BEEN LIMITED EXPLORATION OF CCEPS TO GUIDE OTHER DIAGNOSTIC TESTS IN EPILEPSY MEDICINE, SUCH AS STIMULATION-INDUCED SEIZURES. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO TACKLE THESE LIMITATIONS USING DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS AND CONTROL THEORY TO ENHANCE THE UTILITY OF SPES IN THE EPILEPSY CLINIC, THEREBY IMPROVING LOCALIZATION OF EPILEPTOGENIC NETWORKS AND INCREASING THE CHANCES OF POST-SURGICAL SEIZURE FREEDOM. TO DO THIS, WE WILL FIRST COMPARE THE LOCALIZATION EFFICACY FOR SPES-EVOKED BIOMARKERS IN COMPARISON WITH WELL-STUDIED INTERICTAL BIOMARKERS IN A RETROSPECTIVE COHORT OF 124 PATIENTS FROM FOUR LEVEL 4 EPILEPSY CENTERS (UAB, NEW YORK UNIVERSITY, JOHNS HOPKINS UNIVERSITY, AND THE UNIVERSITY OF PENNSYLVANIA). WE WILL THEN OPTIMIZE SPES PARAMETERS, SUCH AS PULSE AMPLITUDE, PULSE WIDTH, AND POLARITY, IN A PROSPECTIVE COHORT OF 50 PATIENTS AT UAB TO IDENTIFY THE MOST ROBUST PARAMETERS FOR LOCALIZING HYPEREXCITABLE REGIONS USING BOTH THE CCEP WAVEFORM AND HYPEREXCITABILITY METRICS DERIVED FROM THE DYNAMICAL NETWORK MODELS. NEXT, WE WILL USE AN INNOVATIVE BAYESIAN NEURAL NETWORK MODEL TO PREDICT EFFECTIVE CONNECTIONS FROM A SET OF STIMULATION SITES, PIONEERING A METHOD TO IMPUTE CCEP AMPLITUDES IN REGIONS NOT DIRECTLY SAMPLED WITH IEEG ELECTRODES. LASTLY, WE WILL USE A CCEP-DERIVED DYNAMICAL NETWORK MODEL TO PREDICT STIMULATION FREQUENCIES THAT MAY BE USED TO TRIGGER SEIZURES, INCREASING THE DIAGNOSTIC YIELD FROM PATIENTS UNDERGOING INTRACRANIAL MONITORING. BY REFINING SPES PROTOCOLS AND DERIVING COMPLEMENTARY CLINICAL TESTS USING THE EVOKED RESPONSES, THIS WORK HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IMPROVE THE ACCURACY OF EPILEPTOGENIC NETWORK LOCALIZATION, DRASTICALLY REDUCE THE TIME PATIENTS SPEND IN THE HOSPITAL FOR INTRACRANIAL MONITORING, AND INCREASE THE LIKELIHOOD OF SEIZURE FREEDOM AFTER SURGICAL INTERVENTION. SUCCESSFUL OUTCOMES FROM THIS STUDY COULD BE PARADIGM-SHIFTING FOR THE DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT OF EPILEPSY, ULTIMATELY ENHANCING CLINICAL CARE FOR THIS HIGH-RISK PATIENT POPULATION.
