description: MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION AND INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINE SECRETION AS MECHANISMS DRIVING CNS CONSEQUENCES OF INTERMITTENT EXPOSURE TO PATHOGENS - INCREASED APPRECIATION FOR CHRONIC MANIFESTATIONS OF INFECTION EXPOSURE, AND THE HOST INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE TO INFECTION, HAS REVEALED NOVEL FACTORS THAT COULD DRIVE NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE SUCH AS DEMENTIA AND EXCITING OPPORTUNITIES FOR PREVENTION OF THESE DEVASTATING CONDITIONS. INDEED, A ROBUST LITERATURE HAS DOCUMENTED CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) MANIFESTATIONS WITH EXPOSURE TO A PATHOGEN BOTH DURING ACUTE SICKNESS AND IN THE LONG- TERM RECOVERY PERIOD. FOR INSTANCE, WE HAVE PRELIMINARY DATA THAT INTERMITTENT VIRUS EXPOSURE IMPAIRS COGNITION, ALTERS BRAIN MICROVESSEL ENERGY METABOLISM, INDUCES NEUROINFLAMMATION, INCREASES HIPPOCAMPAL BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER PERMEABILITY, AND RESULTS IN DISTINCT TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC PROFILES RELATIVE TO AGE-MATCHED. WHILE ACCUMULATING EVIDENCE SUPPORTS CHRONIC NEUROINFLAMMATION (VIA ACTIVATED MICROGLIA AND A PROINFLAMMATORY CYTOKINE MILIEU) AS A MECHANISM BY WHICH INFECTION EXPERIENCE PERTURBS BRAIN FUNCTION, THE EXTENT TO WHICH NEUROINFLAMMATION REPRESENTS A CONVERGENCE POINT THROUGH WHICH DIVERSE PATHOGEN SUBTYPES POTENTIAL INDUCE THEIR EFFECTS REMAINS UNKNOWN. FOR THIS RESEARCH PROGRAM, IN EXPLORING THE INTERACTION BETWEEN INFECTION HISTORY, NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE VULNERABILITY, AND BOTH SYSTEMIC AND NEUROINFLAMMATION, WE WILL CONTRIBUTE FUNDAMENTAL AND CRITICALLY NEEDED KNOWLEDGE REGARDING THE CHRONIC BRAIN AND BEHAVIOR IMPACTS OF EXPOSURE TO DISTINCT PATHOGEN SUBTYPES. IN THIS PROPOSAL, WE WILL 1) INVESTIGATE VIRAL INFECTION CONTRIBUTIONS TO LONG-TERM BRAIN AND BEHAVIOR FUNCTION IN NORMAL AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE MOUSE MODELS, 2) CHARACTERIZE TRANSCRIPTIONAL AND EPIGENETIC PROFILES OF DISTINCT POPULATIONS OF PATHOGEN-EXPOSED CELLS IN THE BRAIN, 3) INTERROGATE MICROGLIA AND INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES AS MECHANISMS DRIVING THESE NEUROLOGICAL CONSEQUENCES, 4) DISCERN THE EXTENT TO NEUROTROPISM AND PATHOGEN SUBTYPE IS REQUIRED FOR THESE EFFECTS. OUR APPROACH IS INNOVATIVE AS OUR RECURRENT INFECTION EXPOSURE REGIMEN REPRESENTS A DEPARTURE FROM THE SCIENTIFIC STATUS QUO AND MORE TRANSLATIONALLY MIMICS HUMAN SYSTEMIC INFECTION EXPERIENCE DURING ADULTHOOD. FURTHER, IT LEVERAGES CUTTING-EDGE SPATIAL TRANSCRIPTOMICS TO COMPREHENSIVELY EXAMINE PATHOGEN-INDUCED TRANSCRIPTOMIC PROFILE SHITS AT A SUB-CELLULAR LEVEL IN BRAIN AND REVEAL NEW TARGETS. FINALLY, OUR USE OF BOTH NEUROTROPIC AND PERIPHERALLY-RESTRICTED INFECTIONS WILL ENABLE US TO DISCERN THE EXTENT TO WHICH DIFFERENT PATHOGENS CONVERGE ON SIMILAR TARGETS TO INDUCE CNS EFFECTS. OUR ACCOMPLISHED INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH TEAM OF EXPERTS IN NEUROSCIENCE, INFECTIOUS DISEASE, IMMUNOLOGY, AND NEUROLOGICAL DISEASES IS WELL-POISED TO CARRY OUT THE PROPOSED STUDIES. MORE BROADLY, A KEY COMPONENT OF THIS PROGRAM IS IN PAIRING OUR IMPACTFUL RESEARCH WITH EFFORTS TO ENGAGE KEY STAKEHOLDERS IN THE COMMUNITY THROUGH OUR ROBUST AND ESTABLISHED NEUROSCIENCE OUTREACH INITIATIVES. THESE ACTIVITIES REPRESENT A PRIORITY FOR THE NINDS AS WELL AS THE MILLIONS OF PATIENTS, CAREGIVERS, AND CLINICIANS SHOULDERING THE BURDEN OF INFECTION-INDUCED CHRONIC DISEASE.  DISEASE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AUTOMATED PROGRAMMING FOR PERSONALIZED DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION IN PARKINSONS DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT SUCCESSFUL IMPLEMENTATION OF DEEP BRAIN STIMULATION (DBS) FOR TREATMENT OF PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD) HINGES ON APPROPRIATE SELECTION OF STIMULATION PARAMETERS (CONTACT CONFIGURATION, AMPLITUDE, PULSE WIDTH, FREQUENCY) TO MAXIMIZE THERAPEUTIC BENEFIT AND MINIMIZE SIDE EFFECTS. THERE IS AN URGENT NEED TO DEVELOP MORE EFFICIENT PRO- GRAMMING METHODS TO EXPAND DBS ACCESS WHILE MAINTAINING AND POTENTIALLY IMPROVING CLINICAL OUTCOMES. OB- JECTIVE AND RAPIDLY MEASURABLE ELECTROPHYSIOLOGIC BIOMARKERS NOW EXIST THAT COULD GUIDE AUTOMATED SELECTION OF STIMULATION PARAMETERS USING MACHINE LEARNING ALGORITHMS. DBS-LOCAL EVOKED POTENTIAL (DLEP), A BRAIN SIGNAL MEASURED FROM NON-STIMULATING CONTACTS ON THE DBS ELECTRODE, HAS EMERGED AS A PROMISING MARKER OF TARGET ENGAGEMENT AND THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY IN PD. THE MOST TROUBLESOME SIDE EFFECT OF DBS ARE MUSCLE CONTRACTIONS FROM INADVERTENT SPREAD OF STIMULATION WHICH CAN BE RECORDED AS MOTOR EVOKED POTENTIALS (MEP) FROM FACE AND LIMB MUSCLES. META-ACTIVE LEARNING (META-AL) IS A NOVEL REINFORCEMENT LEARNING METHOD THAT, BY USING A DATABASE OF PRIOR PATIENTS, CAN ACTIVELY SELECT PARAMETERS IN CLOSED-LOOP TO FIND OPTIMAL PATIENT-SPECIFIC PARAMETERS IN A FEW ITERATIONS THAT MAXIMIZE DLEP AND MINIMIZE MEP. THE GOAL OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE AN AUTOMATED DBS PROGRAMMING PLATFORM FOR PATIENTS WITH PD. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT META-AL IS BETTER THAN ALTER- NATIVE ALGORITHMS TO EFFICIENTLY OPTIMIZE DBS PARAMETERS, AND THAT DLEP AND MEP ARE SUPERIOR BIOMARKERS TO LOCAL FIELD POTENTIAL BETA POWER FOR THIS PURPOSE. A PRACTICAL, FULLY AUTOMATED DBS PROGRAMMING SYSTEM DOES NOT EXIST – OUR MULTI-DISCIPLINARY TEAM HAS THE ENGINEERING AND CLINICAL EXPERTISE TO ACHIEVE IT. IN AIM 1, WE WILL OPTIMIZE AND VALIDATE META-AL ALGORITHM FOR AUTOMATED DBS PROGRAMMING. WE WILL BUILD A SIMULATED TRAINING ENVIRONMENT BASED ON EXPERIMENTAL DATA TO TRAIN META-AL AND TO COMPARE ITS PERFORMANCE AGAINST OTHER ALGO- RITHMS. OUR ALGORITHM WILL GENERATE VISUAL BIOMARKER RESPONSE MAPS DEPICTING THE TRADE-OFF BETWEEN THERAPEUTIC BENEFIT, SIDE-EFFECT RISK, AND ENERGY EFFICIENCY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DEPLOY META-AL ALGORITHM INTRAOPERATIVELY TO FIND PATIENT-SPECIFIC OPTIMAL DBS PARAMETERS. WE WILL REFINE TECHNICAL INFRASTRUCTURE TO DEPLOY META-AL IN CLOSED-LOOP DURING DBS SURGERY. WE WILL TEST THE ALGORITHM IN 40 PATIENTS WITH PD (20 SUBTHALAMIC; 20 PALLIDAL NUCLEUS TARGET). IN AIM 3, WE WILL EVALUATE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY OF SELECTED OPTIMAL STIMULATION PARAMETERS AND COMPARE THEM TO CLINICALLY OPTIMIZED SETTINGS AND TO SETTINGS BASED ON BETA POWER. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL CONDUCT A 4-WEEK AT-HOME TESTING TO ASSESS LONG-TERM EFFICACY OF BIOMARKER-BASED STIMULATION. FINALLY, WE WILL EXPLORE HOW CLINICIANS INTER- ACT WITH AI OUTPUT TO SUPPORT AND IMPROVE CLINICIAN/MACHINE DECISION-MAKING. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PRO- JECT WILL CREATE A SET OF NOVEL ALGORITHMS AND DEFINE NECESSARY REAL-TIME RECORDING/STIMULATION PROCEDURES TO ACHIEVE THIS GOAL. THE END PRODUCT WILL BE A PRACTICAL, FULLY AUTOMATED DBS PROGRAMMING SYSTEM THAT WILL BE DEPLOYABLE IN CLINICAL PRACTICE AND IN CLINICAL TRIALS COMPARING CONVENTIONAL AND AUTOMATED DBS PROGRAMMING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: LRP8 AND APOLIPOPROTEIN E ALLELE-SPECIFIC MODULATION OF NEURAL REPAIR - PROJECT SUMMARY ADULT CNS TRAUMA FREQUENTLY CAUSES NEURONAL DISCONNECTION AND PERSISTENT DEFICITS DUE TO FAILED AXON REGENERATION. FOR TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURY (TBI), THIS INCLUDES COGNITIVE DEFICITS AS WELL AS PROGRESSIVE DYSFUNCTION IN CHRONIC TRAUMATIC ENCEPHALOPATHY (CTE). FOR SPINAL CORD INJURY (SCI), MOTOR, SENSORY AND AUTONOMIC DEFICITS FAIL TO RESOLVE, CAUSING LIFE-LONG DISABILITY. WHILE MODEL SYSTEM SCREENING HAS IDENTIFIED MULTIPLE CANDIDATE NEURAL REPAIR PATHWAYS, APOE–LRP8 SIGNALING IS UNIQUE IN ALSO BEING IMPLICATED CLINICALLY. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT CORTICAL AXON REGENERATION REQUIRES LRP8 AND IS MODIFIED BY APOE VARIANTS. APOE2-EXPRESSING MICE SHOW REPARATIVE CORTICOSPINAL AND RAPHESPINAL AXON GROWTH WITH GREATER MOTOR FUNCTION THAN CONTROLS AFTER SCI. DISTINCT FROM APOE IN OTHER SETTINGS, THERE IS NO CHANGE IN INFLAMMATION OR SCARRING. AFTER AXOTOMY, APOE EXERTS ALLELE- SPECIFIC EFFECTS ON LRP8 LOCALIZATION AND SIGNALING IN CORTICAL NEURONS. APOE ALLELES REGULATE SYNAPTIC ORGANIZATION GENE EXPRESSION BY CORTICAL NEURONS AFTER INJURY, WITH LITTLE EFFECT ON GLIAL GENE EXPRESSION. THUS, THIS PROJECT HAS IDENTIFIED A ROLE FOR APOE–LRP8 SIGNALING IN THE SUCCESS OF AXON REGROWTH FOLLOWING CNS TRAUMA OF RELEVANCE FOR TBI AND SCI. WE AIM TO EXPLORE THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF TARGETING THIS PATHWAY FOR NEURAL REPAIR. IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES WITH AAV-APOE2 INJECTION AFTER TRAUMA, WE OBSERVED ROBUST INCREASES IN AXONAL GROWTH AND RECOVERY AFTER SCI. WE WILL EXTEND THESE FINDINGS BY DELAYING AAV ADMINISTRATION TO THE CHRONIC PHASE AFTER SPINAL CORD CONTUSION AND BY ASSESSING SYSTEMIC DELIVERY. WE WILL ALSO EXAMINE THE CELLULAR MECHANISM OF LRP8–APOE ACTION IN NEURAL REPAIR. WE WILL USE LRP8 NULL MICE AND STUDY GENES THAT ARE DIFFERENTIALLY EXPRESSED IN RESPONSE TO APOE2 AND SCI. ONE TARGET OF LRP8 SIGNALING IS SRC KINASE. WE WILL DETERMINE THE POTENTIAL FOR SRC KINASE INHIBITION TO ACHIEVE NEURAL REPAIR AFTER SCI. THESE EXPERIMENTS WILL UTILIZE AN ORALLY AVAILABLE BRAIN- PENETRANT KINASE INHIBITOR WITH A DIRECT PATH TO CLINICAL TRANSLATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HIGH-EFFICIENCY DEVELOPMENT OF RED GENETICALLY-ENCODED CALCIUM SENSORS USING MACHINE-LEARNING-GUIDED SCREENING AND IN VIVO VALIDATION - PROJECT SUMMARY / ABSTRACT MONITORING NEURAL ACTIVITY WITH GENETICALLY ENCODED CALCIUM INDICATORS (GECIS) IS A CORNERSTONE OF MODERN NEUROSCIENCE, YET RED FLUORESCENT GECIS REMAIN SUBOPTIMAL COMPARED TO THEIR GREEN COUNTERPARTS. CURRENT RED GECIS, SUCH AS JRCAMP1 AND JRGECO1, SUFFER FROM LIMITATIONS IN BRIGHTNESS, DYNAMIC RANGE (∆F/F0), KINETICS, AND PHOTOSTABILITY, RESTRICTING THEIR USE IN DEEP-BRAIN IMAGING AND DUAL-COLOR EXPERIMENTS. ADDITIONALLY, BLUE-LIGHT PHOTOACTIVATION ARTIFACTS IN RED GECIS COMPLICATE MULTIPLEXED IMAGING WITH OPTOGENETIC ACTUATORS. A SIGNIFICANT BOTTLENECK IN IMPROVING RED GECIS IS THE SLOW, LABOR-INTENSIVE PROCESS OF ITERATIVE PROTEIN ENGINEERING. OUR CENTRAL GOAL IS TO OVERCOME THESE BARRIERS AND ENGINEER NEXT-GENERATION RED GECIS WITH ENHANCED BIOPHYSICAL PROPERTIES THAT MATCH OR EXCEED THE PERFORMANCE OF THE BEST GREEN GECIS. WE PROPOSE AN INTEGRATED, INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACH GUIDED BY THREE SPECIFIC AIMS. AIM 1 FOCUSES ON USING MACHINE LEARNING (ML)-DRIVEN OPTIMIZATION TO PREDICT SINGLE-SITE MUTATIONS THAT IMPROVE BRIGHTNESS, CALCIUM SENSITIVITY, DECAY KINETICS, AND DYNAMIC RANGE OF RGECIS. THESE ML PREDICTIONS, TRAINED ON ~1,000 CHARACTERIZED VARIANTS DATASETS, WILL GUIDE TARGETED ENGINEERING EFFORTS, SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCING THE EXPERIMENTAL BURDEN. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ACCELERATE OPTIMIZATION BY CONSTRUCTING COMBINATORIAL MUTATIONAL LIBRARIES AT UP TO FOUR KEY SITES IDENTIFIED VIA ML AND SCREENING THESE LIBRARIES USING OUR HIGH-THROUGHPUT SCREENING PLATFORM, CAPABLE OF FUNCTIONALLY EVALUATING THOUSANDS OF VARIANTS WITHIN HOURS. THIS AIM WILL GENERATE SYNERGISTIC MUTATION COMBINATIONS THAT PRODUCE SUPERIOR RED GECIS BEYOND WHAT SINGLE MUTATIONS CAN ACHIEVE. FINALLY, IN AIM 3, WE WILL RIGOROUSLY VALIDATE THE OPTIMIZED RED GECIS IN VIVO USING TWO-PHOTON AND THREE-PHOTON MICROSCOPY IN AWAKE AND ANESTHETIZED MICE AND RATS. THIS WILL COMPREHENSIVELY VALIDATE THEIR RESPONSE AMPLITUDES, KINETICS, AND SIGNAL-TO-NOISE RATIOS ACROSS MULTIPLE IMAGING CONDITIONS AND CORTICAL AND SUBCORTICAL BRAIN REGIONS. OUR PROJECT IS HIGHLY INNOVATIVE, AS IT UNIQUELY INTEGRATES ML-DRIVEN PREDICTIONS WITH RAPID EXPERIMENTAL VALIDATION, ACCELERATING SENSOR OPTIMIZATION WHILE MINIMIZING THE INEFFICIENCIES OF TRADITIONAL TRIAL-AND-ERROR APPROACHES. WE WILL ESTABLISH A ROBUST OPTIMIZATION PIPELINE THAT CONTINUOUSLY IMPROVES PREDICTIVE ACCURACY AND SENSOR PERFORMANCE BY ITERATIVELY REFINING OUR ML MODELS BASED ON EXPERIMENTAL FEEDBACK. THE SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE THE NEUROSCIENCE COMMUNITY WITH NEXT-GENERATION RED GECIS THAT MATCH OR SURPASS GREEN GECIS, ENABLING HIGH-FIDELITY DUAL-COLOR IMAGING, DEEP-BRAIN CALCIUM IMAGING, AND ADVANCED FUNCTIONAL IMAGING IN PREVIOUSLY INACCESSIBLE EXPERIMENTAL CONTEXTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NOVEL NON-VIRAL GBA1 GENE THERAPY FOR PARKINSON'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY PARKINSON’S DISEASE (PD) IS A PROGRESSIVE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY THE LOSS OF DOPAMINERGIC (DA) NEURONS, LEADING TO SEVERE MOTOR IMPAIRMENTS AND DISABILITY. WHILE THE CURRENT STAND-OF-CARE TREATMENTS, LIKE LEVODOPA, OFFER SYMPTOMATIC RELIEF, THEY DO NOT STOP OR REVERSE NEURODEGENERATION. THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR DISEASE-MODIFYING THERAPIES TARGETING THE ROOT CAUSES OF PD. BOTH MUTATIONS IN THE GCASE-ENCODING GBA1 GENE AND MUTATION-FREE REDUCTION OF GCASE ACTIVITY INCREASE THE RISK OF PD AND DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES (DLB), AS GCASE DEFICIENCY PROMOTES TOXIC GLYCOLIPID BUILDUP AND Α-SYNUCLEIN AGGREGATION, THEREBY DISRUPTING ESSENTIAL CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. THIS PROJECT AIMS TO ENHANCE GCASE ACTIVITY IN THE MIDBRAIN VIA SYSTEMIC GBA1 GENE THERAPY USING A COMPLEMENTARY DELIVERY STRATEGY, COMPRISING FOCUSED ULTRASOUND (FUS)-MEDIATED BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER (BBB) OPENING AND BARRIER-BREACHING BIODEGRADABLE NANOPARTICLES (NPS), AND PROMOTER OPTIMIZATION. THIS APPROACH ADDRESSES THE LIMITATIONS OF ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUSES, SUCH AS LIVER TOXICITY, IMMUNOGENICITY, LIMITED PACKAGING CAPACITY, AND ENORMOUS COSTS, WHILE ENABLING EFFICIENT GENE TRANSFER TO THE TARGET BRAIN AREA VIA A MINIMALLY INVASIVE ADMINISTRATION ROUTE FOR DISEASE-MODIFYING INTERVENTION. BASED ON OUR PILOT DATA SHOWING THAT INTRACRANIAL ADMINISTRATION OF OUR PATENTED NPS CARRYING GBA1 PLASMID REDUCES LB-LIKE PATHOLOGY AND MOTOR SYMPTOMS IN AN Α-SYNUCLEIN PREFORMED FIBRIL (PFF)-INDUCED MOUSE MODEL OF SPORADIC PD, IN AIM 1, WE WILL INVESTIGATE THE EXPRESSION AND SAFETY OF GBA1 PLASMIDS WITH DIFFERENT PROMOTERS DELIVERED VIA OUR NPS, ADMINISTERED EITHER LOCALLY THROUGH CONVECTION-ENHANCED DELIVERY OR SYSTEMICALLY VIA TAIL VEIN INJECTION COMBINED WITH FUS-MEDIATED BBB OPENING. WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE PHYSICOCHEMICAL PROPERTIES AND PHYSIOLOGICAL STABILITY OF THESE NPS AND EVALUATE THE DOSE-DEPENDENT GBA1 TRANSGENE EXPRESSION AND LOCAL AND SYSTEMIC SAFETY PROFILES IN HEALTHY MOUSE BRAINS THROUGH IMAGING, BIOCHEMICAL, AND HISTOLOGICAL TECHNIQUES TO DETERMINE OPTIMAL DOSING. IN AIM 2, WE WILL USE GENETICALLY DEFINED AND CLINICALLY RELEVANT HUMAN CELL MODELS - INCLUDING CRISPR- EDITED SH-SY5YL444P/+ KNOCK-IN CELLS AND Α-SYNUCLEIN PFF-TREATED IPSC-DERIVED DA NEURONS FROM PD PATIENTS WITH AND WITHOUT GBA1 MUTATIONS - TO EVALUATE THE NEUROPROTECTIVE MECHANISMS OF NON-VIRAL GBA1 THERAPY. UNLIKE PRIOR STUDIES USING OVEREXPRESSION OR TOXIN-BASED MODELS, THIS AIM UTILIZES DISEASE-RELEVANT SYSTEMS AND INTEGRATES ADVANCED TRANSCRIPTOMIC AND LIPIDOMIC PROFILING TO UNCOVER DOWNSTREAM PATHWAYS AND IDENTIFY BIOMARKERS OF THERAPEUTIC RESPONSE. IN AIM 3, WE WILL EVALUATE THE THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS OF GBA1 GENE THERAPY IN THE PFF-INDUCED MOUSE MODELS OF PD WITH OR WITHOUT THE L444P GBA1 MUTATION, COMPARING INTRACRANIAL AND SYSTEMIC DELIVERY METHODS DESCRIBED ABOVE. WE WILL ASSESS MOTOR DEFICITS, DA NEURON LOSS, LEWY BODY PATHOLOGY, AND NEUROINFLAMMATION THROUGH BEHAVIORAL ASSAYS, BIOCHEMICAL ANALYSES, AND HISTOLOGICAL ANALYSES, AS WELL AS OMICS PROFILING. THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A FOUNDATION FOR THE ULTIMATE CLINICAL DEVELOPMENT OF NON-VIRAL DISEASE- MODIFYING GENE THERAPY FOR BOTH GBA1-RELATED AND IDIOPATHIC PD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EFFECT OF APOE GENOTYPE ON ENOS REGULATION AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF VCID - VASCULAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA (VCID) OCCURS WHEN THE CEREBROVASCULATURE CAN NO LONGER MAINTAIN HOMEOSTASIS UNDER METABOLIC, ENVIRONMENTAL, GENETIC AND NEURODEGENERATIVE INSULTS, INCLUDING LATE-ONSET ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (LOAD). CEREBROVASCULAR FUNCTION RELIES ON ENDOTHELIAL NITRIC OXIDE SYNTHASE (ENOS) ACTIVITY, WHICH MAINTAINS ENDOTHELIAL HOMEOSTASIS, NO BIOAVAILABILITY, AND VASCULAR INTEGRITY. DYSREGULATED ENOS ACTIVITY DRIVES ENDOTHELIAL DYSFUNCTION, AND ENOS DEFICIENT MICE DEVELOP SEVERAL HALLMARKS OF VCID PATHOLOGY, INCLUDING HYPOPERFUSION, BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER (BBB) BREAKDOWN, CEREBRAL AMYLOID ANGIOPATHY, TAU PATHOLOGY, WHITE MATTER DAMAGE, AND COGNITIVE DECLINE, SUGGESTING A CENTRAL ROLE FOR ENOS IN VCID AND LOAD PROGRESSION. THE NOS3 AND APOE4 (APOLIPOPROTEIN E4) GENES ARE THE ONLY CONSISTENT GENETIC FACTOR INFLUENCING THE RISK AND PROGRESSION OF BOTH LOAD AND CEREBROVASCULAR DISEASE. INTRIGUINGLY, RECENT STUDIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT LOAD-ASSOCIATED VASCULAR DECLINE IS MEDIATED BY ENOS DYSREGULATION IN AN APOE GENOTYPE DEPENDENT MANNER, SUGGESTING THAT APOE ISOFORMS MAY DIFFERENTIALLY INFLUENCE ENOS HOMEOSTASIS TO DRIVE VCID, THOUGH THE UNDERLYING MECHANISMS ARE POORLY UNDERSTOOD. OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES SHOW THAT APOE PLAYS A CONSTITUTIVE ROLE IN MAINTAINING ENOS HOMEOSTASIS AND NO BIOAVAILABILITY IN BRAIN ENDOTHELIA. HOWEVER, APOE4 SIGNIFICANTLY IMPAIRS ENOS ACTIVITY, AND ACCELERATES MICROVASCULAR DYSFUNCTION, PARTICULARLY IN THE PRESENCE OF VCID STRESSORS, LEADING TO ENDOTHELIAL SENESCENCE, WHICH MAY DESCRIBE THE INCREASED PREVALENCE AND ACCELERATED DISEASE PROGRESSION OBSERVED IN APOE4 CARRIERS. THIS PROJECT WILL TAKE A SYSTEMATIC APPROACH IN DETERMINING THE MECHANISMS BY WHICH APOE GENOTYPE AND LOAD CONDITIONS (E.G., WESTERN DIET, PATHOGENIC AMYLOID/TAU) INFLUENCE ENOS STABILIZATION (AIM 1), AND THE RESULTING IMPACT OF ENOS DYSREGULATION ON CEREBROVASCULAR IMPAIRMENT (AIM 2) AND VCID PROGRESSION (AIM 3). TO ADDRESS THESE AIMS, THIS PROJECT WILL USE A MULTI-MODAL APPROACH IN DETERMINING THE EFFECT OF APOE GENOTYPE ON ENOS HOMEOSTASIS UNDER LOAD CONDITIONS INCLUDING: APOE EXPOSURE AND ENOS MODULATION IN BRAIN ENDOTHELIA, IN VITRO BBB INTEGRITY AND TRANSIT USING A 3D BRAIN-CHIP MODULE, IN VIVO ASSESSMENTS OF CEREBROVASCULAR ABNORMALITIES, CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW, AND BBB INTEGRITY, ALONGSIDE EVALUATIONS OF WASTE ELIMINATION AND VCID PATHOLOGY IN LOAD MICE. AT EACH OF THESE STAGES, TO STRATEGICALLY TARGET ENOS, WE WILL EMPLOY BOTH PHARMACOLOGIC AND GENETIC APPROACHES, USING A WELL CHARACTERIZED ENOS ENHANCING PEPTIDE (CAVNOXIN), ALONGSIDE ESTABLISHED ENOS MOUSE MODELS, WHICH DISPLAY CONSTITUTIVELY ENHANCED OR INHIBITED ENOS ACTIVITY. IN THE SHORT TERM, THIS PROJECT WILL NOT ONLY ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE ROLE OF APOE GENOTYPE AND ENOS DYSREGULATION ON CEREBROVASCULAR DECLINE BUT WILL ALSO SHED LIGHT ON THE MOLECULAR UNDERPINNINGS DRIVING THE ONSET AND PROGRESSION OF VCID AND LOAD. IN THE LONG TERM, IT IS ANTICIPATED THAT THE FINDINGS FROM THIS PROJECT WILL FACILITATE THE DEVELOPMENT OF NOVEL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS AND STRATEGIES TO TREAT NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS.

description: SCALABLE INTERFACES FOR SYNCHRONOUS PROBING OF DOPAMINE SIGNALING AND NEURONAL ACTIVITY - PROJECT SUMMARY DOPAMINE NEUROTRANSMITTERS AND NEUROMODULATORS PLAY A CENTRAL ROLE IN LEARNING AND OTHER FLEXIBLE BEHAVIORS. THESE MOLECULES ALSO CONTROL WHETHER NEURONS RESPOND (I.E., SPIKE) TO INPUT SIGNALING, AS WELL AS THE STRENGTH OF CONNECTIONS BETWEEN NEURONS. THIS TIGHT INTERACTION BETWEEN MOLECULES AND NEURONAL ACTIVITY ULTIMATELY HELPS SHAPE HOW THE BRAIN IS WIRED. HOWEVER, DOPAMINE’S FUNCTIONS HAVE LARGELY BEEN STUDIED IN ISOLATION—EITHER IN RELATION TO BEHAVIOR, IN SENTIENT ANIMALS; OR TO NEURONAL ACTIVITY, IN BRAIN TISSUE SLICES. CURRENT TECHNOLOGY DOES NOT ALLOW US TO MEASURE THESE TWO FUNCTIONS TOGETHER. HERE, WE AIM TO BRIDGE THIS GAP BY DEVELOPING AND APPLYING NEW TOOLS CAPABLE OF MEASURING THE SYNCHRONOUS INTERPLAY BETWEEN DOPAMINE AND NEURONAL ACTIVITY IN AWAKE BEHAVING ANIMALS. WE PREVIOUSLY ESTABLISHED MULTI-MODAL SYSTEMS THAT ENABLED RECORDING OF DOPAMINE AND ELECTRICAL NEURAL ACTIVITY IN NONHUMAN PRIMATES—SETTING A FOUNDATION TO BUILD THE PROPOSED TOOLS HERE. KEY UNADDRESSED NEEDS FOR MONITORING THE TARGETED CELLULAR-SCALE INTERACTIONS INCLUDE FOCAL, CELL-SPECIFIC, AND MULTI- SITE MEASUREMENTS. FOCAL SENSORS ARE REQUIRED TO PROBE THE MOLECULAR AND NEURONAL ACTIVITY WITHIN THE MICROSCALE DOMAIN IN WHICH THEY INTERACT. FURTHERMORE, THESE SENSORS SHOULD BE ABLE TO DETECT CELL-SPECIFIC NEURONAL ACTIVITY, IN THE FORM OF ACTION POTENTIALS (I.E., SPIKES). FINALLY, THESE SENSORS SHOULD BE ABLE TO RECORD FROM MULTIPLE DISTRIBUTED LOCATIONS IN THE BRAIN IN ORDER TO DELINEATE SITE-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS. THIS MULTI-CHANNEL CAPABILITY NECESSITATES SMALL SENSORS, TO REDUCE IMPLANT-INDUCED TRAUMA, WHILE ALLOWING SCALING OF CHANNEL NUMBERS. WE PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED MICRO-INVASIVE SENSORS THAT DIRECTLY ENABLE SUCH SCALABILITY WITH MINIMAL TRAUMA AND WERE SHOWN TO PROVIDE CHRONIC (> 1 YEAR) MEASUREMENTS OF DOPAMINE IN THE STRIATUM OF MONKEYS AND RODENTS. THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE ORGANIZED AS FOLLOWS. AIM 1 IS TO DESIGN FOCAL JUXTAPOSED SENSORS CAPABLE OF MEASURING DOPAMINE AND NEURONAL ACTIVITY WITHIN MICROSCALE PROXIMITY AND TO TEST THESE SENSORS IN SIMPLE REWARD-RELATED BEHAVIORS TO VALIDATE THEIR MEASUREMENT CAPABILITIES IN MONKEYS. AIM 2 IS TO CREATE SCALABLE ARRAYS TO ENABLE MEASUREMENTS OF HOW THESE MULTI-MODAL SIGNALS ARE COORDINATED ACROSS WIDESPREAD BRAIN REGIONS (I.E., CORTEX AND STRIATUM).

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE NEURAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING TEMPORAL INTEGRATION - PROJECT SUMMARY A CENTRAL CHALLENGE IN NEUROSCIENCE IS TO UNDERSTAND HOW THE BRAIN PERFORMS FUNDAMENTAL COMPUTATIONS THAT ALLOW ANIMALS TO SENSE, INTERPRET, AND RESPOND TO THE WORLD. ONE KEY COMPUTATION IS TEMPORAL INTEGRATION, THE ABILITY TO ACCUMULATE SENSORY INFORMATION OVER TIME. THIS PROCESS IS ESSENTIAL FOR BEHAVIORS INCLUDING THE VESTIBULO-OCULAR REFLEX (VOR) IN HUMANS, WHICH STABILIZES VISION DURING HEAD MOVEMENTS, AND FOR MAINTAINING POSTURE AND COORDINATED MOVEMENT. WHEN TEMPORAL INTEGRATION IS DISRUPTED, PEOPLE CAN EXPERIENCE GAZE INSTABILITY, NYSTAGMUS, IMBALANCE, AND OTHER MOVEMENT DISORDERS. DESPITE DECADES OF RESEARCH IN VERTEBRATES, MANY OF THE CELLULAR AND NETWORK MECHANISMS UNDERLYING TEMPORAL INTEGRATION REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. THIS PROPOSAL LEVERAGES THE FRUIT FLY DROSOPHILA, WHICH SENSES ANGULAR VELOCITY USING SPECIALIZED SENSORY ORGANS THAT FUNCTION LIKE GYROSCOPES, CALLED HALTERES. THE HALTERE-MOTOR SYSTEM IS ANALOGOUS TO VERTEBRATE GAZE CONTROL CIRCUITS BUT OFFERS UNIQUE EXPERIMENTAL ADVANTAGES: THE COMPLETE WIRING DIAGRAM IS KNOWN, INDIVIDUAL NEURONS CAN BE TARGETED GENETICALLY, AND NEURAL ACTIVITY CAN BE RECORDED AND MANIPULATED WITH PRECISION. WE HAVE DEVELOPED A NOVEL EXPERIMENTAL PARADIGM THAT DELIVERS CONTROLLED ROTATIONAL STIMULI WHILE ENABLING SIMULTANEOUS PHYSIOLOGICAL RECORDINGS, IMAGING, AND OPTOGENETIC MANIPULATIONS IN BEHAVING ANIMALS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL USE CONNECTOMICS TO IDENTIFY CANDIDATE NEURONS IN THE HALTERE-MOTOR PATHWAY THAT ARE LIKELY TO PERFORM TEMPORAL INTEGRATION, CONSTRUCT GENETIC DRIVER LINES FOR THEM, AND PERFORM OPTOGENETIC MANIPULATIONS TO ASSESS THEIR PUTATIVE FUNCTION. IN AIM 2, WE WILL ESTABLISH NEW PREPARATIONS FOR WHOLE-CELL RECORDINGS OF THESE NEURONS TO DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, AND NETWORK MECHANISMS THAT ALLOW THEM TO INTEGRATE SENSORY SIGNALS OVER TIME. IN AIM 3, WE WILL INTEGRATE ANATOMICAL AND PHYSIOLOGICAL DATA INTO DETAILED COMPUTATIONAL MODELS OF THE CELLS AND CIRCUITS THAT PREDICTS HOW NEURAL PROPERTIES PRODUCE TEMPORAL INTEGRATION AND GUIDE BEHAVIOR. THIS INTEGRATIVE APPROACH COMBINES GENETICS, PHYSIOLOGY, AND COMPUTATIONAL MODELING TO UNCOVER THE PRINCIPLES OF TEMPORAL INTEGRATION AT MULTIPLE LEVELS, FROM SINGLE NEURONS TO CIRCUITS. BECAUSE SIMILAR MECHANISMS ARE THOUGHT TO OPERATE IN HUMAN GAZE AND POSTURE CONTROL, OUR WORK WILL PROVIDE INSIGHT INTO DISORDERS SUCH AS GAZE- EVOKED NYSTAGMUS, BALANCE IMPAIRMENTS, AND OTHER CONDITIONS CAUSED BY NEURAL INTEGRATOR DYSFUNCTION. BEYOND HUMAN HEALTH, THESE STUDIES WILL ADVANCE FUNDAMENTAL UNDERSTANDING OF HOW NERVOUS SYSTEMS ACROSS SPECIES ACCUMULATE INFORMATION OVER TIME TO DRIVE ADAPTIVE BEHAVIOR, OFFERING A FRAMEWORK FOR FUTURE INVESTIGATIONS OF SENSORY-MOTOR COMPUTATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MITIGATING NETWORK DYSFUNCTION UNDER AMYLOID-Β PATHOLOGY - PROJECT SUMMARY SOLUBLE AΒ OLIGOMERS CONTRIBUTE TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE BY DISRUPTING EXCITATORY AMINO ACID TRANSPORTERS (EAATS) IN ASTROCYTES AND NEURONS, ELEVATING EXTRACELLULAR GLUTAMATE. EVEN MODEST, CHRONIC GLUTAMATE ACCUMULATION PERTURBS SYNAPTIC FUNCTION, DRIVING HYPEREXCITABILITY, INTERNEURON DYSFUNCTION, AND SYNAPTIC LOSS. THIS PROJECT TESTS A MITIGATION-FIRST STRATEGY: STABILIZING NETWORK ACTIVITY DESPITE ONGOING AΒ- RELATED EAAT IMPAIRMENT. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT HIPPOCAMPAL SHARP WAVE–RIPPLES (SWRS) ARE HIGHLY SENSITIVE TO EAAT ATTENUATION AND THAT MILD HYPERPOLARIZATION RESTORES SWRS. WE THEREFORE HYPOTHESIZE THAT MILD HYPERPOLARIZATION—VIA M-CURRENT (KV7) ENHANCEMENT OR COMPLEMENTARY MECHANISMS—WILL REDUCE SWR DISRUPTIONS IN 5XFAD HIPPOCAMPAL SLICES. WE WILL QUANTIFY SWRS IN EX VIVO SLICES FROM 5XFAD MICE AND WILD-TYPE LITTERMATES ACROSS 1–9 MONTHS, SPANNING MODERATE TO ADVANCED AΒ PATHOLOGY. PHARMACOLOGY WILL PRIORITIZE KV7 CHANNEL OPENERS AND EXTEND TO ADDITIONAL CONDUCTANCES THAT BIAS MEMBRANES NEGATIVE, INCLUDING GIRK (KIR3) ACTIVATORS, BK (KCA1.1) MODULATORS, HCN (IH) MODULATORS, AND SELECTED GI/O-COUPLED RECEPTOR PATHWAYS. DOSING WILL BE GUIDED BY SWR DOSE–RESPONSE TO IDENTIFY “NEUTRAL” WINDOWS THAT PRESERVE PHYSIOLOGICAL OSCILLATIONS. IMPACT: SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION WILL ESTABLISH MILD HYPERPOLARIZATION AS A NETWORK-STABILIZING THERAPEUTIC CONCEPT FOR EARLY AD, PROVIDE A PRACTICAL SCREENING FRAMEWORK CENTERED ON SWR PRESERVATION, AND HIGHLIGHT REPURPOSABLE COMPOUNDS ALREADY INVESTIGATED FOR EPILEPSY, DEPRESSION, TBI, STROKE, AND AD SYMPTOM RELIEF. THIS MITIGATION-FOCUSED APPROACH HAS STRONG TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE AND THE POTENTIAL FOR RAPID CLINICAL IMPACT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ELDER MISTREATMENT AND SELF-NEGLECT AMONG PEOPLE LIVING WITH DEMENTIA AND THEIR CAREGIVERS - ABSTRACT ELDER MISTREATMENT (EM) AND SELF-NEGLECT (SN) AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (ADRD) ARE URGENT BUT UNDER-ADDRESSED PUBLIC HEALTH CHALLENGES. AFFECTING AN ESTIMATED 43% AND 37% OF OLDER ADULTS WITH ADRD RESPECTIVELY, EM AND SN CONTRIBUTE TO INJURY, FUNCTIONAL DECLINE, CHRONIC ILLNESS EXACERBATION, INSTITUTIONALIZATION, AND PREMATURE DEATH. YET LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT ADRD-SPECIFIC RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS, THE IMPACT OF EM AND SN ON HEALTH OUTCOMES, OR HOW CHANGES IN DEMENTIA CARE DELIVERY INFLUENCE DETECTION AND RESPONSE. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH LEVERAGES THE UCLA ALZHEIMER’S AND DEMENTIA CARE (ADC) PROGRAM, WHICH MAINTAINS A LARGE, LONGITUDINAL DATASET THAT INCLUDES STRUCTURED DATA AND RICH, UNSTRUCTURED CLINICAL NOTES FROM DEMENTIA CARE SPECIALISTS (DCS). BUILDING ON THE PI’S PRIOR WORK DEVELOPING METHODS TO ABSTRACT EM/SN INFORMATION FROM DCS NOTES, THIS PROJECT WILL EXPAND THE EXISTING DATASET TO INCLUDE THREE COHORTS OF ADC PATIENTS (N=3,212) SPANNING PRE- AND POST-IMPLEMENTATION OF THE CENTERS FOR MEDICARE & MEDICAID SERVICES (CMS) GUIDING AN IMPROVED DEMENTIA CARE EXPERIENCE (GUIDE) MODEL — A NATIONWIDE INITIATIVE THAT ENHANCES STRUCTURED ASSESSMENT, CAREGIVER SUPPORT, AND HOME VISITS. AIM 1 WILL IDENTIFY INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL RISK AND PROTECTIVE FACTORS ASSOCIATED WITH DOCUMENTATION OF EM/SN AMONG OLDER ADULTS WITH ADRD. AIM 2 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER DOCUMENTED EM/SN CONCERN PREDICTS SURVIVAL AND LONG-TERM CARE PLACEMENT, ADJUSTING FOR DEMENTIA SEVERITY AND COMORBIDITIES. AIM 3 WILL LEVERAGE THE GUIDE MODEL AS A NATURAL EXPERIMENT TO EXAMINE HOW CHANGES IN DEMENTIA CARE DELIVERY INFLUENCE EM/SN DETECTION AND REPORTING, AND WHETHER GUIDE PARTICIPATION MODIFIES ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN INDIVIDUAL-LEVEL CHARACTERISTICS AND EM/SN DETECTION. THIS STUDY WILL GENERATE FOUNDATIONAL EVIDENCE ON THE MULTILEVEL DETERMINANTS OF EM AND SN IN DEMENTIA CARE, ELUCIDATE THE IMPACT OF THESE PHENOMENA ON PATIENT OUTCOMES, AND ASSESS THE ROLE NEW MODELS OF CARE CAN PLAY IN IMPROVING DETECTION AND RESPONSE. FINDINGS WILL INFORM THE DESIGN OF INTERVENTIONS THAT IMPROVE DEMENTIA CARE QUALITY, ENHANCE CAREGIVER SUPPORT, AND ADVANCE ELDER JUSTICE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AYA PATHWAYS: CHARACTERIZING COSTS OF FERTILITY PRESERVATION OPTIONS FOR ADOLESCENT AND YOUNG ADULT CANCER SURVIVORS - PROJECT SUMMARY ACROSS THE US, THERE ARE OVER 2 MILLION AYA CANCER SURVIVORS AND THAT NUMBER CONTINUES TO GROW. ABOUT 80% OF AYAS DIAGNOSED WITH CANCER BECOME LONG-TERM SURVIVORS WITH MANY LIVING WELL INTO ADULTHOOD. WITH THE GROWING NUMBER OF AYA CANCER SURVIVORS, SURVIVORSHIP PLANNING IS CRUCIAL AND INCLUDES QUALITY OF LIFE CONSIDERATIONS, LIKE FERTILITY PRESERVATION. SEVERAL CANCER TYPES AND TREATMENTS CAN CAUSE INFERTILITY, AND THE NEGATIVE EFFECTS OF INFERTILITY-RELATED DISTRESS CAN BE DEVASTATING AND LONG-LASTING—PARTICULARLY FOR AYAS. FERTILITY PRESERVATION METHODS FOR YOUNG MEN INCLUDE SPERM BANKING AND TESTICULAR TISSUE FREEZING. FOR YOUNG WOMEN, THERE ARE SEVERAL MEDICALLY-APPROPRIATE THERAPIES, INCLUDING EGG FREEZING AND OVARIAN TISSUE FREEZING. THESE THERAPIES ARE EFFECTIVE, BUT MAY ALSO BE COSTLY, AS ONLY ABOUT 20 STATES MANDATE INSURANCE COVERAGE FOR FERTILITY PRESERVATION. YET, MANY AYAS MAY STILL NOT QUALIFY FOR COVERAGE AS THEY OFTEN DO NOT MEET INFERTILITY REQUIREMENTS UNTIL THEY REACH ADULTHOOD. ADDITIONALLY, SOME PROCEDURES CAN TAKE UP TO TWO WEEKS, POTENTIALLY DELAYING THE START OF CANCER TREATMENT. THEREFORE, CHOOSING THE “RIGHT” FERTILITY PRESERVATION METHOD FOR EACH AYA AND THEIR FAMILY IS PREFERENCE-SENSITIVE. SPECIFICALLY, THIS DECISION DEPENDS ON BOTH THE MEDICAL EVIDENCE AND THE INFORMED, VALUES-CONCORDANT PREFERENCES OF THE PATIENT. WITH THE MULTITUDE OF COSTS RELATED TO AYA CANCER CARE, FINANCIAL HARDSHIPS ARE DETRIMENTAL TO THE FINANCIAL WELLBEING OF MANY AYAS AND THEIR FAMILIES. FINANCIAL HARDSHIP IS SERIOUS AND ASSOCIATED WITH DIMINISHED HEALTH-RELATED OUTCOMES AND QUALITY OF LIFE AMONG CANCER SURVIVORS. WE PROPOSE CHARACTERIZING THE COSTS OF AYA FERTILITY PRESERVATION CARE, INCLUDING THE DIRECT FINANCIAL BURDEN FROM OUT-OF-POCKET FEES AND THE UNFORESEEN INDIRECT COSTS LIKE TRANSPORTATION AND TIME OFF WORK FOR PARENTS. WE WILL INCORPORATE OUR FINDINGS INTO PATHWAYS FOR AYA TO SUPPORT AYAS AND THEIR FAMILIES AS THEY DECIDE WHETHER TO UNDERGO FERTILITY PRESERVATION AND WHICH FERTILITY PRESERVATION OPTION IS RIGHT FOR THEM. INCORPORATING FERTILITY PRESERVATION COST INFORMATION TO IMPROVE INFORMED DECISION-MAKING BY ENGAGING WITH AYAS, THEIR PARENTS, AND CLINICIANS HAS THE POTENTIAL TO PREPARE PATIENTS AND THEIR FAMILIES FOR MAKING WELL- INFORMED DECISIONS TO IMPROVE QUALITY OF LIFE INTO SURVIVORSHIP.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: APPLICATION OF MEDIATION MIXTURE MODELING AND MACHINE LEARNING TO UNDERSTAND HETEROGENEITY OF RISK PATHWAYS ON YOUTH'S ONSET OF SUBSTANCE USE - ABSTRACT THE LITERATURE HIGHLIGHTS THE COMPLEX INTERPLAY OF FACTORS INFLUENCING THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUBSTANCE USE. TO INCREASE THE ACCURACY OF IDENTIFYING AT-RISK GROUPS FOR SUBSTANCE USE, THIS SECONDARY DATA ANALYSIS PROJECT AIMS TO APPLY ADVANCED QUANTITATIVE METHODS IN STUDYING THE HETEROGENEITY OF RISK PATHWAYS LEADING TO YOUTH'S EARLY INITIATION OF SUBSTANCE USE, USING THE ADOLESCENT BRAIN COGNITIVE DEVELOPMENT (ABCD) STUDY®, A NATIONAL LONGITUDINAL DATASET IN TRACKING YOUTHS' BEHAVIORAL HEALTH. INFORMED BY TWO MODELS IN EXPLAINING THE ETIOLOGY OF EARLY SUBSTANCE USE, THE DEVIANCE PRONENESS MODEL AND THE NEGATIVE AFFECT REGULATION MODEL, THE PROPOSED STUDY WILL EXAMINE THE FOLLOWING MEDIATION PATHWAYS: PARENT MENTAL HEALTH  YOUTH EXTERNALIZING SPECTRUM  SUBSTANCE USE; IN THE NEGATIVE AFFECT REGULATION MODEL: PARENT MENTAL HEALTH  YOUTH INTERNALIZING SPECTRUM  SUBSTANCE USE. WITH THE RECOGNITION OF THE MULTIFACETED NATURE OF THE ETIOLOGY OF SUBSTANCE USE, PRIOR STUDIES ASSUME HOMOGENEITY IN TESTING RISK MECHANISMS, REVEALING ONLY DOMINANT PATHWAYS SHARED BY MOST PARTICIPANTS, NEGLECTING SUBGROUP-SPECIFIC MECHANISMS. PRIOR STUDIES USING MACHINE LEARNING DATA-DRIVEN APPROACH PRIMARILY FOCUSED ON THE PREDICTION OF SUBSTANCE USE, WITH LESS EMPHASIS ON CONNECTING WITH THEORY- DRIVEN MEDIATION APPROACH. BUILT ON RECENT ADVANCES IN METHODOLOGY, THIS IS THE FIRST STUDY TO ENSEMBLE APPROACHES, COMBING THEORY-DRIVEN MEDIATION APPROACH AND DATA-DRIVEN MACHINE LEARNING APPROACH, TO EXPLORE THE COMPLEX INTERACTIVE FEATURES OF FACTORS IN CHARACTERIZING GROUP-SPECIFIC RISK MECHANISMS. THE STUDY AIMS TO ASSESS HETEROGENEITY IN MEDIATION PATHWAYS IN INFLUENCING EARLY SUBSTANCE USE AMONG YOUTH. SPECIFICALLY, THIS STUDY WILL EXPLORE TWO DIFFERENT APPROACHES IN ENSEMBLING MULTIPLE METHODS: DECISION TREE- STRUCTURAL EQUATION MODELING (DT-SEM), AND COMBINED MEDIATION MIXTURE MODELING (MMM) AND CLASSIFICATION TREE METHOD TO ADDRESS THE MEDIATION PATHWAYS AND ASSOCIATIONS INVOLVING DISTINCT GENETIC, FAMILY AND ENVIRONMENTAL BACKGROUNDS. IN THE FORMAL APPROACH, THE MEDIATION MODEL WILL BE SPLIT INTO DIFFERENT SUBCLASSES BASED ON THE PREDICTIVE FACTORS VIA DECISION TREE MODELING. IN THE LATTER APPROACH, THE MMM COMBINES THE MIXTURE MODEL AND MEDIATION MODEL TO ESTIMATE THE HETEROGENEITY OF THEORY-DRIVEN PATHWAYS INTO SUBCLASSES, THEN, THE CLASSIFICATION TREE ESTIMATES THE PREDICTION OF THE ENUMERATED SUBCLASSES WITH A LARGE NUMBER OF OBSERVED GENETIC, FAMILY AND ENVIRONMENTAL VARIABLES TO UNDERSTAND THE FEATURES OF THE SUBCLASSES. THE EMPLOYMENT OF THESE TWO APPROACHES AIMS TO PROVIDE COMPLEMENTARY PERSPECTIVES FOR IDENTIFYING SUBGROUPS TO ENSURE A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF HETEROGENEITY OF MEDIATION PATHWAYS TO YOUTH SUBSTANCE USE. RESULTS WILL IDENTIFY SUBGROUPS THAT ARE VULNERABLE TO SPECIFIC RISK MECHANISMS, IN AN EFFORT TO UNRAVEL THE MULTIFACETED NATURE OF EARLY SUBSTANCE USE. ULTIMATELY, RESULTS WILL INFORM PERSONALIZED INTERVENTIONS FOR IDENTIFYING AT-RISK YOUTH WITH EARLY INITIATION OF SUBSTANCE USE.

description: BRIDGING THE GAP IN PEDIATRIC TMD AND MIGRAINE THROUGH MULTIDIMENSIONAL PHENOTYPING AND PRECISION PAIN PROFILING - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT CHRONIC PAIN DURING ADOLESCENCE IS OFTEN UNDERRECOGNIZED AND INADEQUATELY TREATED, CONTRIBUTING TO LONG-TERM DISABILITY ACROSS THE LIFESPAN. TEMPOROMANDIBULAR DISORDERS (TMD) AND MIGRAINE ARE AMONG THE MOST DISABLING CHRONIC PAIN CONDITIONS IN ADOLESCENCE, YET THE MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THEIR CO-OCCURRENCE REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT NEARLY 60% OF ADOLESCENTS WITH PAINFUL TMD REPORT COMORBID HEADACHE, A SUBGROUP CHARACTERIZED BY ELEVATED PAIN INTENSITY, GREATER FUNCTIONAL IMPAIRMENT, AND INCREASED PSYCHOLOGICAL DISTRESS. ALTHOUGH ADULT STUDIES HAVE IDENTIFIED MIGRAINE AS A SIGNIFICANT RISK FACTOR FOR THE ONSET AND PERSISTENCE OF TMD PAIN, NO PEDIATRIC STUDIES HAVE INTEGRATED MOLECULAR, SENSORY, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL DATA TO PHENOTYPE YOUTH WITH COMORBID TMD AND MIGRAINE. THIS CRITICAL GAP IMPEDES EARLY IDENTIFICATION OF HIGH-RISK SUBGROUPS AND HINDERS EFFORTS TO PERSONALIZE TREATMENT DURING A KEY DEVELOPMENTAL WINDOW, INCREASING THE RISK OF CHRONIC PAIN PERSISTENCE INTO ADULTHOOD. THE LONG-TERM OBJECTIVE OF OUR PROPOSED RESEARCH IS TO ADVANCE INDIVIDUALIZED PAIN MANAGEMENT FOR YOUTH WITH COMORBID TMD AND MIGRAINE BY APPLYING MACHINE LEARNING TO STRATIFY PATIENTS BASED ON INTEGRATED BIOLOGICAL, SENSORY, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL RISK SIGNATURES. A CRITICAL FIRST STEP IS TO ESTABLISH A MULTIDIMENSIONAL DATASET ENCOMPASSING SALIVARY BIOMARKERS, QUANTITATIVE SENSORY TESTING, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL PROFILING TO CHARACTERIZE PHENOTYPIC SIGNATURES IN ADOLESCENTS WITH TMD, WITH AND WITHOUT COMORBID MIGRAINE. THIS APPLICATION WILL APPLY A NOVEL MULTIMODAL PHENOTYPING FRAMEWORK TO CHARACTERIZE NEUROIMMUNE, SENSORY, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL FACTORS CONTRIBUTING TO COMORBID TMD AND MIGRAINE IN ADOLESCENTS BY RECRUITING 140 YOUTH AGED 10 TO 17 YEARS WITH TMD MYALGIA, STRATIFIED BY THE PRESENCE OR ABSENCE OF MIGRAINE. AIM 1 WILL QUANTIFY SALIVARY LEVELS OF PRO-INFLAMMATORY CYTOKINES AND NEUROPEPTIDES, ALONGSIDE CRANIOFACIAL PRESSURE AND THERMAL PAIN THRESHOLDS, TO INVESTIGATE NEUROIMMUNE CORRELATES OF PAIN AND ALTERED NOCICEPTIVE PROCESSING. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS PAIN BURDEN, FUNCTIONAL DISABILITY, SOMATIC SYMPTOMS, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL FUNCTION USING VALIDATED, DEVELOPMENTALLY RELEVANT SELF-REPORT MEASURES, AND WILL EXAMINE THEIR CONVERGENCE WITH BIOLOGICAL AND SENSORY DATA FROM AIM 1 TO ELUCIDATE INTEGRATED BIOBEHAVIORAL MECHANISMS. COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS WILL YIELD A MULTIDIMENSIONAL DATASET THAT DIRECTLY SUPPORTS MY FUTURE R01 FOCUSED ON APPLYING MACHINE LEARNING TO PREDICT TREATMENT RESPONSE AND ADVANCE PERSONALIZED PAIN MANAGEMENT FOR YOUTH WITH COMORBID TMD AND MIGRAINE. BY INTEGRATING BIOLOGICAL, SENSORY, AND PSYCHOSOCIAL DATA, THIS STUDY WILL IDENTIFY DISTINCT CLINICAL AND MECHANISTIC PROFILES THAT DIFFERENTIATE ADOLESCENTS WITH TMD ALONE FROM THOSE WITH COMORBID MIGRAINE, LAYING THE GROUNDWORK FOR DATA-DRIVEN PHENOTYPING AND TREATMENT STRATIFICATION. THE PROPOSED WORK LEVERAGES A COLLABORATIVE, INTERDISCIPLINARY TEAM OF EXPERIENCED AND EARLY-CAREER INVESTIGATORS TO ENSURE METHODOLOGICAL RIGOR AND TRANSLATIONAL RELEVANCE.

description: SPATIAL STRUCTURE-BASED ANNOTATION OF PROTEINS FOR THE NIH HUMAN VIROME PROGRAM - PROJECT SUMMARY  STRUCTURAL ANNOTATION INFRASTRUCTURE FOR THE NIH HUMAN VIROME PROGRAM THE HUMAN VIROME PROFOUNDLY SHAPES GUT MICROBIOME COMPOSITION, HOST IMMUNITY, AND DEVELOPMENT, YET OUR FUNCTIONAL UNDERSTANDING OF ITS COMPONENTS IS LIMITED BY MASSIVE ANNOTATION GAPS. THE NIH HUMAN VIROME PROGRAM (HVP) GENERATES UNPRECEDENTED VIROME DATASETS FROM ~2,000 INDIVIDUALS, BUT 50-90% OF VIRAL SEQUENCES IN THESE DATASETS REMAIN FUNCTIONALLY UNANNOTATED  DARK MATTER . THIS ANNOTATION BOTTLENECK ARISES FROM THE FAST-EVOLVING NATURE OF VIRUSES, WHICH CAUSES PROTEIN SEQUENCES TO DIVERGE BEYOND RECOGNITION BY STANDARD HOMOLOGY SEARCH TOOLS. IN CONTRAST, PROTEIN STRUCTURES ARE SUBSTANTIALLY MORE CONSERVED THAN SEQUENCES, ENABLING FUNCTIONAL ANNOTATION EVEN ACROSS EXTREME SEQUENCE DIVERGENCE. AS DEVELOPERS OF THE EVOLUTIONARY CLASSIFICATION OF DOMAINS (ECOD) DATABASE, WE ARE UNIQUELY POSITIONED TO LEVERAGE LARGE-SCALE ALPHAFOLD-PREDICTED STRUCTURES AND STRUCTURE-GUIDED HOMOLOGY INFERENCE TO BRIDGE THIS GAP. OUR PROOF-OF-CONCEPT ANALYSIS OF 339K VIRAL PROTEINS DEMONSTRATES THAT STRUCTURE-BASED CLASSIFICATION CAN TRACE THE EVOLUTIONARY ORIGINS FOR 47-67% OF THE VIRAL PROTEOME—A 3- TO 4-FOLD IMPROVEMENT OVER SEQUENCE-BASED METHODS ALONE. WE WILL ADDRESS THE VIROME ANNOTATION CHALLENGE THROUGH TWO COMPLEMENTARY AIMS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL ESTABLISH A PRODUCTION-SCALE, AUTOMATED PIPELINE THAT PROCESSES RAW METAGENOMIC DATA THROUGH ASSEMBLY, VIRAL CONTIG IDENTIFICATION, GENE PREDICTION, 3D STRUCTURE MODELING (USING ALPHAFOLD3), AND STRUCTURAL CLASSIFICATION. KEY INNOVATIONS INCLUDE STRUCTURE-AIDED VIRAL CONTIG RESCUE AND ITERATIVE MODELING TO PROPERLY HANDLE POLYPROTEINS, OBLIGATE OLIGOMERS, AND PARTIAL PROTEINS. WE WILL APPLY THIS PIPELINE TO PROCESS HVP DATASETS, EXPECTING TO ASSIGN FOLD GROUPS (ECOD T-GROUPS) AND PREDICT GENERAL FUNCTIONS FOR 50-70% OF VIRAL DOMAINS BASED ON THE CONTEXT PROVIDED BY THE EXISTING ECOD HIERARCHY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL PARTITION 200 VIRAL-RICH STRUCTURAL FOLD GROUPS (COVERING 80% OF VIRAL DOMAINS) INTO SPECIFIC SEQUENCE FAMILIES (ECOD F-GROUPS) AND CHARACTERIZE 100 ENTIRELY NOVEL VIRAL PROTEIN FAMILIES FROM CURRENTLY UNCLASSIFIABLE DOMAINS. BY SYSTEMATICALLY INTEGRATING EXPERIMENTAL AND PREDICTIVE EVIDENCE REGARDING VIRAL PROTEIN FUNCTIONS INTO OUR CLASSIFICATION PROCESS, WE WILL PROVIDE DETAILED FUNCTIONAL DESCRIPTIONS FOR EACH FAMILY. WE EXPECT TO CLASSIFY 40-60% OF VIRAL DOMAINS INTO EXISTING AND NEW FAMILIES IN ECOD (F-GROUPS). FURTHERMORE, BY GENERATING STRUCTURE-GUIDED HMM PROFILES FOR EACH FAMILY, WE WILL EMPOWER THE BROADER SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY TO PERFORM EFFICIENT SEQUENCE-BASED VIRAL PROTEIN ANNOTATION. THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH A ROBUST ANNOTATION INFRASTRUCTURE INTEGRATED WITH HVP CONSORTIUM DATA SYSTEMS, TRANSFORMING VIRAL  DARK MATTER  INTO FUNCTIONALLY ANNOTATED PROTEINS. THIS RESOURCE WILL HELP THE HVP CONSORTIUM AND THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY TO DECIPHER THE EVOLUTION AND FUNCTION OF HUMAN-ASSOCIATED VIRAL PROTEINS. TESTABLE FUNCTIONAL HYPOTHESES GENERATED BY US WILL ACCELERATE THE EXPERIMENTAL CHARACTERIZATION OF CRITICAL VIRAL PROTEINS AND ULTIMATELY INFORM NOVEL STRATEGIES TO MODULATE THE VIROME FOR THERAPEUTIC BENEFIT.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AN INTEGRATED ANALYTICAL FRAMEWORK FOR HUMAN VIROME STUDIES: VALIDATION, STANDARDIZATION, AND STATISTICAL INNOVATION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE HUMAN VIROME PROGRAM (HVP) AIMS TO COMPREHENSIVELY CHARACTERIZE VIRAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS HUMAN BODY SITES IN HEALTH AND DISEASE. HOWEVER, VIROME RESEARCH LACKS BENCHMARKING INFRASTRUCTURE TO VALIDATE COMPUTATIONAL TOOLS, EVALUATE STATISTICAL METHODS, AND ESTABLISH QUALITY CONTROL STANDARDS. UNLIKE BACTERIAL MICROBIOME RESEARCH, WHICH BENEFITS FROM MOCK COMMUNITIES AND STANDARDIZED WORKFLOWS, VIROME RESEARCHERS CANNOT RIGOROUSLY ASSESS WHETHER TOOLS CORRECTLY IDENTIFY VIRUSES, WHETHER ABUNDANCE ESTIMATES ARE ACCURATE, OR WHETHER STATISTICAL METHODS PERFORM APPROPRIATELY ON EXTREMELY SPARSE DATA (70-95% ZEROS). THIS METHODOLOGICAL GAP THREATENS HVP SCIENTIFIC RIGOR AND REPRODUCIBILITY. THIS R03 WILL CREATE AN INTEGRATED BENCHMARKING ECOSYSTEM FOR VIROME RESEARCH COMBINING THREE ELEMENTS: (1) SYNTHETIC GROUND-TRUTH VALIDATION DATA VIA VIROFORGE, (2) VIROME-SPECIFIC DATA INFRASTRUCTURE VIA VIROMEDATA, AND (3) SYSTEMATIC STATISTICAL VALIDATION FOR SPARSE DATA. AIM 1 WILL ENHANCE VIROFORGE, A PRODUCTION-READY SYNTHETIC VIROME PLATFORM, TO GENERATE HVP-VALIDATED DATASETS COVERING DIVERSE BODY SITES, SEQUENCING PLATFORMS, AND STUDY DESIGNS INCLUDING LONGITUDINAL SAMPLING AND BATCH EFFECTS. WE WILL VALIDATE ERROR MODELS AGAINST REAL HVP CONSORTIUM DATA ENSURING SYNTHETIC DATA ACCURATELY REFLECTS ACTUAL SEQUENCING CHARACTERISTICS. AIM 2 WILL DEVELOP VIROMEDATA, A VIROME-SPECIFIC EXTENSION OF BIOCONDUCTOR’S SUMMARIZEDEXPERIMENT PROVIDING STANDARDIZED INFRASTRUCTURE AND TOOL INTEGRATION. VIROMEDATA WILL INCORPORATE BALTIMORE CLASSIFICATION, RDRP CLASSIFIER INTEGRATION, AND VIRUS-HOST ASSOCIATION TRACKING, WITH BOTH R AND PYTHON IMPLEMENTATIONS ENSURING BROAD ACCESSIBILITY. AIM 3 WILL SYSTEMATICALLY VALIDATE STATISTICAL METHODS ON SPARSE VIROME DATA, TESTING WHETHER COMPOSITIONALLY-AWARE METHODS (ANCOM-BC, ALDEX2, AITCHISON DISTANCE) OUTPERFORM BORROWED RNA-SEQ AND MICROBIOME APPROACHES (DESEQ2, BRAY-CURTIS). WE WILL EVALUATE DIFFERENTIAL ABUNDANCE METHODS, DIVERSITY METRICS, AND NORMALIZATION APPROACHES ACROSS VARYING SPARSITY LEVELS (50-95% ZEROS), GENERATING POWER CURVES AND SAMPLE SIZE RECOMMENDATIONS. THE PI SERVES AS CO-PI ON THE HVP CODCC (U24HL175772), ENSURING CONSORTIUM INTEGRATION, DATASET ACCESS, AND DISSEMINATION CHANNELS. BUILDING ON PROVEN TECHNOLOGIES (VIROFORGE V0.10.0, BIOCONDUCTOR SUMMARIZEDEXPERIMENT) MINIMIZES RISK WHILE MAXIMIZING IMPACT. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE VIROFORGE V2.0 WITH HVP-VALIDATED PARAMETERS, VIROMEDATA PACKAGES VIA BIOCONDUCTOR AND PYPI, STATISTICAL VALIDATION RESULTS WITH BEST PRACTICES GUIDELINES, AND TRAINING MATERIALS. THIS ESTABLISHES THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE BENCHMARKING PLATFORM FOR VIROME RESEARCH, PROVIDING VALIDATED TOOLS, QUALITY CONTROL STANDARDS, AND STANDARDIZED INFRASTRUCTURE ENABLING RIGOROUS, REPRODUCIBLE SCIENCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GLUCAGON LIKE PEPTIDE-1 MEDICINE OUTCOMES IN REAL WORLD PATIENTS WITH TYPE 1 DIABETES - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT GLUCAGON LIKE-PEPTIDE-1 (GLP-1) MEDICINES, INCLUDING GLP-1 AGONISTS AND GLP-1/GASTRIC INHIBITORY PEPTIDE DUAL AGONISTS, REDUCE WEIGHT, KIDNEY AND CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE EVENTS FOR PEOPLE WITH TYPE 2 DIABETES AND OVERWEIGHT/OBESITY. PEOPLE WITH TYPE 1 DIABETES (T1D) HAVE EXCESS CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE AND KIDNEY DISEASE, AND OVERWEIGHT/OBESITY PREVALENCE IS GROWING IN THIS POPULATION. THE DETRIMENTAL MILIEU OF OBESITY AND INSULIN RESISTANCE FURTHER EXAGGERATES RISK OF DIABETES-RELATED COMPLICATIONS. IN PEOPLE WITH T1D, LIMITED STUDIES HAVE EXAMINED WEIGHT RESPONSE TO GLP-1 MEDICINES AND OTHER FREQUENTLY PRESCRIBED WEIGHT LOSS MEDICINES. FURTHER, THERE IS A MAJOR KNOWLEDGE GAP ABOUT WHETHER GLP-1 MEDICINES PREVENT KIDNEY DISEASE PROGRESSION, REDUCE CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASE, AND CAUSE RARE, SEVERE ADVERSE EVENTS IN THIS POPULATION. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS STUDY IS TO ASSESS CLINICALLY SIGNIFICANT: WEIGHT LOSS, KIDNEY DISEASE, AND MAJOR ADVERSE EVENTS IN RESPONSE TO GLP-1 MEDICINES IN T1D. THIS PROJECT WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT GLP-1 MEDICINES HAVE CLINICAL BENEFITS RELEVANT TO CARDIORENAL DISEASE PROTECTION AND ARE SAFE IN A POPULATION WITH T1D. IT WILL LEVERAGE EXISTING REAL WORLD ELECTRONIC HEALTHCARE DATA FROM EPIC COSMOS, A DATABASE OF OVER 300 MILLION PEOPLE OF WHOM OVER 943,000 HAVE A T1D DIAGNOSIS. USING LONGITUDINAL, HARMONIZED DATA FROM THIS CUTTING-EDGE PLATFORM, THIS PROJECT WILL COMPARE PATIENTS WITH T1D TREATED WITH A CARDIOPROTECTIVE GLP-1 MEDICINE (LIRAGLUTIDE, SEMAGLUTIDE, DULAGLUTIDE, TIRZEPATIDE) TO ACTIVE COMPARATORS (PHENTERMINE AND METFORMIN) USING PROPENSITY SCORE-BASED METHODS TO ACCOUNT FOR BIAS DUE TO NON-RANDOM TREATMENT. THE PROJECT WILL EXAMINE THE IMPACT OF THESE DRUGS ON: CARDIOPROTECTIVE WEIGHT LOSS (≥10%) (AIM 1); COMPOSITE KIDNEY OUTCOMES INCLUDING PERSISTENT INCIDENCE: URINE ALBUMIN TO CREATINE RATIO [UACR] ≥30 MG/G OR UACR ≥300 MG/G, ≥40% EGFR DECLINE, END STAGE KIDNEY DISEASE, AND ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY (AIM 2); AND SAFETY EVENTS INCLUDING MAJOR ADVERSE CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS, ALL-CAUSE MORTALITY, AND INCIDENCE RATES OF EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT/HOSPITAL ADMISSIONS ALONG WITH ASSOCIATED DIAGNOSES (AIM 3). THIS PROJECT IS A LOGICAL EXTENSION OF THE PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATOR’S INTERVENTIONAL K23 RESEARCH PROJECT WHICH EXAMINES GLP-1 MEDICINE IMPACT ON SURROGATE CARDIOVASCULAR OUTCOME MEASURES IN ADULTS WITH T1D. THE CURRENT RESEARCH PROPOSAL FOCUSES ON IMPROVING HEALTH FOR PEOPLE WITH T1D THROUGH INNOVATIVE USE OF A CUTTING-EDGE RESEARCH PLATFORM COMBINED WITH ADVANCED CAUSAL INFERENCE METHODS. TO ACCOMPLISH THESE GOALS, THIS PROJECT ASSEMBLES A TEAM OF COMPLEMENTARY AND WELL-SUITED EXPERTS, INCLUDING AN ENDOCRINOLOGIST WITH T1D AND GLP-1 MEDICINE RESEARCH EXPERTISE, CLINICAL INFORMATICIAN, PHARMACO-EPIDEMIOLOGIST, DATA SCIENTIST, AND BIOSTATISTICIAN ALL WITH LARGE-SCALE, SECONDARY DATA ANALYTIC EXPERIENCE. THIS RESEARCH IS SIGNIFICANT BECAUSE IT ADDRESSES MAJOR KNOWLEDGE GAPS IN CLINICAL EFFICACY OF GLP- 1 MEDICINES, AND MOST FREQUENTLY PRESCRIBED COMPARATORS, IN THE T1D POPULATION, AND IT WILL INFORM EVIDENCE- BASED GUIDELINES AND FUTURE METHODOLOGY FOR INTERVENTIONAL KIDNEY AND CARDIOVASCULAR OUTCOME TRIALS IN T1D.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DECODING THE PROTEIN BIOCHEMISTRY OF TBCK - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT GENETIC MUTATIONS IN THE GENE ENCODING FOR TBC1-DOMAIN CONTAINING KINASE (TBCK) ARE ASSOCIATED WITH TBCK ENCEPHALONEURONOPATHY (TBCKE), A RARE PEDIATRIC NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER. CHARACTERIZED BY PROFOUND INTELLECTUAL AND PHYSICAL DISABILITIES, NO TREATMENTS ARE CURRENTLY AVAILABLE FOR TBCKE. EMERGING EVIDENCE SUGGESTS THAT TBCK PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN THE MTOR SIGNALING PATHWAY, AUTOPHAGY/LYSOSOME FUNCTION, AND MITOCHONDRIAL HOMEOSTASIS. HOWEVER, THE LACK OF DETAILED CHARACTERIZATIONS OF TBCK AT THE PROTEIN LEVEL HAS HINDERED OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE DISEASE MECHANISMS AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES. TO THIS END, WE WILL CONDUCT THE FIRST PROTEIN BIOCHEMISTRY INVESTIGATION OF HUMAN TBCK. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL USE IN VITRO ENZYME ASSAYS TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT TBCK FUNCTIONS AS A GTPASE-ACTIVATING PROTEIN BY INTERACTING WITH RAB5A. IN ADDITION, WE WILL EMPLOY FLUORESCENCE-BASED ASSAY AND HYDROGEN-DEUTERIUM EXCHANGE MASS SPECTROMETRY TO PROBE PROTEIN-PROTEIN INTERACTIONS OF TBCK. THE OUTCOME OF THIS PILOT PROJECT WILL CLARIFY THE CATALYTIC POTENTIAL OF THIS UNIQUE ‘DARK’ PROTEIN KINASE AND ESTABLISH THE FOUNDATION FOR UNDERSTANDING HOW TBCKE- ASSOCIATED VARIANTS ALTER THE PROTEIN STRUCTURE AND FUNCTION IN VITRO. THIS INFORMATION WILL FACILITATE UNCOVERING NOVEL DRUG TARGETS AND LAY THE FOUNDATION FOR FUTURE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TO TREAT THIS NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GENERATION AND CHARACTERIZATION OF A NOVEL CONDITIONAL SPTLC1 MOUSE MODEL TO INVESTIGATE THE ROLE OF SPHINGOLIPIDS DYSREGULATION IN ALS - ABSTRACT ALTERATIONS IN SPHINGOLIPID METABOLISM ARE INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED AS CONTRIBUTORS TO NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES, INCLUDING AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (ALS). SPTLC1, ENCODING THE LONG-CHAIN BASE SUBUNIT OF SERINE PALMITOYLTRANSFERASE (SPT), CATALYZES THE FIRST AND RATE-LIMITING STEP IN SPHINGOLIPID BIOSYNTHESIS. MUTATIONS IN SPTLC1 HAVE BEEN LINKED TO HEREDITARY SENSORY AND AUTONOMIC NEUROPATHY TYPE I (HSAN1) AND JUVENILE ALS (JALS). THESE MUTATIONS DISRUPT THE BALANCE OF SPHINGOLIPIDS, IMPLICATING SPHINGOLIPID DYSREGULATION IN MOTOR NEURON VULNERABILITY. DESPITE THESE FINDINGS, THE PHYSIOLOGICAL ROLE OF SPTLC1 IN THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) REMAINS POORLY DEFINED, PRIMARILY BECAUSE GLOBAL SPTLC1 KNOCKOUT MICE ARE EMBRYONICALLY LETHAL DUE TO COMPLETE LOSS OF SPT ACTIVITY. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA DEMONSTRATE THAT HOMOZYGOUS DELETION OF SPTLC1 EXON 2 (ΔE2)—WHICH ENCODES A CRITICAL N-TERMINAL TRANSMEMBRANE DOMAIN REQUIRED FOR ER ANCHORING—CAUSES EARLY LETHALITY AND SEVERE MOTOR DYSFUNCTION, INDICATING ITS ESSENTIAL ROLE IN NEURONAL VIABILITY. INTERESTINGLY, OUR FINDINGS SUGGEST THAT TARGETED EXON 2 DELETION PRODUCES A PROTEIN THAT RETAINS PARTIAL LOCALIZATION AND RESIDUAL ENZYMATIC ACTIVITY IN VIVO, UNLIKE THE NULL PHENOTYPE OF GLOBAL SPTLC1 KNOCKOUTS. THIS PROVIDES A TRACTABLE SYSTEM TO MODEL PARTIAL SPT DYSFUNCTION, SIMILAR TO WHAT IS OBSERVED IN HUMAN ALS DISEASE. CURRENTLY, THERE ARE NO IN VIVO MODELS THAT ALLOW PRECISE DISSECTION OF SPTLC1 FUNCTION IN THE CNS. BY CREATING THE FIRST CONDITIONAL SPTLC1 ΔEXON2 MOUSE, THIS PROJECT WILL REVEAL HOW DISRUPTED SPHINGOLIPID HOMEOSTASIS DRIVES NEURODEGENERATION AND WILL ESTABLISH A FOUNDATIONAL TOOL TO STUDY METABOLIC MECHANISMS UNDERLYING ALS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MODELING ALS PATHOGENESIS USING HUMAN IPSC-DERIVED NEUROMUSCULAR ORGANOIDS - PROJECT SUMMARY TITLE: MODELING ALS PATHOGENESIS USING HUMAN IPSC-DERIVED NEUROMUSCULAR ORGANOIDS THREE-DIMENSIONAL (3D) ORGANOID MODELS DERIVED FROM HUMAN INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS (IPSCS) HAVE EMERGED AS POWERFUL TOOLS FOR STUDYING HUMAN DEVELOPMENT AND DISEASE IN VITRO. NEUROMUSCULAR ORGANOIDS (NMOS), WHICH INTEGRATE SPINAL MOTOR NEURONS, SKELETAL MUSCLE FIBERS, AND GLIAL CELLS, ARE PARTICULARLY PROMISING FOR MODELING MOTOR CIRCUITRY AND NEUROMUSCULAR JUNCTIONS (NMJS), THE SYNAPSES ESSENTIAL FOR VOLUNTARY MUSCLE CONTROL. DESPITE RECENT ADVANCES, CURRENT NMO MODELS OFTEN LACK STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL MATURITY, AND THEIR ABILITY TO ACCURATELY REPLICATE HUMAN NEUROMUSCULAR CONNECTIVITY AND PHYSIOLOGY REMAINS LIMITED. FURTHERMORE, THEIR POTENTIAL AS DISEASE MODELS, ESPECIALLY FOR MOTOR NEURON DISORDERS SUCH AS AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS (ALS), HAS YET TO BE FULLY REALIZED. THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS TO ESTABLISH AND VALIDATE A PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT NMO PLATFORM AND APPLY IT TO MODEL ALS PATHOLOGY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SELF-ORGANIZING NMOS DERIVED FROM HUMAN IPSCS CAN RECAPITULATE THE CELLULAR, STRUCTURAL, AND FUNCTIONAL FEATURES OF THE HUMAN NEUROMUSCULAR SYSTEM AND YIELD MECHANISTIC INSIGHT INTO ALS. IN AIM 1, WE WILL INVESTIGATE NEUROMUSCULAR DEVELOPMENTAL AND ARCHITECTURAL ALTERATIONS IN ALS NMOS COMPARED TO ISOGENIC CONTROLS. NMOS WILL BE GENERATED FROM HIPSCS DERIVED FROM JUVENILE AND EARLY-ONSET ALS SUBTYPES (ALS4 AND ALS6) AND ASSESSED FOR CELLULAR COMPOSITION, SPATIAL ORGANIZATION, AND NMJ ULTRASTRUCTURE USING IMMUNOSTAINING, CONFOCAL IMAGING, AND ELECTRON MICROSCOPY. IN AIM 2, WE WILL DEFINE FUNCTIONAL DEFICITS AND SYNAPTIC CHANGES IN ALS NMOS USING MULTIELECTRODE ARRAY (MEA) RECORDINGS AND PHARMACOLOGICAL MODULATION OF SYNAPTIC ACTIVITY. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT WILL YIELD A REPRODUCIBLE, FUNCTIONAL HUMAN NMO PLATFORM FOR STUDYING NEUROMUSCULAR DEVELOPMENT, DISEASE MECHANISMS, AND THERAPEUTIC RESPONSES. THIS WORK WILL ADVANCE ORGANOID TECHNOLOGY AND ADDRESS A CRITICAL GAP IN ALS MODELING BY PROVIDING A SCALABLE, HUMAN-RELEVANT SYSTEM FOR MECHANISTIC INVESTIGATION AND FUTURE DRUG SCREENING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCING CAREGIVING SCIENCE: A TRANSDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH CONFERENCE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT AN ESTIMATED 63 MILLION AMERICANS PROVIDE ESSENTIAL CARE FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH CHRONIC ILLNESS OR DISABILITY. CAREGIVING SPANS THE LIFECOURSE, CROSSES HEALTH CONDITIONS, AND FORMS THE BACKBONE OF OUR LONG-TERM CARE SYSTEMS. ENSURING CAREGIVERS RECEIVE ADEQUATE EDUCATION, TRAINING, AND SUPPORT IS THEREFORE A PRESSING PUBLIC HEALTH PRIORITY. AS THE U.S. POPULATION AGES, THE DEMAND FOR CARE CONTINUES TO GROW—REACHING LEVELS MANY NOW DESCRIBE AS A PUBLIC HEALTH CRISIS—AND UNDERSCORES THE NEED FOR A WORKFORCE EQUIPPED TO GENERATE EVIDENCE-BASED SOLUTIONS. YET CAREGIVING RESEARCH REMAINS FRAGMENTED, WITH MOST CONFERENCES ORGANIZED AROUND SPECIFIC DISCIPLINES, DIAGNOSES, OR AGE GROUPS. THESE SILOS LIMIT OPPORTUNITIES TO SHARE INNOVATIONS THAT COULD ADVANCE SCIENCE ACROSS CAREGIVING POPULATIONS AND HINDER DISSEMINATION OF METHODOLOGIES APPLICABLE ACROSS AGES, DISEASES, AND DISABILITY STATUS. COORDINATED PROGRESS REQUIRES AN INTERDISCIPLINARY NETWORK OF CAREGIVING STAKEHOLDERS WORKING TOGETHER TO DEVELOP AND IMPLEMENT EVIDENCE-BASED APPROACHES. ADVANCING CAREGIVING SCIENCE: A TRANSDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH CONFERENCE IS A BIENNIAL CONFERENCE SERIES DESIGNED TO BRIDGE THESE SILOS BY CONVENING INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCHERS, NATIONAL ORGANIZATIONS AND HEALTH CARE SYSTEM REPRESENTATIVES TO STRENGTHEN SUPPORT FOR CAREGIVERS. SPECIFIC GOALS ARE TO 1) PREPARE THE NEXT GENERATION OF CAREGIVING SCIENTISTS TO GENERATE RESEARCH THAT IS ACTIONABLE THROUGH MENTORSHIP, TRAINING, AND STRUCTURED NETWORKING ACTIVITIES, 2) FOSTER TRANSDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATIONS ACROSS THE LIFECOURSE AND DISEASES/DISABILITIES TO DRIVE INNOVATION IN CAREGIVING RESEARCH AND ITS IMPLEMENTATION, AND 3) SYNTHESIZE AND DISSEMINATE ACTIONABLE RESEARCH FINDINGS FOR STAKEHOLDERS ACROSS THE NATION INCLUDING CAREGIVERS TO MAXIMIZE IMPACT. THIS R13 PROPOSAL BUILDS ON THREE SUCCESSFUL PRIOR CONFERENCES, EACH INCREASING IN VISIBILITY AND ATTENDANCE AND SHAPED BY ATTENDEE FEEDBACK. THE CONFERENCE FORMAT INCLUDES KEYNOTE ADDRESSES FROM NATIONAL LEADERS OF CAREGIVING ORGANIZATIONS AND LEADING SCIENTISTS; PLENARY SESSIONS HIGHLIGHTING DIFFERENT RESEARCH METHODOLOGIES, AND INTERACTIVE PANEL SESSIONS WITH FUNDERS, CAREGIVERS, AND RESEARCHERS OF UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS. NETWORKING AND MENTORSHIP ARE INTEGRATED THROUGHOUT, AND EARLY-CAREER INVESTIGATORS RECEIVE TRAINING IN SECONDARY DATA ANALYSIS, TEAM-SCIENCE, MANUSCRIPT DEVELOPMENT, AND RESEARCH REPORT GENERATION. THE CONFERENCE SERIES ALIGNS WITH NIA STRATEGIC DIRECTIONS (2020–2025) BY EXPANDING THE CAREGIVING RESEARCH WORKFORCE, STRENGTHENING INTERDISCIPLINARY EXCHANGE, ADVANCING UNDERSTANDING OF INTERPERSONAL AND SOCIAL FACTORS AFFECTING CAREGIVERS AND CARE RECIPIENTS, AND DISSEMINATING EFFECTIVE SOLUTIONS ADAPTABLE ACROSS CONTEXTS AND AGE GROUPS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: FEDERATION OF AMERICAN SOCIETIES FOR EXPERIMENTAL BIOLOGY

description: PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES - ABSTRACT THIS APPLICATION REQUESTS PARTIAL FUNDING SUPPORT FOR THE 2026 FEDERATION OF AMERICAN SOCIETIES FOR EXPERIMENTAL BIOLOGY (FASEB) SCIENCE RESEARCH CONFERENCE ON PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES, ENTITLED, “SHAPING THE FUTURE OF PHOSPHATASE-TARGETED THERAPEUTICS,” TO BE HELD AT THE YOURS TRULY DC HOTEL IN WASHINGTON, DC, ON DECEMBER 14–17, 2026. PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES PLAY FUNDAMENTAL ROLES IN CELLULAR SIGNALING PATHWAYS, AND FOR MORE THAN 36 YEARS, THIS CONFERENCE HAS PROVIDED A PREMIER FORUM FOR ADVANCING OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THEIR ROLES IN NORMAL PHYSIOLOGY AND HUMAN DISEASE. RECENT DISCOVERIES HAVE EXPANDED OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE FUNCTIONS AND REGULATION OF MORE THAN 1,000 PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE CATALYTIC AND REGULATORY SUBUNITS, COMPLEXES, AND ISOFORMS THAT GOVERN CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. AS THE CAUSAL ROLES OF SPECIFIC PHOSPHATASES AND THEIR DISEASE-ASSOCIATED MUTATIONS CONTINUE TO BE ELUCIDATED, INVESTIGATORS ACROSS ACADEMIA, MEDICINE, AND INDUSTRY ARE INTEGRATING BASIC, TRANSLATIONAL, AND CLINICAL RESEARCH TO ACCELERATE THERAPEUTIC DISCOVERY. THIS CONFERENCE PROVIDES A FORUM FOR DISSEMINATING EMERGING DISCOVERIES, FOSTERING INTERDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATION, AND TRANSLATING MECHANISTIC INSIGHTS INTO THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES. THE 2026 MEETING REPRESENTS THE 18TH INSTALLMENT OF THIS LONG-STANDING BIENNIAL CONFERENCE, HELD CONTINUOUSLY SINCE 1990, AND REMAINS THE ONLY NORTH AMERICAN CONFERENCE DEDICATED EXCLUSIVELY TO PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES. THE MEETING WILL ALSO CONTINUE THE SUCCESSFUL PARTNERSHIP BETWEEN THE FASEB PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE CONFERENCE AND THE JAPANESE ASSOCIATION FOR PROTEIN PHOSPHATASE RESEARCH (JAPPR), STRENGTHENING INTERNATIONAL COLLABORATION AND SCIENTIFIC EXCHANGE. THE 12 SCIENTIFIC SESSIONS WILL FEATURE INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNIZED LEADERS AND EMERGING INVESTIGATORS PRESENTING ADVANCES IN STRUCTURAL BIOLOGY, SIGNALING, DISEASE MECHANISMS, DRUG DISCOVERY, AND TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE. THE 2026 KEYNOTE LECTURES WILL BE DELIVERED BY TWO INTERNATIONALLY RECOGNIZED LEADERS IN PHOSPHATASE RESEARCH: ANNE BERTOLOTTI, PHD, GROUP LEADER AT THE MRC LABORATORY OF MOLECULAR BIOLOGY (MRC-LMB), AND MICHEL TREMBLAY, PHD, DISTINGUISHED PROFESSOR AT MCGILL UNIVERSITY. THE SPECIFIC AIMS OF THE 2026 FASEB-JAPPR CONFERENCE ARE TO: (1) PRESENT AND DISCUSS THE LATEST ADVANCES IN THE STRUCTURE, REGULATION, AND FUNCTION OF PROTEIN PHOSPHATASES, WITH PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON THEIR ROLES IN CANCER AND OTHER HUMAN DISEASES AND THEIR VALIDATION AS THERAPEUTIC TARGETS; (2) HIGHLIGHT INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGIES, RIGOROUS EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES, AND EMERGING DISCOVERIES THAT INTEGRATE PHOSPHATASE BIOLOGY WITH COMPLEMENTARY SCIENTIFIC DISCIPLINES, FOSTER MULTIDISCIPLINARY COLLABORATION, AND ACCELERATE THERAPEUTIC TRANSLATION; AND (3) STRENGTHEN THE FUTURE BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH WORKFORCE BY SUPPORTING THE PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF EARLY CAREER INVESTIGATORS, INCLUDING GRADUATE STUDENTS, POSTDOCTORAL FELLOWS, AND JUNIOR FACULTY, THROUGH A COLLABORATIVE AND SCIENTIFICALLY RIGOROUS ENVIRONMENT THAT PROMOTES MENTORING, NETWORKING, SCIENTIFIC EXCHANGE, AND OPPORTUNITIES TO PRESENT THEIR RESEARCH. THIS R13 PROPOSAL REQUESTS SUPPORT TO FACILITATE THE PARTICIPATION OF EARLY CAREER INVESTIGATORS AS ORAL AND POSTER PRESENTERS, ENABLING PARTICIPANTS FROM A BROAD RANGE OF INSTITUTIONS AND SCIENTIFIC DISCIPLINES TO ENGAGE WITH LEADERS IN THE FIELD, ESTABLISH COLLABORATIONS, AND ADVANCE PHOSPHATASE RESEARCH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: SYMPOSIUM ON REDUCING STROKE RISK AND OPTIMIZING BRAIN HEALTH IN WOMEN BY LEVERAGING PREVENTION IN MID-LIFE - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT DESPITE LOWER AGE-SPECIFIC RATES OF STROKE IN WOMEN COMPARED TO MEN, STROKE HAS A DISPROPORTIONATE IMPACT ON THE LIVES OF WOMEN. IN ADDITION, MORE WOMEN THAN MEN SUFFER FROM COGNITIVE DECLINE, ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DISORDERS. THIS CONFERENCE, ENTITLED “REDUCING STROKE RISK AND OPTIMIZING BRAIN HEALTH IN WOMEN BY LEVERAGING PREVENTION IN MID-LIFE” WILL BRING TOGETHER A BROAD COALITION OF RESEARCHERS, CLINICIANS, HEALTH PROFESSIONALS, ADVOCATES, AND STROKE SURVIVORS TO DISCUSS CONTEMPORARY ISSUES RELATED TO THE PREVENTION OF STROKE AND PRESERVATION OF BRAIN HEALTH IN WOMEN, WITH A PARTICULAR EMPHASIS ON THE MID-LIFE PERIOD. THE CONFERENCE WILL FOCUS ON THREE INTER-RELATED THEMES RELEVANT TO STROKE AND BRAIN HEALTH IN WOMEN: 1) PREVENTING STROKE IN WOMEN BY LEVERAGING INTERVENTIONS APPLIED IN MID-LIFE, 2) OPTIMIZING BRAIN HEALTH OF WOMEN IN LATER LIFE BY DESIGNING INTERVENTIONS IN MID-LIFE, AND 3) CLINICAL CARE TO OPTIMIZE STROKE RECOVERY AND MENTAL HEALTH OUTCOMES IN WOMEN DURING THE TRANSITIONAL CARE PERIOD. THE CONFERENCE WILL EXPAND ON PREVIOUS COLLABORATIONS AND NETWORKING INITIATED BY THE MULTIDISCIPLINARY, AD HOC WORKING GROUP ON STROKE IN WOMEN -- PREVENTION AND OUTCOMES IN WOMEN ENHANCING STROKE SUPPORT (PROWESS). THE CONFERENCE HAS BEEN DESIGNED TO SUPPORT EARLY CAREER INVESTIGATORS WORKING IN THE AREA OF STROKE, BRAIN HEALTH, SEX DIFFERENCES, AND WOMEN, WITH THE GOAL OF ASSISTING THEM TO DEVELOP FOCUSED HYPOTHESIS DRIVEN RESEARCH RELEVANT TO THE MISSION OF NINDS. THE CONFERENCE WILL RESULT IN THE DISSEMINATION OF A SUMMARY MANUSCRIPT AND DEVELOPMENT OF COLLABORATIONS TO ADVANCE FUTURE RESEARCH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DETERMINING THE ROLE OF THE MITOCHONDRIAL PERMEABILITY TRANSITION PORE ON AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION IS A HALLMARK OF AGING AND AGE-RELATED DISEASES, INCLUDING HEART ATTACK, STROKE, AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS. SEVERE MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION OFTEN RESULTS FROM THE OPENING OF THE MITOCHONDRIAL PERMEABILITY TRANSITION PORE (MPTP), A PATHOLOGICAL CHANNEL IN THE INNER MITOCHONDRIAL MEMBRANE TRIGGERED BY EXCESSIVE CYTOSOLIC CA2⁺ AND HIGH REACTIVE OXYGEN SPECIES (ROS) LEVELS. DURING CONDITIONS SUCH AS ISCHEMIA/REPERFUSION (I/R) INJURY, MITOCHONDRIA IMPORT CA2⁺ INTO THE MATRIX TO BUFFER CYTOSOLIC LEVELS. THIS ACCUMULATION CAN CAUSE MITOCHONDRIAL SWELLING AND MPTP OPENING, ALLOWING CA2⁺ RELEASE BACK INTO THE CYTOSOL. PROLONGED MPTP ACTIVATION LEADS TO OUTER MEMBRANE RUPTURE, FURTHER CA2⁺ RELEASE, AND ULTIMATELY, CELL DEATH. WHILE EXTENSIVELY STUDIED IN I/R-RELATED DISEASES, THE ROLE OF THE MPTP IN NORMAL AGING REMAINS POORLY UNDERSTOOD. TO ADDRESS THIS KNOWLEDGE GAP, WE DEVELOPED A CAENORHABDITIS ELEGANS MODEL TO STUDY MPTP FUNCTION IN AGING. OUR FINDINGS REVEAL THAT MPTP ACTIVATION ACCELERATES AGING, WHILE ITS INHIBITION EXTENDS LIFESPAN, DEMONSTRATING ITS DIRECT ROLE IN LONGEVITY REGULATION (ANGELI ET AL., 2021, ELIFE). WITH ITS SHORT LIFESPAN, GENETIC TRACTABILITY, AND CONSERVED MITOCHONDRIAL PROCESSES, C. ELEGANS OFFERS A POWERFUL MODEL FOR UNCOVERING HOW THE MPTP INFLUENCES AGING. THE CELLULAR CA2⁺ SIGNALING PATHWAYS THAT REGULATE MPTP OPENING REMAIN LARGELY UNKNOWN. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGEST THAT CA2⁺ RELEASED FROM THE ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM (ER)—THE LARGEST INTRACELLULAR CA2⁺ RESERVOIR—ACTIVATES CALMODULIN, A KEY MEDIATOR OF CA2⁺-DEPENDENT SIGNALING, POSSIBLY VIA INTERACTIONS WITH KINASES, PHOSPHATASES, AND OTHER CALMODULIN-BINDING PROTEINS (CBPS). WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT AN ER-TO-CYTOPLASM CA2⁺ SIGNALING CASCADE TRIGGERS MPTP ACTIVATION, DRIVING ORGANISMAL AGING. AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER ITR-1, THE ER RECEPTOR RESPONSIBLE FOR CA2⁺ RELEASE, ALONG WITH CALMODULIN (CMD-1) AND CBPS, ARE REQUIRED FOR MPTP ACTIVATION AND MPTP-DEPENDENT AGING. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL LEVERAGE THE ADVANTAGES OF C. ELEGANS TO IDENTIFY SPECIFIC TISSUES WITH A PREDOMINANT INFLUENCE ON THIS PROCESS. OUR PRELIMINARY FINDINGS INDICATE ROBUST MPTP ACTIVATION IN THE INTESTINES, WHICH SERVE MULTIPLE FUNCTIONS BEYOND DIGESTION, INCLUDING DETOXIFICATION, IMMUNITY, AND FAT METABOLISM. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS WHETHER INTESTINAL MPTP ACTIVATION IS SUFFICIENT TO DRIVE ORGANISMAL AGING. THESE STUDIES WILL PROVIDE NOVEL INSIGHTS INTO THE ROLE OF THE MPTP IN AGING, WITH BROAD IMPLICATIONS FOR HUMAN HEALTH.
