description: WHEN PLASTIC MEETS FLOW: MECHANOBIOLOGICAL CONSEQUENCES OF MICROPLASTIC EXPOSURE ON THE ENDOTHELIUM - PROJECT SUMMARY MICROPLASTIC CONTAMINATION REPRESENTS AN EMERGING ENVIRONMENTAL CARDIOVASCULAR RISK FACTOR, WITH PATIENTS HARBORING DETECTABLE MICROPLASTICS IN ATHEROSCLEROTIC PLAQUES EXHIBITING AN INCREASED RISK OF CARDIOVASCULAR COMPLICATIONS SUCH AS MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION OR STROKE, YET THE MECHANISTIC PATHWAYS LINKING MICROPLASTIC EXPOSURE TO CARDIOVASCULAR PATHOPHYSIOLOGY REMAIN UNDEFINED. THE VASCULAR ENDOTHELIUM FUNCTIONS AS THE PRIMARY INTERFACE FOR MICROPLASTIC-CARDIOVASCULAR INTERACTIONS AND SERVES AS A SOPHISTICATED MECHANOSENSOR MAINTAINING VASCULAR HOMEOSTASIS THROUGH FLOW-MEDIATED RESPONSES, BUT CURRENT RESEARCH HAS FOCUSED ON BASIC CYTOTOXICITY USING STATIC CULTURE CONDITIONS THAT FAIL TO RECAPITULATE THE DYNAMIC MECHANICAL ENVIRONMENT OF THE CARDIOVASCULAR SYSTEM. THIS INVESTIGATION ESTABLISHES THE FIRST COMPREHENSIVE CHARACTERIZATION OF MICROPLASTIC EFFECTS ON ENDOTHELIAL MECHANOBIOLOGY UNDER PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT FLOW CONDITIONS THROUGH THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1 INVESTIGATES HOW MICROPLASTIC EXPOSURE IMPAIRS ENDOTHELIAL CELL MECHANICAL INTEGRITY AND CELL-MATRIX ADHESION USING TRACTION FORCE MICROSCOPY AND CELL ADHESION ASSAYS; AIM 2 CHARACTERIZES DISRUPTION OF SHEAR STRESS-ACTIVATED MECHANOTRANSDUCTION SIGNALING PATHWAYS THROUGH IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE, WESTERN BLOT ANALYSIS, AND GENE EXPRESSION STUDIES UNDER CONTROLLED FLOW; AND AIM 3 EVALUATES ENDOTHELIAL BARRIER DYSFUNCTION AND TESTS THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS USING CLINICALLY RELEVANT ANTIOXIDANTS AND ANTI-INFLAMMATORY COMPOUNDS. THE RESEARCH EMPLOYS HUMAN AORTIC AND UMBILICAL VEIN ENDOTHELIAL CELLS EXPOSED TO ENVIRONMENTALLY RELEVANT CONCENTRATIONS OF POLYSTYRENE AND POLYETHYLENE MICROPLASTICS, UTILIZING INNOVATIVE METHODOLOGY INCLUDING LAMINAR AND DISTURBED FLOW CHAMBERS, TRACTION FORCE MICROSCOPY, AND COMPREHENSIVE BARRIER FUNCTION ANALYSIS. THIS PARADIGM- SHIFTING INVESTIGATION WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION FOR MICROPLASTIC CARDIOVASCULAR RISK ASSESSMENT GUIDELINES, GENERATE PRELIMINARY DATA THAT COULD COMPLIMENT FUTURE CLINICAL STUDIES, AND TRAIN UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH TECHNIQUES COMBINING ENVIRONMENTAL TOXICOLOGY WITH CARDIOVASCULAR MECHANOBIOLOGY, PREPARING THEM TO ADDRESS COMPLEX GLOBAL HEALTH CHALLENGES WHILE DEVELOPING EXPERTISE IN CELL CULTURE, QUANTITATIVE MICROSCOPY, MOLECULAR BIOLOGY, AND DATA ANALYSIS ESSENTIAL FOR CAREERS IN BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MOLECULAR MECHANISMS UNDERLYING MOTOR EXIT POINT GLIA FUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE NERVOUS SYSTEM IS DIVIDED INTO TWO SEPARATE, YET CONNECTED, DOMAINS: THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) AND PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (PNS), IN WHICH DISTINCT CELL TYPES OFTEN CARRY OUT THE SAME BIOLOGICAL FUNCTION. FOR INSTANCE, OLIGODENDROCYTES ARE RESTRICTED TO THE CNS AND SCHWANN CELLS TO THE PNS, AND BOTH GLIAL CELL TYPES FUNCTION TO MYELINATE AXONS, FACILITATING EFFICIENT NERVE CONDUCTION. THE RATIONALE FOR THIS PROJECT IS THAT THE NERVOUS SYSTEM BOUNDARIES, CALLED TRANSITION ZONES (TZ), THAT WERE LONG THOUGHT TO BE SELECTIVELY PERMEABLE TO AXONS ONLY, ARE OCCUPIED BY DYNAMIC GLIAL CELLS AND THEIR PERMEABILITY IS PRECISELY REGULATED OVER THE COURSE OF NERVOUS SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT. WE RECENTLY CHARACTERIZED A NOVEL POPULATION OF GLIA THAT RESIDE AT THESE TZS. MOTOR EXIT POINT (MEP) GLIA ORIGINATE IN THE SPINAL CORD AND MIGRATE INTO THE PNS TO MYELINATE MOTOR AXONS. MEP GLIA ALSO REGULATE OLIGODENDROCYTE MIGRATION AT THE VENTRAL BORDER OF THE SPINAL CORD AND PREVENT OLIGODENDROCYTES TO ECTOPICALLY MIGRATE INTO THE PNS. UNLIKE TRADITIONAL MYELINATING GLIA, MEP GLIA DISPLAY CENTRAL/PERIPHERAL HYBRID CHARACTERISTICS, AND ARE CONVENIENTLY LOCATED AT THE EDGE OF THE SPINAL CORD, IN CLOSE PROXIMITY TO THE CNS AND PNS. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS, WHICH IS FORMULATED BASED ON PRELIMINARY DATA, IS THAT THESE TWO SUBTYPES OF CNS- DERIVED GLIA CAN FUNCTION IN BOTH HALVES OF THE NERVOUS SYSTEM. THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE ACCOMPLISHED BY THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) DEFINE MEP GLIA GENE EXPRESSION PROFILE. USING SINGLE CELL RNA-SEQUENCING ZEBRAFISH DATASETS, WE WILL USE IN SITU HYBRIDIZATION TO UNCOVER ADDITIONAL MEP GLIAL MARKERS. FOR EACH VALIDATED MARKER, WE WILL CREATE REPORTER AND MUTANT LINES, AND STUDY THE FUNCTION OF GENES PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN IN THE CONTEXT OF GLIAL BIOLOGY. THIS AIM WILL GENERATE HYPOTHESIS-DRIVEN PROJECTS FOR INCOMING STUDENTS. (2) INVESTIGATE PNS MYELINATING GLIA MIGRATING INTO THE SPINAL CORD. IN A RECENT STUDY, WE GENETICALLY INDUCED THE PRESENCE OF SCHWANN CELLS AND MEP GLIA IN THE POST-EMBRYONIC SPINAL CORD. IN THIS AIM, WE WILL DETERMINE THEIR ABILITY TO PRODUCE MYELIN IN THE HEALTHY AND DEMYELINATED CNS. (3) CHARACTERIZE OLIGODENDROCYTE MYELIN IN THE PNS. THE WORKING HYPOTHESIS IS THAT AT THE CNS/PNS INTERFACE, MOTOR AXON MYELINATION INVOLVES MULTIPLE POPULATIONS OF MYELINATING GLIA, AND THIS ARCHITECTURE IS PLASTIC UPON PERTURBATIONS. WE PREVIOUSLY DEMONSTRATED THE PRESENCE OF MYELINATING OLIGODENDROCYTES ON PNS MOTOR AXONS UPON PERTURBATION, BUT THE INTEGRITY AND MAINTENANCE OF THESE ECTOPIC MYELIN SHEATHS REMAIN UNKNOWN. THIS PROJECT IS INNOVATIVE BECAUSE WE PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE A PREVIOUSLY UNKNOWN SOURCE OF MYELIN-FORMING CELLS AND THEIR PLASTICITY. THE KNOWLEDGE WE WILL GAIN FROM THE PROPOSED EXPERIMENTS MAY PROVIDE AN INNOVATIVE BASIS FOR NOVEL MYELIN-REPAIR THERAPIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MICROENVIRONMENTAL RESCUE OF AGE-RELATED CELLULAR DYSFUNCTION IN A 3D BIOPRINTED MAMMARY MODEL SYSTEM - PROJECT SUMMARY DURING THE COMPLEX PROCESS OF CELLULAR AND TISSUE DECLINE DUE TO ORGANISMAL AGING, DISEASES SUCH AS DIABETES, NEURODEGENERATION, MUSCLE ATROPHY, AND CANCER BECOME COMMONPLACE. THESE DISEASES EACH HAVE UNIQUE GENETIC FEATURES AND TARGETING THEM CAN LEAD TO THERAPIES PRESERVING TISSUE FUNCTIONS. HOWEVER, RESTORATION TO A YOUTHFUL STATE IS RARE. THUS, IT IS CRITICAL TO RESEARCH AND DESIGN METHODS OF RESTORATIVE OR PREVENTATIVE TREATMENTS TO CURE THESE DISEASES. A MAJOR CHALLENGE IN RESEARCHING AGE-RELATED TISSUE DECLINE IS ENSURING THAT THE FINDINGS RELIABLY PREDICT OUTCOMES AT THE ORGANISMAL LEVEL. TO THIS END, WE AND OTHERS HAVE DEMONSTRATED THE POWERFUL REGENERATIVE CAPABILITIES OF THE MOUSE MAMMARY GLAND DURING THE PROCESS OF MAMMARY GLAND BIOGENESIS. WHEN THE MOUSE MAMMARY GLAND IS CLEARED OF NASCENT EPITHELIAL TISSUES AND INJECTED WITH DISPERSED MOUSE MAMMARY EPITHELIAL CELLS OR TISSUE FRAGMENTS MIXED WITH CANCER CELLS, DYSFUNCTIONAL STEM CELLS, OR NORMAL NON-MAMMARY STEM CELLS, THEY ARE REDIRECTED/RESCUED WHILE FUNCTIONALLY CONTRIBUTING TO GLAND REGENERATION. OTHER DATA HAS DEMONSTRATED THAT CANCER CELLS EXPOSED TO THE REGENERATIVE EMBRYONIC ENVIRONMENT CAN ALSO BE REDIRECTED TO A NORMAL FUNCTIONAL STATE. CONSISTENT WITH THIS, OUR PRELIMINARY EVIDENCE SHOWS THAT INTERACTIONS WITH INDUCED PLURIPOTENT STEM CELLS CAN REDUCE TUMOR FORMATION RATES OF BREAST CANCER CELLS IN MICE. THESE DATA, COUPLED WITH THE FINDING THAT EVS ISOLATED FROM PLURIPOTENT CELLS CAN ALSO PROMOTE HEALING, BLOCK SENESCENCE, AND REDUCE MOLECULAR MARKERS OF AGING, INDICATE THAT CELLS/TISSUES CAN BE REJUVENATED VIA EXPOSURE TO A REGENERATIVE ENVIRONMENT. HOWEVER, OUR UNDERSTANDING OF THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS FOR WHY THIS HAPPENS IS LACKING. WHILE THE GOLD STANDARD CLEARED MAMMARY GLAND MOUSE MODEL IS AN IMPORTANT TOOL FOR STUDYING REGENERATIVE MODELS, IT IS DIFFICULT TO DETERMINE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS WHEN USED EXCLUSIVELY. TO SOLVE THIS ISSUE OUR GROUP HAS DESIGNED A LOW-COST, ADAPTABLE 3D BIOPRINTER CAPABLE OF MANUFACTURING LUMINAL CHIMERIC MAMMARY EPITHELIAL ORGANOIDS IN VITRO. THIS TOOL, IN TANDEM WITH THE MOUSE MAMMARY GLAND MODEL SYSTEM, ENABLES US TO ASK DISCREET MOLECULAR-DRIVEN QUESTIONS ABOUT HOW REGENERATIVE ENVIRONMENTS AND SIGNALING CAUSE THEIR OBSERVED EFFECTS. WE HAVE FOUND THAT AS THESE REGENERATIVE CHIMERIC ORGANOIDS FORM IN VITRO, THE EXCHANGE OF INTERCELLULAR MACHINERY, SUCH AS MITOCHONDRIA, READILY OCCURS. HERE WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THAT THE EXPOSURE OF DYSFUNCTIONAL ORGANOIDS/TISSUES TO YOUTHFUL REGENERATIVE SIGNALING REVERSES AGE-RELATED DECLINE THROUGH INTERCELLULAR TRANSFER OF MOLECULAR MACHINERY, INCLUDING MITOCHONDRIA. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE AIM TO 1: DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR EFFECT OF REGENERATIVE INTERCELLULAR TRANSFER ON AGED/SENESCENT CELLS AND 2: DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR EFFECT OF INTERCELLULAR TRANSFER ON CANCER CELLS. THESE DATA WILL ALLOW US TO UNDERSTAND A CRITICAL ASPECT OF THE REJUVENATING EFFECTS OF EXPOSURE TO REGENERATIVE ENVIRONMENTS AND, THUS, BROADEN OUR CAPABILITIES TO DEVELOP DOWNSTREAM CLINICAL TREATMENTS TO PREVENT OR CURE MANY AGE-RELATED DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: GENOMIC DETERMINANTS AND ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS OF HUMAN ASSOCIATED AKKERMANSIA GROWN ON CORE HUMAN MILK OLIGOSACCHARIDES - AKKERMANSIA MUCINIPHILA IS A MUCIN-DEGRADING BACTERIUM COMMON TO THE HUMAN GUT THAT HAS BEEN SHOWN TO POSITIVELY IMPACT HUMAN HEALTH. HOWEVER, THE AKKERMANSIA GENUS IS DIVERSE, AND WE LACK A CLEAR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW THIS DIVERSITY IMPACTS THE PHYSIOLOGICAL ACTIVITY AND ECOLOGICAL DYNAMICS ACROSS THE LINEAGE. THE LONG- TERM GOAL OF OUR RESEARCH PROGRAM IS TO HELP DEVELOP TARGETED, THERAPEUTIC USES OF AKKERMANSIA, EITHER THROUGH STIMULATING ENDOGENOUS STRAINS WITH DIETARY INTERVENTIONS (~70% PREVALENCE) OR BY ADMINISTERING SPECIES AS PROBIOTICS IN A CONTEXT-DEPENDENT MANNER. BEFORE THESE THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS CAN BE REALIZED, WE NEED A DEEPER UNDERSTANDING OF THE METABOLIC STRATEGIES AND ECOLOGICAL DYNAMICS THAT ALLOW EACH AKKERMANSIA SPECIES TO COLONIZE, COMPETE, AND PERSIST IN THE GUT. THE OVERALL OBJECTIVES FOR THIS APPLICATION ARE (I) TO DEFINE THE GENOMIC AND METABOLIC DETERMINANTS BY WHICH SELECT AKKERMANSIA SPECIES AND STRAINS DEGRADE NON-FUCOSYLATED, CORE HUMAN MILK OLIGOSACCHARIDES (HMOS) DURING GROWTH, AND (II) TO IDENTIFY ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS AMONG AKKERMANSIA AND OTHER HMO-DEGRADING BACTERIA OF THE INFANT GUT MICROBIOTA. THE RATIONALE FOR PRIORITIZING EXPERIMENTS USING HMOS IS THAT THEY ARE SELECTIVE, DIETARY SUBSTRATES KNOWN TO INFLUENCE THE COMPOSITION, DEVELOPMENT, AND ACTIVITY OF THE GUT MICROBIOTA EARLY IN LIFE. FURTHER, ALTHOUGH HMOS ARE TYPICALLY AVAILABLE ONLY DURING BREASTFEEDING, HMOS ARE USED IN PREBIOTIC DIETARY FORMULATIONS FOR ADULTS. THUS, THE PROPOSED STUDIES WILL INFORM STRATEGIES TO STIMULATE OR ADMINISTER AKKERMANSIA THROUGHOUT HUMAN LIFE. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS APPLICATION IS THAT THE INCREASED GENOMIC CAPACITY FOR SUGAR DEGRADATION OBSERVED IN SELECT AKKERMANSIA GENOMES WILL RESULT IN MORE EFFICIENT AND POTENTIALLY NOVEL MECHANISMS OF DEGRADATION OF NON-FUCOSYLATED, CORE HMOS BY THOSE SPECIES/STRAINS. FURTHER, BECAUSE OF THE MORE EFFICIENT USE OF HMOS BY THESE SPECIES, THEY WILL BE ABLE TO CO-EXIST WITH OR POTENTIALLY OUTCOMPETE OTHER HMO-DEGRADING BACTERIA. TO TEST THESE HYPOTHESES, WE WILL USE LABORATORY CULTIVATION STUDIES COUPLED WITH MULTI-OMIC (I.E., GENOMIC, TRANSCRIPTOMIC, AND METABOLOMIC) APPROACHES TO INVESTIGATE TWO INDEPENDENT, BUT COMPLIMENTARY SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) – IDENTIFY THE GENOMIC DETERMINANTS AND METABOLIC OUTPUT OF GROWTH ON THE CORE HMOS LACTO-N-TETRAOSE (LNT) AND LACTO-N-NEOTETRAOSE (LNNT) ACROSS (AIM 1A) AND WITHIN (AIM 1B) HUMAN-ASSOCIATED AKKERMANSIA SPECIES. (2) CHARACTERIZE THE ECOLOGICAL INTERACTIONS AMONG SELECT AKKERMANSIA AND BIFIDOBACTERIUM SPECIES WHEN CO-CULTURED ON LNT AND LNNT. THIS WORK IS EXPECTED TO HAVE A SIGNIFICANT IMPACT BECAUSE AKKERMANSIA ARE BEING PURSUED FOR VARIOUS THERAPEUTIC APPLICATIONS WITH AN INCOMPLETE UNDERSTANDING OF THEIR BASIC BIOLOGY. GIVEN THAT AKKERMANSIA SPECIES ARE FUNCTIONALLY DISTINCT, IDENTIFYING MECHANISMS THAT FAVOR ONE SPECIES OVER ANOTHER IN A CONTEXT-DEPENDENT MANNER MAY INFORM FUTURE THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS SPECIFIC TO A PARTICULAR DISEASE STATE OR LIFE-STAGE. STUDIES WILL BE CONDUCTED BY STUDENT SCIENTISTS AT A PRIMARILY UNDERGRADUATE INSTITUTION, SIMULTANEOUSLY FULFILLING THE RESEARCH AND TRAINING MISSIONS OF THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF GENERAL MEDICAL SCIENCES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: CHAPERONE-MEDIATED AUTOPHAGY IN AGING-ASSOCIATED CARDIOVASCULAR FIBROSIS - ABSTRACT:  AGING IS ASSOCIATED WITH ACTIVATION OF PERIVASCULAR AND INTERSTITIAL CARDIAC FIBROBLASTS LEADING TO THE DEPOSITION OF LARGE AMOUNTS OF CROSS-LINKED EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX IN THE HEART AND IN THE LARGE ARTERIES. FIBROSIS IN AGING HEARTS IS ASSOCIATED WITH A UNIQUE PERTURBATION OF THE FIBROBLAST PHENOTYPE THAT REDUCES TURNOVER OF MATRIX PROTEINS, IN THE ABSENCE OF ANY CHANGES IN NEW COLLAGEN TRANSCRIPTION. CHAPERONE-MEDIATED AUTOPHAGY (CMA), THE MOST SELECTIVE FORM OF AUTOPHAGY CAN SELECTIVELY REMOVE SPECIFIC PROTEINS TO TERMINATE THEIR FUNCTION, REGULATING A RANGE OF CELLULAR PROCESSES, INCLUDING SURVIVAL, PROLIFERATION, AND DIFFERENTIATION. CMA EXHIBITS A MARKED DECLINE IN AGING TISSUES IN BOTH RODENT MODELS AND IN HUMAN CELLS THAT MAY PERTURB PROTEOME RENEWAL AND CAUSE DEFECTIVE ORGAN FUNCTION. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SHOW THAT DEVELOPMENT OF FIBROSIS IN AGING HEARTS IS ASSOCIATED WITH A DECLINE IN FIBROBLAST CMA ACTIVITY. ACCORDINGLY, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE AGE-RELATED CMA DECLINE IN FIBROBLASTS MEDIATES PROGRESSIVE FIBROTIC REMODELING IN AGING HEART AND VESSELS, PROMOTING DIASTOLIC DYSFUNCTION AND CONTRIBUTING TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF HEART FAILURE.  THE HYPOTHESIS WILL BE TESTED IN 3 SPECIFIC AIMS:  SPECIFIC AIM 1: TO EXAMINE THE TIME COURSE OF FIBROBLAST CMA DECLINE IN AGING HEARTS AND TO STUDY THE EFFECTS OF FIBROBLAST-SPECIFIC CMA DISRUPTION IN AGE-ASSOCIATED CARDIOVASCULAR FIBROSIS AND DYSFUNCTION. THE TIME COURSE OF FIBROBLAST CMA DECLINE IN AGING HEARTS AND VESSELS WILL BE STUDIED USING CMA REPORTER KFERQ-DENDRA MICE. MICE WITH FIBROBLAST-SPECIFIC DISRUPTION OF LAMP2A, THE CRITICAL LYSOSOMAL MEMBRANE PROTEIN INVOLVED IN BINDING AND INTERNALIZATION OF CMA SUBSTRATES, WILL BE USED TO EXAMINE THE ROLE OF FIBROBLAST CMA IN CARDIOVASCULAR AGING.  SPECIFIC AIM 2: TO EXAMINE THE EFFECTS OF FIBROBLAST-SPECIFIC CMA ACTIVATION IN DELAYING AGE-ASSOCIATED FIBROTIC CARDIAC AND VASCULAR REMODELING AND DYSFUNCTION. MICE WITH FIBROBLAST-SPECIFIC OVEREXPRESSION OF LAMP2A WILL BE USED TO STUDY THE EFFECTS OF FIBROBLAST CMA ACTIVATION ON CARDIAC AND VASCULAR AGING.  SPECIFIC AIM 3: TO DISSECT THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS RESPONSIBLE FOR THE EFFECTS OF CMA FAILURE ON AGING-ASSOCIATED FIBROSIS AND DYSFUNCTION AND TO IDENTIFY CMA TARGETS IN AGING MOUSE CARDIAC FIBROBLASTS. OUR PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGEST POTENTIAL EFFECTS OF CMA DISRUPTION ON THE NF-B CASCADE, MEDIATED THROUGH ACCUMULATION OF THE IB KINASE.  OUR PROPOSAL WILL TEST A NOVEL CONCEPT THAT MAY HAVE MAJOR IMPLICATIONS IN THE PATHOGENESIS OF AGING-ASSOCIATED HEART FAILURE AND MAY SUGGEST PROMISING THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REAL-LIFE DUAL-TASK TRAINING FOR OLDER ADULTS AT RISK TO FALL: A PILOT CLINICAL TRIAL - ONE IN FOUR OLDER ADULTS REPORTED A FALL IN THE LAST YEAR. THESE FALLS CAN RESULT IN NEGATIVE CONSEQUENCES ON HEALTH, QUALITY OF LIFE, AND PARTICIPATION IN MEANINGFUL ACTIVITIES. DOING TWO THINGS AT ONCE (I.E., DUAL-TASKING) INCREASES THE RISK OF FALLING FOR OLDER ADULTS. ADDITIONALLY, DUAL-TASKING BECOMES INCREASINGLY DIFFICULT FOR OLDER ADULTS AS THE COMPLEXITY OF A TASK INCREASES. DUAL-TASK TRAINING CAN IMPROVE THE ABILITY OF OLDER ADULTS TO DO TWO THINGS AT ONCE BY PROVIDING TRAINING IN ISOLATING AND SHIFTING ATTENTIONAL FOCUS BETWEEN TASKS AND THEIR COMPONENTS (E.G., COGNITIVE AND MOTOR COMPONENTS OF TASKS). WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT DUAL-TASK TRAINING EMBEDDED IN REAL-LIFE ACTIVITIES WILL RESULT IN IMPROVED DUAL-TASK PERFORMANCE, REDUCED FALL RISK, AND BETTER PARTICIPATION IN EVERYDAY ACTIVITIES (INSTRUMENTAL ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING [IADLS]) FOR OLDER ADULTS.   THE OVERALL GOAL OF THIS STUDY IS TO ASSESS FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY AND SIGNAL OF EFFICACY OF A NOVEL 6-WEEK REAL- LIFE DUAL-TASK TRAINING INTERVENTION (REAL-DTT) INTERVENTION COMPARED TO A 6-WEEK EVIDENCE-BASED FALL PREVENTION INTERVENTION (FALLSTALK®). REAL-DTT WILL INCLUDE OCCUPATIONAL THERAPY WITH IADLS USING FOUR PROTOCOLIZED LEVELS (INCREASING IN TASK COMPLEXITY) OF COGNITIVE SKILLS, AND FOUR PROTOCOLIZED LEVELS OF MOTOR SKILLS FOR EACH OF THE INCLUDED IADLS (E.G., LAUNDRY, MEAL PREPARATION, CLEANING, SHOPPING, MEDICATION MANAGEMENT, PUBLIC TRANSPORTATION, DISHES/MEAL CLEAN-UP, AND MONEY MANAGEMENT). ADDITIONALLY, PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE A STRUCTURED DEBRIEF ACTIVITY TO IDENTIFY HIGHER RISK FALL BEHAVIORS WITHIN IADL EXPERIENCES AND REFLECT ON WHEN THEY FOCUS ON THE MOTOR TASK VS. WHEN THEY FOCUS ON THE COGNITIVE TASK. FALLSTALK® IS AN EVIDENCE-BASED BEHAVIOR- CHANGE INTERVENTION THAT VARIES BASED ON THE FALL RISKS IDENTIFIED BY EACH INDIVIDUAL. IN THIS CLINICAL TRIAL, OLDER ADULTS AT RISK TO FALL (N= 66 ENROLLED, N=54 COMPLETERS) WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO REAL-DTT OR FALLSTALK®.   THE SPECIFIC AIMS ARE TO 1) ASSESS FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF THE REAL-DTT AND FALLSTALK® INTERVENTIONS AND DESCRIBE ANY DIFFERENCES BETWEEN THE INTERVENTIONS, AND 2) DETERMINE CHANGES ON DUAL-TASK PERFORMANCE (PRIMARY OUTCOME), FALL RISK, AND IADL PERFORMANCE, BETWEEN GROUPS (REAL-DTT AND FALLSTALK®) AND WITHIN GROUPS (PRE-ASSESSMENT TO POST-ASSESSMENT). OUR EXPECTED OUTCOMES ARE DATA ON FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, AND SIGNAL OF EFFICACY OF THE NOVEL REAL-DTT INTERVENTION. THE RESULTS WILL SUPPORT APPROPRIATE MODIFICATIONS TO THE REAL-DTT INTERVENTION, DETERMINE NUMBER OF PARTICIPANTS NEEDED FOR FUTURE TRIALS, CONSIDER REFINED OUTCOME MEASURES, AND ALLOW FOR AN OPTIMIZED VERSION OF THE REAL-DTT. ULTIMATELY, IN ALIGNMENT WITH THE NATIONAL INSTITUTE ON AGING STRATEGIC PRIORITIES, THE REAL-DTT INTERVENTION WILL BE DESIGNED TO REDUCE FALL RISK AND IMPROVE PARTICIPATION IN IADLS TO PROMOTE WELL-BEING (PROMOTING EFFECTIVE/SAFE PARTICIPATION) AND INDEPENDENCE OF OLDER ADULTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AFFECTIVE FORECASTING AND TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING ACROSS ADULTHOOD - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT THE TENDENCY TO DEVALUE DELAYED REWARDS IN FAVOR OF MORE IMMEDIATE REWARDS, KNOWN AS TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING, HAS SERIOUS IMPLICATIONS FOR HEALTH BEHAVIOR AND OUTCOMES. DEVELOPING STRATEGIES TO REDUCE TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING IS THEREFORE CRUCIAL. HOWEVER, EXISTING INTERVENTIONS HAVE NOT BEEN SUCCESSFUL IN EITHER HEALTHY OLDER ADULTS OR THOSE SUFFERING FROM NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDERS LIKE ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO ADDRESS THIS CRITICAL KNOWLEDGE GAP BY INVESTIGATING ANOTHER POTENTIAL STRATEGY FOR REDUCING TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING––AFFECTIVE FORECASTING. AFFECTIVE FORECASTING, OR PREDICTING ONE’S FEELINGS ABOUT RECEIVING A FUTURE OUTCOME, IS PROMISING BECAUSE IT RELIES ON PSYCHOLOGICAL AND BRAIN MECHANISMS THAT ARE PRESERVED IN OLDER AGE. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF THIS PROPOSAL IS THAT ENGAGING IN AFFECTIVE FORECASTING DURING DECISION MAKING MAY EFFECTIVELY REDUCE TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING, PARTICULARLY IN OLDER ADULTS. THIS HYPOTHESIS WILL BE TESTED BY PURSUING TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) DETERMINE THE EXTENT TO WHICH SPONTANEOUS PREDICTED FEELINGS ARE RELATED TO TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING AND IF AGE MODERATES THIS RELATIONSHIP, AND 2) DETERMINE IF ENGAGING IN DIRECTED AFFECTIVE FORECASTING CAN REDUCE TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING ACROSS ADULTHOOD. WE WILL INVESTIGATE THESE AIMS USING TWO STUDIES WITH PARTICIPANTS AGED 25-85. BOTH STUDIES WILL USE BINNED RECRUITMENT TO CREATE SAMPLES EQUALLY DISTRIBUTED ACROSS THE LIFESPAN. IN STUDY 1, PARTICIPANTS (N = 200) RECRUITED ONLINE WILL COMPLETE A WELL-ESTABLISHED INTERTEMPORAL CHOICE TASK WHERE THEY DECIDE BETWEEN SMALLER, SOONER AND LARGER, LATER MONETARY REWARDS. THEN, PARTICIPANTS WILL PREDICT HOW THEY WOULD FEEL IF THEY RECEIVED THE DELAYED REWARDS AT THE SPECIFIED TIME. THREE OF THESE REWARDS WILL BE REALIZED AFTER THE STATED TIME DELAY, AND PARTICIPANTS WILL PROVIDE IN-THE-MOMENT FEELING RATINGS UPON RECEIVING THE REWARD, USING A SMARTPHONE-BASED APP. THIS WILL ALLOW US TO INVESTIGATE THE ACCURACY OF AFFECTIVE FORECASTING FOR DELAYED MONETARY REWARDS AND ITS RELATIONSHIP WITH TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING. IN STUDY 2, PARTICIPANTS (N = 100) WILL BE RECRUITED TO AN IN-PERSON STUDY. HALF OF THE PARTICIPANTS WILL BE ASSIGNED TO COMPLETE AN INTERTEMPORAL CHOICE TASK IN WHICH THEY ENGAGE IN AFFECTIVE FORECASTING BEFORE MAKING EACH CHOICE. THIS AFFECTIVE FORECASTING CONDITION WILL ENTAIL ASKING PARTICIPANTS TO PREDICT THEIR FUTURE FEELINGS ABOUT RECEIVING A FUTURE REWARD AT THE TIME OF CHOICE. THE OTHER HALF OF THE PARTICIPANTS WILL COMPLETE A CLASSIC INTERTEMPORAL CHOICE TASK. WE WILL EXAMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THIS NEW STRATEGY AND THE ROLE OF AGE IN ITS EFFICACY. THIS RESEARCH IS EXPECTED TO YIELD CRITICAL INSIGHTS INTO THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN AFFECTIVE FORECASTING AND TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING AND HOW THESE PROCESSES ARE IMPACTED BY AGE. CONSISTENT WITH THE NIH STAGE MODEL FOR BASIC SCIENCE RESEARCH, THIS R21 PROPOSAL PROVIDES FOUNDATIONAL WORK NECESSARY FOR SUBSEQUENT R01 INVESTIGATIONS THAT WILL COMPARATIVELY EVALUATE AFFECTIVE FORECASTING AGAINST ESTABLISHED TEMPORAL DISCOUNTING INTERVENTIONS, DETERMINE THE EFFICACY FOR HEALTH-RELATED OUTCOMES, AND EXAMINE THESE MECHANISMS WITHIN CLINICAL POPULATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: INVESTIGATING INTER-ORGANELLE DYNAMICS DURING AGING - PROJECT SUMMARY WITHIN EUKARYOTIC CELLS, SPECIALIZED COMPARTMENTS KNOWN AS ORGANELLES ARE MEMBRANE BOUND UNITS THAT ALLOW FOR DISTINCT BIOCHEMICAL REACTIONS TO OCCUR. ALTHOUGH THE METABOLIC FUNCTION OF INDIVIDUAL ORGANELLES IS WELL ESTABLISHED, THE CELL MUST COORDINATE THE ACTIVITY OF THESE ORGANELLES TO MAINTAIN CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. HOWEVER, THEIR COMPARTMENTAL NATURE PRESENTS A CHALLENGE TO THE CELL. SITES OF INTER-ORGANELLE CONTACTS ARE BECOMING INCREASINGLY RECOGNIZED FOR THEIR IMPORTANCE IN MAINTAINING CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. INDEED, ORGANELLES DO NOT ACT AS AUTONOMOUS ISOLATED UNITS BUT DYNAMICALLY INTERACT WITH ONE ANOTHER BY FORMING TRANSIENT CONTACTS. THESE CONTACT SITES FORM PLATFORMS THAT MEDIATE SIGNALING, THE TRANSFER OF MATERIALS (E.G., CA2+ AND PHOSPHOLIPIDS) AND PROMOTE ORGANELLE MORPHOLOGY CHANGES. AS ORGANELLE FITNESS IS CRITICAL FOR CELLULAR HEALTH, INTER-ORGANELLE COMMUNICATION IS VITAL FOR THE CELL TO ADAPT TO INTRA- AND EXTRACELLULAR STRESSES TO MAINTAIN CELLULAR HOMEOSTASIS. WHILE ORGANELLULAR FITNESS HAS BEEN SHOWN TO DECLINE WITH AGE, THE ROLE OF INTER-ORGANELLE COMMUNICATION IN THIS DECLINE IS NOT KNOWN. MOREOVER, ORGANELLES UNDERGO MORPHOLOGICAL CHANGES DURING AGING AND IN AGE-RELATED DISEASES, YET THE REASONS HAVE REMAINED UNCLEAR. HERE, UNDER THE R21 NIH EXPLORATORY/DEVELOPMENTAL RESEARCH GRANT PROGRAM (PA-25-304), WE PROPOSE TO UTILIZE THE STRENGTHS OF C. ELEGANS, E.G., SHORT LIFESPAN, OPTICAL CLARITY AND GENETIC AMENABILITY, TO DETERMINE THE SPATIAL CONTEXT OF INTER-ORGANELLE COMMUNICATION TO IDENTIFY ORGANELLULAR SIGNATURES THAT DEVELOP DURING AGING AND PROTEOSTASIS DECLINE. THESE STUDIES WILL ESTABLISH A PLATFORM TO UNDERSTAND THE IMPACT AGING HAS ON ORGANELLE INTERACTIONS AND FUNCTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EXAMINING THE IMPACT OF WEATHER-RELATED BARRIERS ON PRIMARY CARE UTILIZATION IN OLDER ADULTS WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS - PROJECT ABSTRACT NATIONALLY, MISSED VISITS ARE A WIDESPREAD AND COSTLY ISSUE, WITH NO-SHOW RATES RANGING FROM 4% TO 55% AND COSTING THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM OVER $150 BILLION ANNUALLY. MISSED PRIMARY CARE VISITS ALSO POSE A SIGNIFICANT THREAT TO THE HEALTH OF ELDERLY PATIENTS AND THE EFFICIENCY OF THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM. WITH 80% OF OLDER ADULTS IN THE U.S. HAVING AT LEAST ONE CHRONIC CONDITION, CONSISTENT PRIMARY CARE IS VITAL FOR DISEASE MONITORING AND TREAT- MENT—ESPECIALLY FOR COMMON CONDITIONS SUCH AS DIABETES, HYPERTENSION, CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DIS- EASE, CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE, AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND OTHER NEUROCOGNITIVE DISORDERS. HOWEVER, MISSED VISITS DISRUPT THIS CONTINUITY OF CARE, CONTRIBUTING TO POOR HEALTH OUTCOMES, INCLUDING INCREASED MORTALITY RISK, DELAYED FOLLOW-UP, AND GREATER PATIENT ATTRITION. THESE DISRUPTIONS ARE ESPECIALLY PROBLEMATIC FOR OLDER ADULTS WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS WHO ARE MORE LIKELY TO MISS VISITS. ONE UNDERSTUDIED BARRIER TO PRIMARY CARE ACCESS IS INCLEMENT WEATHER, SUCH AS EXTREME TEMPERATURES, HIGH HEAT INDEX, AND HEAVY PRECIPITATION. WHILE SOME RE- SEARCH SHOWS A LINK BETWEEN SPECIFIC WEATHER EVENTS AND MISSED VISITS, FINDINGS VARY BY REGION, AND MOST STUD- IES HAVE NOT FOCUSED ON ELDERLY PATIENTS OR THOSE WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS. THERE REMAINS A CRITICAL GAP IN UNDER- STANDING WHO IS MOST AT RISK AND HOW MUCH PRIMARY CARE IS AFFECTED. TELEMEDICINE OFFERS A PROMISING SOLUTION, HAVING PROVEN EFFECTIVE IN REDUCING MISSED VISITS DURING THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC. BOTH PATIENTS AND CLINICIANS REPORTED SATISFACTION WITH TELEMEDICINE, PARTICULARLY WHEN IN-PERSON VISITS WERE NOT FEASIBLE DUE TO WEATHER. THIS STUDY AIMS TO QUANTIFY HOW INCLEMENT WEATHER CONTRIBUTES TO MISSED PRIMARY CARE VISITS AMONG ELDERLY ADULTS WITH CHRONIC CONDITIONS AND EVALUATE WHETHER TELEMEDICINE CAN MITIGATE THESE EFFECTS BY PROVIDING AN ACCESSIBLE ALTERNATIVE DURING INCLEMENT WEATHER. USING ELECTRONIC HEALTH RECORD DATA FROM 2022–2025 LINKED WITH DETAILED WEATHER INFORMATION, WE WILL ASSESS THE IMPACTS OF INCLEMENT WEATHER ON PATTERNS OF MISSED VISITS, TIME INTERVALS BETWEEN APPOINTMENTS, AND SUBSEQUENT EMERGENCY OR HOSPITAL USE WITHIN A LARGE, DIVERSE POPU- LATION OF ELDERLY PATIENTS ACROSS ILLINOIS AND WISCONSIN. ULTIMATELY, THIS RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS TO GUIDE FUTURE INTERVENTIONS, SUCH AS PROACTIVELY SCHEDULING TELEMEDICINE VISITS AHEAD OF FORECASTED INCLEMENT WEATHER, THAT HEALTHCARE SYSTEMS CAN ADOPT TO MAINTAIN ACCESS, CONTINUITY, AND HEALTH FOR ALL PATIENTS.

description: L1 RETROTRANSPOSON CONTRIBUTION TO NORMAL BRAIN AGING AND ALZHEIMERS DISEASE IN VIVO - AMONG KEY CHARACTERISTICS OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE ARE TOXICITY FROM AMYLOID PLAQUES, NEUROFIBRILLARY TAU TANGLES, AND CHRONIC INFLAMMATION RESULTING IN THE LOSS OF COGNITIVE FUNCTION. THESE MORPHOLOGICAL CHANGES ARE PRECEDED BY ALTERED TRANSCRIPTIONAL PROFILES, INFLAMMATION, AND INCREASED DNA DAMAGE, ALL OF WHICH ARE THOUGHT TO PROMOTE NEURODEGENERATION. AMONG POTENTIAL ENDOGENOUS CONTRIBUTORS TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE IS THE LINE-1 (L1) RETROTRANSPOSON. L1 IS A REPETITIVE GENETIC ELEMENT THAT INCREASES ITS COPY NUMBER IN THE HOST GENOME THROUGH RETROTRANSPOSITION, WHICH INVOLVES BREAKING GENOMIC DNA. IN ADDITION TO RETROTRANSPOSITION, L1 EXPRESSION CAN GENERATE DNA BREAKS AND TRIGGER CGAS ACTIVATION, WHICH CAN CONTRIBUTE TO SENESCENCE, APOPTOSIS, AND INFLAMMATION OBSERVED IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PATIENTS. L1 MRNA EXPRESSION AND RETROTRANSPOSITION HAVE BEEN DETECTED IN NORMAL HUMAN AND MOUSE BRAIN AREAS THAT ARE AFFECTED BY ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. WE HAVE REPORTED DIFFERENT PATTERNS OF ENDOGENOUS L1 EXPRESSION IN THE MALE AND FEMALE MOUSE BRAINS, WHICH MAY BE RELEVANT TO A HIGHER RISK OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE IN FEMALES. COMBINED THESE FINDINGS LEAD US TO PROPOSE THAT L1 CAN BE A PLAUSIBLE INTRINSIC GENETIC VARIABLE THAT CAN CONTRIBUTE TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PROGRESSION IN VIVO BY TRIGGERING PERSISTENT TRANSCRIPTIONAL CHANGES CONSISTENT WITH THOSE OBSERVED IN AD PATIENTS. SEVERAL STUDIES EXPLORING TRANSPOSONS’ ROLE IN NEURODEGENERATION HAVE ESTABLISHED SOME CRITICAL CORRELATIONS AND ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN L1, AGING, AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. HOWEVER, STUDIES THAT DIRECTLY TEST L1 CONTRIBUTION TO BRAIN AGING OR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE IN VIVO CANNOT BE PERFORMED IN HUMANS. OUR AIMS ARE DESIGNED TO TEST THIS CONTRIBUTION USING MOUSE MODELS OF L1 RETROTRANSPOSITION AND ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. IN AIM 1, WE WILL USE AN EXISTING CUSTOM L1 TRANSGENIC MOUSE MODEL TO TEST WHETHER CHRONIC L1 TRANSGENE EXPRESSION ACCELERATES NORMAL BRAIN AGING BY TRIGGERING AGE-ASSOCIATED TRANSCRIPTIONAL CHANGES. IN AIM 2, BY USING EXISTING MOUSE MODELS OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND L1 WE WILL TEST CONTRIBUTION OF CHRONIC PHYSIOLOGICAL L1 TRANSGENE EXPRESSION TO TRANSCRIPTIONAL, HISTOLOGICAL, AND BEHAVIORAL CHANGES DURING ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PROGRESSION. IN BOTH AIMS ENDOGENOUS L1 EXPRESSION WILL BE ASSESSED. IF SUCCESSFUL, OUR STUDIES WILL DETERMINE CLINICAL RELEVANCE OF L1 EXPRESSION TO NORMAL AGING AND/OR ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PROGRESSION, WHICH WILL HAVE IMPORTANT PRECLINICAL AND CLINICAL RAMIFICATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ESTABLISHING PROCOTYLA FLUVIATILIS AS A COMPARATIVE MODEL FOR AGING RESEARCH - SUMMARY AGING REMAINS ONE OF THE MOST PRESSING BIOLOGICAL CHALLENGES, YET THE CELLULAR AND MOLECULAR MECHANISMS THAT LIMIT LIFESPAN, EVEN IN HIGHLY REGENERATIVE ANIMALS, REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD. FLATWORMS ARE RENOWNED FOR THEIR STEM CELL–DRIVEN REGENERATIVE ABILITIES, BUT EVEN AMONG CLOSELY RELATED SPECIES, THEY EXHIBIT STRIKING VARIATION IN REPRODUCTIVE STRATEGIES, REGENERATIVE POTENTIAL, AND LONGEVITY. THE NORTH AMERICAN PLANARIAN PROCOTYLA FLUVIATILIS PROVIDES A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO DISSECT THESE RELATIONSHIPS: IT REPRODUCES SEASONALLY AND UNDERGOES RAPID SOMA DECLINE FOLLOWING EGG-LAYING, DESPITE MAINTAINING ABUNDANT STEM CELLS AND ROBUST REGENERATIVE ABILITIES. PRIOR STUDIES ON REGENERATION IN P. FLUVIATILIS HAVE ESTABLISHED ESSENTIAL GENOMIC RESOURCES, FUNCTIONAL ASSAYS, AND METHODS FOR MECHANISTIC STUDIES. BUILDING ON THESE TOOLS, THIS PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH P. FLUVIATILIS AS A RIGOROUS NEW MODEL FOR AGING RESEARCH BY (1) DEFINING HOW STEM CELL FUNCTION AND TISSUE STRUCTURE CHANGE ACROSS ITS SEASONAL LIFE CYCLE, (2) MAPPING AGE-ASSOCIATED CELLULAR AND TRANSCRIPTIONAL CHANGES USING SINGLE-CELL SEQUENCING, AND (3) TESTING WHETHER CONSERVED GENETIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL REGULATORS OF LIFESPAN ALSO ACT IN THIS REGENERATIVE SPECIES. BY INTEGRATING STEM CELL BIOLOGY, MOLECULAR GENETICS, AND FUNCTIONAL PERTURBATION, THIS WORK WILL REVEAL HOW REGENERATION INTERSECTS WITH LOSS OF SOMATIC MAINTENANCE, OFFERING NEW INSIGHT INTO CONSERVED MECHANISMS THAT GOVERN TISSUE HEALTH AND LONGEVITY ACROSS SPECIES, INCLUDING HUMANS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ALPHA-KETOGLUTARATE: A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC STRATEGY TO IMPROVE NEUROGLIOVASCULAR COUPLING AND COGNITIVE AGING IN OLDER ADULTS - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT  NORMAL COGNITIVE FUNCTION REQUIRES ADEQUATE BLOOD SUPPLY TO THE BRAIN TO SUPPORT NEURONAL ACTIVITY. IN THE HEALTHY YOUNG BRAIN, CEREBRAL BLOOD FLOW IS RAPIDLY ADJUSTED TO MEET THE INCREASED OXYGEN AND NUTRIENT DEMANDS OF ACTIVE BRAIN REGIONS VIA A HOMEOSTATIC MECHANISM TERMED NEUROGLIOVASCULAR COUPLING (NGVC). THIS MECHANISM INVOLVES A COMPLEX INTERCELLULAR SIGNALING NETWORK BETWEEN NEURONAL, GLIAL, AND ENDOTHELIAL CELLS, WHICH COME TOGETHER TO FORM THE NEUROGLIOVASCULAR UNIT (NGVU). PRECLINICAL AND CLINICAL STUDIES DEMONSTRATE THAT EXPERIMENTALLY INDUCED NGVC DYSFUNCTION IN YOUNG ANIMALS RESULTS IN COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND THAT NGVC IS IMPAIRED IN NORMAL AGING AND IS IMPLICATED IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF AGE-RELATED COGNITIVE DECLINE. IMPORTANTLY, RESTORATION OF NGVC IN AGED ANIMALS BY TARGETED PHARMACOLOGICAL TREATMENTS IMPROVES NGVC FUNCTION AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE. HOWEVER, THERE ARE NO CLINICALLY APPROVED TREATMENTS TO REVERSE AGE-RELATED NGVC DYSFUNCTION IN HUMANS.  CELLULAR DAMAGE CAUSED BY MITOCHONDRIAL DYSFUNCTION AND EXACERBATED OXIDATIVE STRESS, BOTH PROCESSES RECOGNIZED AS KEY HALLMARKS OF BRAIN AGING, HAVE BEEN LINKED TO NGVU DISRUPTION AND SUBSEQUENT NGVC DYSFUNCTION. YET, TO DATE, VERY FEW CLINICAL TRIALS HAVE TESTED ANTI-AGING INTERVENTIONS FOR THEIR ABILITY TO REDUCE OXIDATIVE STRESS SPECIFICALLY WITHIN NGVU CELLS, AND TO ASSESS THEIR EFFECTS ON NGVC RESPONSES AND COGNITION IN OLDER ADULTS. ALPHA- KETOGLUTARATE (AKG) IS AN ENDOGENOUSLY PRODUCED INTERMEDIATE OF THE TRICARBOXYLIC ACID CYCLE INVOLVED IN CRITICAL CELLULAR METABOLISM PROCESSES, BUT WHOSE LEVELS DECLINE 10-FOLD BETWEEN MIDLIFE AND OLDER AGE. THIS NATURAL DECLINE SPARKED THE INTEREST IN USING DIETARY AKG SUPPLEMENTATION AS AN ANTI-AGING INTERVENTION SUPPORTING CELLULAR ANTIOXIDANT DEFENSES AND MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION. EARLY CLINICAL TRIALS INDICATE AKG IS SAFE AND IMPROVES FRAILTY OUTCOMES IN OLDER ADULTS. HOWEVER, ITS POTENTIAL TO REDUCE OXIDATIVE STRESS WITHIN NGVU CELLS AND IMPROVE NGVC AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE IN THIS POPULATION REMAINS UNKNOWN.  CLINICALLY, MITOCHONDRIAL FUNCTION AND OXIDATIVE STRESS ARE ASSESSED USING CIRCULATING OR CEREBROSPINAL BIOMARKERS. HOWEVER, THESE BIOMARKERS LACK SPECIFICITY FOR THE STATUS OF INDIVIDUAL NGVU CELL TYPES. EMERGING EVIDENCE SUPPORTS THE USE OF EXTRACELLULAR VESICLES (EVS) AS POTENTIAL BIOMARKERS IN AGE-RELATED NEUROLOGICAL IMPAIRMENTS. BECAUSE EVS CARRY SURFACE MARKERS SPECIFIC TO THEIR CELL OF ORIGIN, ISOLATING AND ANALYZING EVS FROM NEURONS, ASTROCYTES, AND VASCULAR CELLS MAY PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHT INTO CELL-SPECIFIC CONTRIBUTIONS TO NGVC IMPAIRMENT AND ASSOCIATED COGNITIVE DECLINE AS WELL AS INTO CELL-SPECIFIC RESPONSES TO TARGETED INTERVENTIONS.  THIS PROPOSAL WILL TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT AKG SUPPLEMENTATION WILL IMPROVE NGVC RESPONSES AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE IN OLDER ADULTS. WE WILL ALSO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT THESE EFFECTS ARE MEDIATED BY A DECREASE IN AGE- RELATED OXIDATIVE STRESS WITHIN NGVU CELLS. THESE HYPOTHESES WILL BE TESTED IN A RANDOMIZED, DOUBLE-BLIND, PLACEBO- CONTROLLED CLINICAL TRIAL WITH 24 WEEKS OF AKG SUPPLEMENTATION IN COMMUNITY DWELLING OLDER ADULTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: UNRAVELING PATHWAYS TO CEREBRAL SMALL VESSEL DISEASE IN VCID AND AD WITH FERUMOXYTOL-ENHANCED MRI - ABSTRACT ANTI-AMYLOID THERAPIES HAVE ADVANCED THE TREATMENT OF ALZHEIMER’ DISEASE (AD) PROTEINOPATHY AND RELATED COGNITIVE DECLINE; HOWEVER, CLINICAL STUDIES OFTEN OVERLOOK THE CONTRIBUTION OF COMORBID CEREBRAL SMALL VESSEL DISEASE (CSVD) IN MIXED DEMENTIAS. THIS CREATES A CRITICAL GAP IN DEMENTIA RESEARCH BOTH IN UNDERSTANDING AND ADDRESSING VASCULAR CONTRIBUTIONS TO COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT AND DEMENTIA (VCID) AND IN EVALUATING VASCULAR VULNERABILITIES THAT MAY INFLUENCE THE RISK OF IATROGENIC COMPLICATIONS SUCH AS AMYLOID-RELATED IMAGING ABNORMALITIES (ARIA). THE GAP LARGELY STEMS FROM THE ABSENCE OF SENSITIVE AND SPECIFIC VASCULAR BIOMARKERS CAPABLE OF DETECTING EARLY MICROVASCULAR DYSFUNCTION AND CAPTURING THE UNDERLYING PATHOPHYSIOLOGY OF CSVD, THE MOST PREVALENT FORM OF VCID. MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING (MRI) REMAINS THE STANDARD FOR NON-INVASIVE ASSESSMENT OF CSVD. HOWEVER, COMMONLY USED MRI MARKERS SUCH AS WHITE MATTER HYPERINTENSITIES (WMHS) ON T2-FLAIR PRIMARILY REFLECT NON- SPECIFIC DOWNSTREAM SEQUELAE OF CSVD RATHER THAN THE UNDERLYING MICROVASCULAR DYSFUNCTION. TO OVERCOME THIS LIMITATION, THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL INVESTIGATE NOVEL MICROVASCULAR MARKERS USING UNIQUE FERUMOXYTOL-ENHANCED MRI TO TEST HYPOTHESES THAT LINK SPECIFIC VASCULAR PROCESSES TO CSVD IN INDIVIDUALS WITH MIXED VCID AND AD BURDEN. IN PRELIMINARY STUDIES, WE HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT FERUMOXYTOL-ENHANCED MRI ENABLES UNIQUE AND QUANTITATIVE CHARACTERIZATION OF THE MICROVASCULATURE, INCLUDING VASCULAR DENSITY AND HEMODYNAMIC MEASURES OF MICROVASCULAR PULSATILITY. THESE TECHNIQUES HAVE NOT BEEN APPLIED TO VCID OR AD POPULATIONS. HARNESSING THE UNIQUE CHARACTERIZATION PROVIDED BY FERUMOXYTOL-ENHANCED MRI, THIS STUDY AIMS TO FURTHER OUR UNDERSTANDING OF MICROVASCULAR INVOLVEMENT IN VCID AND AD. TO ACHIEVE THIS, WE WILL CONDUCT A SINGLE-VISIT STUDY IN COGNITIVELY UNIMPAIRED INDIVIDUALS WITH BIOMARKER EVIDENCE OF BOTH VCID AND AD BURDEN (N=40; 50% AMYLOID- POSITIVE). PARTICIPANTS WILL BE RECRUITED FROM ONGOING AGING STUDIES WITH EXISTING DATA INCLUDING MEDICAL HISTORY, VASCULAR RISK FACTORS, COGNITIVE ASSESSMENTS, AND IMAGING AND BIOFLUID BIOMARKERS OF VCID AND AD. USING FERUMOXYTOL-ENHANCED MRI, WE AIM TO CHARACTERIZE THE RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN MICROVASCULAR PULSATILITY, VESSEL DENSITY, AND CSVD-RELATED TISSUE INJURY. OUR GOAL IS TO IDENTIFY POTENTIALLY MODIFIABLE TARGETS WITHIN CSVD PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND INVESTIGATE THE INFLUENCE OF AD ON CSVD MANIFESTATION. COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY WILL PROVIDE NEW INSIGHTS INTO CSVD PATHOPHYSIOLOGY IN INDIVIDUALS WITH MIXED VCID AND AD BURDEN, ESTABLISH A NOVEL IMAGING PLATFORM FOR MICROVASCULAR ASSESSMENT, AND GENERATE PRELIMINARY DATA AND RATIONALE TO SUPPORT FUTURE EXTRAMURAL FUNDING APPLICATIONS WITH BROADER SCIENTIFIC SCOPE (NIH R01). ULTIMATELY, THIS WORK WILL LAY A FOUNDATION FOR LONGITUDINAL STUDIES ON CSVD PROGRESSION THAT AIM TO IDENTIFY ITS CONTRIBUTIONS TO VCID AND GUIDE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES TARGETING MODIFIABLE VASCULAR PROCESSES IN MIXED DEMENTIAS.

description: IMPROVING THE MENTAL HEALTH OF HOME HOSPICE CAREGIVERS THROUGH A SINGLE SESSION INTERVENTION - PROJECT SUMMARY  APPROXIMATELY 2.3 MILLION FAMILY CAREGIVERS (CGS) OF PATIENTS AT THE END OF LIFE (EOL) EXPERIENCE SIGNIFICANT MENTAL HEALTH SYMPTOMS. DESPITE SUPPORTIVE SERVICES FROM HOSPICE, 33% OF HOSPICE CGS EXPERIENCE MODERATE-TO-SEVERE ANXIETY, AND 23% OF HOSPICE CGS EXPERIENCE MODERATE-TO-SEVERE DEPRESSION. THIS CONTRASTS WITH A 6% PREVALENCE RATE NATIONALLY FOR ANXIETY OR DEPRESSION IN THE GENERAL POPULATION. FAMILY CGS OF PATIENTS RECEIVING HOME HOSPICE CARE (HOSPICE CGS) PLAY A CRUCIAL ROLE IN DAILY CAREGIVING DUTIES, PROVIDING ON AVERAGE 12.6 HOURS OF CAREGIVING PER DAY. HOWEVER, THIS RESPONSIBILITY IS ALSO ASSOCIATED WITH POORER MENTAL HEALTH OUTCOMES FOR THE CGS. THEREFORE, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED TO TEST FEASIBLE AND ACCEPTABLE METHODS TO PROVIDE MENTAL HEALTH CARE TO CGS OF HOME HOSPICE PATIENTS TO IMPROVE THEIR HEALTH AND WELL-BEING, WHILE ALSO ENABLING THEM TO BETTER SUPPORT THE INDIVIDUALS THEY CARE FOR.  THE OVERALL OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO ADAPT AND TEST THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF A SINGLE SESSION INTERVENTION (SSI) AIMED AT IMPROVING THE MENTAL HEALTH OF HOME HOSPICE CGS IN A PILOT RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIAL (RCT) WITH A 1:1 (SSI VS. USUAL CARE) ALLOCATION. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS OF OUR PROPOSAL IS THAT IMPLEMENTING A SSI WILL BE FEASIBLE AND ACCEPTABLE IN HOME HOSPICE CGS AND WILL SHOW PRELIMINARY EFFICACY IN IMPROVING CG MENTAL HEALTH OUTCOMES. FOR AIM 1, WE WILL ADAPT AN SSI FOR HOSPICE CGS USING FEEDBACK FROM HOSPICE/MENTAL HEALTH PROVIDERS AND SSI EXPERTS. WE WILL EMPLOY A MODIFIED DELPHI APPROACH TO GATHER FEEDBACK TO REFINE OUR SSI INTERVENTION UNTIL EXPERT APPROVAL IS ACHIEVED. ADJUDICATION WILL RESULT IN AN SSI PROTOCOL AND MANUAL, WITH COMPONENTS OF MINDFULNESS AND SOLUTION-FOCUSED THERAPY, WHICH WILL BE PILOT TESTED IN AIM 2. FOR AIM 2, WE WILL DETERMINE THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF IMPLEMENTING AN SSI FOR HOME HOSPICE CGS. HOME HOSPICE CGS (N = 60) WILL BE RANDOMIZED TO SSI OR USUAL CARE. FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY MEASURES WILL BE BASED ON PROCTOR'S TAXONOMY OF IMPLEMENTATION OUTCOMES. PRELIMINARY EFFECTS ON ANXIETY, DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS, AND CG STRESS WILL BE EXPLORED.  OUR PROPOSAL IS EXPECTED TO HAVE A SIGNIFICANT AND POSITIVE IMPACT BY ESTABLISHING THE FEASIBILITY AND ACCEPTABILITY OF AN SSI TO IMPROVE THE MENTAL HEALTH OF HOME HOSPICE CGS WHO ARE OFTEN OVERBURDENED AND OVERWHELMED. THE DEVELOPMENT OF CG-FOCUSED INTERVENTIONS IN HOME HOSPICE IS CRITICAL IN SUPPORTING FAMILY CGS AND IS A CENTRAL TENET OF HIGH-QUALITY PALLIATIVE AND HOSPICE CARE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A HYDRO-METEOROLOGICAL MALARIA MODEL FOR ADAPTIVE AND TAILORED VECTOR CONTROL STRATEGIES IN AFRICA - PROJECT SUMMARY  A HYDRO-METEOROLOGICAL MALARIA MODEL FOR ADAPTIVE AND TAILORED VECTOR CONTROL STRATEGIES IN AFRICA SIGNIFICANT PROGRESS IN GLOBAL MALARIA CONTROL HAS BEEN ACHIEVED OVER THE PAST TWO DECADES, PRIMARILY DUE TO THE WIDESPREAD SCALE-UP OF LONG-LASTING INSECTICIDE-TREATED NETS AND INDOOR RESIDUAL SPRAYING. HOWEVER, THE EMERGENCE OF INSECTICIDE RESISTANCE AND SHIFTS IN VECTOR BITING AND RESTING BEHAVIORS HAVE SUBSTANTIALLY REDUCED THE EFFECTIVENESS OF THESE CORE INTERVENTION TOOLS. ADDITIONALLY, MALARIA RISK VARIES ACROSS REGIONS DUE TO DIFFERENCES IN CLIMATE, MOSQUITO BIOLOGY, HUMAN BEHAVIOR, LAND USE, AND THE EFFECTIVENESS OF MALARIA CONTROL EFFORTS. AS MALARIA RISK FLUCTUATES DUE TO ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECOLOGICAL DYNAMICS, PREVIOUSLY EFFECTIVE CONTROL METHODS MAY BECOME LESS RELIABLE. EFFECTIVE MALARIA CONTROL REQUIRES APPROACHES THAT ADAPT TO VARIABLE ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS AND VECTOR ECOLOGY. ACCURATE MALARIA RISK PREDICTION IS CRITICAL FOR INFORMING THESE APPROACHES. HOWEVER, CURRENT METHODS FOR PREDICTING MALARIA RISK FACE SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGES. STATISTICAL MODELS THAT RELY ON CORRELATIONS BETWEEN CLIMATE VARIABLES AND MALARIA INCIDENCE OFTEN PERFORM POORLY IN ATYPICAL SCENARIOS SUCH AS DROUGHTS OR FLOODS. IN CONTRAST, MECHANISTIC MODELS TYPICALLY OPERATE AT COARSE SPATIAL SCALES AND DO NOT ADEQUATELY ACCOUNT FOR CRITICAL SURFACE HYDROLOGY PROCESSES, LIMITING THEIR ABILITY TO CAPTURE THE SPATIAL AND TEMPORAL DYNAMICS OF MALARIA RISK. THESE SHORTCOMINGS HINDER THE DEVELOPMENT OF ADAPTABLE MALARIA CONTROL SOLUTIONS. THE CENTRAL OBJECTIVE OF THIS APPLICATION IS TO DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A HYDRO-METEOROLOGICAL MALARIA MODEL TO IMPROVE FORECASTS OF MALARIA RISK, AND TO USE THE MODEL TO DESIGN VECTOR CONTROL STRATEGIES SUITABLE FOR VARYING ENVIRONMENTAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL CONDITIONS. TO ACHIEVE THIS OBJECTIVE, WE HAVE DESIGNED TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) DEVELOP AND VALIDATE A HYDRO-METEOROLOGICAL MALARIA MODEL THAT INTEGRATES WEATHER FORECASTING, HYDROLOGY, VECTOR AND MALARIA EPIDEMIOLOGICAL MODEL TO ENHANCE MALARIA RISK PREDICTION, AND 2) ANALYZE SHIFTS IN MALARIA RISK RESULTING FROM ENVIRONMENTAL MODIFICATIONS, WEATHER VARIABILITY, AND CHANGES IN VECTOR ECOLOGY, AND IDENTIFY ADAPTIVE VECTOR CONTROL STRATEGIES TAILORED TO LOCAL TRANSMISSION DYNAMICS. KEY OUTCOMES OF THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE THE DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A NOVEL TOOL THAT USES WEATHER, HYDROLOGICAL ANALYSIS, AND DISEASE DATA TO PREDICT MALARIA RISK OVER SPACE AND TIME, AND GUIDE EFFECTIVE MOSQUITO CONTROL STRATEGIES BASED ON PREVAILING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS. ALTHOUGH THE TOOL IS VALIDATED USING ENVIRONMENTAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL DATA FROM WESTERN KENYA, THE RESULTING MODEL IS EXPECTED TO BE TRANSFERABLE ACROSS DIVERSE ECOLOGICAL AND EPIDEMIOLOGICAL SETTINGS.

description: INTERFERON-Γ IN COMBINATION WITH DONOR LEUKOCYTE INFUSION TO TREAT RELAPSED ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA AND MYELODYSPLASTIC SYNDROMES AFTER HAPLOIDENTICAL DONOR STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT ALLOGENEIC STEM CELL TRANSPLANTATION (ALLOSCT) OFFERS A POTENTIAL CURE FOR ACUTE MYELOID LEUKEMIA (AML) AND MYELODYSPLASTIC SYNDROME (MDS); HOWEVER, DISEASE RELAPSE—REFLECTING FAILURE OF THE GRAFT-VERSUS-LEUKEMIA (GVL) EFFECT—REMAINS THE LEADING CAUSE OF DEATH AFTER BOTH HLA-MATCHED AND HAPLOIDENTICAL TRANSPLANTATION (HAPLO-SCT). DONOR-DERIVED ALLOREACTIVE T CELLS MEDIATE GVL BY RECOGNIZING AND ELIMINATING RECIPIENT LEUKEMIA CELLS, YET ONLY 10–20% OF PATIENTS WHO RELAPSE AFTER ALLOSCT ACHIEVE DURABLE SURVIVAL. NEW STRATEGIES TO ENHANCE GVL WITHOUT INCREASING GRAFT-VERSUS-HOST DISEASE (GVHD) ARE URGENTLY NEEDED. PRECLINICAL STUDIES BY DR. SHLOMCHIK (CO-I) DEMONSTRATED THAT IFN-Γ RECEPTOR SIGNALING IS ESSENTIAL FOR EFFECTIVE GVL, AS LEUKEMIAS LACKING THIS PATHWAY ARE RESISTANT TO IMMUNE ELIMINATION. CONSISTENT WITH THIS, AML SAMPLES OBTAINED AT POST-TRANSPLANT RELAPSE SHOW REDUCED HLA EXPRESSION, WHICH CAN BE RESTORED BY IFN-Γ EXPOSURE. BUILDING ON THESE FINDINGS, DR. ITO (PI) CONDUCTED A PHASE I CLINICAL TRIAL COMBINING IFN-Γ WITH DONOR LYMPHOCYTE INFUSION (DLI) IN RELAPSED AML/MDS AFTER HLA-MATCHED ALLOSCT (NCT04628338; JCI INSIGHT, 2025), ACHIEVING DURABLE COMPLETE REMISSIONS (CR) IN FOUR OF SIX TREATED PATIENTS. A MULTICENTER PHASE II TRIAL IN HLA-MATCHED RECIPIENTS IS ONGOING (NCT06529731). GIVEN THE HIGHER GVHD RISK ASSOCIATED WITH HAPLOIDENTICAL DLI, THE SAFETY OF IFN-Γ IN THIS SETTING REQUIRES DEDICATED EVALUATION. MOREOVER, RELAPSE FOLLOWING HAPLO-SCT FREQUENTLY RESULTS FROM LOSS OF THE MISMATCHED HLA LOCUS THROUGH LOSS OF HETEROZYGOSITY (HLA-LOH), CONFERRING IMMUNE ESCAPE. WE THEREFORE PROPOSE A SUB- COHORT STUDY WITHIN NCT06529731 TO TEST IFN-Γ/DLI IN PATIENTS WITH RELAPSED AML/MDS AFTER HAPLO-SCT WHO HAVE MEASURABLE BONE MARROW DISEASE AND NO EVIDENCE OF HLA-LOH. PARTICIPANTS WILL RECEIVE IFN-Γ (100 ΜG SUBCUTANEOUSLY THREE TIMES WEEKLY FOR FOUR WEEKS). IF WELL TOLERATED, UP TO TWO DLIS WILL BE ADMINISTERED CONCURRENTLY WITH IFN-Γ OVER 12 WEEKS. THE PRIMARY ENDPOINT IS SAFETY, DEFINED BY THE INCIDENCE OF STEROID- AND RUXOLITINIB-REFRACTORY GVHD. SECONDARY ENDPOINTS INCLUDE PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OUTCOMES, WHILE COLLECTING SEQUENTIAL BIOSPECIMENS FOR FUTURE EXPLORATORY CORRELATIVE STUDIES CHARACTERIZING PHENOTYPIC, TRANSCRIPTIONAL, AND FUNCTIONAL CHANGES IN LEUKEMIA CELLS AND IMMUNE CELLS. USING A BAYESIAN OPTIMAL INTERVAL (BOIN) DESIGN, 6–12 PATIENTS WILL BE ENROLLED WITH PREDEFINED GVHD-BASED STOPPING RULES. IF THIS STUDY DEMONSTRATES SAFETY WITH EARLY EFFICACY SIGNALS, IT WILL PROVIDE THE FOUNDATION FOR A SUBSEQUENT PHASE II TRIAL FOCUSED ON EFFICACY, ADDRESSING A CRITICAL UNMET NEED IN POST-HAPLO-SCT RELAPSE OF AML/MDS.

description: THE EFFECT OF ELECTRONIC CIGARETTE VAPOR ON FORMATION OF INTRACELLULAR BACTERIAL COMMUNITIES AND RECURRENCE OF OTITIS MEDIA - PROJECT ABSTRACT INFECTIONS CAUSED BY NONTYPEABLE HAEMOPHILUS INFLUENZAE (NTHI) STRAINS REPRESENT A MAJOR CAUSE OF OTITIS MEDIA (OM), EXACERBATIONS OF CHRONIC OBSTRUCTIVE PULMONARY DISEASE (COPD), AND BACTERIAL SINUSITIS. FURTHERMORE, NTHI CAUSES CHRONIC, TREATMENT-REFRACTORY DISEASES, IN PART BY FORMING INTRACELLULAR BACTERIAL COMMUNITIES (IBCS) WITHIN EPITHELIAL CELLS THAT PROVIDE A REFUGE FROM BOTH THE HOST IMMUNE SYSTEM, AND FROM CLINICAL INTERVENTIONS. THE BACTERIAL AND HOST ELEMENTS THAT IMPACT NTHI PERSISTENCE AND RECURRENCE OF OM ARE NOT COMPLETELY UNDERSTOOD. THEREFORE, THE DELINEATION OF HOST-PATHOGEN INTERACTIONS AND ENVIRONMENTAL EXPOSURES THAT LEAD TO OM-DERIVED SEQUELAE WILL INFORM NOVEL THERAPEUTIC APPROACHES. CIGARETTES AND AIR POLLUTION ARE BOTH SOURCES OF TOXIC GASES AND FINE PARTICULATE MATTER THAT ARE LINKED WITH SUSCEPTIBILITY TO OM IN CHILDREN. ELECTRONIC CIGARETTE (E-CIG) UTILIZATION HAS DRAMATICALLY INCREASED IN THE PAST SEVERAL YEARS BOTH AS A TOOL FOR CESSATION OF TRADITIONAL SMOKING, BUT MOSTLY IN NEW ADOLESCENT NICOTINE USERS. THE EFFECT OF E-CIG AEROSOL AND NICOTINE ON SUSCEPTIBILITY OF CHILDREN TO OM AS WELL AS EXACERBATION AND RECURRENCE OF NTHI-MEDIATED DISEASE THUS REPRESENTS A NEW HEALTH PROBLEM THAT IS UNDERSTUDIED. FURTHER, THE CONTRIBUTION OF AEROSOL AND NICOTINE EXPOSURE WITH INCREASED INFLAMMATION, INFECTION SUSCEPTIBILITY AND FIBROSIS ASSOCIATED WITH OM ARE UNCLEAR. OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT PASSIVE EXPOSURE TO E-CIG AEROSOL AND NICOTINE ENHANCES INVASION, IBC FORMATION, PERSISTENCE, AND RECURRENCE OF NTHI. EXPOSURE TO AEROSOLS IS A KNOWN RISK FACTOR FOR OM, BUT THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS INVOLVED HAVE NOT BEEN INVESTIGATED. AIM 1: DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF PRODUCTS OF E-CIG COMBUSTION AND NICOTINE ON MIDDLE EAR EPITHELIAL CELL FUNCTION AND IBC FORMATION. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT E-CIG AEROSOL AND NICOTINE MODULATE EPITHELIAL RESPONSES THAT PROMOTE NTHI INVASION AND IBC FORMATION IN VITRO. AIM 2: DETERMINE THE EFFECT OF THE PRODUCTS OF E-CIG COMBUSTION AND NICOTINE ON OM DISEASE SEVERITY, PERSISTENCE AND AS A STIMULUS OF RECURRENT EPISODES OF OM. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT E-CIG AEROSOL WILL PROMOTE SUPPURATIVE INFLAMMATION AND IBC FORMATION DURING EXPERIMENTAL OM, THAT WILL BE FURTHER EXACERBATED IN THE PRESENCE OF NICOTINE. FURTHERMORE, WE HAVE ESTABLISHED A PRECLINICAL MODEL WHERE IBCS REMAIN FOR WEEKS IN THE MIDDLE EAR FOLLOWING RESOLUTION OF DISEASE. WE WILL DETERMINE WHETHER SUBSEQUENT EXPOSURE TO E-CIG AEROSOL WILL PROMOTE EGRESS OF NTHI FROM THESE INTRACELLULAR RESERVOIRS TO ESTABLISH A RECURRENT EPISODE OF OM. THE OUTCOMES OF OUR COMPREHENSIVE APPROACH WILL SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW ENVIRONMENTAL PARTICLES AND NICOTINE INFLUENCE NTHI PATHOGENIC LIFESTYLES THAT IMPACT PERSISTENCE AND RECURRENCE AND REVEAL NOVEL APPROACHES FOR THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRACE METALS IN ENVIRONMENTAL MEDIA AND THEIR ASSOCIATION WITH LIVER DISEASE - PROJECT ABSTRACT CHRONIC LIVER DISEASE (CLD) IS A MASSIVE THREAT TO PUBLIC HEALTH. CLD IS A COMPLEX DISEASE SPECTRUM THAT INCLUDES HEPATIC STEATOSIS AND FIBROSIS, THE END STAGE OF WHICH IS CIRRHOSIS. PROGRESSION FROM CIRRHOSIS TO HEPATOCELLULAR CARCINOMA (HCC) IS WELL ESTABLISHED AND HCC INCIDENCE HAS RISEN DRAMATICALLY IN THE LAST THREE DECADES. WE SEE ESPECIALLY STEEP INCREASES IN THE SOUTHEASTERN UNITED STATES. A POTENT YET UNDERSTUDIED RISK FACTOR FOR THESE CONDITIONS IS CHRONIC EXPOSURE TO ENVIRONMENTAL CONTAMINANTS, AS MULTIPLE CLASSES OF CHEMICALS, INCLUDING TOXIC METALS, ARE WIDESPREAD IN THE US POPULATION, WITH HIGH BURDENS IN SOUTHERN STATES AND RURAL RESIDENTS. EXPOSURE TO EVEN TRACE AMOUNTS OF TOXIC METALS, ESPECIALLY OVER LONG PERIODS OF TIME, HAS BEEN LINKED TO A WIDE RANGE OF CHRONIC DISEASES. TOXIC METALS CAN BE FOUND IN SOILS, HOUSEHOLD DUST, AND DRINKING WATER, POSING SIGNIFICANT RISKS TO THE GENERAL POPULATION. THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO CONNECT NON-OCCUPATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL SOURCES OF METAL EXPOSURE TO CLINICALLY ADJUDICATED LIVER DISEASE OUTCOMES. HERE, WE WILL LEVERAGE AVAILABLE BIOLOGICAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL SPECIMENS FROM AN ACTIVE COHORT (THE SOUTHERN LIVER HEALTH STUDY; STRIVE) FROM THE SOUTHEASTERN U.S. TO CONDUCT BOTH A CROSS-SECTIONAL (AIM 1; 800 TOTAL PARTICIPANTS) AND LONGITUDINAL (AIM 2; 300 PARTICIPANTS) STUDIES TO TEST THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS THAT METAL CONTAMINATION INCREASES THE RISK OF CIRRHOSIS AND PROGRESSION FROM CIRRHOSIS TO HCC. SIMULTANEOUSLY, OUR WORK TESTS WHETHER MEASURING EXPOSURES DIRECTLY IN ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLES (DRINKING WATER, HOUSE DUST, AND SOIL) PREDICTS LIVER DISEASE RISK. EVEN BEYOND LIVER DISEASE, COLLECTING BIOLOGICAL SAMPLES, PARTICULARLY WHOLE BLOOD, IS CITED AS ONE OF THE MOST RATE- AND COST-LIMITING STEPS; DIRECTLY CONTRIBUTING TO SAMPLING GAPS IN LARGE COHORT STUDIES THAT MISREPRESENTS THE HETEROGENEITY OF THE GENERAL U.S. POPULATION. YET, RARELY DO STUDIES CONNECT METAL CONTAMINATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLES WITH BOTH THE BODY BURDEN AND ACTUAL DISEASE OUTCOMES. EVEN FEWER STUDIES ASSOCIATE METALS MEASURED IN ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLES WITH ADJUDICATED DISEASE PROGRESSION OVER TIME. WE WILL FIRST EXAMINE HOW METAL CONTAMINANTS MEASURED IN THE HOME ENVIRONMENT RELATE TO HOW THESE METALS ACCUMULATE IN THE BODY (I.E., THE “BODY BURDEN”) FOR 400 CIRRHOSIS PATIENTS AND 400 OTHERWISE HEALTHY INDIVIDUALS TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT EXPOSURE TO A MIXTURE OF METALS IN THE HOME ENVIRONMENT IS CROSS-SECTIONALLY ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED RISK OF LIVER FIBROSIS/CIRRHOSIS (AIM 1). NEXT, WE WILL NEST A CASE-CONTROL STUDY OF 100 PARTICIPANTS THAT HAVE PROGRESSED TO HCC AND 200 PARTICIPANTS THAT HAVE NOT PROGRESSED BEYOND CIRRHOSIS WITHIN A SIMILAR TIME FRAME TO TEST THE THAT PERSISTENT OR INCREASING CONCENTRATIONS OF METAL CONTAMINANTS IN ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLES ARE LONGITUDINALLY ASSOCIATED WITH AN INCREASED RISK OF PROGRESSION FROM CIRRHOSIS TO HCC. BY USING MULTIPLE MATRICES, OUR WORK WILL PROVIDE MUCH NEEDED INSIGHTS INTO ROUTES OF EXPOSURE TO TOXIC METAL MIXTURES EXPERIENCED BY THE GENERAL POPULATION. OUR APPROACH USING ENVIRONMENTAL SAMPLING ALSO HAS IMMENSE POTENTIAL TO OFFER LESS INVASIVE, COST-EFFICIENT AND SCALABLE SAMPLING STRATEGIES, WITH THE GOAL TO HELP REDUCE THE BURDEN OF LIVER DISEASES IN THE OVERALL POPULATION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TREATMENT OF CEP290-ASSOCIATED RETINAL DEGENERATION - ABSTRACT MUTATIONS IN THE CEP290 GENE ARE A LEADING CAUSE OF LEBER CONGENITAL AMAUROSIS (LCA), A HEREDITARY RETINAL DYSTROPHY THAT RESULTS IN SEVERE VISION LOSS DURING INFANCY OR EARLY CHILDHOOD. WHILE GENE AUGMENTATION THERAPY USING ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUS (AAV) VECTORS HAS SHOWN PROMISE IN TREATING INHERITED RETINAL DEGENERATIONS, CEP290-LCA PRESENTS SIGNIFICANT CHALLENGES DUE TO THE GENE’S LARGE SIZE AND THE DIVERSE MUTATIONS DISTRIBUTED THROUGHOUT THE GENE. EXISTING GENE THERAPY APPROACHES FOR CEP290-LCA HAVE TARGETED SPECIFIC MUTATIONS AND/OR ACHIEVED LIMITED SUCCESS IN RESTORING CEP290 GENE FUNCTION. THE PROPOSED STUDY AIMS TO OVERCOME THESE LIMITATIONS AND DEVELOP MUTATION-INDEPENDENT, GENERIC CEP290 GENE THERAPY VECTORS. WE HAVE PIONEERED AN INNOVATIVE STRATEGY THAT EMPLOYS UP TO FOUR AAV VECTORS IN CONJUNCTION WITH A UNIDIRECTIONAL DNA RECOMBINATION SYSTEM TO DELIVER AND RECONSTITUTE LARGE GENES. USING THIS APPROACH, WE HAVE SUCCESSFULLY ENGINEERED TRIPARTITE AAV-CEP290 VECTORS THAT PRODUCE FULL-LENGTH CEP290 PROTEINS EFFICIENTLY IN VITRO AND IN MOUSE RETINAS. IN THE PROPOSED STUDY, WE WILL EVALUATE AND COMPARE THE THERAPEUTIC EFFICACY OF TWO SETS OF AAV-CEP290 VECTORS IN TWO CEP290-LCA MOUSE MODELS. THE EFFICACY OF THESE GENE THERAPY VECTORS WILL ALSO BE COMPARED WITH EXISTING SPLIT-INTEIN-BASED CEP290 VECTORS. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS STUDY WILL NOT ONLY PAVE THE WAY FOR EFFECTIVE AND MUTATION-INDEPENDENT GENE THERAPIES FOR CEP290-LCA BUT ALSO PUSH THE BOUNDARIES OF WHAT IS POSSIBLE IN THE FIELD OF GENE THERAPY BY ENABLING THE DELIVERY OF LARGE GENES THAT HAVE PREVIOUSLY BEEN CHALLENGING TO TARGET.

description: UNDERSTANDING THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN EXPANDING ACCESS TO DIABETIC RETINOPATHY SCREENING - 1 PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT: DIABETIC RETINOPATHY (DR) IS THE LEADING CAUSE OF BLINDNESS AMONG U.S. ADULTS.  2 ROUGHLY 20% OF PATIENTS WITH DR SUFFER FROM VISION-THREATENING COMPLICATIONS. ESTIMATES SUGGEST THAT THE VAST  3 MAJORITY OF BLINDNESS CAUSED BY DR COULD BE PREVENTED THROUGH EARLY DETECTION AND TREATMENT. TO THAT END,  4 CLINICAL GUIDELINES RECOMMEND ANNUAL DR SCREENING FOR MOST DIABETIC PATIENTS, BUT ONLY 50–70% OF PATIENTS  5 WITH DIABETES RECEIVE THIS CARE. ONE MAJOR BARRIER TO RECOMMENDED DR SCREENING IS LIMITED ACCESS TO EYE CARE 6 PROFESSIONALS.  7 RECENT INNOVATIONS IN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) MAY EXPAND ACCESS TO DR SCREENING. FDA-APPROVED  8 AUTONOMOUS AI DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS DETECT DR WITHOUT REQUIRING THE INVOLVEMENT OF A PHYSICIAN. WE PROPOSE THE  9 FIRST STUDY OF HOW AI EXPANDS ACCESS TO DR SCREENING AND RECOMMENDED TREATMENT. TO DO SO, WE WILL USE 10 100% OF MEDICARE CLAIMS DATA TO IDENTIFY ADOPTION OF AUTONOMOUS AI DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS FOR DR. WE WILL ALSO 11 IMPLEMENT A QUASI-EXPERIMENTAL RESEARCH DESIGN, EXPLOITING VARIATION IN THE TIMING OF AI ADOPTION. MEDICARE 12 CLAIMS ARE AN IDEAL SETTING FOR THIS ANALYSIS, SINCE MEDICARE BEGAN REIMBURSING CLINICIANS FOR THIS CLINICAL 13 APPLICATION OF AI IN 2021. 14 AIM 1 WILL QUANTIFY THE ADOPTION OF AUTONOMOUS AI DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS FOR DR. WE WILL COMPARE THE 15 CHARACTERISTICS OF AI-ADOPTERS AND NON-ADOPTERS, TO UNDERSTAND WHETHER AI ADOPTION IS CORRELATED WITH MARKERS 16 OF CLINICAL NEED, SUCH AS EYE CARE PROFESSIONAL SHORTAGES AND LOW RATES OF DR SCREENING. 17 AIM 2 WILL TEST FOR CHANGES IN RATES OF DR SCREENING AND DIAGNOSIS, FOLLOWING AI ADOPTION. A MEDICAL 18 PRACTICE THAT ADOPTS AN AUTONOMOUS AI DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEM IS NO LONGER CONSTRAINED BY PHYSICIAN AVAILABILITY IN 19 THEIR PROVISION OF DR SCREENING SERVICES. WE THEREFORE HYPOTHESIZE AN INCREASE IN THE NUMBER AND SHARE OF 20 DIABETIC PATIENTS RECEIVING ANNUAL DR SCREENING, FOLLOWING ADOPTION OF AI. WE WILL TEST FOR THIS USING A 21 DIFFERENCE-IN-DIFFERENCES RESEARCH DESIGN TO COMPARE OUTCOMES BEFORE AND AFTER ADOPTION, IN AI-ADOPTERS AND 22 NON-ADOPTERS. 23 AIM 3 WILL TEST FOR CHANGES IN RECOMMENDED TREATMENT FOR PATIENTS WITH DR, FOLLOWING AI ADOPTION. WE 24 HYPOTHESIZE THAT RATES OF RECOMMENDED TREATMENT (E.G., FOLLOW-UP VISITS TO AN EYE CARE PROFESSIONAL) FOR DR WILL 25 REMAIN THE SAME OR SLIGHTLY DECREASE FOLLOWING ADOPTION OF AUTONOMOUS AI DIAGNOSTIC SYSTEMS. THIS IS LARGELY 26 DUE TO THE FACT THAT PATIENTS DIAGNOSED BY AI WITH DR WILL, BY DEFINITION, NOT YET HAVE A RELATIONSHIP WITH AN EYE 27 CARE PROFESSIONAL, MAKING IT POTENTIALLY MORE DIFFICULT TO OBTAIN RECOMMENDED TREATMENT. 28 THIS STUDY RESPONDS DIRECTLY TO THE NATIONAL EYE INSTITUTE’S CALL (PAR-25-357) FOR VISION-RELATED SECONDARY 29 DATA ANALYSIS. OUR FINDINGS WILL GUIDE CLINICAL PRACTICE, MEDICARE POLICY, AND AI ADOPTION DECISIONS – WITH THE 30 ULTIMATE GOAL OF REDUCING PREVENTABLE BLINDNESS AND IMPROVING POPULATION EYE HEALTH.

description: METABOLIC PERTURBATIONS IN THE DEVELOPING ALBINO RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM - PROJECT SUMMARY  RETINAL GANGLION CELLS (RGCS) FROM EACH EYE EXTEND THEIR AXONS IPSI- AND CONTRALATERALLY TO THE BRAIN TO ESTABLISH THE CIRCUIT FOR BINOCULAR VISION. THE INAPPROPRIATE SIDEDNESS OF RGC PROJECTIONS IS DEBILITATING IN GENETIC DISORDERS SUCH AS ALBINISM, IN WHICH HYPOPIGMENTATION OF THE RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM (RPE) IS LINKED TO OPTIC NERVE MISROUTING AND ALTERED STEREO VISION. WE PREVIOUSLY IDENTIFIED TRANSCRIPTIONAL REGULATORS OF THE SPECIFICATION AND DIFFERENTIATION OF IPSI AND CONTRA RGCS, DEMONSTRATED THAT THE VENTRAL CILIARY MARGIN ZONE (CMZ) IS A SOURCE OF IPSI RGCS, AND POINTED TO THE CELL CYCLE REGULATOR CYCLIN D2 IN THE VENTRAL CMZ AS BEING CRUCIAL FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF IPSI RGC CELL FATE. IN THE ALBINO RETINA, THESE PROCESSES AND THE CELLULAR INTEGRITY OF THE RPE IN THE ABSENCE OF MELANIN ARE DISRUPTED, MAKING THE ALBINO AN EXCELLENT COMPARATIVE MODEL FOR THE PROPOSED STUDIES: THE CMZ DISPLAYS COMPROMISED NEUROGENIC PROPERTIES INCLUDING AN EXTENDED G1 PERIOD DURING THE CELL CYCLE OF RETINAL PROGENITORS, AND DIMINISHED EXPRESSION OF CYCLIN D2, TOGETHER CAUSING REDUCED OUTPUT OF IPSI RGCS.  THE LINK BETWEEN THE PRESENCE OF MELANIN IN THE RPE IN PIGMENTED ORGANISMS AND PROPER DEVELOPMENT OF RGC PROJECTION REMAINS UNANSWERED. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT FACTORS IN THE RPE DIRECT THE CMZ AND NEURAL RETINA TOWARD THE PROPER BALANCE OF IPSI/CONTRA RGC FATES. SIGNALS FROM THE RPE THAT MAY NORMALLY REGULATE NEUROGENESIS AND THAT ARE MISSING OR DOWNREGULATED FROM THE ALBINO RPE OR ABERRANT SIGNALS THAT ARE UPREGULATED IN THE ALBINO RPE MAY CAUSE THE ALTERATIONS OF NEUROGENESIS AND, THUS, AN IMBALANCE IN THE IPSI VS CONTRA RGC POPULATIONS SEEN IN THE ALBINO. HERE WE WILL CHRONICLE THE WAYS IN WHICH THE DEVELOPING (EMBRYONIC) ALBINO RPE IS PERTURBED. WE WILL PURSUE OUR TRANSCRIPTOMICS DATA INDICATING THAT MITOCHONDRIA ARE UNDER STRESS, AND CHRONICLE THESE PERTURBATIONS BY HIGH-RESOLUTION AND ELECTRON MICROSCOPY. WE WILL ALSO INTERROGATE METABOLIC AND CALCIUM DYNAMICS THAT ARE DYSREGULATED IN ALBINO V PIGMENTED RPE. THIS DISCOVERY-BASED EFFORT WILL SET THE STAGE FOR TREATING RPE WITH FACTORS THAT WILL ALLAY SUCH DYSFUNCTION IN VIVO AND IN VITRO, THAT COULD MODIFY RGC NEUROGENESIS TO ESTABLISH PROPER BINOCULAR CIRCUITRY. IMPACT: OUR STUDIES, FOR WHICH THE VISUAL SYSTEM IS SUPREMELY SUITED, WILL ILLUMINATE HOW NEURONAL DIFFERENTIATION PROGRAMS GOVERN AXON PROJECTION AND CONNECTIVITY IN THE NERVOUS SYSTEM. GENETIC DISORDERS SUCH AS ALBINISM INVOLVE INAPPROPRIATE SIDEDNESS OF RGC PROJECTIONS AND SERVE AS A MODEL FOR THESE STUDIES. AS BOTH ALBINISM AND DISORDERS IN THE MATURE EYE SUCH AS AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION (AMD) PRESENT RPE CELLULAR PATHOLOGY AND DISABLE INTERACTIONS BETWEEN RPE CELLS AND THE ADJACENT LAYER OF NEURAL RETINAL CELLS, THE PROPOSED WORK MAY SHED LIGHT ON THIS AND OTHER RETINAL DISEASES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: MICRORNA MECHANISM OF ANGELMAN SYNDROME - PROJECT SUMMARY ANGELMAN SYNDROME (AS) IS A SEVERE NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY, MOTOR DYSFUNCTION, SLEEP DISTURBANCES, EEG ABNORMALITIES, AND EPILEPSY. DESPITE ITS SIGNIFICANT IMPACT, THERE IS CURRENTLY NO EFFECTIVE THERAPY FOR AS. EXISTING TREATMENTS PRIMARILY INVOLVE COMBINATIONS OF MEDICINES TO ALLEVIATE SOME OF THE MOST DEBILITATING SYMPTOMS. THERE REMAINS AN URGENT CLINICAL NEED TO IDENTIFY NOVEL MOLECULAR TARGETS THAT CAN CORRECT THE CORE PATHOLOGIES OF AS. MICRORNAS (MIRNAS) ARE ~22 NUCLEOTIDE-LONG NONCODING RNAS THAT NEGATIVELY REGULATE GENE EXPRESSION BY BINDING TO COMPLEMENTARY SITES IN THE 3’ UNTRANSLATED REGION OF TARGET MESSENGER RNAS. MIRNAS PLAY A SIGNIFICANT ROLE IN REGULATING GENE EXPRESSION AND HAVE BEEN IMPLICATED IN CONTROLLING FUNDAMENTAL NEURAL FUNCTIONS, INCLUDING NEUROGENESIS, NEURONAL MATURATION, SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY, AND EXCITATORY/INHIBITORY (E/I) BALANCE. DYSREGULATED MIRNA EXPRESSION IS INCREASINGLY IMPLICATED IN THE PATHOGENESIS OF VARIOUS NEUROLOGICAL AND NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS. WE RECENTLY CONDUCTED AN UNBIASED GENOME-WIDE MIRNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS USING HIPPOCAMPAL TISSUE COLLECTED FROM ADULT AS MODEL MICE AND THEIR WILD-TYPE (WT) LITTERMATE CONTROLS. WE IDENTIFIED A NOVEL CLUSTER OF MIRNAS, MIR-183/96/182, SIGNIFICANTLY DOWNREGULATED IN AS MICE COMPARED TO WT CONTROLS. IMPORTANTLY, TREATMENT WITH CANNABIDIOL, KNOWN TO AMELIORATE MULTIPLE PATHOLOGIES IN AS ANIMAL MODELS AND INDIVIDUALS WITH AS, REVERSED THE DOWNREGULATION OF MIR-183 AND MIR-96, AMONG OTHERS, IN AS MODEL MICE. THE PIVOTAL ROLE OF MIR- 183/96/182 IN REGULATING NEURITE OUTGROWTH, MEMORY FORMATION, AND CIRCADIAN RHYTHMS SUGGESTS ITS POTENTIAL INVOLVEMENT IN AS PATHOGENESIS. OUR STUDY AIMS TO TREAT CORE AS PATHOLOGIES BY TARGETING MIR-183/96/182. WE WILL TEST OUR CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS THAT MIR-183/96/182 AUGMENTATION CAN ALLEVIATE AS-ASSOCIATED PATHOLOGIES AND FUNCTIONAL ALTERATIONS IN BOTH MOUSE MODELS AND HUMAN CORTICAL ORGANOIDS (HCOS). IN AIM 1, WE WILL PROFILE THE DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION OF MIR-183/96/182 IN MOUSE BRAINS AND ASSESS THE EFFECTS OF MIR-183/96/182 AUGMENTATION ON BEHAVIORAL IMPAIRMENTS, EEG ABNORMALITIES, AND EPILEPTIC PHENOTYPES IN AS MODEL MICE. WE WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE THE MOLECULAR TARGETS OF MIR-183/96/182 IN REGULATING AS PHENOTYPES. WE WILL FIRST FOCUS ON CACNB4, WHICH MIRDB PREDICTS AS THE TOP BIOLOGICALLY PLAUSIBLE DIRECT TARGET WITH BINDING SITES FOR MIR- 183/96/182. TO FURTHER EVALUATE THE TRANSLATIONAL POTENTIAL OF THIS APPROACH, IN AIM 2, WE WILL VALIDATE THE DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION OF MIR-183/96/182 USING AS PATIENTS' IPSCS-DERIVED HCOS AND TEST THE EFFECTS OF MIR- 183/96/182 AUGMENTATION ON CORTICAL NEURONAL GENERATION AND ALTERED NEURAL PROPERTIES IN UBE3A-DEFICIENT ORGANOIDS. COMPLETING THIS STUDY WILL SHED LIGHT ON MIRNA MECHANISMS OF AS PATHOLOGY AND IDENTIFY MIR- 183/96/182 AUGMENTATION AS A NOVEL THERAPEUTIC APPROACH FOR AS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: NOVEL THEORETICAL MODELS AND METHODS FOR REDUCING SOCIOECONOMIC DISPARITIES IN TOBACCO USE - ALTHOUGH TOBACCO CONTROL INTERVENTIONS HAVE REDUCED OVERALL SMOKING PREVALENCE, TOBACCO USE REMAINS A LEADING CAUSE OF PREVENTABLE DISEASE AND DEATH. THERE IS A DYNAMIC INTERPLAY OF INDIVIDUAL, SOCIAL, AND SOCIETAL FACTORS THAT UNDERLIE DIFFICULTY IN SMOKING CESSATION, PARTICULARLY FOR POPULATIONS WITH LOW INCOME OR LIMITED RESOURCES. ALTHOUGH SMOKING AND SMOKING CESSATION BEHAVIORS ARE LINKED BY COMPLEX FEEDBACK LOOPS (I.E., A SET OF BALANCING AND REINFORCING CAUSAL FEEDBACK MECHANISMS) INTERACTING AT MULTIPLE LEVELS, A MORE COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF THESE COMPLEX FEEDBACK MECHANISMS FROM A HIGHER-LEVEL SYSTEMS VIEW IS CURRENTLY LACKING. TOWARDS REDUCING THE PREVALENCE OF TOBACCO USE, A PROMISING AND INNOVATIVE APPROACH IS TO IDENTIFY STAKEHOLDER-INFORMED TARGETS OF INTERVENTIONS (OR LEVERAGE POINTS) IN MULTILEVEL FEEDBACK MECHANISMS DRIVING THE DYNAMICS OF SMOKING CESSATION. THE GOAL OF THIS R21 APPLICATION IS TO IDENTIFY AND MODEL MULTILEVEL INTERVENTION STRATEGIES THAT CAN BE PRIORITIZED FOR ADDRESSING TOBACCO USE AND TO DEVELOP A NOVEL, MULTILEVEL ADAPTIVE INTERVENTION TRIAL DESIGN THAT CAN IDENTIFY THE OPTIMAL ORDER TO TARGET MULTILEVEL LEVERAGE POINTS. AIM 1 IS TO IDENTIFY KEY LEVERAGE POINTS OF INTERVENTION FOR REDUCING SOCIOECONOMIC DISPARITIES IN SMOKING. WE WILL ACCOMPLISH THIS USING COMMUNITY-BASED SYSTEM DYNAMICS (CBSD) TO DEVELOP AN INITIAL FEEDBACK THEORY OF SMOKING AND HEALTH-RELATED SOCIAL NEEDS DYNAMICS VIA KEY INFORMANT INTERVIEWS AND GROUP MODEL BUILDING. CBSD IS AN APPROACH TO GROUP MODEL BUILDING THAT DIRECTLY INVOLVES COMMUNITIES IN THE PROCESS OF CONCEPTUALIZING, FORMULATING, AND ANALYSIS OF SYSTEM DYNAMICS SIMULATION MODELS. AIM 2 IS TO DEVELOP A NOVEL CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN TO TEST ADAPTIVE, MULTILEVEL INTERVENTIONS. BUILDING ON A FRAMEWORK FOR SEQUENTIAL, MULTIPLE ASSIGNMENT, RANDOMIZED TRIALS (SMARTS), WE WILL DESIGN AND DEVELOP THE METHODOLOGY TO ANALYZE CLINICAL TRIAL DATA THAT CAN BE USED TO IDENTIFY DYNAMIC TREATMENT REGIMENS, OR SEQUENCES OF TREATMENT THAT CHANGE ADAPTIVELY BASED ON RESPONSE, FOR MULTILEVEL INTERVENTIONS. THIS PROJECT SEEKS TO CARRY OUT CONCEPTUAL WORK IN PARALLEL WITH METHODOLOGICAL WORK TO IMPROVE UPON TRIAL DESIGN AND ANALYSIS THAT CAN INFORM ADVANCEMENTS IN CLINICAL AND TRANSLATIONAL SCIENCE TO REDUCE HEALTH DISPARITIES. THE NIMHD HAS CALLED FOR RESEARCH ON MULTILEVEL INTERVENTIONS TO ADDRESS HEALTH DISPARITIES, INCLUDING THROUGH STRENGTHENING THEORETICAL FRAMEWORKS THAT CAN RECOGNIZE THE COMPLEX SET OF FACTORS INVOLVED IN MULTILEVEL CHANGE. BY MODELING THE MULTILEVEL DRIVERS OF A SIGNIFICANT HEALTH DISPARITY ISSUE, IDENTIFYING LEVERAGE POINTS FOR INTERVENTION, AND ADDRESSING A GAP IN CLINICAL TRIAL DESIGN, THE FINDINGS WILL COST-EFFECTIVELY INFORM THE MOST OPTIMAL SET OF MULTILEVEL INTERVENTION TARGETS THAT CAN BE FURTHER EXAMINED AND TESTED IN A FUTURE STUDY.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT OF A CULTURALLY TAILORED SLEEP INTERVENTION USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR FILIPINO IMMIGRANTS - PROJECT ABSTRACT POOR SLEEP IS A PREVALENT PUBLIC HEALTH PROBLEM THAT IS ASSOCIATED WITH INCREASED MORBIDITY AND HEALTHCARE UTILIZATION. EPIDEMIOLOGICAL DATA INDICATE THAT ASIAN AMERICAN ADULTS ARE AT INCREASED RISK OF EXPERIENCING SHORT SLEEP AND POOR SLEEP QUALITY. THIS RISK IS PARTICULARLY SUBSTANTIAL AMONG FILIPINO AMERICANS, ONE OF THE LARGEST SUBGROUPS OF ASIAN AMERICANS. OUR RESEARCH USING A NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE COHORT OF U.S. ADULTS FOUND THAT FILIPINO AMERICAN ADULTS HAD THE HIGHEST PREVALENCE OF SHORT SLEEP DURATION AMONG ALL POPULATION GROUPS EXAMINED. THEY ALSO REPORTED GREATER DIFFICULTY FALLING ASLEEP AND STAYING ASLEEP THAN OTHER ASIAN AMERICAN SUBGROUPS. DESPITE THE CAUSAL LINK BETWEEN POOR SLEEP AND ADVERSE PHYSICAL AND MENTAL HEALTH, NO INTERVENTION TO DATE HAS ADDRESSED SLEEP ISSUES AMONG FILIPINO AMERICANS. EXISTING NON-PHARMACOLOGICAL SLEEP INTERVENTIONS ARE EFFECTIVE IN IMPROVING SLEEP OUTCOMES, BUT THEY ARE PRIMARILY CONSTRAINED BY HIGH COSTS, LACK OF ACCESSIBILITY. EMERGING RESEARCH HAS SHOWN THAT ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI)-DRIVEN LIFESTYLE INTERVENTIONS CAN SIGNIFICANTLY IMPROVE SLEEP DURATION AND QUALITY. INTEGRATING AI TECHNOLOGIES INTO SLEEP INTERVENTIONS IS HIGHLY PROMISING BECAUSE THEY ARE COST-EFFECTIVE, ENGAGING, AND OFFER AN AUTOMATED, SELF-PACED DELIVERY MODALITY. TO ADDRESS THESE GAPS, OUR TEAM DEVELOPED A GENERATIVE AI-POWERED SLEEP CHATBOT THAT DELIVERS PERSONALIZED ADVICE GROUNDED IN COGNITIVE BEHAVIORAL THERAPY FOR INSOMNIA (CBT-I) VIA A TEXT MESSAGING APP. IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDY, THE CHATBOT DEMONSTRATED HIGH FEASIBILITY AND STRONG ACCEPTABILITY. PARTICIPANTS REPORTED IMPROVEMENTS IN MULTIPLE SLEEP OUTCOMES AFTER CHATBOT USE, INCLUDING LONGER SLEEP DURATION AND BETTER SLEEP QUALITY. BUILDING ON THIS WORK, WE WILL CONDUCT A SINGLE-ARM, PRE-POST STUDY TO PILOT TEST OUR GENERATIVE AI-BASED SLEEP INTERVENTION AMONG FILIPINO AMERICANS WITH POOR SLEEP. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL EXAMINE THE FEASIBILITY, ACCEPTABILITY, USABILITY, AND ENGAGEMENT OF THE INTERVENTION, AS WELL AS PRE-POST CHANGES IN SLEEP OUTCOMES. USING A CONVENIENCE SAMPLING STRATEGY, WE WILL ENROLL 40 FILIPINO AMERICANS AGED 30 TO 70 YEARS WHO HAVE SHORT SLEEP DURATION AND POOR QUALITY OF SLEEP. THE STUDY WILL LAST FOR FOUR WEEKS, INCLUDING A 1-WEEK BASELINE ASSESSMENT, A 2-WEEK INTERVENTION PERIOD, AND A 1-WEEK POST-INTERVENTION ASSESSMENT. DURING THE 2-WEEK SLEEP INTERVENTION, PARTICIPANTS WILL ENGAGE WITH AN AI CHATBOT THROUGH TEXTING TO RECEIVE PERSONALIZED EDUCATION AND GUIDANCE FOR SLEEP PROMOTION. A DEBRIEFING SESSION WILL FOLLOW THE INTERVENTION TO GATHER EACH PARTICIPANT'S FEEDBACK AND IDENTIFY AREAS FOR IMPROVEMENT. THIS PROPOSED STUDY REPRESENTS A PIONEERING EFFORT TO HARNESS GENERATIVE AI TO IMPROVE SLEEP HEALTH AMONG ASIAN AMERICANS. FINDINGS FROM THIS STUDY WILL LAY THE GROUNDWORK FOR FURTHER REFINEMENT AND EFFICACY TESTING OF OUR AI-BASED SLEEP INTERVENTION ON A LARGER SCALE. MORE IMPORTANTLY, THE AI-BASED SLEEP INTERVENTION HOLDS POTENTIAL FOR EXPANSION TO OTHER POPULATION GROUPS THAT EXPERIENCE POOR SLEEP.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EMPOWERING NUTRITION THROUGH GRAPHIC-STYLE STORIES: CO-DESIGNING AN ACCEPTABLE AND FEASIBLE COMMUNITY-BASED PROGRAM WITH ADULTS WITH INTELLECTUAL AND DEVELOPMENTAL DISABILITIES AND THEIR CAREGIVERS - PROJECT SUMMARY ADULTS WITH IDD OFTEN HAVE POOR DIETARY QUALITY, CHARACTERIZED BY HIGH INTAKE OF REFINED CARBOHYDRATES, SATURATED FAT, SODIUM, AND PROCESSED FOODS, ALONG WITH INSUFFICIENT INTAKE OF FRUITS AND VEGETABLES. IN ADDITION, FOOD SELECTIVITY AND A PROPENSITY TO OVEREAT CONTRIBUTE TO POOR EATING PATTERNS. THIS, IN TURN, IS ASSOCIATED WITH A HIGHER PREVALENCE OF OVERWEIGHT AND OBESITY THAT IS APPROXIMATELY TWO TIMES HIGHER THAN WHAT IS FOUND IN THE GENERAL POPULATION. AS A RESULT, THEY ENCOUNTER INCREASED RISKS FOR CHRONIC DISEASES. WITH TOO FEW RESOURCES SPECIFICALLY TAILORED FOR THIS UNIQUELY VULNERABLE POPULATION, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR AN ENGAGING AND EASY-TO- IMPLEMENT COMMUNITY-BASED NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM THAT TARGETS BOTH ADULTS WITH IDD AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. PREVIOUS STUDIES HAVE DEMONSTRATED THAT NARRATIVES ARE ENGAGING, MEMORABLE, AND ACTIONABLE IN PROMOTING HEALTHY LIFESTYLES IN COMMUNITY SETTINGS, PARTICULARLY IN ADULTS WITH LOWER HEALTH LITERACY LEVELS, SUCH AS ADULTS WITH IDD. THEREFORE, WE WILL CO-DESIGN AN INNOVATIVE, THEORY-BASED NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM, EMPOWER ADULTS WITH IDD, IN PARTNERSHIP WITH ADULTS WITH IDD, THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS. THERE ARE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: (1) TO ITERATIVELY CO-DESIGN, EMPOWER ADULTS WITH MILD IDD, AN ENGAGING AND EASY-TO- IMPLEMENT NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAM WITH ADULTS WITH IDD, THEIR CAREGIVERS, AND COMMUNITY PARTNERS AND TO TEST ITS ACCEPTABILITY AND FEASIBILITY AT ADSCS, AND (2) TO DETERMINE THE PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OF EMPOWER ADULTS WITH IDD ON FOOD AND BEVERAGE CONSUMPTION, AND FOOD SELECTIVITY IN ADULTS WITH IDD, AND THEIR CAREGIVERS' FOOD LITERACY TO PROMOTE HEALTHY EATING IN ADULTS WITH IDD. IN ORDER TO EXAMINE AIM 1 A DETERMINANTS ASSESSMENT WILL BE CONDUCTED WITH 45 DYADS OF ADULTS AND THEIR CAREGIVERS TO INFORM THE DEVELOPMENT OF GRAPHIC STYLE STORIES AND OTHER EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS. TOPICS MAY INCLUDE MYPLATE FOOD GROUPS, PORTION CONTROL, INCORPORATING FRUITS AND VEGETABLES INTO MEALS AND SNACKS, WATER CONSUMPTION, AND ALTERNATIVES TO PROCESS FOODS IN THE CONTEXT OF INTERACTION BETWEEN ADULTS WITH IDD AND THEIR CAREGIVERS. THE ITERATIVE CO-DESIGNED GRAPHIC STYLE STORIES AND OTHER EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS WILL BE TESTED FOR ACCEPTABILITY WITH 6 DYADS AND THEN 6- WEEK SHORT VERSION OF THE PROGRAM THAT INCORPORATED THOSE MATERIALS WILL BE IMPLEMENTED FOR FEASIBILITY TEST WITH 10 DYADS. AFTER THE REVISION BASED ON THE FEEDBACK THROUGH THIS PROCESS, THE PROGRAM WILL BE FINALIZED. TO EXAMINE AIM 2, THE PRELIMINARY EFFICACY OF THE FULL 6-MONTH PROGRAM WILL BE TESTED WITH 45 DYADS ON FOOD CONSUMPTION, FOOD SELECTIVITY, MOTIVATION FOR HEALTHY EATING IN ADULTS WITH IDD AND CAREGIVER'S FOOD LITERACY USING A ONE-GROUP PRE- AND POST-TEST DESIGN AT THREE ADSCS, WITH BASELINE, 3-, 6-, AND 9-MONTH ASSESSMENTS. WE EXPECT THAT THE PROGRAM ITERATIVELY CO-DESIGNED WITH ADULTS WITH IDD AND THEIR CAREGIVERS WILL BE ENGAGING AND FEASIBLE TO IMPLEMENT WITHIN COMMUNITY ADULT DAY SERVICE CENTERS AND IMPROVE FOOD CONSUMPTION OF ADULTS WITH IDD. IF SUCCESSFUL, THE PROGRAM WILL GREATLY IMPACT THE LIVES OF COUNTLESS ADULTS WITH IDD AND HELP THEM TO WARD OFF UNNECESSARY CHRONIC DISEASES CAUSED BY UNHEALTHY EATING HABITS WITH OVERALL HEALTH AND WELL-BEING.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: STRIOSOMAL CONTROL OF DOPAMINE CIRCUIT IMPACTED BY MATERNAL IMMUNE ACTIVATION - THIS PROJECT PROPOSES TO INVESTIGATE THE INFLUENCE OF MATERNAL IMMUNE ACTIVATION (MIA) ON DOPAMINE FUNCTION WITH A LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO ELUCIDATE CIRCUIT VULNERABILITIES THAT COULD CONTRIBUTE TO SUSCEPTIBILITY NEUROPSYCHIATRIC OUTCOMES ASSOCIATED WITH DOPAMINE DYSREGULATION. THE FOCUS IS ON EVALUATING THE IMPACT OF IN UTERO IMMUNE ACTIVATION ON A STRIATAL CIRCUIT CALLED THE STRIOSOME-DENDRON BOUQUET, WHICH DIRECTLY CONTROLS DOPAMINE NEURONS IN THE SUBSTANTIA NIGRA PARS COMPACTA (SNC). AIM 1 WILL DETERMINE WHETHER MIA CAUSES STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL ALTERATIONS IN THE STRIOSOME-DOPAMINE CIRCUIT. AIM 2 WILL ASSESS THE ROLE OF THE DOPAMINE-ANTAGONISTIC NOCICEPTIN SYSTEM IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND FUNCTION OF THIS CIRCUIT. THE CENTRAL HYPOTHESIS IS THAT MIA DISRUPTS THE MATURATION OF STRIOSOMAL REGULATION OF DOPAMINE SIGNALING, WITH LONG-TERM CONSEQUENCES FOR BEHAVIORAL VULNERABILITY. THIS WORK WILL ELUCIDATE NOVEL DEVELOPMENTAL MECHANISMS OF DOPAMINE CIRCUIT DISRUPTION AND IDENTIFY POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC TARGETS.
