description: DEVELOPING METHODS FOR TRACKING BRAIN LIPIDS IN VIVO - PROJECT SUMMARY NEURONS AND GLIA CONTAIN THOUSANDS OF LIPIDS TO SUPPORT UNIQUE CELLULAR FUNCTIONS WITHIN SPECIFIC COMPARTMENTS. SPECIFIC LIPIDS CAN DEFINE ORGANELLE IDENTITY, INITIATE SIGNALING PATHWAYS, AND SCULPT CELL MORPHOLOGY AND FUNCTION. ALTHOUGH LIPID DYSREGULATION DRIVES NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES, THE LIPIDOME IS LESS AMENABLE TO GENETIC MANIPULATION AND VISUALIZATION THAN THE PROTEOME. WHERE DO SPECIFIC LIPIDS LIVE AND FUNCTION WITHIN BRAIN CELLS? CAN LIPIDS BE GENETICALLY TRACKED WITH A PRECISION APPROACHING THAT OF TAGGED PROTEINS? THIS PROPOSAL FOCUSES ON CREATING GENETIC TOOLS FOR TAGGING LIPID TAILS AND TRACKING LIPID HEADS IN VIVO. BY GENETIC INDUCTION AND SUBCELLULAR TARGETING OF AN ENZYME THAT MODIFIES LIPID TAILS FOLLOWED BY MASS SPECTROMETRY (“PROXIMITY LIPIDOMICS”), WE WILL DETERMINE LIPIDOMIC DIFFERENCES BETWEEN NEURONS AND GLIA. WE WILL TAG SYNAPTIC VESICLE AND ACTIVE ZONE LIPIDOMES IN NEURONS, AND ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM LIPIDOMES IN GLIA AND NEURONS. IN PARALLEL, BY USING PROTEIN DOMAINS SELECTIVE TO INDIVIDUAL LIPID HEADGROUPS, AND CONTROLS THAT LACK LIPID BINDING CAPACITY, WE WILL CREATE A GENETIC TOOLKIT FOR TRACKING THREE SPHINGOLIPIDS, TWO PHOSPHOLIPIDS, AND FREE STEROLS AT INTRACELLULAR OR EXOPLASMIC LEAFLETS. THESE STUDIES WILL MARKEDLY STRENGTHEN OUR ABILITY TO TRACK LIPIDS IN INTACT BRAINS ACROSS NEURONS AND GLIA WITH UNPRECEDENTED GENETIC CONTROL. IF SUCCESSFUL, THIS PROJECT WILL FACILITATE THE INTERPRETATION OF BULK LIPIDOMICS DATASETS BY ASSIGNING LIPIDS TO SUBCELLULAR HOMES, GENERATE HYPOTHESES FOR LIPID FUNCTION IN SPECIFIC ORGANELLES AND CELLS, AND ILLUMINATE HOW NEURONAL AND GLIAL LIPIDS FUNCTION IN THE BRAIN. THESE STUDIES WILL BROADLY INFORM OUR UNDERSTANDING OF HOW LIPIDS LOCALIZE TO NEURONS AND GLIA ACROSS HEALTH, AGING, AND NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASES. AS THIS UNDERSTANDING IS FUNDAMENTAL TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF THERAPIES THAT MODULATE LIPIDS OR RELY ON LIPID QUANTITATION, THESE STUDIES WILL STRENGTHEN THE INTERPRETATION AND SELECTION OF LIPID BIOMARKERS, THEREBY SHAPING FUTURE THERAPEUTIC STRATEGIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: AAV-MEDIATED GENE SILENCING FOR THE TREATMENT OF HYPOMYELINATION WITH ATROPHY OF THE BASAL GANGLIA AND CEREBELLUM (H-ABC) - HYPOMYELINATION WITH ATROPHY OF THE BASAL GANGLIA AND CEREBELLUM (H-ABC) IS A RARE LEUKODYSTROPHY CAUSED BY SPORADIC MUTATIONS IN THE TUBB4A GENE. TUBB4A IS MAINLY EXPRESSED IN THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. THE BRAIN REGIONS WITH THE HIGHEST EXPRESSION ARE THE WHITE MATTER, CEREBELLUM, AND BASAL GANGLIA. ITS EXPRESSION IS FOUND IN NEURONS AND OLIGODENDROCYTES, AND MUTATIONS LEAD TO DEFICITS IN BOTH CELL TYPES. MUTATIONS IN TUBB4A DISRUPT THE MECHANICAL AND DYNAMIC PROPERTIES OF MICROTUBULES AND ARE LINKED TO A RANGE OF NEUROLOGICAL DISORDERS. H- ABC IS A PROGRESSIVE NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE AT THE SEVERE END OF THE TUBB4A-RELATED LEUKODYSTROPHY SPECTRUM. CHILDREN WITH H-ABC GRADUALLY LOSE CONTROL OF THEIR MOTOR SKILLS, LOSING THE ABILITY TO SIT, STAND, TALK, OR WALK INDEPENDENTLY. ULTIMATELY, CHILDREN WITH H-ABC OFTEN DO NOT SURVIVE INTO ADULTHOOD. CURRENTLY, THERE ARE NO FDA- APPROVED TREATMENTS THAT CAN EFFECTIVELY MODIFY THE DISEASE’S COURSE. TO ADDRESS THIS ISSUE, WE WILL DEVELOP AN ADENO-ASSOCIATED VIRUS (AAV)-MEDIATED GENE-SILENCING APPROACH TO TREAT THIS DEVASTATING DISEASE. MUTATIONS IN TUBB4A ARE TOXIC. DOWNREGULATING TUBB4A WITH AAV-DELIVERED ARTIFICIAL MIRNAS (AMIRS) CAN EFFICIENTLY REDUCE GENE EXPRESSION ACROSS MULTIPLE CELL TYPES AND OFFER LONG-TERM THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS WITHOUT ANY KNOWN HARMFUL EFFECTS. CONSIDERING THE GENETIC CAUSE AND THE CNS FEATURES OF H-ABC, I HAVE DESIGNED AN AAV9 VECTOR TO DELIVER AMIR-TUBB4A TO SUPPRESS TUBB4A AS A TREATMENT FOR H- ABC. THE AAV9-AMIR-TUBB4A VECTOR HAS SHOWN PROMISE BY EXTENDING SURVIVAL, INCREASING BODY WEIGHT GAIN, AND DELAYING SEIZURE ONSET IN DISEASED ANIMALS THROUGH DELIVERY TO OLIGODENDROCYTES. NONETHELESS, THE THERAPEUTIC EFFECTS NEED FURTHER ENHANCEMENT BEFORE PROGRESSING TO THE NEXT STAGE. RECENTLY, AN AAV CAPSID (BI-HTFR1) WAS DEVELOPED TO BIND TO THE HUMAN TRANSFERRIN RECEPTOR (HTFR1), WHICH IS EXPRESSED ON THE BLOOD- BRAIN BARRIER. BI-HTFR1 DEMONSTRATES 40 TO 50 TIMES HIGHER REPORTER EXPRESSION THAN AAV9 IN THE CNS OF HUMAN TFRC KNOCK-IN MICE. I HYPOTHESIZE THAT SILENCING TUBB4A IN BOTH NEURONS AND OLIGODENDROCYTES USING A HIGHLY EFFECTIVE AAV CAPSID COULD SIGNIFICANTLY RESCUE THE EFFECTS OF H-ABC. THE RESEARCH AIM IS TO DEVELOP A BI-HTFR CAPSID-BASED, IV-DELIVERABLE, EFFECTIVE, AND SAFE GENE THERAPY FOR TREATING H-ABC IN A PRECLINICAL MOUSE MODEL. WE WILL CONTINUE TO IDENTIFY EFFECTIVE AMIR-TUBB4A AND GENERATE THE VECTOR GENOME EXPRESSING AMIR-TUBB4A IN BOTH NEURONS AND OLIGODENDROCYTES FOR PACKAGING INTO BI-HTFR1 CAPSID. WE WILL CROSS THE TUBB4A-D249N MICE WITH TFRC KI MICE TO GENERATE THE HABC-TFRC MICE THAT CAN BE TRANSDUCED BY BI-HTFR1 CAPSID. WE WILL EVALUATE ITS THERAPEUTIC OUTCOMES IN HABC-TFRC MICE AND THE SAFETY PROFILE IN TFRC KI MICE. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THIS PROJECT MAY LEAD TO A CLINICAL TRIAL FOR THE TREATMENT OF HUMAN H-ABC.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services

recipient.name: THE UNIVERSITY OF TEXAS SOUTHWESTERN MEDICAL CENTER

description: POST-VIRAL GUILLAIN-BARRE SYNDROME: HUMAN INBORN ERRORS OF IMMUNITY AND A NEW MODEL OF PATHOGENIC MECHANISM - PROJECT SUMMARY GUILLAIN-BARRÉ SYNDROME (GBS) WAS FIRST DEFINED AS A DISTINCT CLINICAL AND PATHOLOGICAL CONDITION BY THREE FRENCH PHYSICIANS, GUILLAIN, BARRÉ, AND STROHL IN 1916. SINCE THEN, OVER 100 YEARS OF RESEARCH HAS GREATLY IMPROVED THE EPIDEMIOLOGICAL, CLINICAL AND PATHOLOGICAL CHARACTERIZATION OF THIS DISEASE. IT IS NOW LARGELY RECOGNIZED AS AN INFECTION-TRIGGERED, IMMUNE-MEDIATED PERIPHERAL NEUROPATHY. APART FROM CAMPYLOBACTER JEJUNI (C. JEJUNI), WHICH ACCOUNTS FOR ~30% OF GBS CASES, VIRAL INFECTION IS ANOTHER MAJOR TRIGGER OF GBS (~30-40%), WITH MORE THAN 10 VIRUSES INVOLVED, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO SARS-COV-2 AND THE INFLUENZA, ZIKA, AND CHIKUNGUNYA VIRUSES. THE BLOOD CIRCULATING ANTI-GANGLIOSIDE ANTIBODIES, DETECTED IN ~40-50% OF THE GBS CASES, HAVE BEEN PROPOSED TO BE PATHOGENIC ESPECIALLY IN CASES PRECEDING C. JEJUNI INFECTION. YET, THE ROOT CAUSE OF DISEASE PATHOGENESIS REMAINS UNCLEAR, AS THE GANGLIOSIDE MOLECULAR MIMICRY MODEL REMAINS HYPOTHETICAL, AND THE MECHANISM FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF GBS FOLLOWING INFECTION BY THE VARIOUS VIRUSES IS EVEN MORE UNCLEAR, AS THERE NO MICROBIAL MIMICS OF GANGLIOSIDES HAVE BEEN FOUND. WE DECIDED TO DISSECT THE IMMUNOPATHOGENESIS OF POST-VIRAL GBS FOLLOWING A HUMAN MONOGENIC APPROACH. FROM WHOLE EXOME/GENOME SEQUENCING DATA OF A COHORT OF 22 PATIENTS WITH SARS- COV-2 POST-VIRAL GBS, WE DISCOVERED BI-ALLELIC DAMAGING MUTATIONS IN MAP3K6 AND OPTN, ENCODING MOLECULES CRITICAL IN THE HOST CELLULAR APOPTOSIS OR AUTOPHAGY PATHWAYS, RESPECTIVELY, IN THREE PATIENTS. WE AIM TO TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT 1) RECESSIVE DEFICIENCIES OF MAP3K6 AND OPTN UNDERLIE GBS PATHOGENESIS IN HUMANS, FOLLOWING INFECTION BY SARS-COV-2, AND PROBABLY OTHER VIRUSES; 2) THE UNDERLYING MECHANISM OF DISEASE MAY BE RELATED TO DEFECTIVE NEURONAL CELL SELF-REMOVAL RESULTING IN LEUKOCYTE-MEDIATED INFLAMMATION AND AUTOIMMUNITY. WE WILL CHARACTERIZE BOTH CANDIDATE GBS-CAUSING INBORN ERRORS OF IMMUNITY (IEIS) THOROUGHLY, TO DISCOVER THE MOLECULAR, CELLULAR, AND IMMUNOLOGICAL MECHANISMS OF DISEASE. WE WILL ALSO SEARCH FOR NEW IEIS, RELATED TO MAP3K6 OR OPTN OR NOT, VIA WHOLE GENOME SEQUENCING OF A GROWING COHORT OF PATIENTS WITH GBS FOLLOWING INFECTION BY DIVERSE VIRUSES, AND CHARACTERIZE ALL NEW CANDIDATE IEIS IN GREAT DEPTH. THIS HIGHLY INNOVATIVE PROJECT IS SUPPORTED BY STRONG PRELIMINARY STUDIES. WE HAVE MOST OF THE REQUIRED EXPERIMENTAL TOOLS ESTABLISHED. THE CLARIFICATION OF GBS PATHOGENESIS MECHANISMS DUE TO DEFICIENCIES OF MAP3K6, OPTN AND OTHER RELATED MOLECULES WILL ENABLE US TO GAIN COMPLETELY NEW KNOWLEDGE ABOUT THE MOLECULAR AND CELLULAR BASIS OF THE IMMUNOPATHOLOGY OF POST- VIRAL GBS IN PREVIOUSLY HEALTHY PEOPLE. THE SUCCESSFUL INVESTIGATION OF A NEW MODEL OF GBS PATHOGENESIS MAY ALSO INFORM THE DESIGN OF PREVENTIVE AND THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTION STRATEGIES FOR ALL THE AFFECTED INDIVIDUALS, WHILE PAVING THE WAY FOR FURTHER INVESTIGATION OF THE IMMUNOPATHOGENESIS OF GBS FOLLOWING OTHER INFECTIOUS OR NON- INFECTIOUS TRIGGERS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: REGULATION OF FULL-LENGTH SPASTIN AND THE ETIOLOGY OF HEREDITARY SPASTIC PARAPLEGIA - PROJECT SUMMARY SPASTIN IS A MEMBER OF THE AAA-ATPASE FAMILY OF HEXAMERIC ENZYMES THAT USE ATP HYDROLYSIS TO SEVER MICROTUBULES. SPASTIN REMODELS THE CYTOSKELETON AND PLAYS FUNDAMENTAL ROLES IN SEVERAL CELLULAR PROCESSES, INCLUDING CELL DIVISION AND NEURONAL MORPHOGENESIS. MUTATIONS IN THE SPAST GENE, WHICH ENCODES THE SPASTIN PROTEIN, ARE THE MOST COMMON CAUSE OF AUTOSOMAL-DOMINANT HEREDITARY SPASTIC PARAPLEGIA (HSP), A PROGRESSIVE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISORDER CHARACTERIZED BY CORTICOSPINAL NEURONAL DEGENERATION AND LOWER LIMB SPASTICITY.  THE COMMONLY POSTULATED ETIOLOGY OF HSP IS THAT MUTATIONS REDUCE MICROTUBULE-SEVERING ACTIVITY. BECAUSE OVEREXPRESSION OF SPASTIN'S AAA-ATPASE DOMAIN FRAGMENTS MICROTUBULES AND LEADS TO THEIR DISAPPEARANCE IN CELLS, A DECREASE IN SEVERING ACTIVITY IS EXPECTED TO INCREASE MICROTUBULE MASS. PARADOXICALLY, HOWEVER, WHEN SPASTIN IS MUTATED OR KNOCKED DOWN IN MANY TISSUES, MICROTUBULE MASS DECREASES. THIS IS DUE TO A SECOND ACTIVITY OF SPASTIN, RECENTLY DISCOVERED IN OUR LAB: SPASTIN ALSO PROMOTES THE REGROWTH OF MICROTUBULE FRAGMENTS, WHICH ACT AS SEEDS, THEREBY INCREASING MICROTUBULE NUMBER AND MASS. DEPENDING ON THE BALANCE OF THE SEVERING AND REGROWTH, SPASTIN CAN EITHER DESTROY OR AMPLIFY THE MICROTUBULE CYTOSKELETON. SPASTIN IS THEREFORE A POTENTIALLY TOXIC PROTEIN WHOSE ACTIVITY MUST BE TIGHTLY CONTROLLED IN CELLS.  CURRENTLY, OUR BIOCHEMICAL AND BIOPHYSICAL UNDERSTANDING OF SPASTIN IS LIMITED BY THE INABILITY TO PURIFY THE FULL-LENGTH PROTEIN, M1. FUNCTIONAL AND STRUCTURAL STUDIES HAVE BEEN LIMITED TO TRUNCATED PROTEINS THAT LACK THE HYDROPHOBIC N-TERMINAL. IN EXCITING NEW RESULTS, WE HAVE BEEN ABLE TO EXPRESS AND PURIFY M1. SURPRISINGLY, WE FOUND THAT PURIFIED M1 HAS ROBUST MICROTUBULE-SEVERING ACTIVITY, EVEN THOUGH ITS EXPRESSION IN CELLS HAS LITTLE EFFECT ON THE MICROTUBULE CYTOSKELETON. M1 MUST BE TURNED OFF IN CELLS. THUS, OUR PRELIMINARY RESULTS SUPPORT OUR HYPOTHESIS THAT SPASTIN'S HYDROPHOBIC N-TERMINUS IS A REGULATORY DOMAIN THAT INHIBITS MICROTUBULE SEVERING AND THAT MISREGULATION MAY UNDERLIE HSP.  TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE WILL PURSUE TWO SPECIFIC AIMS: (I) CELLULAR STUDIES WILL IDENTIFY KEY RESIDUES WITHIN THE N-TERMINAL HYDROPHOBIC DOMAIN THAT ARE REQUIRED FOR MEMBRANE ASSOCIATION; AND A CHEMICALLY INDUCIBLE HETERODIMERIZATION SYSTEM WILL TEST WHETHER FORCED RECRUITMENT OF CYTOPLASMIC M87 SPASTIN TO MEMBRANES INHIBITS SEVERING. (II) WE WILL BIND PURIFIED M1 TO LIPOSOMES AND LIPID NANODISCS TO INHIBIT THE SEVERING AND RESCUE ACTIVITIES, AND TEST WHETHER THE HYDROPHOBIC DOMAIN INTERFERES WITH HEXAMERIZATION USING SINGLE-MOLECULE ASSAYS AND NEGATIVE-STAIN ELECTRON MICROSCOPY.  SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THESE AIMS WILL DETERMINE WHETHER MEMBRANE RECRUITMENT IS NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT TO REGULATE SPASTIN'S MICROTUBULE SEVERING AND GROWTH ACTIVITIES. THE IN VITRO STUDIES WILL ELUCIDATE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF REGULATION AND GIVE INSIGHT INTO THE ETIOLOGY OF AXON DEGENERATION IN HSP.

description: SPINAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING EARLY MOTOR DYSFUNCTION IN ASD - PROJECT SUMMARY (ABSTRACT) AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDER (ASD) AFFECTS APPROXIMATELY ONE IN 36 CHILDREN, WITH ABOUT 80% EXHIBITING EARLY MOTOR IMPAIRMENTS THAT PRECEDE AND PREDICT LATER SOCIAL AND COMMUNICATION DEFICITS. DESPITE THEIR PREDICTIVE VALUE, THE NEURAL MECHANISMS UNDERLYING THESE EARLY MOTOR DYSFUNCTIONS REMAIN UNKNOWN. FOUNDATIONAL MOTOR BEHAVIORS SUCH AS MUSCULAR TONE, POSTURE, BALANCE, AND MUSCLE COORDINATION ARE GOVERNED BY SPINAL MOTONEURONS (MNS) AND THEIR DESCENDING EXCITATORY INPUTS FROM THE RETICULOSPINAL AND VESTIBULOSPINAL PATHWAYS, ALL SYSTEMS THAT MATURE EARLY IN LIFE. HOWEVER, THE STRUCTURE, CONNECTIVITY AND MOLECULAR PROFILE OF THESE SPINAL CIRCUITS HAVE NEVER BEEN EXAMINED IN ASD. THIS PROJECT WILL INVESTIGATE THE INTEGRITY AND FUNCTION OF SPINAL MNS AND THEIR DESCENDING INPUTS IN TWO COMPLEMENTARY MOUSE MODELS OF ASD: PRENATAL VALPROIC ACID (VPA) EXPOSURE, REPRESENTING ENVIRONMENTAL/EPIGENETIC RISK, AND THE 16P11.2 DELETION (DEL) MODEL, REPRESENTING A HIGH-CONFIDENCE GENETIC CAUSE. THE WORK INTEGRATES BEHAVIORAL, ANATOMICAL, MOLECULAR, AND PHYSIOLOGICAL ANALYSES TO LINK SPECIFIC CELLULAR AND CIRCUIT ALTERATIONS TO MEASURABLE EARLY MOTOR OUTCOMES. IN AIM 1, WE WILL CHARACTERIZE THE DEVELOPMENT OF EARLY MOTOR DEFICITS AND ASSESS MN NUMBER, SPATIAL ORGANIZATION, AND EXPRESSION OF THREE 16P11.2 GENES—MAPK3, TAOK2, AND KCTD13—AT SINGLE-CELL RESOLUTION USING MULTIPLEX RNASCOPE AND IMMUNOFLUORESCENCE. IN AIM 2, WE WILL TEST THE RECRUITMENT AND SYNAPTIC INTEGRITY OF LUMBAR MNS BY RETICULOSPINAL AND VESTIBULOSPINAL PATHWAYS USING EX VIVO CALCIUM IMAGING AND CRE-DEPENDENT SYNAPTOPHYSIN-GFP LABELING OF DESCENDING TERMINALS. TOGETHER, THESE STUDIES WILL DEFINE HOW GENETIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL ASD ETIOLOGIES CONVERGE OR DIVERGE AT THE LEVEL OF SPINAL MOTOR CIRCUITS. BY ESTABLISHING CAUSAL LINKS BETWEEN SPECIFIC CIRCUIT DEFICITS AND EARLY MOTOR PHENOTYPES, THE PROJECT WILL IDENTIFY BIOMARKERS OF ATYPICAL MOTOR DEVELOPMENT AND PROVIDE A FOUNDATION FOR TARGETED EARLY INTERVENTIONS IN ASD.

description: UNRAVELING THE ROLE OF WATER HYACINTH IN MODULATING SCHISTOSOMIASIS TO FACILITATE SCALING A PROVEN DISEASE CONTROL INTERVENTION - SCHISTOSOMIASIS IS A DEBILITATING PARASITIC DISEASE THAT IMPOSES MAJOR HEALTH AND ECONOMIC BURDENS WORLDWIDE AND REMAINS RELEVANT TO AMERICAN HEALTH THROUGH INTERNATIONAL TRAVEL, MILITARY DEPLOYMENT, IMMIGRATION, AND GLOBAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE PREPAREDNESS. IN THE LAKE VICTORIA BASIN, MILLIONS ARE INFECTED WITH SCHISTOSOMA MANSONI, AND REINFECTION REMAINS HIGH DESPITE ANNUAL MASS DRUG ADMINISTRATION. OUR TEAM PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED AN INNOVATIVE INTERVENTION IN SENEGAL: AQUATIC VEGETATION REMOVAL (AVR) TO REDUCE SNAIL HABITAT AND INTERRUPT PARASITE TRANSMISSION. IN RANDOMIZED CONTROLLED TRIALS, AVR SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCED SCHISTOSOMA INFECTIONS WHILE THE HARVESTED VEGETATION WAS CONVERTED INTO COMPOST, LIVESTOCK FEED, AND BIODIGESTER FUEL, GENERATING ECONOMIC RETURNS THAT EXCEEDED INTERVENTION COSTS. BEFORE AVR CAN BE EXPANDED TO EAST AFRICA, AN IMPORTANT SCIENTIFIC QUESTION MUST BE RESOLVED. THE DOMINANT INVASIVE AQUATIC PLANT IN LAKE VICTORIA IS WATER HYACINTH (PONTEDERIA CRASSIPES), WHICH DIFFERS ECOLOGICALLY FROM VEGETATION IN SENEGAL. PRELIMINARY ANALYSES SUGGEST A HUMP-SHAPED RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN WATER HYACINTH DENSITY AND S. MANSONI PREVALENCE. THIS PATTERN MAY RESULT FROM WATER HYACINTH SIMULTANEOUSLY INCREASING SNAIL HABITAT AND PARASITE DENSITY WHILE REDUCING HUMAN WATER CONTACT AT HIGH COVERAGE LEVELS. REMOVING HYACINTH WITHOUT UNDERSTANDING THESE MECHANISMS COULD UNINTENTIONALLY INCREASE DISEASE RISK. KENYA PROVIDES A UNIQUE NATURAL LABORATORY UNAVAILABLE IN THE UNITED STATES BECAUSE ACTIVE SCHISTOSOMIASIS TRANSMISSION OCCURS ACROSS NATURAL GRADIENTS OF WATER HYACINTH, ALLOWING ECOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL MECHANISMS TO BE STUDIED UNDER REAL-WORLD CONDITIONS. THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO IDENTIFY THE ECOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL MECHANISMS DRIVING THIS NON-LINEAR PATTERN TO ENSURE THAT AVR CAN BE SAFELY ADAPTED TO EAST AFRICA. WE WILL (1) QUANTIFY HOW WATER HYACINTH DENSITY AFFECTS SNAIL AND CERCARIAL DENSITIES USING FIELD SURVEYS, CERCARIAL SHEDDING ASSAYS, AND REMOTE SENSING, AND (2) DETERMINE HOW WATER HYACINTH INFLUENCES HUMAN WATER-CONTACT BEHAVIOR THROUGH STRUCTURED OBSERVATIONS AND HOUSEHOLD SURVEYS. BY IDENTIFYING GENERALIZABLE ECOLOGICAL AND BEHAVIORAL MECHANISMS GOVERNING ENVIRONMENTALLY MEDIATED TRANSMISSION, THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE THE SCIENTIFIC FOUNDATION FOR ADAPTING AVR TO NEW SETTINGS AND DESIGNING FUTURE INTERVENTION TRIALS. THE RESULTING KNOWLEDGE WILL BE BROADLY APPLICABLE TO ENVIRONMENTALLY MEDIATED PARASITIC DISEASES AND WILL INFORM PREVENTION STRATEGIES RELEVANT TO AMERICANS THROUGH TRAVEL MEDICINE, MILITARY DEPLOYMENT, IMMIGRATION, AND GLOBAL INFECTIOUS DISEASE PREPAREDNESS. BECAUSE THESE MECHANISMS ARE EXPECTED TO BE REPRODUCIBLE ACROSS ENDEMIC SETTINGS, THIS WORK WILL ESTABLISH PRINCIPLES THAT CAN GUIDE FUTURE IMPLEMENTATION AND EVALUATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL DISEASE-CONTROL INTERVENTIONS.

description: FUNCTIONAL CONNECTOMICS VIA HIGH-SPEED TWO-PHOTON VOLTAGE IMAGING AND OPTOGENETICS - PROJECT SUMMARY THE GOAL OF THIS TARGETED PLANNING PROJECT IS TO ESTABLISH A NEW PARADIGM FOR “FUNCTIONAL CONNECTOMICS.” EXISTING CONNECTOMICS APPROACHES OPERATE ONLY ON POST-MORTEM TISSUE, HAVE LOW THROUGHPUT, OR SPARSELY SAMPLE A LOCAL REGION’S CONNECTOME, AND NONE CAN MEASURE THE PHYSIOLOGICAL STRENGTH OF CONNECTIONS OR TRACK HOW THEY CHANGE IN THE LIVING BRAIN. HERE WE WILL COMBINE ULTRA-FAST TWO-PHOTON VOLTAGE IMAGING (2P-FACED) WITH TWOPHOTON OPTOGENETIC STIMULATION TO ACHIEVE HIGH-THROUGHPUT MEASUREMENT AND TRACKING OF A LOCAL FUNCTIONAL CONNECTOME IN THE RODENT BRAIN. OWING TO THE HIGH SPEED AND SCALE OF 2P-FACED PAIRED WITH FAST SINGLE-CELL OPTOGENETIC STIMULATION, WE WILL BUILD A SYSTEM THAT CAN MEASURE, MONITOR, AND TRACK SYNAPTIC WEIGHTS ACROSS TENS OF THOUSANDS OF CANDIDATE SYNAPTIC CONNECTIONS IN AWAKE ANIMALS, OVER DAYS TO WEEKS TO MONTHS. UNIQUELY, THE SYSTEM WILL READ OUT BOTH SUBTHRESHOLD SYNAPTIC POTENTIALS AND SUPRATHRESHOLD SPIKES, ENABLING FOR THE FIRST TIME THE DIRECT MEASUREMENT OF BOTH MONOSYNAPTIC CONNECTIVITY AND ITS FUNCTIONAL IMPACT ON SPIKING IN THE SAME NEURONS IN VIVO. RATHER THAN TARGETING A SINGLE CIRCUIT OR BEHAVIOR, THE PLATFORM IS DESIGNED AS A GENERAL-PURPOSE SYSTEM FOR MEASURING AND DYNAMICALLY TRACKING FUNCTIONAL CONNECTOMES THROUGHOUT THE BRAIN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: EPITHELIAL DYNAMICS DURING DEVELOPMENTAL PROCESSES - PROJECT SUMMARY LONG TERM MAINTENANCE OF EPITHELIAL TISSUES REQUIRES CONSTANT REMODELING. AS EPITHELIA GROW THE PROCESS OF RADIAL CELL INTERCALATION CAN BE AN IMPORTANT MECHANISM FOR CELL ADDITION. HOWEVER, CONTINUED GROWTH AND CELL ADDITION (TYPICALLY VIA PROLIFERATION) CAN ALSO LEAD TO CELL CROWDING WHICH CAN DRIVE CELL EXTRUSION AS A MECHANISM TO DECREASE APICAL TISSUE AREA. IN ADDITION TO CELL EXTRUSION, WE HAVE IDENTIFIED MACROPINOCYTOSIS AS A MECHANISM FOR ALTERING APICAL SURFACE AREA IN RESPONSE TO CROWDING. MACROPINOCYTOSIS IS AN ENDOCYTIC PROCESS THAT RESULTS IN LARGE SCALE ENGULFMENT OF EXTRACELLULAR MATERIAL BUT IMPORTANTLY ALSO LEADS TO LARGE SCALE ENGULFMENT OF APICAL MEMBRANE WHICH DRAMATICALLY DECREASES APICAL SURFACE AREA. IN THIS PROPOSAL WE AIM TO UNDERSTAND THE MOLECULAR REGULATORS AND THE PHYSICAL PARAMETERS THAT MODULATE CELL INTERCALATION, CELL EXTRUSION AND MACROPINOCYTOSIS. THEME 1. PHYSICAL AND MOLECULAR REGULATION OF RADIAL INTERCALATION. MULTI-CILIATED CELL (MCC) AND IONOCYTE (IC) RADIAL INTERCALATION INTO THE SKIN OF XENOPUS EMBRYOS REPRESENTS AN EXPERIMENTALLY PLIABLE SYSTEM WHICH ALLOWS US TO ADDRESS BOTH THE PHYSICAL DEMANDS OF INTERCALATION AND THE BROADER REMODELING OF THE EPITHELIUM IN RESPONSE TO THAT INTERCALATION. WE AIM TO UNDERSTAND BOTH THE PENETRATIVE CAPACITY OF INTERCALATING CELLS AS WELL AS THE RESTRICTIVE CAPACITY OF THE EPITHELIUM AND HAVE IDENTIFIED NOVEL REGULATORS OF JUNCTIONAL INTEGRITY THAT IMPINGE ON THIS PROCESS. THEME 2. REGULATION OF BIDIRECTIONAL CELL EXTRUSION. WE HAVE RECENTLY PUBLISHED THAT ALL MCCS UNDERGO BI- DIRECTIONAL CELL EXTRUSION. THE FIRST WAVE OF BASAL CELL EXTRUSION IS REGULATED VIA NOTCH SIGNALING, AND WE WILL ADDRESS THE TEMPORAL CONTROL OF THIS REGULATION WHICH WE HYPOTHESIZE STEMS FROM A TRANSCRIPTIONAL SHIFT IN RECEPTOR SUBTYPE. ADDITIONALLY, CELLS THAT EVADE NOTCH SIGNALING ARE TARGETED FOR APICAL CELL EXTRUSION VIA A MECHANOSENSORY MECHANISM THAT WE HYPOTHESIZE IS LINKED TO CELL CROWDING AND THE NEED TO DECREASE APICAL TISSUE AREA. WE WILL ADDRESS THE CONSEQUENCE OF MODULATING CELL NUMBER / TYPE ON THE TIMING OF APICAL EXTRUSION. USING A LONG-TERM LIGHT-SHEET IMAGING PARADIGM WE HAVE IDENTIFIED NUMEROUS MACROPINOCYTOTIC EVENTS THAT INCREASE AS DEVELOPMENT PROGRESSES. IMPORTANTLY, THESE EVENTS RESULT IN A SIGNIFICANT LOSS OF APICAL SURFACE AREA AND WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT SIMILAR TO APICAL CELL EXTRUSION, THESE EVENTS COUNTER CELL CROWDING BY DECREASING APICAL TISSUE AREA, BUT IN A MORE SUBTLE AND LESS PERMANENT MANNER. WE WILL ADDRESS BOTH THE REGULATION OF THESE EVENTS AND THE FUNCTIONAL CONSEQUENCE OF INHIBITING THEM, WHICH WE HYPOTHESIZE WILL ALTER CELL CROWDING THEREBY AFFECTING CELL EXTRUSION. WHILE THESE THEMES ADDRESS DISTINCT BIOLOGICAL QUESTIONS THERE IS CONSIDERABLE OVERLAP IN THE REAGENTS, EXPERIMENTAL DESIGN AND IMAGING PARADIGMS. ADDITIONALLY, IN EACH PROJECT WE WILL ADDRESS BOTH THE MOLECULAR AND PHYSICAL MECHANISM THAT REGULATE THESE PROCESSES AND WE ARE EXCITED BY HOW OUR PROJECTS SYNERGIZE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: FLEXIBLE BAYESIAN METHODS FOR ZERO-INFLATED MICROBIOME DATA TO UNDERSTAND MICROBIAL COMMUNITY DYNAMICS AND FUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT: RECENT TECHNOLOGICAL AND COMPUTATIONAL INNOVATIONS HAVE DRAMATICALLY IMPROVED THE SCALE AND SPEED IN WHICH RESEARCHERS COLLECT AND PROCESS MICROBIOME DATA. COUPLED WITH ADVANCES IN STATISTICAL AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS FOR MICROBIOME DATA ANALYSIS, THESE DEVELOPMENTS HAVE HELPED RESEARCHERS BETTER UNDERSTAND THE VARIOUS ROLES THE MICROBIOME PLAYS IN HUMAN HEALTH AND DISEASE. THIS HAS LED RESEARCHERS TO EXPLORE THE FEASIBILITY OF MICROBIOTA-BASED DIAGNOSTICS, THERAPIES, AND PREVENTION OF DISEASE, POTENTIALLY THROUGH PERSONALIZED TREATMENT STRATEGIES. A MAJOR CHALLENGE IN DEVELOPING MICROBIOTA-BASED PERSONALIZED MEDICINE IS OUR LIMITED UNDERSTANDING OF THE MECHANISMS THAT GOVERN MICROBIAL COMMUNITY ASSEMBLY, STABILITY, AND FUNCTION. FURTHER, STATISTICAL METHODS DEVELOPED AND APPLIED TO DESCRIBE THESE MECHANISMS ARE STILL IN THEIR INFANCY, AS EVEN THE MOST BASIC INFERENTIAL TASKS ARE CHALLENGED BY THE COMPLEXITY OF MICROBIOME DATA.  THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO PURSUE THE NEXT GENERATION OF STATISTICAL METHODS DESIGNED TO HELP UNLOCK THE POTENTIAL OF MICROBIOTA-BASED PERSONALIZED MEDICINE BY INTRODUCING A SUITE OF SCALABLE BAYESIAN METHODS FOR EXPLORATORY AND CONFIRMATORY MICROBIOME DATA ANALYSIS. BUILDING ON OUR UNIQUE EXPERIENCE IN MICROBIOME, MOBILE HEALTH, AND ECOLOGICAL RESEARCH, THE METHODS DEVELOPED BY MY LAB WILL BE DESIGNED TO INVESTIGATE MICROBIAL COMMUNITY ASSEMBLY, STABILITY, AND FUNCTION. EACH METHOD WILL ACCOMMODATE THE HIGH-DIMENSIONAL, OVERDISPERSED, ZERO-INFLATED, AND COMPOSITIONAL STRUCTURE CHARACTERISTIC OF MICROBIOME DATA AND WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY A USER- FRIENDLY SOFTWARE PACKAGE FOR OTHER RESEARCHERS TO APPLY AND EXTEND OUR WORK. SPECIFICALLY, THE PROPOSED METHODS WILL ALLOW RESEARCHERS TO (1) STUDY HOW MICROBES RESPOND TO, AND INFLUENCE, ABIOTIC AND BIOTIC FACTORS AND HOW THESE RELATIONS MAY DIFFER BY INTERACTIONS THEREOF; (2) INVESTIGATE HOW CLUSTERS OF MICROBIAL COMPOSITION VARY OVER TIME, SPACE, AND OTHER ENVIRONMENTAL AND HOST-ASSOCIATED FACTORS; AND (3) CHARACTERIZE STABLE STATES OF MICROBIAL COMPOSITION AND FUNCTION, IDENTIFY MOMENTS WHEN INDIVIDUALS TRANSITION THROUGH THESE STATES, AND UNDERSTAND THE MECHANISMS DRIVING THESE TRANSITIONS. ADDITIONALLY, THIS WORK WILL FACILITATE A PRODUCTIVE RESEARCH AND MEN- TORING ENVIRONMENT FOR UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS IN MY LAB THROUGH MULTIFACETED ACADEMIC, RESEARCH, PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT, AND COLLABORATIVE OPPORTUNITIES.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: TRANSFORMING SPATIAL PROTEOMICS VIA SIMULTANEOUS MULTIPLEXED IMAGING AT SINGLE-PROTEIN RESOLUTION - PROJECT SUMMARY UNDERSTANDING BIOLOGICAL PROCESSES REQUIRES NOT ONLY MEASURING HOW MUCH OF A PROTEIN IS PRESENT, BUT ALSO KNOWING WHERE EACH PROTEIN IS LOCATED, HOW IT IS ORGANIZED, AND WITH WHOM IT INTERACTS. EXISTING MASS SPECTROMETRY–BASED PROTEOMICS METHODS PROVIDE COMPREHENSIVE MOLECULAR PROFILING BUT LACK THE SPATIAL RESOLUTION NECESSARY TO RESOLVE NANOSCALE PROTEIN ORGANIZATION. IMAGING-BASED SPATIAL PROTEOMICS TECHNIQUES SUCH AS IMAGING MASS SPECTROMETRY, MULTIPLEXED ION BEAM IMAGING, AND CODEX CAN PROFILE UP TO 100 PROTEINS WITH SUBCELLULAR RESOLUTION, BUT THEY ARE LIMITED TO 200–500 NM RESOLUTION AND CANNOT VISUALIZE NANOSCALE PROTEIN ASSEMBLIES AT THE MOLECULAR SCALE. SINGLE-MOLECULE LOCALIZATION MICROSCOPY (SMLM) ACHIEVES NANOMETER PRECISION, ENABLING VISUALIZATION OF PROTEINS AT THE SCALE OF INDIVIDUAL MOLECULES. AMONG THESE METHODS, DNA-PAINT PROVIDES THEORETICALLY UNLIMITED MULTIPLEXING BUT SUFFERS FROM SLOW ACQUISITION, SEQUENTIAL IMAGING REQUIREMENTS, SAMPLE DAMAGE FROM REPEATED WASHING, SYSTEM INSTABILITY DURING MULTI-ROUND IMAGING, AND HIGH BACKGROUND IN THICK SAMPLES. THIS PROJECT INTRODUCES SIMUL-PROTEOMICS, A NEXT-GENERATION SPATIAL PROTEOMICS PLATFORM THAT ENABLES HIGH-THROUGHPUT, SIMULTANEOUS MULTIPLEXED IMAGING AT SINGLE-PROTEIN RESOLUTION. BY INTEGRATING TRANSFORMATIVE SPECTRAL PHASOR ANALYSIS, SPECTRALLY ENGINEERED PROBES SUCH AS QUANTUM DOTS, AND LIGHT SHEET ILLUMINATION, SIMUL-PROTEOMICS DIRECTLY OVERCOMES THE LIMITATIONS OF DNA-PAINT. THIS APPROACH ELIMINATES SEQUENTIAL READOUT, MINIMIZES SAMPLE PERTURBATION, AND IMPROVES SPEED BY MORE THAN 100-FOLD FOR UP TO 60-PLEXED IMAGING, ENABLING QUANTITATIVE NANOSCALE MAPPING OF PROTEIN DISTRIBUTIONS AND INTERACTIONS IN CELLS, TISSUES, AND SMALL ORGANISMS IN A SINGLE ROUND. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL DELIVER A TRANSFORMATIVE TECHNOLOGY PLATFORM CAPABLE OF RESOLVING NANOSCALE PROTEIN ORGANIZATION IN COMPLEX BIOLOGICAL SYSTEMS WITH UNPRECEDENTED THROUGHPUT. THIS WILL OPEN THE DOOR TO ANSWERING FUNDAMENTAL BIOLOGICAL QUESTIONS ABOUT PROTEIN ASSEMBLIES, SIGNALING NETWORKS, AND SPATIAL REGULATION IN HEALTH AND DISEASE. BY ACHIEVING HIGH- THROUGHPUT SINGLE-PROTEIN SPATIAL PROTEOMICS, THE PROJECT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IMPACT DIVERSE FIELDS INCLUDING CANCER BIOLOGY, NEUROBIOLOGY, AND DEVELOPMENTAL BIOLOGY, WHILE ALSO LAYING THE GROUNDWORK FOR FUTURE TRANSLATIONAL APPLICATIONS IN DIAGNOSTICS AND THERAPEUTICS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: APPLYING NEW GENOMIC TOOLS TO STUDY CENTROMERE ORGANIZATION, REPLICATION, AND FUNCTION - PROJECT SUMMARY CENTROMERES PLAY A CRITICAL ROLE IN CHROMOSOME SEGREGATION DURING CELL DIVISION, YET MANY FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS ABOUT THEIR STRUCTURE, REPLICATION, AND FUNCTION REMAIN UNANSWERED DUE TO LONGSTANDING TECHNICAL CHALLENGES IN STUDYING THESE HIGHLY REPETITIVE GENOMIC REGIONS. TO OVERCOME THESE HURDLES, WE COMBINE NOVEL GENOMIC TECHNOLOGIES AND MODERN GENETIC TOOLS TO INVESTIGATE BASIC CENTROMERE BIOLOGY AT UNPRECEDENTED RESOLUTION. BY BUILDING ON RECENT ADVANCES IN LONG-READ SEQUENCING AND GENOME ASSEMBLY, WE ARE GENERATING COMPLETE SATELLITE DNA ANNOTATIONS FOR A NEW GAPLESS, DIPLOID HUMAN REFERENCE ASSEMBLY. USING THIS REFERENCE ALONG WITH DIMELO-SEQ, A LONG-READ PROTEIN-DNA INTERACTION MAPPING METHOD THAT WE PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED, WE ARE MAPPING CENTROMERE-ASSOCIATED PROTEINS LIKE CENTROMERE PROTEIN A (CENP-A) ALONG LONG, SINGLE CHROMATIN FIBERS MAPPED TO THEIR EXACT LOCATIONS WITHIN EACH HUMAN CENTROMERE. THIS IS REVEALING THE FINE-SCALE ASSOCIATIONS BETWEEN ENDOGENOUS DNA METHYLATION, CENTROMERE PROTEIN LOCALIZATION, AND REPETITIVE DNA SEQUENCES, WHICH TEND TO BE HYPERMETHYLATED EXCEPT AT SUBREGIONS WHERE CENP-A LOCALIZES AT HIGH DENSITY. THE CAUSAL, FUNCTIONAL, AND MECHANISTIC REASONS FOR DNA HYPOMETHYLATION AT CENTROMERES REMAIN UNKNOWN AND ARE AMONG THE MOST PRESSING FUNDAMENTAL QUESTIONS IN CENTROMERE BIOLOGY. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT LOCALIZED DNA HYPOMETHYLATION HELPS TO RESTRICT CENP-A POSITIONING AND PROMOTE THE EPIGENETIC TRANSMISSION OF CENTROMERE IDENTITY. TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS, WE ARE WORKING COLLABORATIVELY TO DISSECT THE CAUSAL AND FUNCTIONAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN DNA METHYLATION AND CENP-A POSITIONING USING DIMELO-SEQ AND CAREFULLY ENGINEERED GENETIC PERTURBATION EXPERIMENTS. MOVING FORWARD, WE ARE FURTHER REFINING DIMELO-SEQ TO QUANTITATIVELY MAP CENP-A AND OTHER PROTEINS AT SINGLE- NUCLEOSOME RESOLUTION THROUGHOUT THE CELL CYCLE TO UNDERSTAND THE STRUCTURE AND DYNAMICS OF THE INNER KINETOCHORE. WE ARE ALSO COMBINING DIMELO-SEQ WITH OTHER SINGLE-MOLECULE SEQUENCING TECHNOLOGIES TO STUDY HOW CENTROMERIC CHROMATIN IS REPLICATED AND HOW REPLICATION FORK SPEEDS VARY THROUGHOUT PERICENTROMERIC REGIONS. FINALLY, WE ARE DEVELOPING EXPERIMENTAL SYSTEMS THAT WILL ENABLE US TO UNCOVER THE SPECIFIC MECHANISMS RESPONSIBLE FOR DNA HYPOMETHYLATION AT HUMAN CENTROMERES AND FURTHER EXPLORE THE SIGNIFICANCE OF THIS HYPOMETHYLATION FOR CENTROMERE FUNCTION AND EPIGENETIC PROPAGATION. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL COMBINE CUTTING-EDGE GENOMIC APPROACHES WITH TARGETED GENETIC PERTURBATIONS TO DISSECT CAUSAL RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN DNA SEQUENCE, EPIGENETIC MARKS, AND CENTROMERE FUNCTION. BY OVERCOMING PREVIOUSLY INSURMOUNTABLE TECHNICAL BARRIERS, THIS RESEARCH PROMISES TO SIGNIFICANTLY ADVANCE OUR UNDERSTANDING OF CENTROMERE BIOLOGY AND CHROMOSOME SEGREGATION - PROCESSES FUNDAMENTAL TO CELL DIVISION AND GENOME STABILITY ACROSS EUKARYOTES.

description: TARGETING PURINE CATABOLISM AND SIGNALING IN T CELL AUTOIMMUNITY - SUMMARY:  PROPERLY ALLOCATING METABOLIC RESOURCES IS CRUCIAL FOR SUPPORTING THE ENERGETICALLY DEMANDING PROCESSES OF T- CELL PROLIFERATION AND INFLAMMATION THAT DRIVE AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES, SUCH AS MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS AND RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS. ADDITIONALLY, METABOLITES CAN ACT AS LIGANDS THAT INTERACT WITH SPECIFIC CELL-SURFACE RECEPTORS, SHAPING THE T-CELL RESPONSE IN PHYSIOLOGICAL AND PATHOLOGICAL CONTEXTS. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO UNDERSTAND HOW PURINE NUCLE- OSIDES, SPECIFICALLY ADENOSINE AND INOSINE, REGULATE T-CELL INFLAMMATION AND EXPLORE THE POTENTIAL THERAPEUTIC BENEFITS OF TARGETING PURINE METABOLISM AND SIGNALING IN ANIMAL MODELS OF AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES. THROUGH AN INTEGRATED ANALYSIS OF METABOLOME, STABLE ISOTOPE TRACING, TRANSCRIPTOME, AND T-CELL FUNCTION, WE HAVE REVEALED THAT EFFECTOR T CELLS CATABOLIZE (I.E., BREAK DOWN TO RELEASE ENERGY) PURINE. WE ALSO DISCOVERED THAT PURINES ENGAGE CELL SURFACE PURINE-RECEPTOR SIGNALING AND INTRACELLULAR PURINE CATABOLISM DIFFERENTLY, LEADING TO OPPOSING IMMUNE MODULATORY EFFECTS ON T CELLS. EXTRACELLULAR ADENOSINE ACTS ON THE ADENOSINE A2A RECEPTOR AND SUP- PRESSES T-CELL INFLAMMATION. ON THE OTHER HAND, EQUILIBRATIVE AND CONCENTRATIVE NUCLEOSIDE TRANSPORTERS (ENTS/CNTS), ALONG WITH ADENOSINE DEAMINASE (ADA), ALLOW T CELLS TO TAKE UP ADENOSINE AND CONVERT IT INTO ITS IMMEDIATE METABOLIC PRODUCT, INOSINE. SUBSEQUENTLY, PURINE NUCLEOSIDE PHOSPHORYLASE (PNP) BREAKS DOWN INO- SINE, PRODUCING CARBON AND ENERGY THAT SUPPORT T-CELL PROLIFERATION AND INFLAMMATION. ACCORDINGLY, GENETICALLY OR PHARMACOLOGICALLY ABLATING PURINE CATABOLIZING ENZYME PNP IN T CELLS SUPPRESSES INFLAMMATION AND AUTOIMMUN- ITY IN VIVO.  HENCE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT THE ADENOSINE-INOSINE AXIS ACTS AS AN IMMUNE-METABOLIC CHECKPOINT COORDINATING BIOENERGETIC AND RECEPTOR-SIGNALING RESPONSES TO REGULATE T-CELL-MEDIATED INFLAMMATION AND AUTOIMMUNITY. THE AIMS OF THIS PROPOSAL ARE TO 1) DECIPHER THE MOLECULAR AND SIGNALING MECHANISMS THAT CONTROL PURINE METABOLISM IN T CELLS; 2) DETERMINE THE OUTCOMES OF MODULATING PURINE METABOLISM AND RECEPTOR SIGNALING IN REGULATING THE EFFECTOR FUNCTION OF T CELLS; AND 3) DEVELOP AND TEST COMPLEMENTARY PHARMACOLOGICAL, GENETIC, AND METABOLIC STRATEGIES TO MODULATE INFLAMMATORY RESPONSE AND AUTOIMMUNITY IN ANIMAL MODELS. THIS PROJECT’S EXPECTED OUT- COMES ARE SIGNIFICANT AS THEY WILL REVEAL THE FUNDAMENTAL PRINCIPLES OF THE EMERGING CONNECTIONS BETWEEN CELL METABOLISM, SIGNALING, AND T-CELL AUTOIMMUNITY. NOTABLY, THE PNP INHIBITOR (FORODENSINE) AND ADA INHIBITOR (PENTOSTATIN) WERE CLINICALLY USED TO TREAT LEUKEMIA. OUR PROPOSED PRECLINICAL STUDIES ARE INNOVATIVE AS THEY WILL REPURPOSE THESE TWO DRUGS FOR TREATING AUTOIMMUNITY. THESE STUDIES ARE CRITICAL TO DEVELOPING NOVEL APPROACHES AND THERAPEUTIC INTERVENTIONS THAT IMPROVE CLINICAL OUTCOMES OF AUTOIMMUNE DISEASES SUCH AS MULTIPLE SCLERO- SIS AND RHEUMATOID ARTHRITIS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE RESILIENT BRACE: A FLEXIBLE, ADJUSTABLE, CONNECTED BRACING SYSTEM FOR ADOLESCENT IDIOPATHIC SCOLIOSIS - PROJECT SUMMARY MORE THAN 12,000 ADOLESCENTS ANNUALLY ARE DIAGNOSED WITH IDIOPATHIC SCOLIOSIS (IS), A PROGRESSIVE ABNORMAL CURVATURE OF THE SPINE. CURRENT STANDARD OF CARE IS FOR PATIENTS TO WEAR A RIGID BRACE FOR UP TO 18 HOURS/DAY TO PREVENT THE CURVATURE FROM WORSENING (PROGRESSING), BUT THIS TREATMENT FAILS FOR ONE QUARTER OF PATIENTS WHO ARE CONSCIENTIOUS IN FOLLOWING IT. WORSE STILL, NEARLY HALF OF ADOLESCENT PATIENTS DO NOT WEAR THEIR BRACE AS PRESCRIBED BECAUSE THE DEVICES ARE UNCOMFORTABLE AND RESTRICTIVE, DIFFICULT TO USE AND ADJUST, AND CONSPICUOUS AND SOCIALLY STIGMATIZING. PATIENTS FOR WHOM BRACING IS UNSUCCESSFUL––EITHER BECAUSE THEY FAIL TO RESPOND OR THROUGH DISUSE– –RISK PERMANENT DEFORMITY AND FREQUENTLY MUST UNDERGO SPINAL FUSION SURGERY. BESIDES COSTING THE HEALTHCARE SYSTEM HUNDREDS OF MILLIONS OF DOLLARS EACH YEAR, THESE SURGERIES LEAVE YOUNG PATIENTS WITH LIFE-LONG CONSEQUENCES INCLUDING REDUCED SPINAL MOBILITY AND INCREASED RISK OF CHRONIC PAIN.  TO IMPROVE PATIENT COMPLIANCE AND TREATMENT EFFECTIVENESS, THINKS WORKS, PBC, IS DEVELOPING A NOVEL PATIENT-CENTERED, LOW-PROFILE, FLEXIBLE SCOLIOSIS BRACE THAT IMPROVES COMFORT, ALLOWS MOBILITY, AND PROVIDES REAL- TIME TREATMENT MONITORING. INSPIRED BY THE HUMAN SPINE, THE TW BRACE HAS A FLEXIBLE MECHANICAL COLUMN THAT ALLOWS IT TO DELIVER TREATMENT WHILE PRESERVING MOVEMENT. FURTHERMORE, WHEREAS CURRENT BRACES, AT BEST, ONLY STOP THE PROGRESSION OF A PATIENT'S CURVE, THE TW BRACE CAN EASILY BE CONFIGURED TO ATTEMPT TO CORRECT THE PATIENT'S CURVE. THE MECHANICAL COLUMN IS TETHERED TO PATIENTS BY A FABRIC STRAPPING SYSTEM THAT IS BARELY NOTICEABLE; IT IS SUFFICIENTLY LOW PROFILE THAT IT CAN BE CONCEALED UNDER CLOTHING.  WE CONDUCTED A PILOT STUDY WITH AN EARLY PROTOTYPE OF THE BRACE. AFTER WEARING THE PROTOTYPE FOR 20 MINUTES, 14 OF 20 ADOLESCENT IS PATIENTS EXPERIENCED A REDUCTION IN AN ABNORMAL CURVATURE. IMPORTANTLY––FOR PATIENT COMPLIANCE––16 PREFERRED THE TW BRACE OVER THEIR EXISTING RIGID BRACE. THESE PROMISING RESULTS SUGGEST THE TW BRACE SYSTEM CAN DELIVER EFFECTIVE TREATMENT THAT IS MUCH MORE ACCEPTABLE TO ADOLESCENT PATIENTS.  HERE, WE PROPOSE TO REFINE ASPECTS OF THE TW BRACE DESIGN AND INVESTIGATE WHETHER SUBJECTS FIND THE BRACE ACCEPTABLE FOR EXTENDED WEAR. IN PARTICULAR, WE WILL TEST ALTERNATIVE MATERIALS FOR THE MECHANICAL COLUMN AND STRATEGIES FOR MARKING THE STRAPS TO MAKE THESE COMPONENTS MORE COMPATIBLE WITH X-RAY IMAGING. WE WILL CONDUCT A STUDY WITH YOUNG ADOLESCENTS TO GATHER FEEDBACK ON THE BRACE'S FASTENING (SECUREMENT) MECHANISM AND TO ENSURE THEY CAN GENERATE SUFFICIENT FORCE TO USE THE BRACE INDEPENDENTLY. THEN, WE WILL CONDUCT A 2-DAY WEAR TEST AND COLLECT FEEDBACK ON SUBJECTS' EXPERIENCES WEARING THE BRACE.  THESE STUDIES WILL PROVIDE CRITICAL INSIGHTS FOR FINALIZING THE DESIGN OF THE BRACE, AND THE RESULTS WILL PROVIDE A STARTING POINT FOR ENGAGING WITH THE FDA TO PLAN AN EXPLORATORY CLINICAL TRIAL. THIS WILL ACCELERATE DEVELOPMENT OF THIS GROUNDBREAKING TREATMENT TO IMPROVE THE OUTCOMES AND QUALITY-OF-LIFE FOR ADOLESCENT IS PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT OF A PHENOLICS DEPLETION CHIP (PDC) FOR USE IN INSULIN DELIVERY PATCH PUMPS - DEVELOPMENT OF A PHENOLICS DEPLETION CHIP (PDC) FOR USE IN  INSULIN DELIVERY PATCH PUMPS PROJECT SUMMARY:  THE OVERARCHING AIM OF THIS PROJECT IS TO DEVELOP A SMALL, LOW POWER, PHENOLIC DEPLETION CHIP (PDC) THAT WILL REMOVE PHENOLIC COMPOUNDS (PHENOL AND META-CRESOL) FROM INSULIN FORMULATIONS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO INJECTION IN A BODY WORN INSULIN INFUSION DEVICE. REMOVING THE PHENOLIC COMPOUNDS WILL REDUCE IRRITATION, MINIMIZE SITE LOSS, PREVENT FORMATION OF INSULIN FIBRILS AND REDUCE INTERFERENCE WITH CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORS (CGMS). IF SUCCESSFULLY DEVELOPED, THE PDC WILL EXTEND THE LIFETIME OF WEARABLE CONTINUOUS SUBCUTANEOUS INSULIN INFUSION (CSII) DEVICES AND ALLOW FOR INTEGRATION OF CGMS INTO A SINGLE BODY WORN ARTIFICIAL PANCREAS. IN PHASE I, SFC’S PATENTED FLOW-THROUGH RING ELECTRODE STRUCTURE WILL BE MODIFIED WITH SUBSTRATE COATINGS THAT WILL ELECTROCHEMICALLY OXIDIZE AND TRAP PHENOLIC COMPOUNDS. THE PROOF-OF-CONCEPT FOR DEVELOPMENT OF THIS DEVICE WILL BE DEMONSTRATED BY ACCOMPLISHING THE FOLLOWING TASKS. TASK 1: MODIFY THE FLOW-THROUGH RING ELECTRODE BY COATING WITH VARIOUS SUBSTRATES FOR ELECTROCHEMICAL OXIDATION AND REMOVAL OF PHENOLIC PRESERVATIVES FROM SOLUTION. TASK 2: OPTIMIZE DESIGN AND OPERATIONAL PARAMETERS OF PDC FOR REMOVAL OF PHENOLIC COMPOUNDS. TASK 3: DESIGN PROTOTYPE PDC TO REDUCE PHENOLIC LOAD WITHOUT DAMAGING INSULIN.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A CARDIOPULMONARY UNIT-ON-A-CHIP TO INVESTIGATE THE PATHOPHYSIOLOGY AND DEVELOP TARGETED TREATMENTS FOR RIGHT VENTRICULAR HYPERTROPHY CAUSED BY PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION - PROJECT SUMMARY: RIGHT VENTRICULAR HYPERTROPHY (RVH), THE PRIMARY CAUSE OF MORTALITY IN PATIENTS WITH PULMONARY ARTERIAL HYPERTENSION (PAH), DEVELOPS FROM INCREASED RESISTANCE IN THE PULMONARY CIRCULATION, NECESSITATING GREATER WORK FROM THE HEART. THE COMPLEX PATHOBIOLOGY OF PAH-RVH INVOLVES MECHANICAL, ELECTRICAL, CHEMICAL, CELLULAR, AND MOLECULAR CHANGES IN THE RV, INCLUDING THE INFLUENCE OF BIOLOGICAL SEX AND SEX HORMONES. DESPITE THE SIGNIFICANT CLINICAL NEED, THE STRUCTURAL, METABOLIC, AND MOLECULAR FOUNDATIONS OF RVH, INCLUDING SEX-BASED DIFFERENCES, REMAIN UNDER- INVESTIGATED. THIS IS DUE TO THE ABSENCE OF SOPHISTICATED MODELS THAT ACCURATELY MIMIC HUMAN PAH-RVH, HINDERING THE DEVELOPMENT OF EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS. TRADITIONAL APPROACHES, SUCH AS ANIMAL MODELS, RV BIOPSIES, AND 2D CELLULAR MODELS, ARE INSUFFICIENT. THESE METHODS FAIL TO CAPTURE THE FULL SPECTRUM OF RVH MANIFESTATIONS IN HUMANS, DIFFERENTIATE ADAPTIVE FROM MALADAPTIVE HYPERTROPHY, OR ELUCIDATE THE INTERACTION BETWEEN THE RV AND PULMONARY VASCULATURE. THUS, THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED FOR AN INNOVATIVE MODEL THAT ACCURATELY REFLECTS PAH-RVH IN BOTH SEXES TO BRIDGE KNOWLEDGE GAPS AND FACILITATE TARGETED THERAPY DEVELOPMENT. MICROFLUIDIC TECHNOLOGY HAS GIVEN RISE TO THE CUTTING-EDGE EXPERIMENTAL MODEL SYSTEM TERMED ‘ORGAN- OR DISEASE-ON-A-CHIP’, ALLOWING FOR MICROSCALE ORGAN SYSTEM REPRESENTATION. IN THE ABSENCE OF EXISTING MODELS FOR PAH, WE RECENTLY DEVELOPED A MICROFLUIDIC CHIP THAT SIMULATES THE CONDITIONS OF PAH-AFFECTED PULMONARY ARTERIES OR ARTERIOLES. WE REFINED THE DEVICE TO MIMIC BOTH THE RV AND PULMONARY ARTERY, SEPARATED BY A COLLAGEN LAYER, ENABLING THE CULTURING OF CARDIOMYOCYTES AND PULMONARY ARTERIAL CELLS. WE NOW SEEK TO DEVELOP A MORE SOPHISTICATED MODEL SYSTEM TERMED ‘CARDIOPULMONARY UNIT-ON-A-CHIP’ BY INCORPORATING THREE MAJOR PHYSIOLOGICALLY RELEVANT FEATURES OF THE RV: RHYTHMIC CONTRACTION AND EXPANSION, BLOOD FLOW-INDUCED PRESSURE, AND ELECTRICAL STIMULATION. THIS MODEL WILL INTEGRATE TWO CHIPS, ONE EMULATING THE RV AND THE OTHER THE PULMONARY ARTERY (PA), EQUIPPED TO PRODUCE RHYTHMIC HEARTBEATS, RIGHT VENTRICULAR OR PULMONARY ARTERIAL PRESSURE, AND AN ELECTROPHYSIOLOGICAL ENVIRONMENT. BY CULTURING RELEVANT CELLS ON THE CHIPS, WE AIM TO REPLICATE KEY PAH-RVH PATHOLOGIES, EXPLORE THE EFFECTS OF BIOLOGICAL SEX AND SEX HORMONES, AND ASSESS THE BENEFITS OF CURRENT PAH AND RV-TARGETED MEDICATIONS. THE INVESTIGATIVE TEAM COMPRISES EXPERTS IN PAH MODELS, CARDIAC PHYSIOLOGY, MICROFLUIDICS, CELL BIOLOGY, PATIENT CARE, AND BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT, AND IS HIGHLY QUALIFIED TO ACCOMPLISH THE GOALS OF THIS PROJECT. THIS IS A TRULY INNOVATIVE PROJECT, BOTH IN CONCEPT AND POTENTIAL CLINICAL APPLICATION. IT DEPLOYS MICROENGINEERING PRECISION TO UNDERSTAND PATHOLOGICAL PROCESSES AND DEVELOP RVH THERAPIES. THIS NOVEL MODEL HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TRANSFORM EXPERIMENTAL MODEL SYSTEMS, WITH APPLICATIONS EXTENDING BEYOND PAH-RVH TO OTHER CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES. IMPORTANTLY, THIS NEAR-PHYSIOLOGICAL MODEL, WHICH EMULATES THE TISSUE-LEVEL FUNCTIONALITY OF TWO VITAL ORGAN SYSTEMS (THE HEART AND PULMONARY VASCULATURE), ALIGNS WITH THE NIH PRECISION MEDICINE INITIATIVE'S FOCUS ON PERSONALIZED MEDICINE AND THE FDA’S EFFORTS TO MODERNIZE DRUG DEVELOPMENT, ADHERING TO THE 3RS PRINCIPLE (REPLACE, REDUCE, REFINE) FOR ETHICAL ANIMAL RESEARCH.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: ADVANCING PEDIATRIC ECMO THROUGH A BIOCOMPATIBLE SYSTEM DESIGN - PROJECT SUMMARY INFLO MEDICAL IS REVOLUTIONIZING PEDIATRIC ECMO WITH A NEXT-GENERATION SYSTEM ENGINEERED TO MINIMIZE HEMOLYSIS AND THROMBOSIS, DELIVERING SAFER, MORE RELIABLE LIFE SUPPORT FOR CRITICALLY ILL CHILDREN. EXTRACORPOREAL MEMBRANE OXYGENATION (ECMO) THERAPY IS ONE OF THE MOST POWERFUL TOOLS IN MODERN PEDIATRIC CRITICAL CARE—OFTEN THE LAST RESORT FOR CHILDREN SUFFERING FROM LIFE-THREATENING HEART AND LUNG FAILURE. HOWEVER, DESPITE ITS LIFE-SAVING POTENTIAL, CURRENT ECMO TECHNOLOGY IS CONSTRAINED BY OUTDATED DESIGNS AND HIGH COMPLICATION RATES, PARTICULARLY IN PEDIATRIC PATIENTS THAT OFTEN PRESENT WITH DISTURBED COAGULATION PATHWAYS. THROMBOSIS IN THE PUMP AND OXYGENATOR COMPONENTS REMAINS A MAJOR CHALLENGE, CONTRIBUTING TO A STAGGERING 38% COMPLICATION RATE IN CHILDREN AND LIMITING BROADER CLINICAL ADOPTION. AS THE GLOBAL BURDEN OF CRITICAL ILLNESS— INCLUDING CONDITIONS LIKE SEPSIS, WHICH CAUSES 1 IN 5 CHILD DEATHS—CONTINUES TO RISE, THERE IS AN URGENT NEED FOR SAFER, MORE ACCESSIBLE ECMO SOLUTIONS TAILORED TO THE UNIQUE NEEDS OF PEDIATRIC PATIENTS. TO ADDRESS THESE URGENT GAPS, INFLO MEDICAL WILL OPTIMIZE ITS NEXT-GENERATION ECMO PLATFORM, THE MOBYBOX, FOR PEDIATRIC USE. THIS COMPACT SYSTEM INCORPORATES A PULSATILE DISPLACEMENT PUMP, AND AN ADVANCED GAS EXCHANGER, SPECIFICALLY ENGINEERED TO REDUCE THROMBOGENICITY AND IMPROVE GAS EXCHANGE PERFORMANCE. EARLY STUDIES IN ANIMAL MODELS AND CLINICAL SETTINGS HAVE ALREADY SHOWN A MARKED REDUCTION IN THROMBUS FORMATION FOR THE ADULT MODEL COMPARED TO EXISTING COMMERCIAL SYSTEMS. THIS NIH SBIR PHASE I PROPOSAL AIMS TO EXPAND MOBYBOX’S CAPABILITIES TO MEET THE DELICATE REQUIREMENTS OF PEDIATRIC ECMO THROUGH TWO COMPLEMENTARY AIMS:  • AIM 1: REDESIGN THE GAS EXCHANGER’S FLOW PATH TO ENHANCE HEMOCOMPATIBILITY WHILE MINIMIZING PRIMING  VOLUME. OXYGENATOR GEOMETRIES WILL BE ITERATIVELY OPTIMIZED USING COMPUTATIONAL FLUID DYNAMICS TO ENSURE  UNIFORM BLOOD FLOW AND REDUCED SHEAR STRESS AT LOW PEDIATRIC FLOW RATES. THESE DESIGNS WILL BE VALIDATED  THROUGH BENCHTOP TESTING AND OVINE ANIMAL MODELS.  • AIM 2: OPTIMIZE THE DISPLACEMENT PUMP FOR PEDIATRIC FLOW CONDITIONS AND BENCHMARK ITS PERFORMANCE  AGAINST TRADITIONAL CENTRIFUGAL PUMPS. BECAUSE ADVERSE EVENTS LIKE THROMBUS FORMATION AND CIRCUIT FAILURE  ARE MORE LIKELY AT LOW FLOW RATES, THIS AIM WILL DIRECTLY EVALUATE BIOCOMPATIBILITY AND BLOOD DAMAGE METRICS,  TESTING THE HYPOTHESIS THAT OUR PULSATILE PUMP REDUCES SHEAR STRESS, HEMOLYSIS, AND CLOTTING RISK. BY ADDRESSING THE CRITICAL LIMITATIONS OF CURRENT ECMO TECHNOLOGY, THIS PROJECT HAS THE POTENTIAL TO SIGNIFICANTLY REDUCE COMPLICATIONS AND EXPAND ACCESS TO LIFE-SAVING EXTRACORPOREAL SUPPORT FOR TENS OF THOUSANDS OF VULNERABLE CHILDREN EACH YEAR. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION WILL GENERATE KEY VALIDATION DATA TO SUPPORT FUTURE FDA 510(K) CLEARANCE AND ACCELERATE THE PATH TO COMMERCIALIZATION FOR PEDIATRIC APPLICATIONS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT AND IMPROVEMENT OF RESEARCH SOFTWARE FOR DNA METHYLATION AND RNA SEQUENCING ANALYSIS - PROJECT SUMMARY I AM A RESEARCH SOFTWARE ENGINEER IN DR. HUI SHEN’S LABORATORY AT THE VAN ANDEL INSTITUTE (VAI), WHERE WE FOCUS ON THE ORIGIN OF CANCER THROUGH DNA METHYLATION AND SINGLE-CELL TECHNOLOGIES. I AM CURRENTLY SUPPORTED BY DR. SHEN’S ESI MERIT AWARD (R37CA230748) AND A COOPERATIVE AGREEMENT FOR THE GENOMIC DATA ANALYSIS CENTER'S INTEGRATIVE CANCER EPIGENOMIC DATA ANALYSIS CENTER (U24CA264023) FROM THE NCI, AS WELL AS A COMMONS FUND AWARD (UM1DA058219). AS PART OF THESE EFFORTS, I DEVELOP STANDARDS-COMPLIANT TOOLS THAT WORK ACROSS A WIDE SPECTRUM OF INPUTS. FOR EXAMPLE, I DEVELOPED OR CO-DEVELOPED BISCUIT, BISCUITEER, DUPSIFTER, AND BISPLOTTI – TOOLS FOR ANALYZING WHOLE GENOME BISULFITE SEQUENCING (WGBS) AND WGBS-LIKE DATA. BISCUIT AND DUPSIFTER ARE AVAILABLE ON BIOCONDA AND HAVE BEEN DOWNLOADED A COMBINED >23,700 TIMES, WHILE BISCUITEER IS AVAILABLE ON BIOCONDUCTOR AND HAS BEEN DOWNLOADED >9,000 TIMES BY >2,700 UNIQUE IP ADDRESSES. I WORKED WITH THE ORIGINAL STORM-SEQ TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPERS (AT VAI AND TAKARA BIO) AND DEVELOPED A QUALITY CONTROL (QC) PIPELINE FOR DETECTING AND MITIGATING CONTAMINATION FROM ADAPTER OLIGONUCLEOTIDES, MISSED PLATE WELLS DURING CELL SORTING, AND FAILED RIBO-DEPLETION. IN ADDITION, I DEVELOPED A PIPELINE FOR ADDING AN  IN SILICO BARCODE  TO EACH READ AND ALIGNING STORM-SEQ DATA TO A REFERENCE GENOME. ALL MY TOOLS ARE WELL-DOCUMENTED IN DETAILED GITHUB REPOSITORY README FILES, R MARKDOWN VIGNETTES, OR STATIC WEBSITES. IN THIS R50 PROJECT, I WILL SUPPORT DR. SHEN’S PROJECTS BY REMOVING UNUSED CODE FROM BISCUIT, IMPROVING THE SPEED WHICH DNA METHYLATION INFORMATION IS EXTRACTED FROM ALIGNED BAMS, AND CREATING A TESTING FRAMEWORK. I WILL SIMPLIFY DUPSIFTER BY RE-CODING HOW THE TWO BISULFITE STRANDS ARE DELINEATED AND ADD FUNCTIONS FOR DIFFERENTIATING UNIQUE MOLECULAR INDEXES (UMIS) IN THE DUPLICATE READ SIGNATURE. FOR THE RNA-SEQ TOOLS, I WILL ADD NEW STORM-SEQ QC METRICS AND A FUNCTION FOR INCLUDING CELL BARCODES AND UMIS SIMULTANEOUSLY. FOR MY INDEPENDENT R50 RESEARCH PROJECTS, I WILL DEVELOP NEW TOOLS FOR ANALYZING THOUSANDS OF WGBS SAMPLES ACROSS MULTIPLE TISSUES FROM THE SEQUENCING READ ARCHIVE (SRA) AND IDENTIFYING CONSERVED HYPER- AND HYPO-METHYLATED REGIONS. I WILL ALSO DEVELOP A TOOL THAT READS RAW FASTQ FILES AND FILTERS OUT POTENTIAL STRAND INVASION EVENTS THAT OCCUR WHEN USING TEMPLATE SWITCHING OLIGONUCLEOTIDES DURING REVERSE TRANSCRIPTION OR RNA-RNA INTERACTION EVENTS. THESE CHIMERIC READS CAN AFFECT DOWNSTREAM ANALYSIS THROUGH IMPROPER COLLAPSING OF UMIS OR MISIDENTIFYING RNA-RNA INTERACTIONS AS STRUCTURAL VARIANTS. THROUGH THIS R50 AWARD, I WILL COMPLETE MY MS IN SOFTWARE ENGINEERING; GROW MY UNDERSTANDING OF DATA COMPRESSION TECHNIQUES; APPLY THAT KNOWLEDGE TO STORE AND MANIPULATE LARGE BIOMEDICAL DATASETS; AND APPLY FORMAL SOFTWARE ENGINEERING PRINCIPLES TO THE TOOLS THAT I DEVELOP, THUS ESTABLISHING MYSELF AS A HIGH-QUALITY RESEARCH SOFTWARE ENGINEER AT VAI, AND FOR THE LARGER RESEARCH SOFTWARE FIELD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: STRUCTURE-BASED INVESTIGATION OF NEUROTRANSMITTERS AS MODIFIERS OF TAU AGGREGATION - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT NEUROTRANSMITTERS (NTS) ARE CRUCIAL SIGNALING MOLECULES IN ANIMALS. BY ACTIVATING RECEPTORS IN NEURONAL CELL MEMBRANES, NTS PLAY WIDESPREAD ROLES IN SYNAPTIC SIGNALING. OUR PROJECT INVESTIGATES AN ADDITIONAL NOVEL ROLE FOR NTS IN MEDIATING PROTEIN AGGREGATION THROUGH DIRECT INTERACTIONS WITH CYTOSOLIC PROTEINS. THIS PROPOSAL ZEROS IN ON THE INVOLVEMENT OF MONOAMINERGIC NTS IN TAU PROTEIN AGGREGATION RELATING TO ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE (AD). IN FORMER CRYOEM STUDIES, WE UNCOVERED A STRUCTURAL BASIS FOR TAU FIBRIL DISAGGREGATION BY NATURAL PRODUCT PHENOLS. BUILDING ON THAT RESEARCH, OUR STRUCTURE-ACTIVITY RELATIONSHIP STUDIES REVEALED THAT MONOAMINERGIC NTS ARE SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTORS TO TAU AGGREGATION. IN THIS REVISED R01 SUBMISSION, WE PROPOSE TO INVESTIGATE CONCENTRATION-DEPENDENT EFFECTS OF MONOAMINERGIC NTS ON TAU SEEDING—A DISEASE-RELEVANT MECHANISM BY WHICH FIBRILLAR AND OLIGOMERIC PROTEINS CATALYZE AGGREGATION. OUR AIMS TEST THE HYPOTHESIS THAT LEVELS OF SPECIFIC MONOAMINERGIC NTS HELP SHAPE PROTEIN AGGREGATION PROPENSITY, MAKING CERTAIN CELLS SELECTIVELY VULNERABLE. THE FOUNDATIONAL STUDIES PROPOSED HERE WILL HELP ESTABLISH A BIOPHYSICAL BASIS BY WHICH MONOAMINERGIC NTS INFLUENCE SEEDING THROUGH A FIBRIL DISAGGREGATION MECHANISM. CRUCIALLY, OUR EXPERIMENTS CONSIDER THE EFFECTS OF DISAGGREGASES ON BOTH FIBRIL AND OLIGOMER STRUCTURES, INVESTIGATING WHETHER FIBRIL DISAGGREGATION COULD LEAD TO OLIGOMER FORMATION. PRELIMINARY DATA INDICATE THAT NTS AND SYNTHETIC DISAGGREGASES ACTIVELY DISAGGREGATE OLIGOMERS AS WELL AS FIBRILS, PREVENTING THE ACCUMULATION OF EITHER MOLECULAR SPECIES. OUR EXPERIMENTAL APPROACHES INTEGRATE CELL SEEDING ASSAYS, FIBRIL DISAGGREGATION MEASURES, AND ELECTRON MICROSCOPY TO DECIPHER THE MOLECULAR STRUCTURES OF FIBRIL COMPLEXES AND THE DETERMINANTS OF DISAGGREGASE POTENCY. STRUCTURAL, CELLULAR, AND BIOCHEMICAL MECHANISTIC STUDIES IN AIMS 1 AND 2 ARE COMPLEMENTED BY MEDICINAL CHEMISTRY APPROACHES IN AIM 3, WHICH FOCUS ON GENERATING SYNTHETIC DISAGGREGASES—PROVIDING AN OPPORTUNITY TO EXPAND UNDERSTANDING OF MOLECULAR DETERMINANTS THAT DEFINE DISAGGREGASE POTENCY. COLLECTIVELY, THIS WORK FILLS KEY GAPS IN KNOWLEDGE BY DEFINING WHICH NTS, PRECURSORS, AND METABOLITES FUNCTION AS TAU DISAGGREGASES, THE CONCENTRATION REGIMES IN WHICH THEY ARE EFFECTIVE, THE GOVERNING FEATURES OF THEIR POTENCY, AND THEIR BINDING SITES ON AD TAU FIBRILS. BY UNCOVERING BIOLOGICAL MECHANISMS THAT REGULATE FIBRIL LOADS AND GENERATING NEW SYNTHETIC DISAGGREGASES, THIS RESEARCH LAYS THE FOUNDATION FOR MANAGING TAU AGGREGATION IN AD.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: APOE AND REELIN INTERACTIONS IN ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY APOE Ε4, WHICH ENCODES APOLIPOPROTEIN E PROTEIN (APOE) Ε4, IS THE STRONGEST GENETIC RISK FACTOR FOR LATE-ONSET ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE. IN THE BRAIN, APOE IS SYNTHESIZED AND LIPIDATED BY ASTROCYTES AND THEN SECRETED TO SHUTTLE CHOLESTEROL TO NEURONS. APOE BINDS TO RECEPTORS ON THE NEURON SURFACE, INCLUDING APOER2 (LRP8) AND VLDLR, AS WELL AS HEPARAN SULFATE (HS). LRP8, VLDLR, AND HS ALL BIND ANOTHER SECRETED PROTEIN, REELIN (ENCODED BY THE RELN GENE), WHICH PLAYS FUNDAMENTAL ROLES IN BRAIN DEVELOPMENT AND SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY. INTRIGUINGLY, RECENT ADVANCES INDICATE THAT REELIN SIGNALING IS A PROTECTIVE PATHWAY AGAINST NEURODEGENERATION. FOR EXAMPLE, THE RARE RELN-COLBOS VARIANT MAY PROTECT FROM THE PSEN1 E280A MUTATION. THIS CHARGE-INCREASING VARIANT H3447R HAS INCREASED AFFINITY FOR HS AND CAN INCREASE DOWNSTREAM DAB1 SIGNALING COMPARED WITH WILD-TYPE (WT) REELIN. SINGLE-NUCLEUS TRANSCRIPTOMICS HAS REVEALED THE LOSS OF RELN+ NEURONS IN THE ENTORHINAL CORTEX IN AD PATIENTS, REDUCING THIS POTENTIALLY PROTECTIVE MOLECULE. NOTABLY, REELIN-DAB1 SIGNALING MODIFIES ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE RISK IN APOE Ε44 INDIVIDUALS. REELIN PROTECTION HAS BEEN PROPOSED TO ACT THROUGH THE PATHWAY: REELIN- APOER2/VLDLR/HS-DAB1-GSK3B-PTAU, RESULTING IN REDUCED TAU PHOSPHORYLATION AND AGGREGATION. IN OUR PRELIMINARY STUDIES USING A SPLIT LUCIFERASE ASSAY, WE FOUND THAT APOE Ε4 INHIBITS REELIN ACTIVATION WHILE APOE Ε3 HAS LITTLE EFFECT. FURTHERMORE, IN IPSC-DERIVED APOE Ε44 ORGANOIDS, WE FOUND THAT EXOGENOUS REELIN PROTEIN CAN REDUCE TAU PHOSPHORYLATION AND NEUROFILAMENT LIGHT CHAIN (NFL) SECRETION, A BIOMARKER OF NEURODEGENERATION. THESE EXCITING DATA, COUPLED WITH FACT THAT REELIN AND APOE BIND TO THE SAME RECEPTORS, HAVE LED US TO THE OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS THAT APOE Ε4 COMPETES WITH REELIN FOR RECEPTOR AND HS BINDING, THEREBY REDUCING PROTECTIVE REELIN SIGNALING AND INCREASING ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE RISK. WE WILL TEST THIS OVERARCHING HYPOTHESIS WITH A MULTI-SCALE, INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACH, WITH THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: 1) STUDY RELN+ CELL ASSOCIATION WITH APOE Ε4 AND AD PATHOLOGY IN AD BRAINS; 2) CHARACTERIZE THE IMPACT OF REELIN ON AD MOLECULAR SIGNATURES, COMPARING APOE Ε44 VS APOE Ε33 IN 3D BRAIN ORGANOIDS WITH ISOGENIC BACKGROUND; 3) DEFINE THE MOLECULAR MECHANISMS OF HOW APOE Ε4 DIMINISHES REELIN SIGNALING. SUCCESSFUL COMPLETION OF THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL OFFER INSIGHTS INTO HOW APOE Ε4 INCREASES ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE RISK VIA INTERACTIONS WITH THE REELIN SIGNALING PATHWAY AND HAS THE POTENTIAL TO IDENTIFY NOVEL APPROACHES TO COUNTERACT APOE Ε4, WHICH IS PRESENT IN APPROXIMATELY HALF OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE PATIENTS.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: A GLIMMER OF POSSIBILITY? GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS—INVESTIGATING THEIR INFLUENCE ON THE MIND, METABOLISM, AND EARLY RISK FOR ADRDS IN THE UNDERSTANDING AMERICA STUDY - ABSTRACT GLUCAGON-LIKE PEPTIDE-1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS AND RELATED THERAPIES (GLPS) ARE NOW USED BY MORE THAN 37 MILLION U.S. ADULTS, YET WHETHER THEY PREVENT, DELAY, OR ACCELERATE COGNITIVE DECLINE AND DEMENTIA IN REAL-WORLD POPULATIONS REMAINS UNKNOWN. TRIALS ARE SHORT-TERM AND HIGHLY SELECTED; MEDICAL RECORDS MISS THE GROWING SHARE OF USERS ACCESSING GLPS OUTSIDE TRADITIONAL CLINICAL CHANNELS; AND EXISTING SURVEYS LACK TIMELY GLP SURVEILLANCE AND OBJECTIVE PHENOTYPING. GLIMMER (GLP INFLUENCE ON METABOLISM AND MIND EXAMINED IN REAL-WORLD, REAL-TIME) IS A NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE, HIGH-FREQUENCY GLP SURVEILLANCE PLATFORM EMBEDDED IN THE UNDERSTANDING AMERICA STUDY (UAS), A PROBABILITY-BASED INTERNET PANEL OF ~14,000 U.S. ADULTS WITH 12+ YEARS OF COGNITIVE, BEHAVIORAL, AND CARDIOMETABOLIC DATA. GLIMMER ADDS THREE NEW DATA STREAMS: MONTHLY GLP SURVEILLANCE ACROSS ALL UAS PARTICIPANTS TO CAPTURE TREATMENT DYNAMICS IN NEAR REAL TIME, ANNUAL CORE SURVEYS OF IDENTIFIED USERS AND NON-USERS TO MEASURE SLOWER-CHANGING DOMAINS, AND DEEP PHENOTYPING WITH BODY COMPOSITION ASSESSMENT, CONTINUOUS GLUCOSE MONITORING, AND DIETARY ECOLOGICAL MOMENTARY ASSESSMENT IN CONSENTING RESPONDENTS. TOGETHER, THESE CAPTURE NEW INITIATORS WITH PRE-TREATMENT BASELINES, TRACK FULL TREATMENT TRAJECTORIES, AND GENERATE THE SAMPLE SIZE, PROTOCOL EVIDENCE, AND PRELIMINARY DATA NEEDED FOR FUTURE RESEARCH. THE RESULTING PUBLICLY AVAILABLE RESOURCE WILL PROVIDE THE FIRST NATIONALLY REPRESENTATIVE, REAL-WORLD PLATFORM LINKING LIFECOURSE GLP USE TO COGNITIVE AGING AND ADRD RISK.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT OF THERAPIES AGAINST PERTUSSIS - PROJECT SUMMARY IN THIS RENEWAL R01 PROJECT WE AIM TO ADVANCE NEW SOLUTIONS FOR PREVENTING AND TREATING PERTUSSIS (WHOOPING COUGH), A RESPIRATORY DISEASE THAT CONTINUES TO SPREAD DESPITE HIGH VACCINATION RATES. WE HAVE DEVELOPED 10 ANTIGEN MRNA VACCINES TO PROTECT AGAINST DIPHTHERIA, TETANUS AND PERTUSSIS AND EVALUATED THEM IN MODELS OF PERTUSSIS IN MICE AND RATS. BORDETELLA PERTUSSIS, THE PATHOGEN RESPONSIBLE FOR PERTUSSIS, IS ABLE TO INFECT INFANTS, CHILDREN, ADULTS, AND ELDERLY DESPITE VACCINATION. IN THIS PROJECT, WE AIM TO DEFINE VACCINE FORMULATIONS THAT BLOCK TRANSMISSION AND THEN USE THESE TARGETS TO DEVELOP ANTIBODY THERAPIES TO TREAT THE DISEASE OF PERTUSSIS IN ORDER TO DECREASE MORBIDITY AND MORTALITY IN INFANTS AND DECREASE DISEASE IN OTHER POPULATIONS INCLUDING ELDERLY. A KEY FOCUS OF THE PROJECT IS TO USE THE FLEXIBILITY OF THE MRNA PLATFORM TO EVALUATE ESTABLISHED AND NOVEL ANTIGENS. TO ADDRESS THIS, WE WILL HARNESS OUR IN-HOUSE MRNA PLATFORM TO RAPIDLY PRODUCE AND TEST NOVEL ANTIGEN CANDIDATES, INCLUDING SPHB1, BRKA, VAG8, AND NOVEL ANTIGENS INCLUDING TOXIN SECRETION APPARATUS PROTEINS. THESE WILL BE DELIVERED AS MRNA VACCINES, PAIRED WITH “GENETIC ADJUVANTS” DESIGNED TO ENHANCE SPECIFIC TYPES OF IMMUNITY. WE WILL EVALUATE THESE CANDIDATES IN A NATURAL TRANSMISSION MODEL USING GREEN OLIVE BABOONS, WHICH MIMIC HUMAN PERTUSSIS TRANSMISSION MORE ACCURATELY THAN MICE OR RATS. OUR GOAL IS TO DEFINE WHICH ANTIGENS CAN GENERATE IMMUNE RESPONSES THAT BLOCK TRANSMISSION OF B. PERTUSSIS. IN PARALLEL, WE WILL DEVELOP MONOCLONAL ANTIBODIES THAT CAN SERVE AS TREATMENTS FOR PERTUSSIS. WHILE SOME ANTIBODIES, SUCH AS THOSE TARGETING PERTUSSIS TOXIN, CAN REDUCE DISEASE SYMPTOMS, THEY DO NOT PREVENT TRANSMISSION. WE AIM TO DISCOVER NEW THERAPEUTIC ANTIBODIES THAT CAN BOTH TREAT ILLNESS AND HELP CLEAR THE INFECTION, REDUCING SPREAD AND IMPROVING RECOVERY IN VULNERABLE POPULATIONS, INCLUDING INFANTS, CHILDREN, AND OLDER ADULTS. THIS PROJECT WILL CREATE URGENTLY NEEDED TOOLS TO REDUCE PERTUSSIS DEATHS, IMPROVE PATIENT RECOVERY, AND LESSEN THE HEALTHCARE AND FINANCIAL BURDENS OF THE DISEASE. IN DOING SO, IT WILL ALSO ESTABLISH A NEW MODEL FOR COMBINING MRNA TECHNOLOGY AND ANTIBODY DISCOVERY TO COMBAT OTHER DISEASES SUCH AS PERTUSSIS AS WELL AS OTHER INFECTIOUS DISEASES.

description: MECHANISM OF THE SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION ACROSS THE BACTERIAL CELL ENVELOPE - PROJECT SUMMARY ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE IS AN URGENT THREAT TO PUBLIC HEALTH, PARTICULARLY AMONG GRAM-NEGATIVE BACTERIA, DUE TO THEIR MULTILAYERED CELL ENVELOPE STRUCTURE, WHICH INCLUDES THE OUTER MEMBRANE (OM). THE OM OUTER LEAFLET IS COMPOSED OF LIPOPOLYSACCHARIDE (LPS) MOLECULES THAT MAKE THE OM IMPERMEABLE TO VARIOUS COMPOUNDS, INCLUDING CLINICALLY USED ANTIBIOTICS. OUR LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO GAIN A COMPREHENSIVE UNDERSTANDING OF HOW BACTERIA BUILD AND MAINTAIN HOMEOSTASIS OF THE OM TO AID ANTIBIOTIC DISCOVERY. BACTERIAL ENVELOPE STRESS RESPONSES ARE SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION PATHWAYS THAT CONFER SIGNIFICANT INTRINSIC RESISTANCE TO ANTIBIOTICS, IMMUNE FACTORS, AND OTHER BIOLOGICAL AGENTS TARGETING THE ENVELOPE. THEY ACHIEVE THIS BY MITIGATING DAMAGE AND INHIBITING THE PENETRATION OR ACTIVITY OF THESE AGENTS. DESPITE THEIR IMPORTANCE, THE MOLECULAR SIGNALS AND ACTIVATION MECHANISMS OF STRESS RESPONSES REMAIN POORLY UNDERSTOOD BECAUSE OF THE COMPLEXITY OF ENVELOPE BIOGENESIS. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO ELUCIDATE HOW THE REGULATOR OF CAPSULE SYNTHESIS (RCS) STRESS RESPONSE MONITORS OM INTEGRITY AND PROMOTES OM HOMEOSTASIS. RCS IS ONE OF THE MOST COMPLEX STRESS RESPONSES IN BACTERIA AND CAN TRANSDUCE THE STRESS SIGNAL FROM THE CELL SURFACE TO THE CYTOPLASM. DISRUPTIONS IN THE LPS LAYER AT THE CELL SURFACE, INCLUDING THOSE CAUSED BY CATIONIC ANTIMICROBIAL PEPTIDES (CAMPS) AND LAST-RESORT ANTIBIOTICS LIKE POLYMYXIN B, HAVE LONG BEEN KNOWN TO STRONGLY ACTIVATE RCS. THROUGH GENETIC ANALYSIS, IN VITRO AND IN VIVO BIOCHEMICAL APPROACHES, AND MOLECULAR DYNAMICS SIMULATIONS, WE AIM TO IDENTIFY THE MOLECULAR SIGNAL AND MECHANISM THAT ACTIVATES THE SENSORY PROTEIN RCSF, AND DETERMINE HOW THE STRESS SIGNAL IS TRANSDUCED ACROSS THE MULTILAYERED CELL ENVELOPE. THROUGH OUR RESEARCH, WE WILL PROVIDE A MECHANISTIC UNDERSTANDING OF THE WELL-ESTABLISHED ROLE OF RCS IN RESISTING CAMPS, AND FACILITATE STUDIES ON THE ROLE OF RCS IN IMMUNE EVASION, HOST SURVIVAL, AND PATHOGENESIS. MORE BROADLY, STUDIES OF RCS WILL PROVIDE A NEW MECHANISTIC PARADIGM FOR A POTENTIALLY WIDELY UTILIZED MECHANISM OF ENVELOPE STRESS RESPONSES AND HOW BACTERIA USE THEM TO PROMOTE ANTIBIOTIC RESISTANCE.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: THE GENETIC ETIOLOGIES OF STILLBIRTH: AN EXTREME ON THE DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS CONTINUUM - ABSTRACT STILLBIRTH (SB), A DEVASTATING PREGNANCY OUTCOME IMPACTING OVER 20,000 FAMILIES ANNUALLY, REPRESENTS A PROFOUND MANIFESTATION OF DISRUPTED HUMAN DEVELOPMENT WITHIN THE BROADER SPECTRUM OF DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS (DDS). WHILE THE ETIOLOGICAL UNDERPINNINGS OF MANY SBS REMAIN ELUSIVE, GENETIC FACTORS PERTURBING FUNDAMENTAL DEVELOPMENTAL PROGRAMS ARE SIGNIFICANT CONTRIBUTORS. HISTORICALLY, GENETIC STUDIES OF SB HAVE BEEN CONSTRAINED BY THE CHALLENGES INHERENT IN ASSEMBLING ADEQUATELY POWERED COHORTS AND SYSTEMATIC PHENOTYPING, COUPLED WITH LIMITATIONS ON CONVENTIONAL GENOMICS TECHNOLOGIES. HOWEVER, EMERGING EVIDENCE FROM OUR GROUPS AND OTHERS INDICATES A COMPLEX GENETIC ARCHITECTURE UNDERLYING SB, ENCOMPASSING A MIXTURE OF HIGHLY DELETERIOUS VARIANTS AND A SPECTRUM OF DOMINANT AND RECESSIVE VARIANTS WITH MORE SUBTLE EFFECTS THAT ARE SHARED WITH OTHER DDS. HERE, WE ENDEAVOR TO INTERROGATE THE GENOMIC LANDSCAPE OF SB, CAPITALIZING ON FOUNDATIONAL RESOURCES CURATED BY THE FETAL GENOMICS CONSORTIUM. DURING THIS BRIDGE FUNDING PERIOD, WE WILL AGGREGATE GENOMIC AND PHENOTYPIC DATA FROM AN INITIAL SEQUENCING COHORT OF >1,000 SB CASES AND THEIR FAMILY MEMBERS. WE WILL ANALYZE SHORT-READ SEQUENCING AS A FRONT-LINE STRATEGY (AIM 1). NOVEL ASSOCIATIONS IN SB WILL BE DELINEATED THROUGH INTEGRATIVE ANALYSIS OF ALL VARIANT CLASSES AND INHERITANCE PATTERNS USING A SOPHISTICATED BAYESIAN ANALYTIC FRAMEWORK, AS WELL AS EXPLORATION OF ALL NONCODING REGULATORY ELEMENTS UTILIZING A CATEGORY-WIDE ASSOCIATION. AIM 2 WILL STRATEGICALLY LEVERAGE A MASSIVE-SCALE DATASET OF ~200,000 CASES WITH HETEROGENEOUS DDS THAT WE HAVE AGGREGATED TO COMPARE THE ARCHITECTURE OF SB AS AN EXTREME PHENOTYPE ALONG THE HUMAN DEVELOPMENTAL CONTINUUM. WE WILL ALSO COMPARE THESE DATA TO POPULATION-SCALE SEQUENCING FROM >1 MILLION INDIVIDUALS THAT WE HAVE PROCESSED IN GNOMAD, THE ALL OF US RESEARCH PROGRAM, AND OTHER RESOURCES TO IDENTIFY VARIANTS UNIQUELY ASSOCIATED WITH INVIABILITY AND NEVER SEEN IN THE GENERAL POPULATION, SOMETIMES REFERRED TO AS THE ‘INTOLEROME’. COLLECTIVELY, THIS MULTIFACETED STUDY OF SB WILL ENABLE ACCESS TO THE COMPLETE SPECTRUM OF SB-ASSOCIATED GENETIC VARIATION AT AN UNPRECEDENTED SCALE AND RESOLUTION.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HIV-1 TAT GENETIC VARIATION IMPACTS NEUROHIV - PROJECT ABSTRACT/SUMMARY HIV-1 VIRAL LOAD CAN BE SUPPRESSED IN PEOPLE LIVING WITH HIV (PLWH) THROUGH CONSISTENT USE OF ANTIRETROVIRAL THERAPY (ART). DESPITE THIS, BETWEEN 15 TO 40% OF LWH ARE PREDICTED TO SUFFER FROM HIV-ASSOCIATED NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT (NCI). ALTHOUGH THE PATHOGENESIS OF NCI IS INCOMPLETELY UNDERSTOOD, HIV-1 TRANSACTIVATOR OF TRANSCRIPTION (TAT) IS CAPABLE OF BEING SECRETED FROM INFECTED CELLS, AND ONCE EXTRACELLULAR IN THE CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS) IT WILL INDUCE NEURONAL DYSREGULATION. EARLY IN THE INFECTION, HIV-1 ESTABLISHES A RESERVOIR IN THE BRAIN, EITHER BY ENTERING AS INFECTED PERIVASCULAR MACROPHAGES OR INFECTING RESIDENT MICROGLIA, PRIOR TO THE PATIENT RECEIVING ART. ART DOES NOT AFFECT THE PRODUCTION OF TAT, WHICH IS CONTINUALLY MADE IN THESE CELLS, LEADING TO QUANTIFIABLE LEVELS OF TAT IN THE ABSENCE OF DETECTABLE VIRAL LOAD. TAT SEQUENCE COMPOSITION VARIES WITHIN AND BETWEEN INDIVIDUALS DUE TO HIV-1’S ERROR-PRONE REVERSE TRANSCRIPTASE AND HOST FACTORS SUCH AS APOBEC3G. WE HAVE SHOWN THAT THIS VARIATION IS ASSOCIATED WITH NEUROCOGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT (NCI), AS SHOWN BY COMPARING THE HIV-1 TAT PROTEIN SEQUENCE COMPOSITION FROM IMPAIRED AND NON-IMPAIRED PLWH WITHIN THE DREXEL MEDICINE CNS AIDS RESEARCH AND ERADICATION STUDY (CARES) COHORT. IN THE PAST 5 YEARS, WE HAVE FURTHER DEMONSTRATED THAT TAT COULD BE THE PRODUCT FROM INTACT OR DEFECTIVE VIRIONS FROM CELLULAR RESERVOIRS IN THE BRAIN NAMELY MICROGLIA AND ASTROCYTES AND OTHER PERIPHERAL TISSUES THAT CAN CAUSE BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER DISRUPTION AND NCI. RECOMBINANT TAT101 INJECTED DIRECTLY INTO THE PREFRONTAL CORTEX (PFC) OF ADULT RATS PRODUCED IMPAIRMENT IN LEARNING AND MEMORY TASKS AND EX VIVO ANALYSIS OF THE BRAIN PFC TISSUE SUGGESTED UPREGULATION OF PATHWAYS THAT INDUCE IMMUNE AND CELLULAR RESPONSE TO TOXICITY AND DOWN REGULATION OF GENES THAT ARE INVOLVED IN PROMOTING COGNITION, SYNAPTIC CONNECTIVITY AND DOPAMINE AND GLUTAMATE NEUROTRANSMISSION. THUS, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT TAT PRODUCED BY MICROGLIAL AND ASTROCYTE RESERVOIRS PROMOTE NEUROTOXICITY AND NCI BY SYNERGISTIC DYSREGULATION OF DOPAMINE-GLUTAMATE HOMEOSTASIS AND HEIGHTENED IMMUNE RESPONSE PROMOTING EXCITOTOXICITY IN NEURONS. TO INVESTIGATE THIS, WE PROPOSE THE FOLLOWING THREE AIMS. AIM 1 WILL USE NEAR FULL-LENGTH SEQUENCING OF PROVIRAL DNA FROM CELLULAR RESERVOIRS DERIVED FROM PLWH FROM NATIONAL NEUROHIV TISSUE CONSORTIUM (NNTC) AND CARES COHORTS TO DETERMINE THE MOLECULAR ARCHITECTURE OF THE PROVIRAL RESERVOIRS AND THE TAT VARIANTS EXPRESSED. AIM 2 WILL EXPLORE THE FUNCTION OF THE DEFECTIVE RESERVOIR AND TAT VARIANTS ASSOCIATED WITH INTACT AND PARTIALLY FUNCTIONAL PROVIRUSES. AIM 3 WILL EXPLORE THE IMPACT OF TAT VARIANTS ON PROMOTING EXCITOTOXICITY IN PFC CAUSING IMPAIRED EXECUTIVE FUNCTION AND IMPULSE CONTROL DISORDERS USING AN IN VIVO MODEL OF TAT NEUROPATHOGENESIS. THESE STUDIES WILL CONTRIBUTE TO DEFINING THE DIFFERENTIAL AND SYNERGISTIC EFFECTS OF TAT IN PROMOTING NCI. OVERALL, THESE STUDIES WILL LEAD TO A BETTER UNDERSTANDING OF THE ETIOLOGY OF HAND, POTENTIAL DEVELOPMENT OF DIAGNOSTIC ASSAY FOR HAND, AND IDENTIFICATION OF NOVEL TAT-MEDIATED TARGETS TO DEVELOP NEW THERAPEUTICS FOR TREATING NCI.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: HEPARAN SULFATE-MEDIATED MECHANISMS OF ALPHA-SYNUCLEIN PATHOLOGY IN DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES DISEASE - PROJECT SUMMARY DEMENTIA WITH LEWY BODIES (DLB) IS A PROGRESSIVE NEURODEGENERATIVE DISEASE CHARACTERIZED BY INTRACELLULAR INCLUSIONS OF FIBRILLAR Α-SYNUCLEIN (Α-SYN) PROTEIN. WHILE Α-SYN INCLUSIONS ARE PRIMARILY DETECTED IN SYNAPTICALLY CONNECTED NEURONS, Α-SYN IS ALSO FOUND IN THE EXTRACELLULAR FLUIDS OF DLB PATIENTS, AND IMPAIRING THE NEURONAL INTERNALIZATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS SLOWS Α-SYN PATHOLOGY IN MOUSE MODELS OF SYNUCLEINOPATHY. HEPARAN SULFATE (HS) PROTEOGLYCANS ARE GLYCOPROTEINS THAT INTERACT WITH PROTEIN FIBRILS ON THE CELL SURFACE AND IN THE SYNAPSES, PROMOTING THE CELLULAR INTERNALIZATION OF AMYLOID-Β AND PRION FIBRILS IN VITRO AND ACCELERATING THE DISEASE PROGRESSION IN ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND PRION-INFECTED MICE. WE AND OTHERS FOUND THAT THE CELLULAR UPTAKE OF PROTEIN FIBRILS IS PROFOUNDLY IMPACTED BY THE HS LENGTH, AND LEVEL AND PATTERN OF SULFATION, WHICH, IMPORTANTLY, VARY WITH BRAIN AGING AND NEURODEGENERATION. DATA FROM OUR LABORATORY SHOWS THAT HS IS A CRUCIAL RECEPTOR FOR THE INTERNALIZATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS IN CORTICAL NEURONS. MOREOVER, GENETICALLY DECREASING HS SULFATION PROFOUNDLY REDUCES THE FORMATION OF Α-SYN INCLUSIONS IN THE SUBSTANTIA NIGRA, HIPPOCAMPUS, AND CORTEX OF MICE INJECTED WITH RECOMBINANT Α-SYN FIBRILS AND SLOWS THE DEVELOPMENT OF BEHAVIORAL DEFICITS. OUR PILOT DRUG TESTS SUGGEST THAT DISRUPTING THE ELECTROSTATIC INTERACTIONS OF HS WITH Α-SYN FIBRILS, POTENTIALLY BY BLOCKING THE HS CELL RECEPTORS OR ALTERING THE LEVELS AND COMPOSITION OF HS, ALMOST COMPLETELY IMPAIRS THE NEURONAL INTERNALIZATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS. WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT HS CONTRIBUTES TO DLB PATHOLOGY BY PROMOTING THE NEURONAL INTERNALIZATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS. IN AIM 1, WE PROPOSE TO MEASURE HOW MANIPULATING HS CHAIN LENGTH AND SULFATION IMPACTS THE NEURONAL INTERNALIZATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS I) IN VITRO, USING CORTICAL NEURONS ISOLATED FROM MOUSE MODELS WITH SHORTER HS CHAINS OR DEFICIENT IN HS SULFATION, AND II) IN VIVO, BY MEASURING THE LEVEL AND BRAIN DISTRIBUTION OF Α-SYN INCLUSIONS, NEURONAL LOSS AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF MOTOR AND COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT IN MICE THAT EXPRESS SHORTER OR LESS SULFATED HS IN SELECTIVE NEURONAL POPULATIONS. WE WILL NEXT TEST THE EFFICACY OF THREE HS-TARGETED DRUGS TO MODULATE THE CHEMICAL COMPOSITION OF HS AND THE INTERNALIZATION AND AGGREGATION OF Α-SYN FIBRILS IN PRIMARY CORTICAL NEURONS AND HUMAN IPSC-DERIVED NEURONS OBTAINED FROM PATIENTS WITH SYNUCLEINOPATHY (AIM 2). THROUGH THESE AIMS, WE EXPECT TO DEFINE NEURONAL HS AS A NEW, FUNDAMENTAL HOST COFACTOR CONTRIBUTING TO THE PROGRESSION OF DLB PATHOLOGY. MOREOVER, OUR STUDIES MAY UNCOVER NEW TARGETS FOR THE RATIONAL DESIGN OF NEUROPROTECTIVE THERAPIES FOR DLB PATIENTS BASED ON SELECTIVELY IMPAIRING THE INTERACTION OF HOST HS WITH Α-SYN FIBRILS.

description: SULFATED GLYCOSAMINOGLYCAN HYDROGELS FOR TREATING BRAIN VOLUME LOSS IN TBI - PROJECT SUMMARY MODERATE TO SEVERE TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURIES (MSTBIS) CAUSE SIGNIFICANT BRAIN VOLUME LOSS AND CAVITATION, WHICH CONTRIBUTES TO LIFE-LONG DISABILITIES AND POOR PROGNOSIS FOR A MAJORITY OF MSTBI PATIENTS. THE BRAIN EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX (ECM) IS A MESHWORK OF HIGHLY GLYCOSYLATED PROTEINS THAT PROVIDE STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL SUPPORT TO NEURAL CELLS IN THE BRAIN. ABERRANT HIGH MANNOSE ECM N-GLYCOSYLATION ACTIVATES THE LECTIN COMPLEMENT PATHWAY AND RECRUITMENT OF INFLAMMATORY MICROGLIA. HOWEVER, THERE ARE NO EFFECTIVE TREATMENTS AND THE ROLE OF THESE FACTORS IN PROMOTING BRAIN VOLUME LOSS IN MSTBI IS UNKNOWN. THERE IS A CRITICAL NEED TO DEVELOP RATIONALLY DESIGNED, ENGINEERED BRAIN TISSUE REPLACEMENT TECHNOLOGIES THAT CAN PREVENT BRAIN VOLUME AND FUNCTION LOSSES POST-MSTBI. WE PREVIOUSLY DEVELOPED A NOVEL ENGINEERED CHONDROITIN SULFATE (ECS) GLYCOMATERIAL AND DEMONSTRATED THAT ACUTELY IMPLANTED ECS MATRICES PROMOTED SUBACUTE AND CHRONIC NEUROPROTECTION AND FUNCTIONAL VASCULAR REPAIR IN MSTBI LESIONS. OUR PRELIMINARY FINDINGS REVEAL THAT THE ABERRANT UPREGULATION OF HIGH MANNOSE N-GLYCANS IN MSTBI LESIONS CORRELATES WITH LECTIN COMPLEMENT AND MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION, AND THAT SULFATION OPTIMIZED CS OLIGOMERS CAN INHIBIT LECTIN COMPLEMENT ACTIVATION AND NEURONAL CYTOTOXITY. BASED ON THIS EVIDENCE, WE HYPOTHESIZE THAT INTRACAVITARY IMPLANTATION OF RATIONALLY DESIGNED ECS MATRIX CARRYING SULFATION OPTIMIZED CS OLIGOMERS WILL MITIGATE COMPLEMENT PATHWAY AND MICROGLIAL ACTIVATION INDUCED BRAIN VOLUME LOSS AFTER MSTBI. WE PROPOSE TO TEST THIS HYPOTHESIS IN THE FOLLOWING THREE SPECIFIC AIMS: AIM 1- DETERMINE LECTIN COMPLEMENT AND MICROGLIA ACTIVATION INHIBITING EFFECTS OF SULFATION OPTIMIZED CS OLIGOMERS IN VITRO; AIM 2- ELUCIDATE MICROGLIAL REGULATION OF ABERRANT ECM REMODELING IN MSTBI; AND AIM 3 - DETERMINE THE EFFECTIVENESS OF SULFATION OPTIMIZED ECS MATRIX IMPLANTS IN MITIGATING CHRONIC BRAIN VOLUME AND FUNCTIONAL LOSSES AFTER MSTBI. OUR PUBLISHED AND PRELIMINARY FINDINGS PROVIDE A COMPELLING BASIS FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF A TARGET SPECIFIC AND DISEASE MODIFYING REGENERATIVE IMMUNOMODULATION THERAPY THAT CAN AMELIORATE ABERRANT ECM REMODELING AND BRAIN VOLUME LOSS IN MSTBI.

agency: Department of Health and Human Services
description: DEVELOPMENT OF A COMMUNITY ENGAGED TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH NETWORK TO ADVANCE SPANISH-LANGUAGE NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT IN COGNITIVE AGING RESEARCH: ECHAR-TR - PROJECT SUMMARY/ABSTRACT HISPANIC OLDER ADULTS IN THE UNITED STATES EXPERIENCE A HIGHER BURDEN OF ALZHEIMER’S DISEASE AND RELATED DEMENTIAS (AD/ADRD), INCLUDING EARLIER SYMPTOM ONSET AND LATER-STAGE DIAGNOSIS COMPARED TO NON-HISPANIC POPULATIONS. TIMELY DIAGNOSIS AND INTERVENTION ARE CRITICAL FOR EFFECTIVE TREATMENT AND IMPROVED OUTCOMES; HOWEVER, SIGNIFICANT GAPS REMAIN. KEY AMONG THESE IS THE LACK OF PSYCHOMETRICALLY ROBUST NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL ASSESSMENT TOOLS AVAILABLE IN SPANISH, THE PREFERRED LANGUAGE FOR NEARLY 40 MILLION HISPANIC INDIVIDUALS IN THE UNITED STATES. LIMITED AVAILABILITY OF VALIDATED TOOLS FOR DIAGNOSIS OF SPANISH-SPEAKING POPULATIONS CONTRIBUTES TO CHALLENGES IN ACCURATE CLINICAL ASSESSMENT AND EARLY DETECTION OF AD/ADRD. THIS PROPOSAL AIMS TO DEVELOP A NATIONWIDE INTERDISCIPLINARY TRANSLATIONAL RESEARCH NETWORK DEDICATED TO RIGOROUSLY ADVANCING THE CREATION AND ROBUST VALIDATION OF SPANISH-LANGUAGE NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL TOOLS FOR AD/ADRD EVALUATIONS. THE NETWORK WILL LEVERAGE EXISTING INFRASTRUCTURE FROM A COMMUNITY ENGAGED RESEARCH NETWORK – THE ECHAR NETWORK – AND WILL INVOLVE COLLABORATION AMONG NEUROPSYCHOLOGISTS, COMMUNITY PARTNERS, AND HEALTH PROVIDERS. IN PHASE I (R61), THE PROJECT WILL ESTABLISH THE NETWORK AND IDENTIFY COGNITIVE HEALTH NEEDS ACROSS SITES. IN PHASE II (R33), ASSESSMENT TOOLS WILL BE DEVELOPED AND PILOTED IN CLINICAL RESEARCH SETTINGS. THESE TOOLS WILL BE REFINED BASED ON PSYCHOMETRIC ANALYSES AND CROSS-SITE FEEDBACK PRIOR TO BROADER DISSEMINATION. THE PROPOSED WORK DIRECTLY ADDRESSES THE NEED FOR VALIDATED NEUROPSYCHOLOGICAL TOOLS TO SUPPORT ACCURATE DIAGNOSIS AND CLINICAL DECISION-MAKING IN SPANISH-SPEAKING POPULATIONS. THIS COMMUNITY-TO-RESEARCH LAB-TOCLINIC MODEL AND MULTI-SITE TRANSLATIONAL FRAMEWORK WILL GENERATE SCALABLE TOOLS AND SHARED RESOURCES THAT ADVANCE COGNITIVE AGING RESEARCH, IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF DEMENTIA CARE FOR A RAPIDLY GROWING SEGMENT OF THE U.S. POPULATION.
